findings.title: Quote failure silently books avg_cost as market price
findings.detail: When the quote call fails or times out, _q() returns avg_cost as the last price without any warning or metadata. Unrealized P&L then reads 0 and market value equals cost. The route injects quote_timeout=3 for every routed call, so the default pane run hits this for TLT (real 81.92, shown 92.00). findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/acct.py:112-134 (fallback at 127 and 133-134; timeout read at 130); injected quote_timeout at backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:297

findings.title: RSI mean-reversion closes longs inside its hold band
findings.detail: rsi_meanrev keeps its position in state['pos'], but the engine never writes state, so the between-threshold branch always returns 0. Any long opened at RSI < lo is flattened as soon as RSI crosses back above lo, instead of being held until RSI > hi. Every rsi_meanrev cell in BMTX, and any BTUNE rsi grid, is affected.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/services/backtest_framework.py:226-241 (return at 240); Backtest.run passes the state dict at about 116-120 and never writes state (no state[...] assignment in the file)
findings.evidence: Scratch test: signal sequence goes 1 -> 0 at RSI 33.18 (inside 30-70); trades [(0,1),(1,0)]. BMTX rsi_meanrev cells therefore reflect an invented exit rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the engine store the target position in state (state['pos'] = target after each decision), or make rsi_meanrev hold explicitly, and add a regression test for the hold band.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed by code and scratch test. backtest_framework.rsi_meanrev returns state.get('pos',0) between thresholds, and nothing in the framework ever writes to state (grep for state[ / setdefault / update returns no writes). verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. Sidecar call with the pane DEFAULT_SYMBOLS (AAPL,SPX,EURUSD,BTCUSDT,GC=F,US10Y,CDXIG) live:true returned symbols [BTCUSDT] only, with dropped_symbols AAPL, SPX, EURUSD, GC=F, US10Y and the warning Dropped 5 null-heavy symbol(s). Independent yfinance check after an outer join of log returns: NaN ratio about 0.43 to 0.44 for each equity, FX, commodity and rate series, and 0.0 for BTC-USD. The nulls are calendar gaps, so the matrix is empty while data exists.

findings.title: Annualized volatility uses sqrt(252) for 24/7 crypto, understating it by about 17%
findings.detail: annualized_vol and rows.annualized_vol use the nominal sqrt(252) for every symbol (corr.py:490-491, 525). The same payload's return_series_summary uses the realized observation density (corr.py:844, 855-875) and gives a different number for BTCUSDT. The pane diagonal labels the nominal value as annualized volatility (CORR.tsx:862).
findings.evidence: BTCUSDT annualized_vol 0.368564 vs return_series_summary annualized_volatility 0.443718 in the same response (annualization_factor 19.11 = sqrt(365)). Independent: sqrt(252) 0.368617, sqrt(365) 0.443783.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one annualization per symbol, sqrt(observations per year) on its own calendar, everywhere in the payload and pane.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed as an internal inconsistency. The same payload has BTCUSDT annualized_vol 0.320958 (nominal sqrt(252) via _annualization_factor, corr.py:1331-1336) and return_series_summary annualized_volatility 0.388067 with factor 19.19 (realized density). That is about 21% apart on this run, versus the 17% the finding cites. The field dictionary calls the nominal number annualized, and the pane diagonal labels it annualized volatility, so the methodology is wrong for a 24/7 asset.

findings.title: Ref mode shows a green live pill
findings.detail: liveSourceMode is state === ok and not cached. It ignores the SRC toggle and the payload's live flag, so when the user selects Ref the pill still reads live with the positive tone.
findings.evidence: Ref call returns metadata.live false, data_state model, sources [computed_return_model], and the pane pill derives from state only, so it shows live.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the pill from metadata.live and data_state (or the coverage statuses), not from the request state.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed by code. CORR.tsx:304-305 sets liveSourceMode = state==='ok' && !cached, which ignores the response's metadata.live. The Pill at 573-579 uses that value for tone and text. A sidecar live:false call returned status ok with metadata.live false and data_state model, so the pill shows a green live label for a non-live result.

findings.title: Reference-mode correlations are generated by construction, not measured
findings.detail: Ref series are built from fixed market betas and volatilities (SAMPLE_MARKET_BETA/VOL at corr.py:34-47, generator at 1074-1100). The matrix therefore encodes assumed cross-asset relationships. The payload labels it computed_reference, but the numbers differ from real data.
findings.evidence: Ref vs real (yfinance 365d log): EURUSD-US10Y ref +0.324 vs real +0.047; BTCUSDT-GC=F ref +0.092 vs real +0.295; AAPL-SPX ref +0.365 vs real +0.337.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the reference matrix clearly labelled as a model, or remove it from the correlation view; do not present its correlations next to measured ones.

findings.title: Downside and Spearman cells silently fall back to Pearson
findings.detail: _matrix_surface uses .get(right, corr), so any missing downside or Spearman cell takes the Pearson value. When there are no negative equal-weight days the downside matrix is empty and every downside cell shows Pearson.
findings.evidence: Code read; not reproduced live (no negative-day case in the test universes).
findings.proposed_fix: Use null for missing downside or Spearman cells and report the fallback in coverage or warnings.

findings.title: Provenance says yfinance for a series that came from ccxt_failover
findings.detail: Envelope sources is ['yfinance'] while the BTCUSDT coverage row says source ccxt_failover. The sources list is set from used_yfinance, which is true when any symbol is live (corr.py:404), so it mislabels mixed provenance.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/corr.py:404 and the sources assignment in execute
findings.evidence: market_coverage row for BTCUSDT: source ccxt_failover, status live; response sources ['yfinance'].
findings.proposed_fix: Build sources from the actual per-symbol sources.

findings.title: Seed contract differs from handler; min_overlap and insufficient-overlap rejection not implemented
findings.detail: corr_seed.py declares universe, method, return_type, window 90d, min_overlap 30, as_of and provider chain binance first; the handler reads symbols, return_method, frequency, missing_data_policy and days, with yfinance/ccxt/coingecko as the chain. min_overlap is never read and thin pairs are not rejected (semantic test corr_insufficient_overlap_rejected_with_warning, corr_seed.py:255, not satisfied).
findings.evidence: grep of corr.py for min_overlap, window, as_of, universe returns no reads.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the declared inputs, enforce min_overlap per pair (null cell plus warning), and align the seed with the handler provider chain.

findings.title: Missing volatility shown as 0.0 in rows
findings.detail: rows.annualized_vol is float(vol.get(symbol) or 0.0), so an undefined volatility becomes zero rather than null.
findings.evidence: Code read.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit null when the volatility is undefined.

findings.title: Ref-mode banner describes a live fetch that never happened
findings.detail: The synthetic banner says the symbols could not be fetched live and were substituted, but in Ref mode no live fetch is attempted.
findings.evidence: Code read; Ref mode sets live false and skips _live_price_series (corr.py:131-137).
findings.proposed_fix: Use wording that matches the mode, for example 'Reference series used (Ref mode)'.

b2.reference_method: Country macro workbook (Bloomberg COUN style): each metric shows its latest official print with date, unit and, where relevant, y/y transform; reference values must be dated and must not sit beside live values as if current.
b2.live_call: POST {country:US,live:true,timeout:8} (pane params): HTTP 200, 0.95 s, sources [btmm,fred,country_reference_profile], 10 rows, pill live+ref. POST {country:JP,live:true}: HTTP 200, generic fallback warning, Inflation 3.0, Unemployment 6.0, Real GDP growth 1.5, top-level source_mode live_macro. TURGDPRQDSMEI fredgraph returns HTTP 404. Check failed for the reference profile and the TR GDP path.

findings.title: TR Real GDP is a constant synthetic series reported as FRED data
findings.detail: TURGDPRQDSMEI does not exist on FRED (404), so ECST falls back to its synthetic baseline, which returns the constant 1.0 for every month. COUN then adds 'fred' to live_sources whenever any indicator row exists, sets source_mode live_macro, and the warnings list stays empty. The Real GDP card shows 1.0 index as a live value.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/coun.py:66-70 (live_sources adds fred unconditionally when indicator_rows exist), :92 (source_mode live_macro), :46-52 (TR map to TURGDPRQDSMEI); ecst.py:346-349 (constant 1.0 branch)
findings.evidence: coun_tr.json: sources ['btmm','fred','country_reference_profile'], warnings [], row {metric:'Real GDP', value:1.0, unit:'index', as_of:'2026-06-01', source_mode:'macro_series_baseline'}; cards include Real GDP 1.0. ecst_tr.json: 115 rows all 1.0, warnings include 'keyless FRED CSV unavailable for TURGDPRQDSMEI'. curl fredgraph TURGDPRQDSMEI: HTTP 404.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive live_sources from each row's real source_mode, drop baseline rows (or mark them unavailable), and replace the TR series id with one that exists on FRED or a verified keyless source.
findings.keyless_source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE (keyless CSV, verified; the TR GDP replacement still needs a verified id)

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: COUN country=TR live_macro=true returns sources ['btmm','fred','country_reference_profile'], warnings [], top-level source_mode live_macro. The Real GDP row is value 1.0 unit index as_of 2026-06-01 with row source_mode macro_series_baseline, and the cards array includes {label:'Real GDP', value:1.0}. coun.py:69-70 adds 'fred' whenever indicator_rows exist, regardless of the ECST source. External check: fredgraph TURGDPRQDSMEI returns HTTP 404. ECST for TURGDPRQDSMEI returns 115 rows all 1.0 with warning "keyless FRED CSV unavailable", which COUN drops (r.warnings is never read). Constant placeholder shown as a live card value is a P0.

findings.title: JP (uncurated country) shows placeholder macro values next to a live rate
findings.detail: Any country outside US/EU/GB/TR gets generic numbers (inflation 3.0%, unemployment 6.0%, GDP growth 1.5%, currency '-') tagged country_reference_profile. The response top-level source_mode is still live_macro with a live BIS policy rate, and the pane shows live+ref. The seed lists JP, CN, BR and IN as valid options, so API and seed consumers reach this path; the COUN pane itself only offers US/EU/GB/TR, and it does not render the response warnings.
findings.evidence: coun_jp.json: warnings ["country 'JP' has no curated profile; using generic reference fallback"], rows Inflation 3.0 %, Unemployment 6.0 %, Real GDP growth 1.5 % (source_mode country_reference_profile), Policy rate 1.25 (BIS); sources ['btmm','country_reference_profile'].
findings.proposed_fix: Return no reference rows for uncurated countries (only the live BTMM/FRED rows with their dates), set source_mode to reference or unavailable accordingly, and show warnings in the pane.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: COUN country=JP returns generic placeholder rows (Inflation 3.0, Unemployment 6.0, Real GDP growth 1.5, reference profile) next to a BIS policy rate 1.25 as_of 2026-11-03, with the top-level source_mode live_macro. The claim is real but overstated. The response does carry a warning ("country 'JP' has no curated profile; using generic reference fallback"), and every placeholder row is labelled country_reference_profile. The COUN pane (COUN.tsx options) offers only US/EU/GB/TR, so the placeholder path is reachable only through the API or seed (coun_seed.py:57 lists JP/CN/BR/IN). The pane also does not render response warnings (no 'warnings' reference in COUN.tsx), which makes this a silent-fallback issue, so P2.

findings.title: Undated reference values contradict live FRED on the same page; inflation shown as an index level
findings.detail: The US Inflation row (3.1% y/y) and Unemployment (3.9%) come from hard-coded, undated reference values. The live FRED rows on the same page disagree: CPIAUCSL implies 3.72% y/y, and UNRATE is 4.1% for 2026-10. The live CPI row is labelled 'Inflation proxy / CPI' with a raw index level (336.298) as its value, so the metric named Inflation shows an index, not a rate. Users see two inflation and two unemployment numbers with no date on the reference ones.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/coun.py:109-118 (hard-coded profiles incl. US inflation 0.031, unemployment 0.039), :254 (CPIAUCSL labelled 'Inflation proxy / CPI', unit index); COUN.tsx:92 (live:true params)
findings.evidence: coun_1.json rows: Inflation 3.1 % y/y (country_reference_profile) and Inflation proxy / CPI 336.298 index as_of 2026-09-01 (fred); Unemployment 3.9 % (reference) and Unemployment rate 4.1 % as_of 2026-10-01 (fred). fred CPIAUCSL: 2026-09-01 336.298, 2025-09-01 324.245, y/y 3.72%.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute y/y inflation from CPI (and label CPI as a level), drop the duplicate reference rows for metrics that have a live series, and date every reference value with its source and vintage.
findings.keyless_source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=CPIAUCSL (keyless CSV, verified)

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced on COUN US live. Rows show Inflation 3.1 % y/y and Unemployment 3.9 % with no as_of (country_reference_profile), hard-coded at coun.py:111 (US inflation 0.031, unemployment 0.039). The live rows on the same page are Inflation proxy / CPI 336.298 index as_of 2026-09-01 and Unemployment rate 4.1 as_of 2026-10-01. External check: FRED CPIAUCSL 2026-09-01 = 336.298 and 2025-09-01 = 324.245, so y/y = 3.72%, not 3.1%. FRED UNRATE 2026-10-01 = 4.1. The contradiction and undated reference values are real. The index label is not a mislabel as claimed, since the metric is named 'Inflation proxy / CPI' with unit index, so the 'metric named Inflation shows an index' part is overstated. This is a stale/undated reference issue, P2.

findings.title: Stale FRED observations are presented as live
findings.detail: EU unemployment comes from LRHUTTTTEZQ156S, whose last observation is 2022-10-01 (6.67%). GB consumer prices (GBRCPIALLMINMEI) stop at 2025-03-01. Both are labelled source fred and the pane shows live+ref, because isLive only checks whether a row is not a reference mode. There is no staleness test for indicator rows.
findings.evidence: coun_eu.json: Unemployment rate 6.666667 % as_of 2022-10-01 source fred; coun_gb.json: Consumer prices 136.1 index as_of 2025-03-01 source fred. fredgraph LRHUTTTTEZQ156S last 2022-10-01; GBRCPIALLMINMEI last 2025-03-01.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a per-row staleness flag (for example older than 2 periods) and make the live pill depend on freshness, not only on the source label.

findings.title: GDP level labelled with unit index
findings.detail: GDPC1 is billions of chained 2017 USD (the ECST catalog says so), but COUN relabels it as 'index', so the card reads Real GDP 24611.077 index.
findings.evidence: coun_1.json row Real GDP 24611.077 index as_of 2026-07-01; ecst.py _SERIES_CATALOG GDPC1 unit 'billions chained USD'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the catalog unit for GDPC1 or show a y/y growth transform.

findings.title: metrics and provider_mode inputs are not read
findings.detail: The seed exposes a metrics multiselect (subset of sections to render) and provider_mode, but the handler never reads either. Selecting metrics has no effect.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/coun.py (no read of params['metrics'] or params['provider_mode']); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/coun_seed.py inputs metrics and provider_mode
findings.evidence: Source inspection; the sidecar output for any metrics value is identical to the default.
findings.proposed_fix: Filter rows by the metrics list and honour or remove provider_mode.

findings.title: Seed default live=True differs from handler default
findings.detail: The handler defaults live to False, which returns only the reference profile. The seed defaults live to True, and the sidecar injects True when the key is omitted, so the two disagree about what a bare call returns.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/coun.py:21 (live = _truthy(...) defaults False); coun_seed.py defaults live True
findings.evidence: POST {country:US} with no live returned the live rows (fred and btmm) in coun_nolive.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the handler default with the seed.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg/EIA/FRED benchmark series for the selected commodity, with a published forecast (EIA STEO or World Bank outlook) and its vintage. The handler's documented method is a clamped log-linear trend over the trailing window of the actual series.

PNGASEUUSDM 1Y -> status ok, label European natural gas USD/MMBtu, latest_actual 2.998 (cpf_eugas.json). PCOPPUSDM 1Y -> label Copper USD/lb, latest_actual 6.218 (cpf_cu.json). findings.title: European gas series served with Henry Hub futures prices
findings.detail: PNGASEUUSDM (European natural gas, USD/MMBtu) is mapped to the NG=F Henry Hub futures. The output is labelled European natural gas but carries Henry Hub prices, about 3 USD/MMBtu against FRED's 25.49. The manifest exposes this series in its options. The pane does not offer it, so the defect is reached through the API and manifest.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:792 (PNGASEUUSDM mapped to NG=F); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/cpf_seed.py (series options include PNGASEUUSDM)
findings.evidence: cpf_eugas.json: commodity European natural gas, unit USD/MMBtu, latest_actual 2.997999906539917, actual 2026-11-06 2.998 (the NG=F value). FRED PNGASEUUSDM CSV fetched: 2026-09-01 25.494.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the mapping, or source a real TTF series (the FRED CSV is keyless) and label it as a proxy when it is one.
findings.keyless_source: FRED PNGASEUUSDM monthly CSV (keyless, verified fetch).

The labelled instrument shows Henry Hub prices as if they were European gas, so P0 holds. Medium confidence only because my FRED fetch for PNGASEUUSDM timed out twice, so the reviewer's ~25.49 comparison is unverified; the mismatch itself does not depend on it.

findings.title: Futures proxy reported as live_official
findings.detail: data_mode is live_official whenever both legs are present. The actual leg is Yahoo front-month futures, and the forecast is a trend extrapolation, so neither is an official series. The pane shows the live actual pill from this value.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:921 and :938 (data_mode); ui/src/functions/CPF.tsx:110 (isLive from live_official) and the live actual pill near :283
findings.evidence: cpf_wti.json: data_mode live_official, sources [yfinance], meta has no official source. cpf_eugas.json and cpf_cu.json show the same label.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a value such as futures_proxy_trend, reserve live_official for official series, and show the proxy in the header.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. cpf_wti and cpf_eugas both return data_mode live_official with sources [yfinance] and no official source. The actual leg is Yahoo front-month futures, and the forecast is a trend extrapolation (CPF.tsx comment and _trend_forecast). _funcs.py:921 sets data_mode to live_official whenever both legs exist. CPF.tsx:110 sets isLive from that value, and :276 shows the 'live actual' pill. False live/official claim, P1.

findings.title: Manifest and help text claim sources the handler never uses
findings.detail: The manifest intent names FRED series with EIA and World Bank forecasts, and the provider chain primary is fred. The handler never calls FRED and never uses a published forecast. The pane notice is honest (trend model), but the manifest and seed help text are not.
findings.evidence: No FRED or EIA forecast fetch in _funcs.py CPFFunction. Forecast leg is _trend_forecast over Yahoo closes.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the intent to describe the trend extrapolation, and set the provider chain to yfinance.

findings.title: Selected FRED series silently replaced by futures levels and units
findings.detail: Each FRED series id is replaced by a futures proxy with its own level and unit, and the response does not say the series differs. WTISPLC is a monthly spot average, but the output is a daily futures print. PCOPPUSDM is USD per metric ton in FRED, but the output unit is USD/lb of HG=F.
findings.evidence: FRED WTISPLC 2026-10-01 102.07 vs served latest_actual 90.83. FRED PCOPPUSDM 2026-09-01 14,473 USD/MT vs served 6.218 USD/lb. cpf_wti.json and cpf_cu.json show the proxy names and units.
findings.proposed_fix: Name the proxy in the series label and unit, or serve the FRED series when it is requested.
findings.keyless_source: FRED WTISPLC, PCOPPUSDM and DHHNGSP CSVs (keyless, verified fetch).

findings.title: show_actual_history=false produces a false outage
findings.detail: When the actual leg is not displayed it is never fetched, but the forecast is built only from actuals. Both legs end up empty, and the handler returns provider_unavailable with a reason claiming the Yahoo feed was unreachable.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:825-827 (actual leg skipped when flag false), :858 (forecast needs actuals), :866-893 (outage return with reason at :882)
findings.evidence: cpf_noactual.json: status provider_unavailable, data_mode no_live_source, reason The live Yahoo futures feed for the actual price leg was unreachable, actual 0, forecast 0. The feed was never requested.
findings.proposed_fix: Fetch the actual leg for the forecast regardless of the display flag, and report the real cause if a fetch fails.

findings.title: cards.forecast_1y is not the 1Y value for other horizons
findings.detail: The card is always the 12th monthly point (index 11, clamped), so with a 6M horizon it returns the 6M endpoint under a 1Y key.
findings.evidence: cpf_wti_6m.json: forecast length 6, cards.forecast_1y 86.460798 = the 2027-05-05 point, horizon 6M.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the card by horizon (forecast_at_horizon) or compute the 1Y value explicitly.

findings.title: provider_mode input is ignored
findings.detail: The manifest exposes provider_mode (LIVE_OFFICIAL and CACHED_SNAPSHOT), but the handler never reads it, so a user cannot choose a cached or official source.
findings.evidence: No provider_mode read in CPFFunction. The pane does not send it.
findings.proposed_fix: Read provider_mode or remove the input from the seed.

findings.title: Forecast dates step 30 days instead of calendar months
findings.detail: Each forecast point adds 30 days, so the 12th point is 360 days out (2027-11-01) rather than 12 calendar months, and the drift accumulates.
findings.evidence: cpf_wti.json: last forecast date 2027-11-01 from vintage 2026-11-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Use calendar month arithmetic (dateutil relativedelta or equivalent).

findings.title: PGOLD FRED CSV did not return data
findings.detail: The FRED fredgraph CSV for PGOLD returned an HTML page rather than CSV data at the time of check, so the manifest's FRED reference for gold is not retrievable. The handler uses GC=F, so the user impact is limited to the label.
findings.evidence: curl https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PGOLD returned HTML (a script-tag page), not observations.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop PGOLD from the FRED-labelled options, or document it as a Yahoo proxy.

Sovereign ratings are agency opinions, not derivable from SEC data.

findings.title: CRPR pane cannot show any equity issuer: symbol routing hits a BOND-only guard
findings.detail: The handler class declares asset_classes=(BOND,), while the manifest seed declares [BOND, EQUITY]. The pane sends only the symbol, so every equity issuer returns unsupported_asset. The SEC corporate path is reached only through an issuer parameter, which the pane never sends. In the UI the corporate feature is effectively dead.
findings.evidence: crpr_aapl.json: status provider_unavailable, metadata.native_asset_classes ['BOND'], requested_asset_class 'EQUITY', reason 'CRPR does not support EQUITY'. crpr_issuer_aapl.json with issuer=AAPL and no symbol returns the SEC-derived AA row.
findings.proposed_fix: Add AssetClass.EQUITY to the handler class (matching the seed), and have the pane or handler map the selected symbol to issuer.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. The handler declares asset_classes=(BOND,) while crpr_seed.py declares [BOND, EQUITY]. Live CRPR symbol=AAPL returns status unsupported_asset, reason 'CRPR does not support EQUITY', native_asset_classes ['BOND']. CRPR.tsx sends only symbol with params {}. The issuer=AAPL path works live (AA row from SEC financials), but the pane never sends issuer, so equity issuers are unreachable from the UI.

findings.title: Sovereign path returns a hard-coded AA+ labelled as model_implied
findings.detail: Any issuer matching the sovereign hint list gets the constant AA+ and implied bucket high_grade, with agency label model_implied and status ok. The code does no modelling and no lookup, so the same rating appears for US10Y and for an Italian label. The pane banner says the rating is model-implied, so this is placeholder data presented as model output.
findings.evidence: crpr_us10y.json and crpr_italy.json both return rows[0] = {agency model_implied, rating AA+, outlook stable}, summary.implied_bucket high_grade, status ok. Both issuers return identical output.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status empty or a labelled not-applicable state for sovereigns, or wire a real sovereign-rating source. Never emit a model_implied agency row without a computation behind it.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed for the code path. For any issuer matching _SOVEREIGN_HINTS (e.g. US10Y, BTP, GILT, BUND), the handler returns a constant AA+ row with agency 'model_implied', implied_bucket high_grade and status ok, with no lookup or model. Live issuer=US10Y returns this constant. Correction to the finding: my live call with issuer='Italy' does not hit the sovereign branch ('ITALY' is not in the hint list); it returns status empty from the SEC ticker lookup. The defect applies to hint-matching labels such as BTP. A constant rating shown under a model_implied label with status ok is placeholder data presented as model output, so P0 is kept, but the Italy evidence should be dropped. The pane's symbol route for these labels is BOND-classed only if the symbol resolves to BOND.

findings.title: Interest coverage divides current EBITDA by a three-year-old interest expense
findings.detail: The interest fact picker takes the latest InterestExpense value regardless of period. For Apple that value is FY2023 (end 2023-09-30, 3.933bn) while EBITDA is FY2026 (171.486bn). The output shows 43.6x as the current coverage, dated 2026-09-26.
findings.evidence: companyfacts CIK0000320193: InterestExpense entries end at 2023-09-30 as the maximum end date; crpr_issuer_aapl.json summary.interest_coverage_x 43.602 and rationale 'as of 2026-09-26'.
findings.proposed_fix: Take interest expense from the same fiscal period as EBITDA, and return null coverage with a warning when the period does not match.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live. Apple companyfacts (fetched by me) has InterestExpense only through FY2023 (last entry end 2023-09-30, 3.933bn), with no later InterestExpense tags. The live issuer=AAPL output reports interest_coverage_x 43.602 = 171.486bn FY2026 EBITDA / FY2023 interest, yet the rationale and as_of are dated 2026-09-26. _first_fact takes the first concept with any data regardless of recency, so stale interest is combined with current EBITDA. Wrong calculation, P1.

findings.title: Fact picker ignores duration and form, so YTD or quarterly flows can become the EBITDA input
findings.detail: _latest_usd_fact selects the maximum end date and, on ties, the first entry encountered, regardless of period length. A flow concept whose newest filing is a 10-Q can therefore resolve to a 9-month YTD value. The simulated 10-Q-only state picks a 272-day operating income figure as the EBITDA numerator.
findings.evidence: sim_latest.py on the Apple companyfacts file, with filings after 2026-07-31 removed: OperatingIncomeLoss = 122.432bn at end 2026-06-27 with start 2025-09-28 (272 days, 9-month YTD), D&A = 9.973bn (also YTD). This is a simulation, not a live call.
findings.proposed_fix: For flow concepts, keep only entries whose duration is about 365 days (fp FY, or a trailing-twelve-month construction), and for balance-sheet concepts keep instant entries only.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live, not only by simulation. For CAT (Dec year-end, fetched by me from companyfacts), the latest OperatingIncomeLoss entries share end 2026-09-30: a 9-month YTD (start 2026-01-01, 11.594bn) and a Q3 quarter (start 2026-07-01, 4.214bn). _latest_usd_fact keeps the first tie, so the YTD value is used. Live issuer=CAT returns ebitda_proxy_usd 13.42bn = 11.594 + 9M D&A 1.826, leverage 2.698x against a point-in-time debt, and implied bucket 'distressed' with rating CCC. Those figures mix 9-month EBITDA into an annual leverage test, so the CCC/distressed result is wrong. The picker ignores period length and form, so P1 stands.

findings.title: Latent double count of the current debt portion in the LongTermDebt fallback
findings.detail: If LongTermDebtNoncurrent is absent, the fallback LongTermDebt is total debt including the current portion, and LongTermDebtCurrent is added on top, double counting the current portion. Not observed for Apple (which reports Noncurrent), so this is code-level only.
findings.evidence: Code path only; the Apple response used LongTermDebtNoncurrent 68.208bn + LongTermDebtCurrent 9.906bn = 78.114bn, which is correct.
findings.proposed_fix: When the fallback concept is LongTermDebt, do not add LongTermDebtCurrent.

findings.title: Coverage uses EBITDA, and missing operating income is silently counted as zero
findings.detail: The label 'interest coverage' is applied to EBITDA / interest, while the conventional ratio is EBIT / interest expense, so the figure is inflated relative to the standard definition. If OperatingIncomeLoss is missing, EBITDA silently becomes D&A alone and leverage is computed on that, with no warning.
findings.evidence: Code logic; no live case required. Apple's response summary shows interest_coverage_x 43.602 computed from ebitda_proxy 171.486bn.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute EBIT / interest expense for coverage, and return null or a warning when operating income is absent.

findings.title: Caller-pinned rating is summarised with a fabricated default bucket
findings.detail: When a rating override is supplied without a bucket parameter, summary.implied_bucket and implied_bucket default to high_grade. A user-pinned rating therefore carries a bucket the caller never gave.
findings.evidence: Code logic. The override branch is reached whenever rating is a non-empty dict; the default is applied literally.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the bucket from the pinned sp rating against the scale, or return null.

findings.title: Seed methodology and semantic tests describe a different CRPR
findings.detail: The seed says the default is a bundled public profile with source_mode manual_or_public_defaults and three agency rows, but the handler now models from SEC data and emits one model_implied row. The seed test crpr_emits_three_agency_rows would fail.
findings.evidence: crpr_aapl-equivalent output (crpr_issuer_aapl.json) has ROWS n=1 with agency model_implied and source_mode model_implied_from_financials.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed methodology and tests to the SEC-derived model and its single row.

findings.title: DARK always reports stale data because the FINRA query returns the oldest 200 rows
findings.detail: The FINRA request has no date range and no sort, only limit 200. FINRA returns rows from the earliest weeks, so the handler sees a latest week of 2025-09-15, trips the 180-day stale guard, and returns provider_unavailable with empty venues for every symbol that has more than 200 ATS rows. The newest data (through 2026-10-12) is never fetched. The pane then shows 'FINRA ATS data unavailable'.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/dark.py:274-287 (payload with limit 200, no date filter or sort), 197-198 (stale guard); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/ui/src/functions/DARK.tsx:237-250
findings.evidence: DARK_d1/d2/d3.json all report latest week 2025-09-15 and empty venues. Direct FINRA: handler-style query returns 200 rows, week range 2021-12-06 to 2025-09-15 (183 weeks); dateRangeFilters 2025-06-01..2026-11-08 returns 72 rows, week range 2025-06-02 to 2026-10-12.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a dateRangeFilters clause on weekStartDate (for example the last 26 weeks) and page with offset until all rows are read, instead of a bare limit 200. (A sortFields attempt returned HTTP 400, so do not rely on sorting.)
findings.keyless_source: FINRA OTC Transparency weeklySummary API (keyless; the date-range query returned HTTP 200 with current rows)

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced directly against the live FINRA weeklySummary endpoint using the handler payload (summaryTypeCode ATS_W_SMBL, issueSymbolIdentifier AAPL, limit 200, no date filter): 200 rows covering only weeks 2021-12-06 to 2025-09-15, returned oldest-first (scratch script: .../scratchpad/b2/work/equity-1/finra_check.py). The same query with dateRangeFilters 2025-06-01..2026-11-08 returns 72 rows through 2026-10-12, so current data exists. Live sidecar DARK for AAPL returns status provider_unavailable, reason 'FINRA latest week 2025-09-15 is stale', venues [] and cards.as_of 2025-09-15. The stale guard at dark.py:197-198 fires on this window, and DARK.tsx:237-250 renders 'FINRA ATS data unavailable'. The payload is the same whether it comes through the wired FINRAAdapter (function_factory.py:44) or the direct path, since both send the same POST. Adapter comment claiming newest week 2026-05-04 is out of date against today's live response. Empty pane while data exists is P0.

findings.title: total_shares_off_exchange sums every returned row, not the requested weeks
findings.detail: total_shares_off_exchange is computed over the whole df (all returned rows) rather than the weeks window. The KPI caption says 8W WINDOW, but the number covers the full 200 rows, which span 183 weeks.
findings.evidence: DARK_d1.json total_shares_off_exchange 4,667,006,047 for weeks=8, identical to weeks=26 and weeks=4 (DARK_d2/d3.json).
findings.proposed_fix: Sum only the weeks included in by_week (the selected window).

findings.title: Manifest documents a modeled fallback that the handler does not run
findings.detail: The seed methodology says that when FINRA is unreachable the chain falls back to a model estimating dark-pool % from yfinance volume buckets. The handler returns provider_unavailable with empty venues instead, so the documented fallback does not exist. The provider chain also lists yfinance as primary while the handler uses FINRA.
findings.evidence: Code read; the handler's own methodology (dark.py:31-40) states no synthetic rows are produced.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the seed methodology and provider chain to match the handler.

findings.title: Silent defaults and caps
findings.detail: dark_pool_pct is capped at 100 with no flag, which can hide a ratio above 100%. The yfinance weekly total is fetched with period 6mo, so older FINRA weeks get no denominator and dark_pool_pct is silently None. With no instrument, the handler silently uses AAPL.
findings.evidence: Code read only.
findings.proposed_fix: Flag capped values, extend the weekly total history to match the requested weeks, and drop the AAPL default in favor of input_required.

b2.reference_method: Two-stage FCFE DCF: PV = sum_t FCFE_0*(1+g_high)^t/(1+r)^t + TV/(1+r)^N, TV = FCFE_N*(1+g_term)/(r-g_term), fair value per share = equity value / shares outstanding. Base cash flow must come from the company's own FCF data, not a placeholder.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/DCF {symbol:AAPL,fcfe:1e10,shares_outstanding:1.5e10,growth_high:0.10,growth_terminal:0.025,wacc:0.08,years:5} HTTP 200 (pane-equivalent); {symbol:AAPL,wacc:0.08,growth_high:0.10,growth_terminal:0.025,years:5} HTTP 200 (provider FCFE); {symbol:AAPL,discount_rate:0.09,growth_rate:0.08,terminal_growth:0.025,projection_years:10} HTTP 200. Saved as DCF_f1.json, DCF_f2.json, DCF_f3.json under C:/Users/KULLAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e0427571f2ca10f3/3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def/scratchpad/b2/work/equity-1/. f1: status ok, fair value 17.14 per share, starting FCFE 10.0B, shares 15.0B. f2: status ok, starting FCFE 105.66B (yfinance freeCashflow), shares 14.53B, fair value 186.94 per share. AAPL spot in the same session was 342.37 (ANR_a1.json).
b2.independent_check: Recomputed the formulas from the returned starting_fcfe, wacc, growth and years: the pane-style run gives PV explicit 52,847,324,560, PV TV 204,270,581,049, fair value 17.1412 per share, matching the handler exactly. The yfinance-base run gives PV explicit 558,376,249,912, PV TV 2,158,289,789,747, fair value 186.9414, also matching. The arithmetic is correct; the problem is the input base (see findings).

findings.title: DCF pane always overrides provider FCFE and shares with placeholder inputs
findings.detail: The pane's persisted defaults are FCFE $10,000M and shares 15,000M. They are always sent, so the handler's yfinance freeCashflow and sharesOutstanding fallbacks never run. The headline fair value shown for AAPL is therefore driven by a $10B placeholder base: $17.14 per share, against $186.94 when the provider base is used. That is about 5% of the 342.37 spot, and the headline is presented as the model's fair value with no placeholder warning.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/ui/src/functions/DCF.tsx:85-86 (defaults 10_000 and 15_000), 101-108 (always sent); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/dcf.py:121-122, 140-149 (provider FCFE used only when fcfe is None)
findings.evidence: DCF_f1.json fair_value_per_share 17.1412 with starting_fcfe 1.0e10 and shares 1.5e10 vs DCF_f2.json fair_value_per_share 186.9414 with starting_fcfe 1.0566e11 and shares 1.4532e10. Both recomputed by hand from the formulas.
findings.proposed_fix: Default fcfe and shares to empty so the handler sources them from the provider; mark any user override as a manual override in the output and header; return needs_input when the provider value is missing rather than substituting a placeholder.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance Ticker.info freeCashflow and sharesOutstanding (already used by the handler; values returned in DCF_f2.json)

verifier.reasoning: Code confirmed: DCF.tsx:85-86 hardcodes fcfe 10_000 and shares 15_000 ($M) and lines 101-108 always send fcfe and shares_outstanding, so the dcf.py yfinance fallbacks (dcf.py:140-149 and 187-197) never run; the pane has no way to request provider FCFE. Sidecar DCF AAPL with the pane's placeholder inputs (fcfe 1e10, shares 1.5e10) returns status ok, fair_value_per_share 17.1412, no warnings. Without those inputs the provider base (starting_fcfe 1.0566e11, shares 1.4532e10) returns 186.9414. I recomputed the placeholder case by hand: explicit PV about 5.28e10 plus PV terminal about 2.04e11 gives equity about 2.571e11, divided by 1.5e10 gives 17.14. The headline 'Fair value / share' card is shown with no placeholder warning, and status stays ok, so a hardcoded placeholder base is presented as the model's fair value. Placeholder shown as real under the rubric is P0.

findings.title: Manifest input names are not read; discount_rate and projection_years are ignored
findings.detail: The manifest declares discount_rate, growth_rate, terminal_growth and projection_years with defaults 0.09/0.08/0.025/10. The handler reads wacc, growth_high, growth_terminal and years. In the f3 run, growth_rate arrived as g_high 0.08 (so that alias works), but discount_rate was ignored (wacc came from the WACC model at 9.94%) and projection_years was ignored (years stayed at 5).
findings.evidence: DCF_f3.json: wacc 0.09940737 (requested 0.09), years 5 (requested 10), g_high 0.08.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the manifest names in the handler (discount_rate, projection_years) or rename the manifest inputs to the handler names, and check that every declared input is consumed.

findings.title: Declared output contract and methodology do not match the payload
findings.detail: must_have includes intrinsic_value_per_share, enterprise_value, projection and assumptions. The handler returns fair_value_per_share, equity_value, rows and no assumptions object. The methodology says FCF = CFO - |Capex| from the FA service and intrinsic value = (EV - net debt)/shares. The handler uses yfinance freeCashflow and an FCFE equity value with no net-debt bridge.
findings.evidence: DCF_f2.json keys: bridge, equity_value, fair_value_per_share, g_high, g_terminal, pv_explicit, pv_terminal, rows, shares_outstanding, starting_fcfe, status, terminal_value, wacc, years. No enterprise_value, intrinsic_value_per_share or assumptions keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the manifest with the FCFE model (equity value, no net-debt step) or add the EV bridge and the missing keys.

findings.evidence: Code read only.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one set of defaults, sourced from the manifest.

findings.title: Returns 2023 FINRA weeks as current because the limit cuts the oldest rows
findings.detail: The endpoint returns rows oldest-first. Requesting weeks*4 rows gets the oldest 48, so for 12 weeks the handler shows 2022-2023 data and reports provider_unavailable, although current FINRA weeks exist. The adapter comment claiming newest-first results is stale.
findings.evidence: AAPL weeks 12: latest week 2023-12-11, status provider_unavailable. Direct probe: limit 48 max 2023-12-11, limit 1500 max 2026-10-12. A sortFields:-weekStartDate body returned HTTP 400.
findings.proposed_fix: Request a limit large enough to cover the history (or paginate), sort by weekStartDate, then take the newest 'weeks' rows.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced. DPF AAPL weeks=12 returned status provider_unavailable with reason 'FINRA latest week 2023-12-11 is stale', and the rows run from 2023-12-11 back to 2023-10. findings.detail: The pane (and seed) offer EUR, which the handler passes through unchanged. The IMF DataMapper has no EUR key; the euro area is EURO. Every indicator therefore fails and the pane shows an empty provider-unavailable state, although the data exists under EURO.

Raw IMF .../NGDP_RPCH/EURO returns 200 with a EURO series.

findings.detail: The seed says ECFC queries FRED release_dates, fills missing cells with a modeled fallback tagged source_mode modeled, and pins the vintage from FRED. The handler calls the IMF DataMapper directly, has no modeled fallback, and never reads vintage or provider_mode. The vintage label is the constant 'imf_weo' with no WEO edition or release date, and as_of is the fetch time, so the forecast batch cannot be identified.

b2.reference_method: FRED series explorer: observation dates and units as published, native frequency, optional y/y or % change transforms, and ALFRED vintages; a series that does not exist must return an explicit error, never fabricated observations.
b2.live_call: POST {series_id:CPIAUCSL} (pane default): HTTP 200, sources [fred], 117 monthly rows 2016-12-01 to 2026-09-01, latest 336.298. POST {series_id:UNRATE,compare_with:DGS10}: HTTP 200, 1500 rows, compare overlay present. findings.detail: Any series id that FRED does not return falls through to _baseline_rows_for_series. Its final else-branch emits 1.0 for every month to 2026-06-01 with unit 'value'. The pane shows only a muted source label and a reference pill, with no banner, and draws the flat line as a chart. The four named series (CPIAUCSL, GDPC1, UNRATE, DGS10) get hand-built synthetic curves through the same path whenever FRED and World Bank both fail.

findings.title: Compare overlay forward-fills a monthly series onto daily dates
findings.detail: The merge is an outer join followed by ffill().bfill(). The monthly UNRATE value is copied onto each later daily date from DGS10, so the Latest card shows UNRATE 4.1 as of 2026-11-05, while the FRED observation is dated 2026-10-01. bfill also fills leading gaps with values that do not exist for that date.
findings.evidence: ecst_cmp.json rows 2026-11-03/04/05 value 4.1 for UNRATE; cards Latest 4.1 As of 2026-11-05. fredgraph UNRATE 2026-10-01 = 4.1.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep each series on its own observation dates (no cross-filling). Date the Latest card with the series' own last observation.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: ECST series_id=UNRATE compare_with=DGS10. The merged rows carry UNRATE value 4.1 on every daily date from 2026-10-02 through 2026-11-05 (forward-filled from the 2026-10-01 observation), and the Latest card reads 4.1 As of 2026-11-05. External check: FRED UNRATE last observation is 2026-10-01 = 4.1. The outer merge with ffill().bfill() is at ecst.py:198-199, so the monthly main series is carried onto daily dates. The bfill leading-gap effect is confirmed in code but I did not isolate a case for it. The wrong as-of date on the headline card is a P1 methodology error.

findings.title: frequency and vintage are silently ignored on the keyless path
findings.detail: The keyless FRED CSV shim logs a server-side warning but the response does not say frequency or vintage was dropped. frequency=monthly on a daily series returns 1500 daily rows labelled daily, with no warning.
findings.evidence: ecst_freq.json: DGS10 frequency monthly -> 1500 rows dated 2020-11-05 onward (daily), data.frequency 'daily', warnings [].
findings.proposed_fix: Return a warning when the requested frequency or vintage cannot be honoured, or implement resampling locally.

findings.title: date_range parser treats any suffix as years
findings.detail: date_range[:-1] is parsed as an integer number of years whatever the unit letter, so '6M' gives 6 years. The pane does not send date_range and the seed offers only 1Y/3Y/5Y/10Y/20Y/MAX, so this is latent, but the API accepts it.
findings.evidence: ecst_6m.json: DGS10 date_range 6M -> 1498 rows 2020-11-09 to 2026-11-05.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse the unit (D/M/Y) and reject unknown units.

findings.title: Pane exposes only series id and compare; no range, frequency or transform controls
findings.detail: The seed promises date range, frequency and vintage controls, and a professional series explorer normally offers y/y or % change transforms. The pane sends only series_id and compare_with, and the chart shows raw index levels (e.g. CPI 336.298 with no y/y), which is a missing feature against the professional equivalent.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/ECST.tsx:103-109 (params: series_id, compare_with only); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/ecst_seed.py date_range/frequency/vintage inputs
findings.evidence: ecst_cpi.json returns levels only; no transform field in the response.
findings.proposed_fix: Add date-range and y/y transform controls to the pane and implement them in the handler.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg-style SEC full-text search: query as typed, optional ticker scope only when selected, form-type and date-range filters, and each hit showing company, form, filing date, a real matched excerpt, and a link to the filing.

(3) POST FTS {query:risk factors, forms:'10-K, 8-K', live:false, limit:3}: still live (metadata live true), query 'AAPL risk factors'.

Snippet check: EFTS _source for these hits carries inc_states (state of incorporation), not matched text; the adapter maps that field to snippet (sec_efts_adapter.py:77). Company names in the rows match the EFTS display names, so the company column is correct while symbol and snippet are not. check_passed false.

findings.title: Snippet evidence is the state of incorporation, not matched filing text
findings.detail: The adapter maps EFTS inc_states (e.g. CA, DE, WY) to snippet, and the handler passes it through as an excerpt. The pane renders these under Snippet evidence, so users read a state code as proof of matched filing text.
findings.evidence: fts_climate.json: 10-K hits for climate change show snippet 'CA' for Apple Inc. fts_8k.json: 8-K hits show 'WY' and 'DE'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use EFTS highlight text for the excerpt, or drop the snippet column. Never map inc_states to an excerpt.

verifier.reasoning: Sidecar fts_8k.json rows show snippet 'WY' (US Energy Corp) and 'DE' (Sanchez Energy). sec_efts_adapter.py:77 sets snippet from inc_states, fts.py:99-101 passes it through, and FTS.tsx:206-216 renders it under 'Snippet evidence' as 'Company: snippet'. findings.title: Other issuers' filings labelled as AAPL
findings.detail: The handler prepends the instrument symbol to the query and then stamps every row with that symbol. When no symbol is sent the sidecar resolves AAPL, so the search is scoped to AAPL text and the results are other companies, each row tagged AAPL. symbol_match is set only in the row data and the pane does not show it.

findings.proposed_fix: Take the symbol from each hit (ticker or CIK) rather than the instrument, and do not prepend a symbol to the query unless the user scoped it.

verifier.reasoning: Sidecar fts_8k.json, query 'AAPL supply chain disruption' with forms 8-K: rows are US Energy Corp (USEG) and Sanchez Energy Corp, each with symbol 'AAPL'. fts.py:94 and 111 stamp symbol = instrument.symbol on every row. symbol_match is set only in the row data (fts.py:113-114); the FTS.tsx type declares it but the render does not use it. Other issuers appear labelled as AAPL.

findings.detail: The manifest declares date_from and date_to inputs and a total_hits must-have field. b2.reference_method: Spot FX board: mid from a reference quote, bid/ask from the quoted dealing spread, change measured against the prior daily close (one session back), pip = 0.0001 (0.01 for JPY pairs), with the quote time shown as as_of.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FXGO {} -> HTTP 200, status ok, broker indicative, data_mode delayed_reference, 1 row (EURUSD bid 1.11425 ask 1.11435 mid 1.1143 change -0.0014 change_pct -0.1255 previous_close 1.1157), cards.status 'live'; provider errors for GBPUSD=X and USDJPY=X (404). POST {pairs:'EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDJPY,EURGBP'} -> status ok, data_mode live_exchange, 4 rows (EURUSD 1.1143/1.1157, GBPUSD 1.3356/1.3386, USDJPY 158.425/157.677, EURGBP 0.8347/0.8335). POST {pairs:'GBPUSD=X'} -> provider_unavailable, 404 on GBPUSDX=X.
b2.independent_check: Raw Yahoo chart meta for EURUSD=X: regularMarketPrice 1.1143 (regularMarketTime 2026-11-06T22:29:32Z), chartPreviousClose 1.1157 -> sidecar mid and previous_close match the raw endpoint exactly. Recomputed change: (1.1143-1.1157)/1.1157 x 100 = -0.1255%, arithmetic matches. But Yahoo's daily series is 11-02 1.11569, 11-03 1.11921, 11-04 1.12072, 11-05 1.12349, 11-06 1.12283, so 1.1157 is the 11-02 close (five sessions back), not the prior session close. Result: check fails (stale quote and wrong previous close).

findings.title: Stale Yahoo quote labelled live and stamped with fetch time
findings.detail: The mid is Yahoo meta.regularMarketPrice whose regularMarketTime is 2026-11-06 22:29 UTC, about 26 hours before the as_of stamp (2026-11-08 00:17 UTC, set at fetch time). The response still says data_mode 'live_exchange' for the four-pair board (_funcs.py:651) and cards.status 'live' (_funcs.py:657). as_of should be the quote time.
findings.evidence: Live FXGO 4-pair call: data_mode live_exchange, as_of 2026-11-08T00:17:21Z; raw Yahoo EURUSD=X regularMarketTime 2026-11-06T22:29:32Z.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the quote's regularMarketTime for as_of, set data_mode delayed_reference (never live_exchange) for Yahoo spot, and mark quotes older than a threshold as stale.
findings.keyless_source: FRED DEXUSEU daily CSV, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DEXUSEU (fetched; last rows 2026-10-27 1.1144 to 2026-10-30 1.1163) gives a keyless daily reference series; ECB eurofxref-daily.xml also returned HTTP 200.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced with pairs=EURUSD,GBPUSD: data_mode 'live_exchange', cards.status 'live', as_of 2026-11-08T00:26:51Z (fetch time, set via _utc_now_iso). Raw Yahoo meta for EURUSD=X and GBPUSD=X shows regularMarketTime 2026-11-06T22:29:32Z, about 26 hours earlier. as_of should be the quote time and the live label is not honest for a Friday-close quote, so the defect stands.

findings.title: previous_close is the close five sessions back, not the prior session
findings.detail: prev comes from meta.chartPreviousClose (_funcs.py:518-520), which for range=5d is the close before the first bar in the window. The field dictionary calls it 'Prior session close' and change 'vs previous close', so the 5-session move is presented as a one-day move.
findings.evidence: chartPreviousClose 1.1157 equals the 2026-11-02 daily close 1.11569; the 11-05 close 1.12349 and 11-06 close 1.12283 are the prior sessions. FXGO change -0.0014 (-0.1255%) is therefore a 5-day change.
findings.proposed_fix: Take the previous daily bar close from the series (or request range 1d with two bars) and label the change window explicitly.

verifier.reasoning: Raw Yahoo range=5d meta has previousClose None and chartPreviousClose 1.1157 for EURUSD=X, which equals the 2026-11-02 daily close (1.11569). The sidecar's previous_close 1.1157 and change_pct -0.1255 therefore represent a 5-session move, while the field dictionary says 'Prior session close' and 'vs previous close'. Mislabelled one-day change is a P1 calculation/labelling defect.

findings.title: yfinance-style pair tickers (GBPUSD=X) are corrupted and 404
findings.detail: _to_yf_fx removes every non-letter first (re.sub strips '='), then calls replace('=X',''), which no longer matches. 'GBPUSD=X' becomes 'GBPUSDX' and the Yahoo URL becomes GBPUSDX=X, a 404. The methodology tells users the EURUSD=X style is expected, so valid input fails and the data exists.
findings.evidence: Live FXGO {pairs:'GBPUSD=X'} -> data_mode provider_unavailable, warnings containing '404 Client Error ... GBPUSDX=X'. Raw Yahoo GBPUSD=X resolves (regularMarketPrice 1.3356).
findings.proposed_fix: Strip a trailing '=X' before removing non-letters (base = pair.upper().removesuffix('=X'); base = re.sub(...)).

verifier.reasoning: _to_yf_fx (_funcs.py ~479) strips non-letters first, which removes '=', so 'GBPUSD=X' becomes 'GBPUSDX' and the trailing replace('=X') no longer matches, giving GBPUSDX=X. Sidecar reproduces 404 for GBPUSDX=X. The defect is wider than the finding states: EURUSD=X also 404s (EURUSDX=X) and the default board's only surviving pair is the plain-letter input. Valid input with data available returns provider_unavailable or degraded output, which fits the P0 'empty when data exists' category.

findings.title: Dealing spread is a fixed 1 pip, not scaled to liquidity as the methodology states
findings.detail: spread = pip * 1.0 (_funcs.py:534) for every pair, so all rows show spread_pips 1.0 regardless of liquidity, although the methodology says the spread is 'scaled to liquidity'.
findings.evidence: Live EURUSD row spread 0.0001, spread_pips 1.0; 4-pair call all rows 1.0 pip (JPY row 0.01 pip size).
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove 'scaled to liquidity' from the text or add a per-pair spread table.

findings.title: Bare board call did not return the default 10-pair grid
findings.detail: With no params the board returned requested_count 3 (EURUSD plus GBPUSD=X and USDJPY=X), not the _BOARD_PAIRS default of ten (_funcs.py:446). The source of the injected pairs was not traced in the sidecar, so the default board shown to users cannot be confirmed as complete.
findings.evidence: Live FXGO {} -> metadata.requested_count 3, provider_errors for GBPUSDX=X and USDJPY=X.
findings.proposed_fix: Trace the default-pairs injection and make the board default explicit in the response (requested list echoed).

b2.reference_method: ISO 6166 check digit for ISIN; OpenFIGI /v3/mapping for identifier cross-reference, with the anonymous rate limit honoured and partial results returned.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/ISIN: (1) ids US0378331005 -> ok, 6 flat rows, match_groups 303; (2) ids AAPL -> ok, 6 flat rows; (3) ids US0378331006 (bad check digit) -> empty, id_type TICKER; (4) 30 tickers -> provider_unavailable, 'function timed out after 14s'; (5) 12 tickers -> provider_unavailable, same timeout, 14.1 s; (6) ids MSFT -> ok, 6 flat rows. Direct OpenFIGI calls: US0378331005 -> 303 rows; 27 sequential AAPL requests -> 5 x HTTP 429 then 200. Scratch files isin_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Luhn-style ISO 6166 check: US0378331005 valid, US0378331006 invalid, matching the sidecar's ID_ISIN detection and TICKER fallback. Direct OpenFIGI query for US0378331005 returns 303 rows, equal to the sidecar's match_groups length, and the top row is APPLE INC / BBG000B9XRY4. check_passed true for the identifier logic and match content; the timeout and rate-limit failures are reported below.

findings.title: Multi-identifier lookups time out and return nothing
findings.detail: Batches of 12 or 30 tickers hit the 14 s function timeout, and the whole response becomes provider_unavailable with no rows. The adapter throttles at a fixed 4 requests per second. OpenFIGI anonymous access allows 25 per minute, so most requests get 429. The adapter sleeps 1 s on each 429 and returns an empty list, which lengthens the call until it times out. Single lookups succeed once the window resets, so the data exists upstream.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/data_sources/reference/openfigi_adapter.py:48 (throttle rps 4.0 on lookup_by), 62-66 (429 sleep and return []), 73 (throttle on lookup); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/api/isin.py:119-128 (per-id sequential calls)
findings.evidence: isin_12_batch.json: status provider_unavailable, reason 'function timed out after 14s', elapsed 14.1 s, rows []. isin_30_batch.json: same. Direct OpenFIGI: 5 x 429 then 200 across 27 sequential requests.
findings.proposed_fix: Batch identifiers into one /mapping request where the API allows it, honour the anonymous budget (about 0.41 requests per second, not 4), and return partial matches with per-id warnings instead of failing the whole call.

verifier.reasoning: Only partly reproduced. A 30-ticker batch timed out at 14.1 s with status provider_unavailable, reason 'function timed out after 14s', and rows []. A 12-ticker batch did NOT reproduce: it returned status ok with 60 rows in 4.7 s and no warnings, on a fresh OpenFIGI window. The mechanism holds: an anonymous budget of 25/min is below 30 ids, and openfigi_adapter.py returns [] on 429 after a 1 s sleep while isin.py makes sequential per-id calls. A direct burst after my calls got 429 on 6 of 6 requests with Retry-After 17-20 s. So the 30-ticker case is a real empty-on-timeout P0, but the claimed 12-ticker trigger is not confirmed. Evidence: .../scratchpad/b2/work/api/isin_30.txt, isin_12.txt

findings.title: Throttle ignores the anonymous rate budget that the adapter itself declares
findings.detail: The class sets rate_limit_rps 0.41 for anonymous use and documents 25 requests per minute, but lookup_by and lookup use a hardcoded @throttle(rps=4.0). The declared budget is never applied on this path.
findings.evidence: Direct OpenFIGI burst: 5 of the first 5 requests returned 429 once the quota was used.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass self.rate_limit_rps to the throttle, or gate on it as BaseDataSource does.

verifier.reasoning: The code fact holds. openfigi_adapter.py:48 and 73 hardcode @throttle(rps=4.0) on lookup_by and lookup. The class declares rate_limit_rps 0.41 (line 22) and documents 25 req/min (line 4), and nothing on the lookup path reads that attribute. 4 rps is 240/min, about 10x the stated budget. The real harm is that 429 is turned into [] (lines 62-66, 85-88) and isin.py (lines 122-128) has no exception path, so rate-limited identifiers appear as zero matches with no warning. That is a silent fallback, so P2 rather than P1. My burst shows the quota exhaustion but does not isolate the throttle as the sole cause. Evidence: .../scratchpad/b2/work/api/ (OpenFIGI burst output recorded in the isin_30 run)

findings.title: HTTP 429 is turned into an empty result with no warning
findings.detail: On a 429 the adapter returns an empty list instead of raising, so the handler sees no exception and records the identifier as an ordinary no-match. The rate-limit condition never reaches the user.
findings.evidence: Code read; a 429 yields rows [] and no error, so the ISIN response shows status empty for that id with no warning. Not reproduced live at the ISIN level because the batch timed out first.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise or return a rate_limited status for the id, add a warning, and let the handler report it separately from no-match.

findings.title: limit_per_input is applied only to the flat rows, not to match_groups
findings.detail: The flat rows are sliced to limit, but match_groups carries every OpenFIGI match. The seed promises up to limit matches per input, and the pane counts and exports match_groups, so the user sees all 303 matches while summary says 6. The pane has a comment noting this discrepancy.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/api/isin.py:144 (slice on flat rows), 147-162 (match_groups unsliced); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/ui/src/functions/ISIN.tsx:204 (comment), 206-209 (matchCount sums groups); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/manifest/seeds/isin_seed.py:140-146
findings.evidence: isin_apple_isin.json: summary.matches 6, limit_per_input 6, match_groups[0].matches length 303. Direct OpenFIGI returns 303.
findings.proposed_fix: Slice match_groups[].matches to limit as well, or change the summary and seed to say that limit applies only to flat rows.

findings.title: ID type and data-mode inputs are not wired to the handler or the pane
findings.detail: The seed defines id_type and provider_mode, and the methodology says id_type forces a flavour. The handler never reads provider_mode. The pane sends only {ids} and has no ID type selector, so auto-detection is the only route in the UI.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/api/isin.py:111 (id_type read, provider_mode never read); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/manifest/seeds/isin_seed.py:60-67, 78-92; C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/ui/src/functions/ISIN.tsx:169 (params: ids only)
findings.evidence: Pane request body contains only ids. No select or option control in ISIN.tsx.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an ID type selector to the pane and remove or implement provider_mode.

findings.title: Invalid ISIN check digits are reclassified as TICKER without a warning
findings.detail: US0378331006 fails the ISO 6166 check digit, so detection falls back to TICKER. The user gets status empty and no hint that the identifier is malformed.
findings.evidence: isin_bad_check.json: match_groups [{input US0378331006, id_type TICKER, matches []}], status empty, warnings [].

findings.title: LITM reports no events for AAPL/TSLA although matching 8-K items exist
findings.detail: The 8-K event rows built by CACT carry only category '8-k', form, dates, accession and document. No item code is passed through, so LITM's filter e.get('code') in keep never matches. LITM also passes max_documents default 1, so only one 8-K is ever examined. The result is a false 'no litigation event' state for every ticker, including AAPL, which has five 8-K filings with item 5.02 in the SEC submissions feed. The sec_edgar EVENTS frame does carry an 'items' column (visible in splc_aapl.json filings rows), so the fix is available without fetching documents.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/_bonus.py:55 (max_documents default 1), :58-59 (keep filter on e.get('code')); backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/cact.py:43-50 (events_8k dict has no code/items)
findings.evidence: litm_aapl_live.json: all_8k_events 1, rows [no_litigation_event_found]. SEC submissions AAPL 8-K 2026-04-20 items '5.02' (ef20071035_8k.htm) not reported. TSLA 8-K 2025-11-07 items '5.02,5.07,9.01' not reported.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate the 'items' field from the sec_edgar EVENTS frame into events_8k as 'item_codes' (split on comma), filter on it, scan all 8-K rows in the months window (not one), and set status 'empty' only after a full scan with the scan count shown.
findings.keyless_source: SEC EDGAR submissions JSON

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed as broken. In default (live) mode LITM calls CACT with max_documents defaulting to 1 (_bonus.py:55). CACT's default events_8k dict (cact.py:43-50) has no 'code' or 'items' key, and the deep-mode categorizer that would add codes only runs with fetch_documents/deep, which LITM never passes. So _bonus.py:59 e.get('code') in keep can never match in the default path. Live LITM AAPL and TSLA both return status 'empty', rows [no_litigation_event_found], all_8k_events 1. The SEC submissions feed I fetched for AAPL has 8-K/A 2026-09-01 items '5.02' and 8-K 2026-04-20 items '5.02', which are in the keep set and not reported. Only the single newest 8-K (2026-11-02, items 2.02,9.01) is examined, so the 5.02 filings are missed. The TSLA example in the finding (2025-11-07) is not in the current feed's 8 most recent 8-Ks, so I could not confirm that specific instance. The claim that the EVENTS frame carries an 'items' column was not verified; the defect does not depend on it. Empty output when matching data exists is P0 under the rubric.

findings.title: LOTS open and sell fail through /api/fn because the route strips the symbol they read
findings.detail: The generic route pops 'symbol' out of params and turns it into an instrument. LOTS open and sell read params['symbol'], which is now missing, so they raise KeyError. The routed layer then returns a generic provider_unavailable envelope with a news query, which is misleading. As a result no tax lot can be opened or sold through the API, and the documented open/sell actions are broken.
findings.evidence: l2_open_old and l5_sell_lot_ids both returned status provider_unavailable, reason "'symbol'", metadata exception_type_original KeyError, requested.query 'AUDTEST stock'. Ledger unchanged (l4 list empty afterwards).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the symbol from instrument.symbol when params has no symbol, or have the route keep symbol in params for LOTS. Return input_error instead of the generic news envelope.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced without mutating the ledger: LOTS action=open with quantity and price but no symbol returns status provider_unavailable, metadata provider_errors ["'symbol'"], exception KeyError. server.py:565 pops 'symbol' from params before the handler call (local_params passed at ~598). lots.py:26 reads params['symbol'] for open and lots.py:35 for sell, so both are broken through /api/fn. The KeyError is raised before open_lot writes, so the probe left the ledger unchanged.

findings.title: Symbol filter on list is ignored when called through /api/fn
findings.detail: The route removes symbol before LOTS runs, so list() always gets symbol=None and returns all lots. The filter the pane or API user sends never applies.
findings.evidence: Code path: server.py pops symbol into instrument, LOTS list reads params.get('symbol') which is None. Not observable here because the ledger is empty (l4 equals l1).
findings.proposed_fix: Use instrument.symbol as the list filter fallback.

findings.title: Acquisition date cannot be supplied, so holding period and term are wrong for historical lots
findings.detail: LOTS open never forwards opened_at to tax_lots.open_lot, which defaults to now. Every imported lot is therefore stamped with today's date, so holding_days and the short/long term split used by realized() are wrong for any lot bought before today.
findings.evidence: tax_lots.open_lot accepts opened_at (line 61) and writes it (line 68). lots.py open call passes only symbol, quantity, price, account. The lots_seed also lists acquired_at as a column that the handler never produces.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept acquired_at / opened_at (ISO date) in LOTS open and validate it is not in the future.

findings.title: lot_ids are silently ignored unless method is SPECIFIC
findings.detail: LOTS passes lot_ids into specific_lot_ids, but tax_lots.sell only uses them when method == 'SPECIFIC'. The default method is FIFO, so a caller who sends lot_ids gets FIFO relief with no warning.
findings.evidence: Code path only (the sell call could not be created). With method FIFO the ordered list ignores keep.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat non-empty lot_ids as method SPECIFIC, or reject lot_ids unless method is SPECIFIC.

findings.title: Hard-coded 365-day threshold and overclaimed subtitle
findings.detail: The long-term cutoff is fixed at 365 days in the service even though the seed exposes long_term_threshold_days. The pane subtitle says Lot-level basis and harvest candidates, but LOTS computes no harvest candidates (that is TLH).

findings.detail: Three of six sidecar calls returned status provider_unavailable with reason 'warming in background' and exception_type_original TimeoutError, including the first all-tab live call and the FX call. An immediate retry returned 170 of 170 resolved. The reference=true call also returned warming, so the cause may be a shared background job, not the MOST code path. The cause is not located in screen-2 code, so treat the mechanism as unverified.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/screen/_funcs.py:393-481 (live budget path); wrapper that emits 'warming in background' not located in this unit
findings.evidence: MOST_all.json, MOST_fx.json, MOST_ref.json each show provider_unavailable and warming text; MOST_all_retry.json shows 170 of 170 resolved in the same session.
findings.proposed_fix: Return the last good snapshot with an explicit stale label while the scan warms, instead of an empty provider_unavailable payload. Locate and fix the sidecar timeout wrapper.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced, and the mechanism is located outside screen-2. First calls on a new param key returned status provider_unavailable, reason 'warming in background', exception TimeoutError, zero rows, in about 1 s: v_MOST_eq.json and the new FX key v_MOST_fx_new.json. The identical repeat returned 50 rows, status ok, scanned 62 of 62, in 0.06 s. The source is backend/showme/server_routes/function_index.py:108-123. For TOP, BRIEF and MOST with no SWR cache hit, if the task is not done after 1.0 s it returns fallback_function_payload 'warming in background' with TimeoutError. The truth-audit doc (docs/audit/truth-audit-summary.md:45) acknowledges this cold-call envelope. It is an honest provider_unavailable label, but a cold live call returns empty when data exists, which meets the P0 empty-when-data-exists criterion. The defect is in the shared route, not in screen-2 code.

Name-only queries therefore never reach the per-ticker feeds that carry the company headlines. The same query with symbol AAPL finds four matching stories.
