findings.title: Surface labelled implied vol is realized vol plus an invented smile; RR/BF cards are fabricated
findings.detail: The grid header reads 'Surface (tenor x delta, implied vol %)' and the KPI cards read '25 delta risk reversal: call minus put' and '25 delta butterfly'. In fact every ATM value is trailing realized vol. The 25-delta RR and BF are not market quotes: RR = 0.06*ATM (sign from the term slope) and BF = 0.015*ATM. Nothing in the response tells the user this, and the pane comment says the cards 'read the real card fields'.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/OVDV.tsx:485-487 and 513; backend/showme/engine/functions/fx/_funcs.py:470-471 (rr_25 = slope_sign*0.06*term; bf_25 = 0.015*term), 502-503 (head_rr, head_bf), 555 (vol_source text)
findings.evidence: OVDV_a.json: risk_reversal_25d_pct=0.215 = 0.06*3.5834; butterfly_25d_pct=0.0538 = 0.015*3.5834; vol_source=live_realized_vol; sources include model:fx_vol_smile. Realized ATM values match the yfinance recomputation exactly.
findings.proposed_fix: Relabel the grid as a realized-vol surface and remove the RR/BF cards (or label them as model output with the formula). Show market RR/BF only when option quotes are available, and say so. No keyless market option-quote source was verified (keyless_source null).

verifier.reasoning: Mostly confirmed. The surface ATM values are trailing realized vol from yfinance (vol_source live_realized_vol, sidecar USDTRY and EURUSD outputs). RR is 0.06*term with slope sign and BF is 0.015*term (_funcs.py:470-471), so they are model outputs, not market quotes. The UI header reads 'Surface · tenor × delta (implied vol %)' (OVDV.tsx:513), and the cards read '25Δ risk reversal' and '25Δ butterfly' (OVDV.tsx:485-491). The data-quality notice that discloses the reference model renders only when !isLive (OVDV.tsx:459), and isLive is true for live_realized_vol, so the pane shows a green live state with no caveat. The UI never renders the methodology text (grep finds only the type field). The finding overstates one point: the API methodology string does disclose 'labelled model' RR scaled to about 6% of ATM, so the defect is the UI presentation rather than a wholly undisclosed response. Fabricated smile values presented as market cards in the UI justify P0, with medium confidence because the API disclosure softens it.

findings.title: Headline 25-delta risk reversal has the wrong sign whenever the 1W-to-1M slope is negative
findings.detail: The surface rows take the sign of RR from the term slope (slope_sign), but the headline card uses head_rr = 0.06*ATM, which is always positive. For USDTRY the 1M surface gives RR = 25C - 25P = -0.0768 while the card shows +0.0768.
findings.evidence: OVDV_usdtry.json 1M row: 25P 1.3378, 25C 1.2610 (surface); card risk_reversal_25d_pct=0.0768.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the headline RR from the same 1M surface row (25C - 25P) so card and grid agree.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. Sidecar OVDV USDTRY: the 1M surface row gives 25P 1.3378 and 25C 1.2610, so 25C minus 25P = -0.0768. The headline card reports risk_reversal_25d_pct 0.0768 and cards.risk_reversal_25d_pct 0.0768. The cause is _funcs.py:502, where head_rr = 0.06*head_term is always positive, while the surface rows use slope_sign (line 470). The card is labelled 'call minus put', so its sign is wrong whenever the 1W-to-1M slope is negative.

findings.title: User-quoted ATM 7.00 percent is shown as 7.15 percent, and an invented term ramp is added
findings.detail: When the user supplies a flat atm_vol, the handler adds 0.15 vol points per tenor step (a 'historical reference-model slope' that is not an input). The 1M headline therefore reads 7.15 instead of the 7.00 the user entered, and 1Y reads 7.60. The vol_source still says user_inputs as if the whole curve was quoted.
findings.evidence: OVDV_quoted.json: input atm_vol=0.07 gives atm_1m_vol_pct=7.15 and series 1W 7.00 / 1M 7.15 / 3M 7.30 / 6M 7.45 / 1Y 7.60.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the user's ATM value exactly for the headline and the flat curve when only atm_vol is given; label any ramp as a model assumption.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. Sidecar OVDV with atm_vol=0.07 returns vol_source user_inputs with series 1W 7.00, 1M 7.15, 3M 7.30, 6M 7.45, 1Y 7.60, and atm_1m_vol_pct and the ATM card both 7.15. The cause is _funcs.py:677, curve = atm + i*0.0015, which adds an undocumented term ramp to a user-quoted flat ATM. The methodology string does not mention the ramp, and the 'user_inputs' label implies the whole curve was quoted, so the user's 7.00 headline is altered to 7.15 (wrong calculation, P1).

findings.title: Silent per-tenor fallback keeps the live label
findings.detail: If a tenor's realized vol is zero or unavailable, that tenor silently takes the hard-coded reference vol, but vol_source and data_mode still say live_realized_vol with no warning.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/fx/_funcs.py:684-691 (atm if atm and atm>0 else _reference_atm_vol(pair)) and 690-691 (return live label)
findings.evidence: Code path; no fixture was forced in this session, so this is reviewed from code only.
findings.proposed_fix: Count fallback tenors and set vol_source to mixed with a warning listing them.

findings.title: Short-window realized vol and managed-currency pairs are presented without caveats
findings.detail: The 1W ATM uses only 5 daily returns (_TENOR_WINDOW_DAYS['1W']=5), which is statistically weak. USDTRY 1M ATM is 1.28 percent from a managed crawl, which is not an option-market level, and no warning is raised.
findings.evidence: OVDV_usdtry.json: series 1W 1.395, 1M 1.2802, 3M 1.6873; OVDV_a.json 1W 3.2003 from 5 returns.
findings.proposed_fix: Use at least 21 returns for the shortest tenor, and warn for managed or pegged pairs.

b2.reference_method: Pro forma what-if: post-trade equity = cash - cost x qty + sum MV; delta of equity, weights and exposure; a buy debits cash and an existing holding is aggregated (manifest port_whatif_seed.py:56-107).
b2.live_call: Three calls. (1) pane default {symbol AAPL, quantity 100, cost 100} -> delta MV +34,237.00, unrealized delta +24,237.00, cash unchanged at 25,000. (2) {AAPL, quantity 10, cost 300} -> timed out after 14.1 s, status provider_unavailable (honest). (3) {NVDA, quantity 10} with no cost -> delta MV +1,866.40, unrealized delta +1,866.40, cost_basis unchanged at 102,425, n_positions 7 to 8, NVDA now listed twice (40 at 135 and 10 at 0). Artifacts in scratchpad work/portfolio-3.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed the delta: 100 x 342.37 = 34,237.00 market-value change, and the cost-100 unrealized gain 100 x (342.37 - 100) = 24,237.00, both matching the handler, so the arithmetic is right but the inputs are wrong. A purchase should reduce cash by 100 x 100 = 10,000 (or 10 x 186.64 for NVDA) and the handler leaves cash at 25,000 in both cases. The equity change is therefore overstated by the full notional.

findings.title: Pane default fabricates a $100 cost and reports a fake P&L gain for any symbol
findings.detail: PortfolioAnalytics.tsx pre-fills the Entry field with '100' for every symbol (line 246) and sends it as cost (line 1038). For AAPL trading at 342.37 the pane therefore reports a hypothetical unrealized gain of +24,237 that exists only because of the placeholder. The placeholder is shown as a real cost.
findings.evidence: whatif_pane_default.json: summary cost 100.0, unrealized_pnl_delta 24237.0, market_value_delta 34237.0
findings.proposed_fix: Leave cost blank by default, require it for a buy, and use the live last price as the default cost with a label.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:246 seeds the Entry field with the value '100' for every non-PSC function, and line 1023-1038 sends it as cost (num(state.entry, 100)). The sidecar call AAPL 100 shares at cost 100 returns summary.cost 100 and unrealized_pnl_delta +24,226.9, which exists only because of the placeholder cost. The value is a visible field value, not a greyed placeholder, so a fabricated cost is shown as a real input. Scratch: whatif_aapl100.json.

findings.title: What-if never debits cash, so hypothetical equity is overstated by the full notional
findings.detail: The handler copies cash unchanged into the scenario (_more.py:49) and only appends the position. Buying 100 AAPL at 100 or 10 NVDA at market therefore raises portfolio value by the whole notional with no cash offset. Delta reports market_value only, so the user sees a gain that is not there.
findings.evidence: whatif_pane_default.json and whatif_no_cost.json: after.totals.cash 25000 unchanged while market_value rises by 34,237 and 1,866.40
findings.proposed_fix: Debit qty x cost (or the live price) from cash for buys, credit for sells, and report the change in total equity as well as market value.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. _more.py:49 copies cash unchanged (before and after totals.cash both 25000), and the hypothetical position is appended with no debit. market_value rises by the full notional (34,226.9 for 100 AAPL at 100; 1,866.4 for 10 NVDA). Those MV figures are arithmetically right for MV alone, but the scenario's total equity (MV plus cash) is overstated by the notional, and a professional what-if would debit cash. Real methodology gap, so P1 is right. Scratch: whatif_aapl100.json and whatif_nvda_nocost.json.

findings.title: Missing cost defaults to zero, so the whole position value shows as a gain
findings.detail: cost is read as float(params.get('cost', 0)) (_more.py:33). A blank or omitted cost makes avg_cost 0, and unrealized P&L equals the full market value with no warning.
findings.evidence: whatif_no_cost.json: cost 0.0 in summary, unrealized_pnl_delta 1866.40 equal to 10 x 186.64
findings.proposed_fix: Require cost for a new position, or default it to the live price and say so in warnings.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed on both paths. Backend: a missing cost gives cost 0.0 (_more.py:33). The sidecar call NVDA quantity 10 with no cost returns unrealized_pnl_delta 1866.40, equal to the full market value, with warnings []. Pane path: the Entry field is read with num(raw, fallback) (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1240), and Number('') is 0, which is finite, so a blank Entry is sent as cost 0 rather than the fallback. The pane therefore reaches the same silent zero-cost gain. Keep P1.

findings.title: Existing holdings are appended as duplicate lines instead of being aggregated
findings.detail: The scenario appends a new PortfolioPosition even when the symbol is already held (_more.py:46-48), so NVDA appears twice (40 at 135 and 10 at 0). n_positions rises by one for a symbol the book already held, and a sell (negative quantity) is booked as a new negative lot.
findings.evidence: whatif_no_cost.json: after.positions contains NVDA 40@135 and NVDA 10@0; delta.n_positions +1
findings.proposed_fix: Merge into the existing lot (weighted average cost on buys, realized P&L on sells) and report the net change in position count.

findings.title: Manifest scenario features are not implemented
findings.detail: The seed promises a list of buy/sell/add/remove actions applied in order, a cash floor, a risk re-estimate, display currency and tax impact (port_whatif_seed.py:56-107). The handler takes one symbol, quantity and cost (_more.py:29-33) and returns no weights, exposure or risk.
findings.evidence: Params accepted: symbol, quantity, cost only
findings.proposed_fix: Implement scenario_actions and cash_floor or narrow the manifest to what is shipped.

findings.title: Two full PORT runs back to back make the what-if slow and prone to timeout
findings.detail: The handler runs PORT twice sequentially (_more.py:52-53), each fetching every quote again. A seven-position book hit the 14 s worker budget in one call and returned provider_unavailable.
findings.evidence: whatif_aapl_dup.json: TimeoutError, function timed out after 14s; successful calls took 5.5 to 6.2 s
findings.proposed_fix: Fetch quotes once and reuse them for both the baseline and the scenario.

findings.title: Function description is empty
findings.detail: The function-index description for PORT_WHATIF is blank.
findings.evidence: function-index: PORT_WHATIF description ''
findings.proposed_fix: Add a description.

b2.reference_method: Fixed-fractional sizing: risk budget = account x risk_pct; shares = budget / |entry - stop|; R = |target - entry| / |entry - stop|; simple Kelly f = max(0, (p R - (1 - p)) / R).
b2.live_call: Five calls. (1) account 100000, entry 100, stop 95, target 115, risk 0.01, win 0.55, LONG -> risk 1000, shares 200, notional 20,000, R 3.0, Kelly 0.40. (2) pane-like {risk_pct 0.01, stop 95, target 115} with no symbol -> input_error 'a LONG target must be above the entry'. (3) {symbol AAPL, account 100000, risk 0.01, stop 300} -> entry 342.37 (live_quote), shares 23.6. (4) SHORT entry 100 stop 105 target 90 win 0.5 -> R 2.0, shares 200, Kelly 0.25. (5) {risk 0.01, account 100000, stop 70000} with no symbol -> status ok, entry 75,688.83 from the BTCUSDT live quote, shares 0.1758. Artifacts in scratchpad work/portfolio-3.
b2.independent_check: Hand check of call (1): unit risk 5, shares 1000/5 = 200, notional 200 x 100 = 20,000, R = 15/5 = 3, Kelly = (0.55 x 3 - 0.45)/3 = 0.40 (kelly_shares 400, kelly_dollars 40,000), all match. Call (4): R = 10/5 = 2, Kelly = (0.5 x 2 - 0.5)/2 = 0.25, match. Call (3) live entry 342.37 equals the yfinance AAPL close on 2026-11-06. The formulas are correct, but the instrument used when no symbol is sent is wrong (see P0).

findings.title: Sizing with no symbol silently uses BTCUSDT's live price as entry
findings.detail: When no symbol is passed, the sidecar injects the agent default instrument BTCUSDT (inputEcho symbol BTCUSDT, instrument BTCUSDT). PSC then fetches the BTCUSDT quote as the entry (psc.py:137-138 and _live_last at psc.py:82-96) and returns status ok with entry_source live_quote. The pane's PSC config has no defaultSymbol (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:178-182) and effectiveSymbol falls back to the tab symbol (line 250), so with no tab symbol the sizing is for BTC with no visible label. The manifest says entry defaults to the symbol's live price, but there is no symbol.
findings.evidence: psc_pane_no_symbol_stop70k.json: instrument.symbol BTCUSDT, entry 75688.83, entry_source live_quote, shares 0.1758, status ok; psc_pane_blank_entry.json: same BTCUSDT default
findings.proposed_fix: Refuse to size when no symbol is supplied and entry is blank (input_required). Never default the instrument for PSC, and echo the symbol used in the data payload.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. With no symbol, the sidecar's agent runtime (_agent_runtime.py _agent_function_params) injects symbol BTCUSDT, which the response echoes in inputEcho and in instrument.symbol. PSC then takes the live BTC quote as entry (75,681.27, entry_source live_quote) and returns status ok with a BTC-sized position. The user asked for sizing without naming a symbol, and the result is for a different instrument presented as a normal result. The pane's PSC config has no defaultSymbol or usesSymbol, so no label is shown in the UI. I did not inspect the rendered pane, so visibility is taken from the config. Scratch: psc_nosymbol.json.

findings.title: Blank-entry error names the wrong cause
findings.detail: With no symbol and blank entry, the reason shown is 'a LONG target must be above the entry' because the injected BTC price (about 75,689) is above the 115 target. The real problem is the missing entry, so the user is told to fix the wrong input.
findings.evidence: psc_pane_blank_entry.json: status input_error, reason 'Position sizing needs: a LONG target must be above the entry.'
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the entry and symbol first, and report 'entry needed: no symbol and no entry' when they are missing.

findings.title: Side, win rate and risk percent are not exposed in the pane, so Kelly and SHORT are unreachable from the UI
findings.detail: buildParams for PSC hard-codes risk_pct 0.01 (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1029) and sends only account, entry, stop and target. Side and win_rate are never sent and have no control, so the Kelly output and the SHORT branch cannot be used from the pane. The manifest declares win_rate (psc_seed.py:109-118) and side (psc_seed.py:119-126).
findings.evidence: Control list for PSC shows account, entry, stop and target only
findings.proposed_fix: Add side, win rate and risk-percent controls and send them.

findings.title: No cap on notional or buying power
findings.detail: shares = risk_dollars / unit risk with no ceiling (psc.py:177-181), so a very tight stop yields a notional far above the account and a leverage_implied well above 1. Professional sizers cap by buying power or a maximum position size.
findings.evidence: Code path only; not run with a tight stop.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an optional max_notional or leverage cap with a warning when the cap binds.

b2.reference_method: Satellite AOI imagery: select a preset AOI, choose the latest cloud-free observation in a window, and show its real capture date. Cloud cover should be observed (or labelled as modelled). NASA GIBS serves daily MODIS tiles with a lag; a blank tile must not be shown as a capture.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/SAT {} -> status ok, aoi_label 'custom bbox', bbox -122.55..-122.30 x 37.70..37.85 (San Francisco), capture 2026-11-08, cloud 60 (sat1.json). POST {aoi:singapore_strait, layer:ndvi} -> still San Francisco bbox, aoi_label 'custom bbox' (sat_sg.json). POST {aoi:cushing_ok, bbox:''} -> Cushing bbox -96.9151..-96.6151 x 35.8351..36.1351 (sat_cush.json). Raw checks in scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2 (gibs_today.bin, gibs_old.bin).
b2.independent_check: Open-Meteo values for the SF bbox centre recomputed from raw: current temp 17.7, cloud 40, wind 14.1, daily cloud mean 60, max 20.1, min 11.6 - all match the backend. Tile check: decoded GIBS PNG for TIME=2026-11-08 has 0 of 589,824 pixels with nonzero RGB (fully black, opaque). TIME=2026-11-01 for the same bbox is 116 KB with imagery. The backend reports the 2026-11-08 tile as the latest capture with tile_reachable true.

findings.title: Selected AOI is silently replaced by San Francisco Bay
findings.detail: The sidecar routed defaults inject a fixed SAT bbox (San Francisco Bay). The handler prefers any bbox over the aoi preset, and the routed default survives the merge because the caller does not send bbox. Every AOI choice therefore renders San Francisco imagery and weather, labelled 'custom bbox'. The pane sends aoi, so the user's selection is ignored.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:365-372 (SAT routed defaults with bbox -122.55,37.70,-122.30,37.85); :787 (defaults.update(merged) keeps it); backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/sat.py:71-80 (bbox_override takes precedence over aoi); ui/src/functions/SAT.tsx:274 (params aoi) and :331 (locationName from aoi_label)
findings.evidence: sat_sg.json: request aoi=singapore_strait; response aoi echo singapore_strait, aoi_label 'custom bbox', bbox_label -122.55000,37.70000,-122.30000,37.85000, tile BBOX=37.700000,-122.550000,37.850000,-122.300000, cloud 60 (SF point). Same bbox on the default call.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the bbox from the SAT routed defaults. In sat.py, apply bbox only when the caller explicitly sends one, and label the AOI with its preset name.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. SAT with aoi=singapore_strait returned aoi echo singapore_strait, aoi_label 'custom bbox', bbox [-122.55,37.70,-122.30,37.85] (San Francisco Bay), and cloud_pct 60 from the SF point. The default call with no params (aoi cushing_ok) also returns the same SF bbox with aoi_label 'custom bbox', so every AOI selection is replaced. Cause: _agent_runtime.py:365-372 injects the SF bbox for SAT, and defaults.update(merged) at ~line 787 keeps it because the pane does not send bbox; sat.py:77-79 then lets bbox_override win over the aoi preset. SAT.tsx:274 does send aoi, so the user's choice is ignored and the imagery shown is a different location. The default makes the defect wider, not narrower. Scratch: .../scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/sat_sg.json and sat_default.json

findings.title: Blank GIBS tile presented as the latest capture
findings.detail: The default capture date is today (date_to). GIBS has no imagery for today yet: TIME=2026-11-08 returns an all-black PNG, while the prior week returns real imagery. The handler checks only for an HTTP 2xx, so an empty tile counts as reachable and the card shows it as latest_capture 2026-11-08 with status ok.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/sat.py:88 (capture_date = date_to), sat.py:284-286 (_probe_tile returns True on any 2xx); routed default date_to=today in _agent_runtime.py:365-372
findings.evidence: Decoded gibs_today.bin (TIME=2026-11-08, 768x768 RGBA, 4.2 KB): 0 of 589,824 pixels have nonzero RGB, alpha 255 everywhere. gibs_old.bin (TIME=2026-11-01): 116 KB with imagery. sat1.json: status ok, latest_capture 2026-11-08, tile_reachable true.
findings.proposed_fix: Walk back to the newest date whose tile has non-trivial pixels (or a size threshold), report the real capture date and the lag, and treat an empty tile as a failed probe.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced directly. The GIBS WMS URL for TIME=2026-11-08 (same bbox and layer the sidecar builds) returns a 4,212-byte 768x768 RGBA PNG with 0 of 589,824 pixels having nonzero RGB and alpha 255, i.e. a solid black tile. TIME=2026-11-01 returns full imagery (589,824 of 589,824 nonzero). The sidecar's default call reports status ok, capture_date 2026-11-08, and cloud_pct 60. sat.py:284-286 (_probe_tile) treats any 2xx/3xx as reachable, and sat.py:88 sets capture_date = date_to (today), so the blank tile is presented as the latest capture. Empty output where data exists qualifies as P0 under the rubric. Scratch PNGs: .../scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/gibs_2026-11-08.png and gibs_2026-11-01.png

findings.title: Layer control missing; two layers map to the same product
findings.detail: The pane hard-codes layer true_color, so ndvi, thermal, moisture and swir cannot be chosen. moisture and swir both map to MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_Bands721, so one of the two labels is wrong. The NDVI layer is an 8-day composite requested with a daily TIME, which is unverified.
findings.evidence: sat.py _GIBS_LAYERS: 'moisture' and 'swir' both -> MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_Bands721.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose the layer select in the pane and give moisture and swir distinct GIBS products, or drop one.

findings.title: Cloud cover is modelled but shown as satellite cloud cover
findings.detail: cloud_pct is Open-Meteo daily cloud_cover_mean, a model value for the centroid, placed in the satellite card for the capture. The values are correct against Open-Meteo, but the label implies an observation.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/sat.py _fetch_conditions (cloud_cover_mean) and the cards/rows built in execute
findings.evidence: Open-Meteo raw for 37.7750,-122.4250: cloud_cover_mean 60, current cloud 40; backend cloud_pct 60 and daily_cloud_mean_pct 60 match.
findings.proposed_fix: Label the value 'modelled cloud cover (Open-Meteo)' or derive cloud from the scene itself.

findings.title: No scene search: date window is informational only
findings.detail: The capture is always date_to, and date_from is returned but never used to select a scene. The seed says the capture date defaults to the latest available, but the handler uses today, which usually has no imagery.
findings.evidence: sat1.json: date_from 2026-11-01, date_to 2026-11-08, capture_date 2026-11-08 (the window is not searched).
findings.proposed_fix: Search backward from date_to for the newest date with real tile content and return that date.

findings.title: Manifest seed describes Sentinel-2 with credential gating
findings.detail: sat_seed.py describes Sentinel-2 imagery via SentinelHub or Planet with a not_configured path when a credential is missing. The handler is keyless NASA GIBS MODIS with Open-Meteo conditions and never reads such a credential.
findings.evidence: sat.py module docstring: keyless NASA GIBS tiles and Open-Meteo; the seed's semantic test expects data_mode not_configured without a SentinelHub credential.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite sat_seed.py to the GIBS contract (presets, layers, keyless sources, honest empty-tile behaviour).

b2.reference_method: US Treasury auction calendar: each announced security with its auction (competitive close) date, offering size and results from TreasuryDirect. Professional calendars list the same per-auction rows.
b2.live_call: POST {action:upcoming,horizon_days:30} -> HTTP 200 ok, sources [treasurydirect], 0 rows, no reason, so the pane shows 'No upcoming Treasury auctions in the 30-day window'. POST {upcoming,horizon 7,limit 2,security_type Note} -> 0 rows. POST {upcoming,horizon 7,reference:true} -> template: 5 rows dated 2026-11-11..2026-11-23 (horizon 7 ignored), fixed offering amounts 70e9/75e9/69e9/70e9/25e9, status provider_unavailable. Harness caveat: the sidecar injects live=true and limit=6 into every request (inputEcho), so live_auctions=false cannot be reached through this API. findings.title: Live TreasuryDirect path always returns zero auctions
findings.detail: The adapter maps the auction date from the field auctionDate, which the live feed never populates. Every row is then dropped by 'if not ad: continue' in upcoming() and recent(). findings.title: Unfilled limit orders are booked as executed fills
findings.detail: _avg_fill returns the book (limit) price when the order has no fill metadata (tca.py:425-427), and _load_fills keeps any row where that value is not None (tca.py:386-388). The executed quantity falls back to the order quantity when filled_qty is 0 (tca.py:398). So an order that never filled becomes a fill at its limit price with full size, producing fake slippage, cost and a 'live' label.

findings.proposed_fix: Count an order only when filled_qty > 0 or explicit fill prices exist; never use the limit price as avg fill; label unfilled orders as excluded.

findings.title: Calendar reported as 0 scheduled when the calendar call failed

findings.title: TSOX default and quick-pick Treasury futures are rejected as unsupported
findings.detail: The seed default symbol ZN=F and the UI quick picks TU=F, ZF=F, ZN=F, ZB=F (ui/src/functions/TSOX.tsx:51-54) all resolve to EQUITY. default_asset_class_name returns EQUITY when no table matches (server.py:905): COMMODITY_FUTURES (server.py:113) has no treasury codes and BOND_SYMBOLS (server.py:115) lists only US yield names. TSOX then refuses its own default, so the ticket is broken out of the box.
findings.evidence: Live TSOX ZN=F -> status unsupported_asset, native_asset_classes ['BOND'], requested_asset_class 'EQUITY'. US10Y control -> BOND and preview ok.
findings.proposed_fix: Map the CME treasury codes (ZT, ZF, ZN, ZB, TN, UB and TU, with =F) to BOND or FUTURE in default_asset_class_name and extend the tests.

verifier.reasoning: Sidecar TSOX ZN=F returns status unsupported_asset, native_asset_classes ['BOND'], requested_asset_class 'EQUITY'. The asset resolver returns EQUITY because ZN is in neither COMMODITY_FUTURES nor BOND_SYMBOLS (server.py ~876-905). TSOXFunction sets asset_classes=(BOND,) (_funcs.py ~434), so it refuses its own seed default ZN=F (tsox_seed.py line 106) and the UI quick picks TU/ZF/ZN/ZB. The ticket is broken out of the box.

findings.title: No price-units check for yield-quoted bonds
findings.detail: TSOX accepts price 110.015625 for US10Y, which is a yield symbol in BOND_SYMBOLS. The preview does not check that a yield-quoted instrument is priced in price units, and it has no yield/price conversion.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/trade/_funcs.py (EMSX preview path used by TSOX); server.py:115
findings.evidence: Live TSOX US10Y preview: price 110.015625 accepted, status preview.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject or convert prices for yield-quoted instruments and show the quote convention in the ticket.

findings.title: Core bond-ticket analytics missing (accrued interest, DV01, multiplier, settlement)
findings.detail: The seed's DV01 formula is documented as 'not computed server-side'. The preview carries no contract multiplier, no accrued interest or dirty price, no settlement date and no DV01, although the quantity is labelled 'contracts_or_face'. A treasury ticket normally shows these before send.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/manifest/seeds/tsox_seed.py (formula_dict DV01 notes); TSOX preview dict in _funcs.py
findings.evidence: Live preview keys contain no dv01, accrued, multiplier or settlement fields.
findings.proposed_fix: Add contract multiplier, notional face, DV01 from the ticket price and modified duration, and a clean/dirty price line for cash bonds.

findings.title: LIMIT ticket without a price is accepted (inherited, code-read)
findings.detail: TSOX inherits the EMSX preview path, so a LIMIT order with no price previews with price null, as shown for EMSX. The seed states that price is required for LIMIT.
findings.evidence: EMSX live probe (same path); TSOX not separately probed to stay within call budget.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate LIMIT price for TSOX as for EMSX.

findings.title: CoinGecko profile row is stamped with the call time and tagged BTCUSDT
findings.detail: When no crypto news is found, the fallback adds a CoinGecko project-profile row. Its published_at is datetime.now() at the call, so it looks like a fresh news item. Its symbol is hard-coded as base+USDT whatever was requested. Verified by calling the helper directly.

findings.proposed_fix: Omit published_at for profile rows, or use the coin's real last-updated time. Tag the row with the requested symbol. Keep project profiles out of the news list.

findings.title: 24h price move becomes a critical news alert
findings.detail: The Binance market-context row is emitted as a news item. severity is critical at a 15 percent move, and alert is true at a 10 percent move. Its link assumes the symbol ends in USDT (symbol[:-4]), so a USDC or FDUSD pair yields a wrong URL. Price moves are not news and should not raise news alerts.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/news/cn.py:478 (URL assumes USDT suffix), :481 (critical at 15 percent), :482 (alert at 10 percent)
findings.evidence: Code path confirmed by reading. Direct helper call for BTCUSDT returned status market_context with alert False at the current move, so the alert trigger has not been observed live.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep market-context rows out of the news alert logic (alert false). Build the URL from the actual pair, or omit it.

verifier.reasoning: Code confirmed: the Binance market_context row (cn.py:478-482) gets severity critical at abs move >=15 and alert True at >=10. The URL uses symbol[:-4] with a fixed _USDT suffix, so non-USDT pairs get the wrong quote. Helper call for BTCUSDT returned -0.17% with alert False, so the 10% trigger was not observed. The row only appears in the no-news fallback path, and importance_score can reach 70 with a large move and volume, so it can reach critical_articles. Real but mostly a classification and URL defect, so P2 rather than P1. Evidence: .../news-1/cn_helpers.py

findings.title: Envelope status ok and sourceDetails ok while the payload is an unavailable placeholder
findings.detail: When no rows are returned, the handler swaps in a provider_unavailable row and sets sources to no_live_source. The envelope still reports status ok and the source detail status ok. Any caller that trusts the envelope will treat the empty result as a success.
findings.evidence: CN_1 envelope: status ok, data_state reference, sourceDetails [{name no_live_source, status ok}], data[0].status provider_unavailable.
findings.proposed_fix: Set the envelope status to match the payload (provider_unavailable) and set the source detail status accordingly.

findings.title: Empty error message on RSS timeout and intermittent empty first call
findings.detail: The per-source warning is built as f'{src_name}: {e}', so a TimeoutError with no message produces 'rss: '. The first AAPL call returned no live rows for this reason. The retry returned four rows.
findings.evidence: CN_1 metadata provider_errors ['rss: ', 'Non-live source labeled as data_state=reference: no_live_source']; CN_2 returned 4 rows from rss with no provider errors.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the exception type name when the message is empty, as the AV handler does (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__).

findings.title: Latent dividend-yield scaling error when the trailing key is absent

b2.reference_method: Economic calendar (Bloomberg ECO style): scheduled release time with timezone, forecast (consensus), previous, actual when printed, and surprise = actual minus forecast in the indicator's own unit. Shows a forward window and states when the feed is stale.

POST {days:30,country:UK,importance:medium}: 0 events, status ok. POST {reference:true,country:US,importance:high}: sources [calendar_feed_model], 5 events flagged as sample, actual null. POST {days:30,country:US} with no importance: 0 events. Raw FF weekly feed: 116 events dated 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-06, fields title/country/date/impact/forecast/previous only.

In-process run of eco.py helpers (no sidecar state change): '65K' parses to (65000.0,'K'); '1.2M' to (1200000.0,'M'); date '2026-11-06T08:30:00-05:00' normalizes to '2026-11-06'. Window check: feed newest date 2026-11-06, today 2026-11-08, so 0 rows fall in the function's forward window. Check failed on unit scaling.

findings.title: Forex Factory K/M suffix is applied and also kept as the unit, so values are 1000x too large
findings.detail: _parse_ff_number multiplies '65K' to 65000.0 and then returns unit 'K'. The pane formats the number with that unit, so a 65 thousand print reads as 65,000.00K. The same happens for M, B and T. The live feed uses these suffixes (e.g. Non-Farm Employment Change forecast 65K).
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/eco.py:490-506 (multiplier applied at :498, unit = suffix at :506); ui/src/functions/ECO.tsx:656-661 (fmtVal appends unit to the number)
findings.evidence: In-process: _parse_ff_number('65K') -> (65000.0,'K',False); _parse_ff_number('1.2M') -> (1200000.0,'M',False); _normalize_events row {forecast:65000.0, unit:'K'}. ff_week.json forecast cell '65K' for Non-Farm Employment Change 2026-11-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep the parsed number in the feed's unit (no multiplier) or multiply and return an empty unit, never both. Add a test for '65K'.

verifier.reasoning: In-process run of the real parser: _parse_ff_number('65K') returns (65000.0,'K',False), '1.2M' returns (1200000.0,'M',False), and '-1.2B' returns (-1200000000.0,'B',False). eco.py:498 applies the multiplier and :506 sets unit=suffix. _normalize_events (eco.py:395-405) takes forecast_unit as the row unit, so a 65K forecast becomes forecast 65000.0 with unit 'K'. ECO.tsx fmtVal (lines 656-658) returns formatNumber(n,2)+unit, which renders '65,000.00K', 1000x too large. The live feed returned no events in my 7-day window, so the full-pane path was verified in code and in the parser, not on a live K print.

findings.title: days is ignored for the Forex Factory feed and a stale feed is reported as live
findings.detail: The FF source is a single weekly snapshot, so the forward window can only contain whatever week the snapshot covers. days (7 or 30) makes no difference. The feed's newest date is 2026-11-06 while today is 2026-11-08, so every event falls before the window (start = yesterday) and the response is status ok with an empty table and the live pill. No staleness warning is raised.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/eco.py:15 (single weekly URL), :208-226 (_forex_factory_events ignores days), :373-374 (window start = yesterday); ui/src/functions/ECO.tsx:111 and :215-216 (live pill when state ok)
findings.evidence: eco_us_high.json (days 7, US high): status ok, source forex_factory, 0 events, pill live. eco_uk30.json (days 30): 0 events. ff_week.json: 116 events, dates 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass days to a per-day or range feed, or warn that only the current FF week is covered. When the newest feed date is before today, return a stale warning and not live.

findings.title: actual is never populated from the live feed, with no warning
findings.detail: The FF feed has no actual field in any row, so _ff_cell(item.get('actual')) is always None. Actual, surprise and the Actual column are blank for every live event, and the response does not say why.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/eco.py:251 (actual from item.get('actual')), :421 (surprise only when actual exists)
findings.evidence: ff_week.json: 'actual key present in any row: False' across 116 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Warn that the feed carries no actuals, and source actuals from a keyed provider when available.

findings.title: Release time is dropped; only the date is kept
findings.detail: The feed carries times with timezone (08:30 ET), but the normalized row keeps only the calendar date. The table has a Time column and the seed's time_utc field expects a timestamp, so intraday release order is lost.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/eco.py:413 (date = event_date.isoformat() or date_text[:16]); :330 (reference template also date-only)
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the ISO datetime converted to UTC and expose it as time_utc.

findings.title: Seed inputs and methodology do not match the code
findings.detail: The seed lists countries (multiselect), categories, date_range and show_only_with_actual, none of which the handler reads (it uses country, importance, days and reference). The methodology claims FRED release_dates, RSS consensus and a sigma-standardised surprise; the code returns the raw actual minus forecast, never sets consensus, and labels forecast as consensus.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/eco.py:36-47 (params read); :421 (raw surprise); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/eco_seed.py methodology, formula_dict surprise (sigma), inputs countries/categories/date_range/show_only_with_actual
findings.evidence: eco_seed.py formula surprise = (actual - consensus)/sigma_24m; eco.py:421 surprise = round(actual - forecast, 6).
findings.proposed_fix: Update the seed to the real sources and formula, or implement the documented ones.

findings.title: importance as a list silently returns no events
findings.detail: The seed default for importance is a list, but the handler does str(importance), so a list becomes the string "['high', 'medium']", which is never a substring of an impact value. Result: zero events, status ok. The pane sends a single string, so the UI is not affected.
findings.evidence: In-process: _normalize_events(rows, country='US', importance=['high','medium'], days=30) -> 0 rows; importance='medium' -> 1 row.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept lists (match any) and reject unknown types with a warning.

findings.title: Documented lookback window is not implemented
findings.detail: The seed describes a window of -30d to +30d, but the handler starts the window at yesterday and never looks back further.
findings.evidence: Source inspection.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement the lookback or correct the description.

findings.title: RSI seed sums gains and losses instead of averaging, skewing RSI on short windows
findings.detail: rsiSeries accumulates gains and losses as sums over the first 14 changes and uses that sum as the Wilder seed, so the seed is 14x too large. Recurrence then decays it only slowly, about (13/14)^n, so the error stays above 1 point until roughly 100 bars. On the 1M window (21 bars) the RSI is 11 points high. The panel labels the value RSI(14) and the methodology says Wilder. HP.tsx:862-885 has the same code.
findings.evidence: gp_aapl_1m.json (21 bars): GP RSI 64.3221 vs Wilder 52.9895; gp_aapl_3m.json (64 bars): 53.8857 vs 51.5549; gp_aapl_1y.json (250 bars): 51.46216 vs 51.46215 (passes). Per-bar GP-vs-Wilder gap: bar 20 +13.2, bar 40 +31.1, bar 60 +0.33, bar 100 +0.44, bar 150 +0.007.
findings.proposed_fix: At i === period set gains = gains / period and losses = losses / period before computing rs (or seed with the simple average), in both GP.tsx and HP.tsx. Better: move RSI to the shared server path so both panes use one implementation.

verifier.reasoning: Code confirmed: ui/src/functions/GP.tsx rsiSeries (lines 752-783) sums gains/losses over the first 14 changes and feeds that sum into the Wilder recurrence, so the seed is 14x too large and the error decays slowly. The same code is in HP.tsx:862-885. Reproduced from raw AAPL daily closes (yfinance, 251 bars) with a Python port of the TS code: first 21 bars GP-code 65.85 vs Wilder 57.16 (+8.7), first 64 bars 62.46 vs 61.18 (+1.3), first 250 bars 53.0056 vs 53.0056 (converges). The magnitude differs from the filed evidence (+11 at 21 bars) because the window differs, but the defect reproduces. Wrong calculation on short windows is P1.

findings.title: Intraday range is silently cut to the last 1000 bars, so the header range is wrong
findings.detail: The pane sends bars=1000 (DEFAULT_BARS). The server trims to the requested window and then keeps only the last `bars` rows (chart_history.py:302-313). Intraday data is limited by the provider (1m = 7 days) or by the 1000-bar cap, so a 1Y or 1M request shows about 2 or 3.5 days. The subtitle still reads the range pill, e.g. '1Y · 1m · 1000 candles', so the header is untrue. The seed says interval is 'validated against range' and has a semantic test gp_invalid_interval_for_range_rejected, but nothing rejects it. The BTC 1M/5m case has no warning at all.
findings.evidence: gp_aapl_1y_1m.json: status ok, 1000 bars 2026-11-04T15:40Z..2026-11-06T21:00Z (about 2.2 days), warnings ['Yahoo limits 1m history to 7 days'], inputEcho range 1Y. gp_btc_5m.json: 1000 bars 2026-11-04T12:55Z..2026-11-08T00:10Z (about 3.5 days), warnings [].
findings.proposed_fix: Return the actual span (first/last bar) and a warning whenever it is shorter than the requested range; compute bars from range/interval, and reject combinations the provider cannot serve, as the seed specifies. Show the actual span in the subtitle.

verifier.reasoning: Code confirmed: chart_history.py ~302-313 keeps windowed_rows[-user_bars:], so bars=1000 (GP.tsx:83,129; HP.tsx:79,122) caps the returned series to the most recent 1000 rows regardless of the requested range. b2.reference_method: Market-implied policy path from Fed funds or SOFR futures (CME FedWatch convention): the implied average policy rate over each meeting period minus the current target, discretized into 25 bp buckets. A T-bill yield is not a policy-rate expectation. The FOMC schedule comes from the Fed calendar.

The probabilities are reproduced, but the implied move is not a market expectation: IRX minus EFFR averaged +15.0 bp over the 36 days since the last target change on 2026-09-17 with no policy move. The key output fails.

findings.title: Hike/cut probabilities built from T-bill vs target basis but labelled live futures
findings.detail: The implied near-term rate is the 13-week T-bill yield (^IRX). Its basis over EFFR is not a policy expectation, yet the handler turns the difference from the target midpoint into a move and a probability distribution. The source is labelled live_fed_funds_futures and data_mode live_official, and the pane shows a green 'live' pill. No fed funds futures are used.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/wirp.py:66-67 (labels), :137 (^IRX as implied rate), :151-155 (target midpoint), :428 (move = implied - target mid); ui/src/functions/WIRP.tsx:205-213 and 297-303 (live pill)
findings.evidence: Live FED: target mid 3.875, ^IRX 4.00 -> move +12.5 bp -> Dec-2026 hike 50.00%, hold 47.73%, cut 2.28%, implied_change_bp +11.93. IRX minus EFFR over 36 days since 2026-09-17: mean +15.0 bp (min +8.5, max +20.8) with no change in target.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the futures label and the live pill for this method; either source SOFR or fed funds futures (not keyless, so the function must say so) or show the T-bill basis without hike/cut probabilities.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. The implied near-term rate is the ^IRX 13-week bill (wirp.py:137). Live output: target mid 3.875, implied 4.00, move +12.5 bp, hike 50.00%, implied_change_bp +11.93, with source_mode live_fed_funds_futures and data_mode live_official. No fed funds futures are used. Independent check: IRX minus DFF since 2026-09-17 has mean +14.94 bp (n=37, min 8.5, max 20.8) while the target stayed at 4.00/3.75 from 2026-09-17, so the basis alone generates the move and the 50% hike. wirp.py:66-67 and the row-level source_mode label say live fed funds futures, and WIRP.tsx:205-213 shows the 'live' pill for that mode. The methodology text does name ^IRX, but the labels still present a futures-derived probability as live. Saved in scratchpad/b2/work/macro-2/wirp_m6.json.

findings.title: Probabilities for a given meeting depend on how many meetings are requested
findings.detail: The implied move is spread across meetings with frac = idx/n, where n is the number of meetings returned. The same market inputs therefore give different probabilities for the same meeting depending on the meetings parameter. Reproduced with the handler's own _live_fed_rows, with the forward-date function patched to six illustrative dates (not the live calendar).
findings.evidence: Illustrative 6-date run: first meeting implied_change_bp +2.02 bp at meetings_limit=6 vs +6.04 bp at meetings_limit=2, for identical target and IRX inputs.
findings.proposed_fix: Scale the cumulative move by time to each meeting (days to decision / days to the last priced meeting), not by list index.

verifier.reasoning: The code defect is real: wirp.py:428-434 computes frac = idx/n with n = len(meetings), and _forward_fomc_dates caps the list at meetings_limit, so the same market inputs give different per-meeting probabilities. Reproduced by importing the handler's _live_fed_rows with six patched dates: first meeting implied_change_bp is +2.02 bp at meetings_limit=6 and +6.04 bp at meetings_limit=2, matching the claim. Downgraded from P1 because the live output is unaffected today: the hard-coded calendar has only one upcoming FOMC date (2026-12-09), so meetings=6 and meetings=2 both return one row with frac=1 (saved in wirp_m6.json and wirp_m2.json). The defect appears once the calendar holds more than one future meeting.

findings.title: Pane cumulative implied move sums values that are already cumulative
findings.detail: The 'Cumulative implied' card sums implied_change_bp across meetings, and cumulativeBpPath runs a second running sum. Each backend implied_change_bp is already the cumulative expected move at that meeting, so both overstate the path.
findings.evidence: Illustrative 6-date run: per-meeting values 2.02, 3.64, ... summed to 30.2 bp, while the final-meeting cumulative move is 12.5 bp (the full IRX-minus-target gap).
findings.proposed_fix: Plot the per-meeting values directly; drop the sum card or define it as the last-meeting move.

verifier.reasoning: The double-accumulation is real. The backend methodology (wirp.py:257-271) and code comment at line 432 say implied_change_bp at meeting n is the move accumulated by that meeting, yet WIRP.tsx sums it into the 'Cumulative implied' card (lines 276-279, 369-372) and runs cumulativeBpPath's running sum over it (lines 95-107). With six patched dates the per-meeting values 2.02..7.32 sum to 30.2 bp, and the UI path becomes [0, 2.02, 5.66, ... 30.2]. The claim's comparison value of 12.5 bp for the final meeting is slightly off: the bucketed final value is 7.32 bp, because sigma widens with sqrt(idx). The overstatement still holds. Downgraded to P2 because today's live pane has one row (11.93 bp), so the sum and path show no visible error until the calendar lists more meetings.

findings.title: Calendar exhausted: one meeting returned with status ok and no warning
findings.detail: The hard-coded 2026 FOMC list has only one date after today, so meetings=6 silently returns one row. The empty-calendar warning fires only when no rows are returned. The 2026 dates match the Fed's published schedule (second days Jun 17, Jul 29, Sep 16, Oct 28, Dec 9); 2027 dates are not in the table.
findings.evidence: POST {FED, meetings:6} -> rows 1 (2026-12-09), warnings []; POST {FED, meetings:2} -> same. Fed calendar page lists the 2026 meetings only (fetched).
findings.proposed_fix: Warn whenever fewer meetings than requested are returned; refresh the calendar from the Fed page.

findings.title: FRED outage fallback anchors on rounded T-bill yield but keeps the live label
findings.detail: If either FRED target leg raises, all three FRED values are set to None. The anchor then becomes the T-bill yield rounded to 25 bp, which can be 12.5 bp away from the true midpoint, and source_mode stays live_fed_funds_futures. Code-path defect; not reproduced live. The route's injected 3 s timeout makes the path more likely.
findings.evidence: With IRX 4.00 and midpoint 3.875, the fallback sets target 4.00 and a zero implied move; the label is unchanged.
findings.proposed_fix: Anchor on the EFFR-derived midpoint when FRED targets are down, change source_mode to a fallback label, and add a warning.

findings.title: Manifest inputs and methodology not implemented
findings.detail: wirp_seed.py defines central_banks, meeting_horizon, source (sofr_futures, ois, stir_futures, modeled), as_of, a per-bank implied_path, a 5 bp default sigma, and a terminal rate. The handler reads only central_bank and meetings, and uses a 12.5 bp sigma.
findings.evidence: Live response has no implied_path, terminal_rate or per-source switch; the source input is ignored.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the seed with the implemented method, or implement the inputs.

b2.reference_method: Professional OMS blotter: every working order (new/accepted/submitted/partially filled) must count as open; filled/cancelled/rejected are terminal; history must honour the broker and status filters the user sets. No external formula; judged against the terminal convention.

Second call {broker_filter:[alpaca_broker], limit:1} returned a recording_broker row, brokers_checked [alpaca_broker]. Third call {broker_filter:[alpaca_broker], status_filter:[open]} returned status empty.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed total_notional from the returned rows: 1*null(0) + 3*190 + 1*null(0) = 570.0, matches. Open count recomputed by the handler rule (status == 'open' only) = 0, but the three working-style rows are status 'submitted', which the terminal convention counts as open. Notional excludes both MARKET rows (price null) silently.

findings.title: Submitted orders are not counted or shown as open
findings.detail: open_count only counts status == 'open' (_funcs.py:352), and the UI OPEN_STATES set (ui/src/functions/AIM.tsx:87-94) omits 'submitted'. order_history.record_order defaults status to 'submitted' (backend/showme/engine/services/order_history.py:44) and the EMSX write at _funcs.py:190 passes no status, so every ticket that reached a broker lands as 'submitted' and is reported as zero open orders and shown under History, not Open.
findings.evidence: Live AIM {} response: cards.open_count 0; rows[0..2].status 'submitted' for all three orders; status_filter options in the seed do not include 'submitted'.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat submitted/accepted/new/pending as open in the backend count and in OPEN_STATES, or add an explicit 'submitted' bucket and offer it in status_filter.

verifier.reasoning: Code confirmed: open_count counts only status=='open' (_funcs.py ~352), and AIM.tsx OPEN_STATES (line 87-94) has no 'submitted', so submitted orders land in History. Live AIM {} call reproduced: cards.open_count 0, and ord-77 (alpaca_broker, LIMIT 190, qty 3) plus two other orders all have status 'submitted' with filled_qty null. order_history.record_order defaults status to 'submitted' and the EMSX write passes no status. Wrong open count and misfiled open orders are a real P1.

findings.title: broker_filter ignored for order-history rows
findings.detail: The broker filter is applied only to live adapter targets (_funcs.py:312); the history tail calls list_orders(limit=...) with no broker argument (_funcs.py:337), so history rows from other brokers leak into a filtered view.
findings.evidence: Live AIM {broker_filter:['alpaca_broker'], limit:1} -> rows[0].broker 'recording_broker', brokers_checked ['alpaca_broker'].
findings.proposed_fix: Pass broker_filter into list_orders (order_history.list_orders already accepts broker=) and filter history rows the same way.

findings.title: Notional card silently drops unpriced rows and mixes units
findings.detail: _notional (_funcs.py:357-364) returns 0 when price is null, so MARKET orders contribute nothing; the total then sums base/quote units across brokers. The duplicate ord-1 rows (recording_broker and rec) are both counted with no de-duplication.
findings.evidence: total_notional 570.0 equals only 3*190; the two 1-share AAPL MARKET orders are excluded without any warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Report priced vs unpriced counts separately, de-duplicate on (broker, order_id), and label the total as indicative.

findings.title: provider_mode and parallel-fan-out claim do not match code
findings.detail: The provider_mode input is never read, and the seed/methodology claim get_open_orders() is called 'in parallel' while the loop is sequential.
findings.evidence: Code read; the handler reads only broker_filter, status_filter, limit.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove or honour provider_mode; correct the methodology text or use asyncio.gather.

b2.reference_method: Professional dealer-quote ladders (Bloomberg ALLQ) show dealer bid/ask from real dealer runs or TRACE-reported trades. For a Treasury alias, a defensible indicative anchor is the market par yield for that tenor from the Treasury daily par curve, converted to price with the bond's own cash flows (a bond whose coupon equals its yield prices at 100). Spreads should be market-derived, not constants.

US10Y spread=0.18: HTTP 200, 11.1 s, sources treasury_fiscaldata, metadata data_mode live_official, summary.mid 105.7788, reference 'avg Treasury Notes coupon 3.399% on 2026-10-31 (type-average anchor, not a per-tenor yield)', rows bid/ask 105.6888/105.8688 (A). US2Y spread=0.18: identical mid 105.7788 and identical reference. US10Y with mid=99.5: mid still 105.7788 (user mid ignored). AAPL and TLT: provider_unavailable / unsupported_asset from the EQUITY compatibility guard. Treasury daily par curve (keyless CSV, latest row 11/06/2026): 2Y 4.51, 10Y 4.86. Handler formula (_stubs.py:783) at 4.86 with years=10 gives 91.7308; at 4.51 with years=2 gives 99.0192; the same formula with years=10 at 4.51 gives 95.0962, showing tenor is ignored on the fallback. findings.title: Bond mid anchored to a historical average coupon, not a market yield
findings.detail: The FiscalData fallback reads avg_interest_rate_amt (average coupon on debt outstanding) as the yield, then prices it with a hard-coded 4% reference coupon and a 10-year duration. The Treasury par yield for 10Y on 11/06/2026 was 4.86%, which gives 91.73 under the handler's own formula and 100 for a par bond. The sidecar shows 105.78, a roughly 14-point overstatement of the headline Mid card.
findings.evidence: allq_us10y.json: summary.mid 105.7788, reference 'avg Treasury Notes coupon 3.399% on 2026-10-31'. FiscalData API returns 3.399 for that date. Treasury par CSV 11/06/2026 10 Yr = 4.86. Handler formula at 4.86 = 91.7308.
findings.proposed_fix: Anchor on the per-tenor par/market yield (the ustreasury path, see next finding) and price with exact cash flows or a par-bond identity; never use a type-average coupon as a yield.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. _treasury_anchor (_stubs.py ~L776) sets yld = avg_interest_rate_amt (average coupon on debt outstanding) and prices it as if it were a yield vs a hard-coded 4% ref and 10y duration. Live ALLQ US10Y returns mid 105.7788 with reference 'avg Treasury Notes coupon 3.399%'. FiscalData API independently returns 3.399 for Notes on 2026-10-31. The Treasury par-yield CSV (year-scoped URL, fetched by me) gives 10 Yr = 4.86 on 11/06/2026, and the handler's own formula at 4.86 yields 91.73. Wrong methodology, not a placeholder, so P1.

findings.title: Tenor ignored on the FiscalData fallback: US2Y and US10Y give the same mid
findings.detail: Both symbols map to the Treasury Notes type average and the price uses a hard-coded 10-year duration, so a 2Y bond is priced like a 10Y bond. The per-tenor branch does use tenor years (line 822), but it is never reached (see the base_url finding).

findings.evidence: allq_us2y.json and allq_us10y.json both return mid 105.7788, best_bid 105.6888, best_ask 105.8688, reference 'avg Treasury Notes coupon 3.399%'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the tenor's years (as _ustreasury_curve_anchor does) in every anchor path, and reject or warn when the anchor is not tenor-specific.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live. ALLQ US2Y and US10Y both return mid 105.7788, best_bid 105.6888, best_ask 105.8688, reference 'avg Treasury Notes coupon 3.399%'. The FiscalData fallback uses a hard-coded years=10.0 and the Notes type for both, so tenor is ignored. The per-tenor branch with tenor years is unreachable in production because of ALLQ#3.

findings.title: Per-tenor Treasury anchor never runs: configured base_url returns HTTP 404, failure swallowed silently
findings.detail: The keyless US Treasury adapter is configured with the URL form .../daily-treasury-rates.csv/all. The exact request the adapter sends returns HTTP 404. _ustreasury_curve_anchor catches the exception and returns None, so ALLQ silently falls back to the FiscalData type average. The year-scoped form returns the CSV (214 rows, latest 11/06/2026). The preferred per-tenor path is therefore dead in production, and no warning is emitted.
findings.evidence: urllib GET of .../daily-treasury-rates.csv/all?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=all -> HTTP 404. GET of .../daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all?type=... -> 200, latest row 11/06/2026 with 10 Yr 4.86, 2 Yr 4.51. Sidecar reference string shows the fallback was used.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct base_url to the year-scoped endpoint (or build the URL per year), and emit a warning when the per-tenor anchor is skipped.
findings.keyless_source: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. I fetched the configured form .../daily-treasury-rates.csv/all with the adapter's query params and got HTTP 404. The year-scoped .../csv/2026/all returns 215 lines with latest row 11/06/2026 and 10 Yr 4.86. ustreasury_adapter.py uses the same base URL default, and data_sources.yaml sets it. _ustreasury_curve_anchor catches the exception and returns None, so the live output silently uses the FiscalData type average. The only warning is the type-average note, nothing about the failed curve fetch.

findings.title: Synthetic composite quotes are stamped live_official with a fabricated quote time
findings.detail: The three dealer rows are fixed multiples of a constant spread input (default 0.18 points, about 17 bp for every tenor), constant sizes (1,000,000 / 750,000 / 500,000), and quote_time = server now. No dealer or TRACE observation exists. The metadata still says data_mode live_official and the response has no synthetic flag, so the pane's live-style badges are not honest.

Arguably P0 as fabricated quotes, but I keep the filed P1.

findings.title: ANR stamps the fetch date as the rating and target as-of date
findings.detail: yfinance recommendations_summary only gives period labels (0m, -1m, -2m, -3m). _date_from_row maps a 0m label to today, so the consensus is dated as today. The target dict is also stamped with today (lastUpdated). The header then shows AS OF <request date>, and source_details asOf claims the same date. In the AAPL run the newest dated broker row is 2026-11-04, yet last_updated, oldest_included_rating_date, price_target.lastUpdated and source_details.asOf all read 2026-11-08. This is a false freshness claim.

findings.proposed_fix: Show the provider's real as-of timestamp (or the period label, e.g. 'current month (0m)'). Derive oldest/last dates only from dated upgrades_downgrades rows. Never default a period label to the request date.

findings.title: Finnhub precedence discards yfinance targets (latent)
findings.detail: If Finnhub returns recommendations, state['target'] is taken only from Finnhub. A Finnhub response with empty targets then falls through to the synthetic spot-based range even when yfinance has real analyst targets, because the yfinance target is never merged.
findings.evidence: Code path only. Needs a Finnhub key, which was not reproduced on the sidecar.
findings.proposed_fix: Merge target fields per key: take each target statistic from the first provider that has it, and keep the source per field.

findings.title: RSI 14 uses a simple-average variant, undisclosed
findings.detail: _rsi averages gains and losses over the last 14 bars with a plain mean, not Wilder's smoothed average. The label 'RSI 14' and the help text do not say which variant is used, so the number will not match a standard RSI.
findings.evidence: Code read only; the value was not compared numerically with a Wilder RSI. Crypto BTC-USD RSI 14 = 35.2 in ANR_k1.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Wilder smoothing (or name the variant, e.g. 'RSI 14 (simple avg)') in the label and methodology.

findings.title: Pane defaults to AMZN and bucket thresholds disagree
findings.detail: With no symbol, the pane silently shows AMZN. Consensus label cutoff for Strong Buy is 4.2 (_consensus_label), but the crypto signal bucket uses 4.5 for Strong Buy, so the same score can be labelled differently in the two views.
findings.evidence: Code read only.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a single threshold table and show an empty state instead of defaulting to AMZN.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg-style audio/video archive: each item is a dated recording or document with its true media type. For SEC data the canonical fields are filingDate (acceptance date) and reportDate (period of report), per the SEC EDGAR submissions JSON. Archive typing must follow the document type, and transcript flags must reflect a stored transcript.

(6) The exact pane request {symbol:AAPL,query:''} gave 6 rows (route default limit 6), so the pane shows only 6 items.

findings.detail: Every SEC row is typed media_type earnings_call (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 6-K, 20-F) or conference (DEF 14A, ARS). has_transcript is set to bool(primary_doc), so every HTML filing is flagged as having a transcript. The play_url is a .htm filing, not audio or video. The pane counts these as 'With transcript / document'. The seed methodology says has_transcript is true only when a stored transcript exists.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/news/av.py:45-55 (form to media map), :324 and :338 (media_type), :347 (has_transcript = bool(primary_doc)); ui/src/functions/AV.tsx:160 (count shown)

Mislabelling filings as earnings calls is real. Downgraded to P2 because the card reads 'With transcript / document' and the field_dictionary defines has_transcript as 'transcript/document directly attached', so the count is closer to a label/semantics defect than a fabricated claim. findings.title: Default 90-day date range is never applied
findings.detail: The manifest defaults date_range to last_90d and describes the empty-input window as the last 90 days. The handler reads only symbol, query, limit and media_timeout, so the window is never applied. Results reach back more than a year.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/manifest/seeds/av_seed.py:68-74 and :97 (default); backend/showme/engine/functions/news/av.py:92 (only limit read, no date filter)

findings.title: Pane shows only 6 archive items because the route injects limit 6
findings.detail: The /api/fn route merges agent defaults including limit 6 when the caller omits it (_agent_runtime.py:288). AV pane sends only {symbol, query} and no limit, so the list is capped at 6 with no notice. The header still reads 'Archive items' and 'N items'.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:288 (limit 6 default); ui/src/functions/AV.tsx:93-98 (params without limit); backend/showme/engine/functions/news/av.py:92 (default 25 only applies when limit absent)

findings.proposed_fix: Have the AV pane send an explicit limit (for example 25 or 50), or have the manifest or route respect a function-specific default.

findings.title: BTC-USD shows global podcast episodes under an 'Audio / Video Archive - BTCUSD' header
findings.detail: When no SEC filer maps to the symbol, the handler silently returns the global podcast archive. The pane header still uses the requested symbol and shows the podcast rows as the symbol's archive. findings.title: event_date is the period of report, not the filing timestamp
findings.detail: event_date is taken from SEC reportDate (period end) and falls back to filingDate. The field dictionary and seed describe it as the filing or recording timestamp. Rows therefore show dates that differ from when the filing was made.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/news/av.py:332-334; field dictionary av.py:58 and av_seed.py field_dict
findings.evidence: 10-K accession 0000320193-26-000026: SEC reportDate 2026-09-26, filingDate 2026-11-03. AV row event_date 2026-09-26, filing_date 2026-11-03. DEF 14A row event_date 2026-02-24 is later than its filing_date 2026-01-08.
findings.proposed_fix: Use filingDate for the date column, or rename the field to period_end and show filing_date separately.

findings.title: Seed describes a media-archive backend and inputs the handler does not implement
findings.detail: The seed methodology says AV is backed by engine/services/media_archive, reads durations from asset manifests, and checks transcripts_archive. No media_archive module exists. The handler never reads transcripts_archive. Inputs media_type, has_transcript and provider_mode are declared but never read.
findings.evidence: Repository search: media_archive appears only in av_seed.py; transcripts_archive appears in av.py zero times. Filters for media_type and has_transcript have no effect on the output.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed methodology to describe the SEC EDGAR and podcast RSS sources actually used. Implement or remove the media_type and has_transcript inputs.

findings.title: Podcast media_type shows a MIME type and duplicated filing titles
findings.detail: Podcast rows set media_type to the enclosure MIME type (audio/mpeg), while the seed enumerates earnings_call, central_bank_presser, conference, podcast and interview. SEC titles repeat the form (for example 'AAPL 10-K - 10-K') because the primary doc description equals the form.
findings.evidence: AV_4 global rows: media_type audio/mpeg. AV_5 rows: titles 'AAPL 10-K - 10-K', 'AAPL 8-K - 8-K'.
findings.proposed_fix: Map MIME types to the enumerated media types, and drop the duplicate description from titles.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg-style multi-asset ticket: asset class resolved correctly (Treasury futures are rates/bond products, not equities), routing by asset class (seed: bond/commodity/derivative -> ibkr), validated enums, LIMIT requires a price, and a pre-trade notional/estimated cost line.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/BBGT x3, all submit=false, paper_mode=true. (1) MSFT SELL 7 LIMIT 425 DAY -> status preview, broker paper, broker_available false, echo exact. (2) BTC-USD BUY 0.5 MARKET IOC -> instrument BTCUSD CRYPTO, preview, price null. (3) ZN=F BUY 2 LIMIT 110.015625 GTC -> status preview BUT instrument.asset_class EQUITY.
b2.independent_check: Echo fidelity for the valid MSFT and BTC tickets matches the request field by field. Expectation for ZN=F (10Y T-note future): asset class FUTURE/BOND (rates), with routing to ibkr per the seed. Result EQUITY fails that expectation.

findings.title: Treasury futures classified as EQUITY, so live routing goes to the equity broker
findings.detail: ZN=F is resolved to EQUITY. Cause: the resolver falls through to 'return EQUITY' because ZN is absent from COMMODITY_FUTURES (server.py:113), and BOND_SYMBOLS (server.py:115) only lists US yield names. _select_broker maps EQUITY to alpaca_broker, so a live BBGT ticket for a Treasury future would be sent to the equity venue. The live branch was not exercised (submit=false rule); the routing is code-verified.
findings.evidence: Live BBGT ZN=F response: instrument.asset_class 'EQUITY', data.asset_class 'EQUITY'.
findings.proposed_fix: Map rates futures (ZN, ZB, ZF, ZT, TU with =F) to BOND or FUTURE in default_asset_class_name and extend COMMODITY/BOND tables; add a test that ZN=F routes to ibkr.

verifier.reasoning: Live sidecar BBGT/EMSX preview for ZN=F reports asset_class EQUITY (reproduced). Routing is deterministic from code: _select_broker (_funcs.py ~24-35) maps EQUITY to alpaca_broker, and BBGT/EMSX (BBGT subclasses EMSX, no asset_classes restriction) reach broker=_select_broker(...) before the live place_order call. The live submit branch was not exercised (submit=false rule), so the wrong-venue outcome is code-verified rather than observed end to end, which caps confidence at medium. Severity P1 stands since a live Treasury future would be routed to the equity adapter.

findings.title: Side, TIF and order type are not validated
findings.detail: Preview echoes arbitrary strings as a successful ticket. The handler reads side/tif/order_type raw (_funcs.py:62-65) and returns status 'preview' with no input error. Shared with EMSX/TSOX/FXGO.
findings.evidence: EMSX probe (same handler) side 'HOLD', tif 'FOO' -> status 'preview', side 'HOLD', tif 'FOO' echoed.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate side in {BUY,SELL}, tif in {DAY,GTC,IOC,FOK}, order_type in {MARKET,LIMIT} and return status input_error otherwise.

findings.title: LIMIT ticket without a price previews as valid
findings.detail: No check that a LIMIT order carries a price; the preview returns status 'preview' with price null. The seed says price is required for LIMIT.
findings.evidence: EMSX probe order_type LIMIT with no price -> status 'preview', price null (same code path BBGT uses).
findings.proposed_fix: Return status input_required with reason 'limit price required' when order_type == LIMIT and price is missing or non-positive.

findings.title: Seed-promised pre-trade notional and cost line are not emitted
findings.detail: The seed defines a Notional formula (quantity x price_or_last) and a notional card, but the preview returns no notional, reference quote, or estimated cost, so the ticket cannot show what it would commit.
findings.evidence: BBGT MSFT 7 @425 preview keys: no notional/notional_usd field; BTC-USD preview has price null and no notional.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit notional = quantity x (limit price or indicative mid) with the quote currency, and mark it indicative when no live quote is used.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg NG1 / CME Henry Hub front-month futures: last, prior settlement or prior session close, and daily % change = last / prior close - 1. Spot-style Henry Hub series are published by EIA (RNGWHHD) and FRED (DHHNGSP). The seed is supposed to describe a benchmark gasoline (RBOB/HO) futures monitor with explicit contract unit, expiry month and roll context.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/BGAS {days:365,live:true} -> 200, 0.86 s, sources yfinance_futures, symbol NG=F, last 2.998, prev 3.533, change_pct -15.14 (bgas_1.json). Same call minutes later with days:20 -> prev 2.947, change_pct +1.73 (bgas_recheck.json). {contract:RB=F} -> RBOB rows with unit USD/gal (bgas_rb.json). {contract:CL=F} -> WTI rows with unit USD/bbl (bgas_cl.json). {live:false,contract:RB=F} -> NG=F model row (bgas_model_rb.json). Sidecar warning in every live call: eia: EIA_API_KEY not set, so the EIA branch was not exercised live.
b2.independent_check: yfinance daily bars for NG=F: 2026-11-05 close 2.947, 2026-11-06 close 2.998, a +1.73% move. This matches the recheck and GLCO, and contradicts the -15.14% from bgas_1.json. Raw Yahoo chart meta for NG=F (range 1d) returned previousClose 3.533 with regularMarketTime 2026-10-15T20:59:57Z, so the prior close is stale. For CL=F the prev/last (90.52/90.83) matches yfinance bars.

findings.title: NG=F daily change uses a stale Yahoo previousClose
findings.detail: The quote prev comes from the chart meta previousClose with no cross-check against the daily bars the same backend already fetches. On one call NG=F showed prev 3.533 and change -15.14%, while the bars show +1.73%. Intermittent: the next call returned prev 2.947. Shared quote path, so BOIL, NGAS and GLCO inherit the same risk.
findings.evidence: bgas_1.json rows[0]: last 2.998, prev 3.533, change_pct -15.14293801302009. bgas_recheck.json: prev 2.947, change_pct 1.7305734645402193. yfinance NG=F 2026-11-05 close 2.947, 2026-11-06 close 2.998. Raw Yahoo NG=F chart meta regularMarketTime 1792097997 = 2026-10-15T20:59:57Z (stale).
findings.proposed_fix: Derive prev from the last completed daily bar before the current session, or reject a previousClose whose meta timestamp is older than the last bar, and flag a mismatch in warnings instead of showing a change.

verifier.reasoning: Code defect is real: yfinance_adapter.py:280 takes close_prev from chart meta previousClose with no cross-check against the daily bars, and the fast_info path (:260) does the same. The reported -15.14% instance was NOT reproduced: three live NG=F calls today (bgas_1.json, bgas_rb/cl runs, ngas_1.json, glco_all.json) all show prev 2.947, equal to the 2026-11-05 bar close, and change +1.73%. Raw Yahoo chart meta for NG=F gives regularMarketTime 2026-11-06T21:59:58Z (fresh). The stale-prev episode is intermittent and I could not verify it, so it is downgraded from P1 to P2 (stale-data risk, unverified instance).

findings.title: as_of is the fetch time, not the quote time
findings.detail: The Quote timestamp is utcnow() at fetch time, so the pane prints AS OF <today> and a live quote pill for a price that is the Friday 2026-11-06 close (the request was made on Sunday 2026-11-08). The real market timestamp (regularMarketTime) is available in the same response and is discarded.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/data_sources/equity/yfinance_adapter.py:252 and :274 (timestamp=utcnow()); backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:487-497 (as_of from quote.timestamp); ui/src/functions/commodity-spot.tsx:189 (fmtAsOf caption) and :132 and :252 (live quote pill)
findings.evidence: bgas_1.json rows[0].as_of 2026-11-08T00:06:28.471434+00:00 while the CL=F chart regularMarketTime is 1794002398 = 2026-11-06T21:59:58Z. The CL=F last bar is 2026-11-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Set as_of from regularMarketTime or the last bar timestamp, expose separate fetched_at, and show a closed-market or stale state when the quote date is not the current session.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. BGAS rows carry as_of 2026-11-08T00:22:44 (fetch time) while the price is the 2026-11-06 close. Raw Yahoo NG=F regularMarketTime is 1794002398 = 2026-11-06T21:59:58Z, which is discarded. 2026-11-08 is a Sunday. yfinance_adapter.py:274 sets timestamp=utcnow(); _funcs.py:487 takes as_of from quote.timestamp; commodity-spot.tsx:189 renders it via fmtAsOf as a live caption. False freshness claim, P1.

findings.title: BGAS identity mismatch: gasoline seed, natural-gas title, any contract served
findings.detail: The seed describes a Benchmark Gasoline Futures monitor (RB/HO/BZ/CL options) but the handler and pane are Natural Gas Spot. The pane has no contract control and always titles the card Natural Gas Spot. With a workspace symbol of RB=F the header reads Natural Gas Spot - RB=F over RBOB rows, and with CL=F it reads Natural Gas Spot over WTI rows.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/manifest/seeds/bgas_seed.py:44 (name Benchmark Gasoline Futures) and :46 (intent); backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:653 (name Natural Gas Spot) and :665 (non-NG symbols accepted from COMMODITY_CONTRACTS); ui/src/functions/BGAS.tsx (title Natural Gas Spot); ui/src/functions/commodity-spot.tsx:235 (header title).

findings.proposed_fix: Pick one identity. Either make BGAS a gasoline benchmark (seed, handler and title agree) or restrict BGAS to NG=F, and make the pane title come from the returned row name, not a hardcoded string.

BGAS with contract=RB=F returns status ok, symbol RB=F, name 'RBOB Gasoline', unit USD/gal, and with contract=CL=F returns 'WTI Crude Oil' rows, all under the hard-coded BGAS title. The title comes from BGAS.tsx ('Natural Gas Spot', passed to CommoditySpotPane) and _funcs.py:653 (name 'Natural Gas Spot'). The seed bgas_seed.py:44 is named 'Benchmark Gasoline Futures' with a RBOB/heating-oil intent. Identity mismatch confirmed. Labelled P1, not P0, because the symbol and unit on the rows are correct.

findings.title: EIA branch ignores the requested contract
findings.detail: When the EIA adapter is configured, BGAS fetches HENRYHUB for any contract and returns it as ok with symbol HENRYHUB, so an RB=F or CL=F request gets Henry Hub spot. Not reproduced live (EIA_API_KEY is unset here), so this is filed as P2 from code reading. Escalate to P0 if EIA is configured in production.

findings.keyless_source: FRED DHHNGSP daily Henry Hub spot CSV (keyless). Fetched https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DHHNGSP: last 2026-11-03 = 2.63 USD/MMBtu (spot, not the NG=F futures print).

findings.title: Advertised inputs are not read and the output contract is incomplete
findings.detail: The manifest exposes range, interval and provider_mode, and the output contract must include contract_unit, expiry_month, candles and data_mode. The handler reads none of range, interval or provider_mode; the pane sends only days and live. Rows carry no expiry month or roll context, so a Bloomberg-style front-month contract label is missing.

No expiry_month, contract_unit or data_mode key. Top-level data keys: field_dictionary, history, methodology, rows, source_mode, status, symbol.

findings.title: live=false ignores the requested contract
