b2.reference_method: Apple LocalAuthentication: capabilities come from LAContext.canEvaluatePolicy for the biometry and device-owner policies and from biometryType. A static status string is not a capability report, and availability must be false off macOS.
b2.live_call: BIO {} -> HTTP 200 status ready. rows[0] = {action:'capabilities', status:'native_bridge_available', mechanism:'macOS LocalAuthentication via Tauri command biometric_capabilities'}. Envelope: data_state 'live', sources ['macos_local_auth_bridge'], sanitizer_summary live 1. BIO {reason:'test'} returned identical content.
b2.independent_check: Cross-checked the native bridge source. tauri/src/biometric.rs returns default capabilities (no biometry, no passcode) for non-macOS targets (lines 224-227) and run_evaluate_policy returns Ok(false) off macOS (lines 279-283). This host is win32, so a 'native_bridge_available' status cannot be true here. The handler does not query the bridge at all.

findings.title: Static 'native_bridge_available' and data_state 'live' on a non-macOS host
findings.detail: BIOFunction returns hard-coded rows that claim the macOS LocalAuthentication bridge is available. The text is the same on every platform, and the envelope marks this static document as live with a macOS source. On Windows the Tauri bridge reports no biometry and every prompt is denied, so the claim is false for this host.
findings.evidence: Live BIO {} -> status ready, row status native_bridge_available, data_state live, sources macos_local_auth_bridge; host platform win32.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the capability rows from the platform and the real bridge result (or report 'unavailable: non-macOS'), and mark static documentation as reference rather than live.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. BIOFunction (backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/_extras.py:137-177) returns hard-coded rows unconditionally: row 'capabilities' has status 'native_bridge_available' with mechanism 'macOS LocalAuthentication via Tauri command biometric_capabilities', and the methodology and sources name the macOS bridge. Nothing checks the host platform. Live call POST /api/fn/BIO returned status ready, rows[0].status native_bridge_available, data_state live, sources [macos_local_auth_bridge]. On this win32 host, tauri/src/biometric.rs:224-227 returns Capabilities::default() for non-macOS (biometry_available false), and run_evaluate_policy at :279-283 returns Ok(false), so every prompt is denied. The 'available' claim and the live label are therefore false for this host. Only the severity wording could be argued (it is static documentation rather than a computed value), but the false live/real claim fits P1 as filed.

findings.title: Seed contract (capabilities/verify fields and semantic tests) is not implemented
findings.detail: bio_seed.py promises capabilities() returning biometry_kind/biometry_available/passcode_available and verify returning allowed/via/reason, with semantic tests on those keys. The handler returns none of them and ignores the reason input. The pane does not use this endpoint (lib/biometric.ts invokes Tauri commands directly), so the UI is unaffected, but API consumers and the seed's tests are.
findings.evidence: Live BIO {reason:'test'} returned status, rows, cards, methodology and field_dictionary only; no allowed, via, biometry_kind or passcode_available keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Either route the function through the bridge (capabilities and a non-prompting status) or retire the seed contract.

findings.title: Pane copy says biometry needs the desktop app, though it is macOS-only
findings.detail: When biometry is absent the card says 'Biometry is only available in the desktop app'. On Windows the desktop app is running, so the message is misleading; the real limit is macOS-only support.

b2.reference_method: He & Litterman (1999) Black-Litterman: prior pi = delta * Sigma * w_mkt; posterior mean pi_BL = pi + tau*Sigma*P'(P*tau*Sigma*P' + Omega)^-1 (Q - P*pi), Omega = diag(P*tau*Sigma*P') (Idzorek-lite); optimal weights (delta*Sigma)^-1 pi_BL. Cited in backend/showme/engine/services/black_litterman.py:18-20.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/BLAK {symbols:[SPY,QQQ,TLT,GLD], live:true} -> 5.8 s, status ok, sources [yfinance], return_data_state live, samples 83, market_cap_data_state approximate, market_weights 0.25 each, prior SPY 0.038334 QQQ 0.061035 TLT 0.011396 GLD 0.058161. Model mode (live false) -> return_data_state synthetic_fallback, sources [synthetic_fallback]. Mixed universe {symbols:[AAPL,SPY,QQQ], live:true} -> market_cap_data_state real, market_weights AAPL 1.0 SPY 0.0 QQQ 0.0, warnings []. View test {symbols:[SPY,QQQ,TLT,GLD], live:true, days:120, views:[{long:[QQQ], short:[TLT], expected:0.05}]} -> posterior SPY 0.03841 QQQ 0.061184 TLT 0.011365 GLD 0.058197, n_views 1.

Same recomputation with 504-day window gives SPY 0.032318, QQQ 0.048816, TLT 0.010987, GLD 0.062637, so the live call used a 120-day window. findings.title: Effective lookback is 120 days, not the declared 1Y or the 504-day default
findings.detail: The pane sends no days value. The route injects days=120 and range=3M for every routed call, and defaults.update(merged) keeps the injected value. BLAK's own default is 504 (blak.py:51) and the seed default window is 1Y (blak_seed.py:160). The envelope inputEcho shows days 120 with no UI control, so the prior and covariance are estimated from about 83 observations.
findings.evidence: LIVE call samples 83; prior SPY 0.038334 equals the 120-day recomputation, while 504-day gives 0.032318 (independent_check).
findings.proposed_fix: Give BLAK an explicit window control that is sent to the handler, default to the seeded 1Y, and show the effective window and observation count in the pane.

verifier.reasoning: Partly confirmed. Without a days param the sidecar and pane run use days=120 and return 83 return samples (inputEcho days 120, samples 83). The function default is 504 and the seed window is 1Y. The finding's mechanism is wrong on one point: passing days=504 explicitly does take effect (samples 347), so the injected value does not win over user input. BLAK also never reads the seed's 'window' input (grep for window in blak.py returns nothing), so the 1Y selector is silently ignored. Severity P1 holds for the default pane output. Evidence: BLAK_d34c1c43.json and BLAK_f3bcc25a.json in the scratch folder.

findings.title: Seed declares Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage that the code never applies
findings.detail: blak_seed.py declares prior_covariance options sample_cov, ledoit_wolf, exp_cov with default ledoit_wolf. The handler always uses the sample covariance df.cov()*252, and no shrinkage code exists in blak.py or black_litterman.py. Users are told the estimator is shrunk when it is not.
findings.evidence: grep for ledoit, shrink, exp_cov in blak.py and black_litterman.py returns no matches. Independent sample-cov recomputation matches the output exactly (independent_check).
findings.proposed_fix: Implement Ledoit-Wolf and exp_cov as declared, or change the seed default and options to sample_cov and document the estimator actually used.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. grep finds no ledoit, shrink or exp_cov anywhere in engine/functions/portfolio. BLAK never reads the prior_covariance input at all (no match in any portfolio handler), so the seed's default ledoit_wolf and its three options are dead inputs. The output is the plain sample covariance df.cov()*252, as the finding says. Users are told the estimator is shrunk when it is not, so the label is false.

findings.title: Pane exposes no views, tau, delta or market-cap inputs
findings.detail: The function usage text says 'Use Advanced only for custom views, tau, delta, or market-cap overrides', but PortfolioAnalytics has no Advanced control for BLAK. buildParams sends only symbols and live (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:994-995). findings.detail: With live false the return series is a deterministic sine template (blak.py:26-34), so the covariance, prior returns and optimal weights are not market data. findings.title: optimal_weight is renormalized and long-only clipped without disclosure
findings.detail: implied_optimal_weights clips negatives and renormalizes to sum 1 (black_litterman.py:154-181). The field dictionary calls the output a mean-variance implied weight and does not mention the renormalization. With no views the optimal weights equal the market weights exactly (round trip), so the column adds no information. For the test view the unnormalized weights sum to about 0.952.
findings.evidence: Independent unnormalized weights QQQ 0.2466, TLT 0.2296, SPY 0.2381, GLD 0.2381 (sum 0.952) vs API renormalized 0.258938 / 0.241062.
findings.proposed_fix: Document the clip and renormalization in methodology and field_dictionary, and show the unconstrained weights alongside.

findings.title: Template mode returns fabricated prices labelled as provider data
findings.detail: With live:false the handler returns a hash-generated price series (close = 50 + seed/13 + ...). Live AAPL is about 342, but the template returns 73.8 to 75.15, and pe is set equal to close in every row. The payload's own field_dictionary still says close is the 'Closing/last price from the provider', and the seed (bql_seed.py:154-162) describes it only as a local model. The routed layer injects live:true, so the template is reachable only when a caller sends live:false explicitly.
findings.evidence: bql_explicit_live_false.json: mode computed_model, sources [showme_query_model], rows[0] {close:73.8,pe:73.8,date:2026-10-30}, rows[-1] {close:75.15,pe:75.15,date:2026-11-08}; field_dictionary.close 'Closing/last price from the provider.'. Live AAPL close 2026-11-06 = 342.37 (yfinance and Yahoo chart agree).
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the synthetic price generator from the function, or return status not_configured/provider_unavailable with rows=[] when no provider data exists. Never reuse provider field descriptions for generated values. If a template is kept for tests, it must be unreachable from /api/fn.

verifier.reasoning: Template path reproduced: explicit live:false returns mode computed_model, sources showme_query_model, AAPL close 73.8 to 75.15 with pe equal to close (code bql.py:92-109 confirms the else-branch copies close into any unknown field). Live AAPL is about 342.37 (yfinance 1mo last 2026-11-06 = 342.37). Not reachable from the pane: BQL.tsx:71-76 always sends live:true, and the sidecar injects live:true when live is omitted (omitted call returned mode live). The template is only reached by explicit live:false. Mode is labelled non-live (BQL.tsx isLive gate). The real defect is the static field_dictionary (bql.py:206) calling template close 'Closing/last price from the provider'. That is a mislabel in a latent path, so P2 rather than P0/P1. findings.title: Injected limit 6 silently truncates the result to 10 rows
findings.detail: The generic agent defaults inject limit 6. _limit_rows clamps the value up to a minimum of 10 and keeps only the tail, so a one-month window returns 10 bars. The seed default is 200 and the user cannot see this.

findings.proposed_fix: Do not inherit limit from generic agent defaults for BQL, or apply the seed default when none is given. Let limit below 10 be honoured rather than silently clamped.

findings.detail: Live rows keep only the columns that exist in yfinance OHLCV (open, high, low, close, volume). Any other field, such as pe or price, is absent from the rows, and no warning is returned. The FLDS catalog advertises these fields as accepted by BQL.

Yet both calls return status ok, summary.notebook_ready true and a Notebook route row marked configured. findings.title: Notebook reported ready with no Jupyter runtime; caller flag trusted

Kernel modules are reported available and the route configured as hardcoded strings. The pane therefore shows a ready notebook bridge when /notebook is 404. The seed's own methodology says it must not claim execution readiness, and its test bquant_jupyter_hint_marks_ready encodes the flag trust.
findings.file_line: C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/engine/functions/api/bquant.py:20-22 (paths and configured), 26 (route configured, hardcoded), 32 (kernel modules available, hardcoded), 47,55 (status ok, notebook_ready); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/ui/src/functions/BQUANT.tsx:65 (configured = status ok), 190 and 200 (ready labels); C:/Users/Kullanıcı/showme/backend/showme/manifest/seeds/bquant_seed.py:126-143,162-166

findings.proposed_fix: Probe the notebook URL (or a kernel) with a short timeout before reporting ok. Derive kernel-module availability by importing the modules. Ignore the caller's jupyter_running flag unless the probe agrees. Report ok only when the probe succeeds.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced. BQUANT returns status ok and notebook_ready true with no arguments, and also with jupyter_running true. GET http://127.0.0.1:56676/notebook returns HTTP 404. The two windows do not cover the middle years, so the timeline has holes. Splits are added once from the splits series and again from actions rows, which double-counts 2000-06-21 and 2005-02-28. The final rows[:80] cap then drops older rows. The Splits KPI in the pane shows 6 instead of 5.

b2.reference_method: Screening and custom-field formula engines parse the whole expression and reject leftover tokens or unbalanced parentheses. A missing input is reported as unknown or missing, not as a false match.
b2.live_call: CDE add {name:'audit_trail', formula:'pe < 25 foo > 3'} -> HTTP 200 status ready, row stored verbatim. CDE evaluate {name:'audit_trail', row:{pe:30,foo:5}} -> status ready (boolean not captured in this log; offline replica gives False). CDE add {name:'audit_tech', formula:'sector = "Technology" AND marketCap > 50000000000'} -> ready, count 2. CDE evaluate audit_tech with row {sector:'Technology'} (marketCap absent) -> status ready (offline replica gives False, no warning). CDE remove audit_trail and audit_tech -> status ready each; store back to example rows, count 0.
b2.independent_check: Offline replica with the same module (eqs.parse_dsl and eqs._eval, run from the backend venv with -I, no sidecar state touched): parse_dsl('pe < 25 foo > 3') returns Cond(pe < 25), so the trailing clause is dropped; _eval gives True for {pe:20} and False for {pe:30,foo:5}. The formula the user typed (pe < 25 AND foo > 3) gives False for {pe:20} because foo is missing. parse_dsl('pe < 25 AND (beta < 1.2') returns And(pe<25, beta<1.2) with no error.

findings.title: Trailing tokens and unbalanced parentheses are silently dropped, so stored formulas evaluate a different expression
findings.detail: parse_dsl discards the parser position and returns only the first node, so anything after a complete comparison is ignored. The optional closing parenthesis is also not required. Add accepts such formulas as ready, and evaluate returns a boolean for the truncated expression.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/eqs.py:180-181 (parse_dsl returns [0] and discards pos), eqs.py:101-107 (RP optional); backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/cde.py:46-65 (add validates only via parse_dsl)
findings.evidence: Live add 'pe < 25 foo > 3' -> status ready. Offline: parse_dsl('pe < 25 foo > 3') -> Cond(pe<25); eval {pe:20} -> True, which is not the formula the user wrote. parse_dsl('pe < 25 AND (beta < 1.2') -> accepted.
findings.proposed_fix: In parse_dsl require pos == len(tokens) and balanced parentheses, and raise ValueError on leftovers. The same fix benefits EQS.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. parse_dsl (backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/eqs.py:180-181) returns only [0] of _parse and discards the position, so trailing tokens are ignored. _parse_primary (eqs.py:101-106) makes the closing RP optional. Offline with the backend venv: parse_dsl('pe < 25 foo > 3') returns Cond(pe<25) only, and eval {pe:20, foo:0} gives True, even though pe=30 gives False and the formula the user wrote is different. parse_dsl('pe < 25 AND (beta < 1.2') is accepted as And(pe<25, beta<1.2). Live via sidecar: CDE add with 'pe < 25 foo > 3' returned status ready, and add with the unbalanced formula also returned ready. Evaluate with pe=20 returned value True. Test fields were removed afterwards and the store was restored to its original two example rows. CDE add validates only through parse_dsl (cde.py:55-63), so the bad formula is stored as valid. This is a silently different expression, which fits P1 (wrong calculation). Note the same parser also serves EQS, so the screener shares the defect.

findings.title: Unreadable cde_fields.json is silently replaced by the next add
findings.detail: _load swallows every exception and returns {}. The next add writes a file holding only the new field, so the previous store is lost with status ready and no warning.
findings.evidence: Offline test on a scratch copy holding '{"keep_me": "pe < 25", ' : after one add the file contained only {new_field: 'pe < 20'}; the call returned status ready, no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Return a load-error status and refuse writes, or move the corrupt file aside before writing.

findings.title: Missing fields and unreadable row JSON evaluate to a silent false
findings.detail: A missing field makes the comparison false, including for != (so a missing field never matches a != test either). Invalid row JSON becomes {} with no error, so an evaluation on an empty row reads as a normal negative result.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/eqs.py:128-133 (if v is None: return False); backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/cde.py:71, 145-153 (invalid JSON -> {}), 79-100 (evaluation returned with no warning)
findings.evidence: Offline: _eval(parse_dsl('pe != 20'), {}) -> False. Live evaluate with a row missing marketCap -> status ready, no missing-field warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Return the evaluation as unknown with the list of missing fields in warnings, and return input_error for unparseable row JSON.

findings.title: remove on an unknown name reports ready; NaN compares as not-equal
findings.detail: remove pops the key without checking whether it existed. Separately, a NaN row value makes != true (eqs._eval has no NaN guard). JSON from the pane cannot carry NaN, so this only matters for direct API callers.
findings.evidence: Offline: _eval(parse_dsl('pe != 20'), {'pe': float('nan')}) -> True. Live remove of an absent name returns status ready.
findings.proposed_fix: Return not_found for unknown names; treat NaN as missing in _eval.

findings.detail: fetch_quote_snapshot uses Yahoo chart range=5d and takes meta.chartPreviousClose, which is the close of the first bar in the 5-day window, not the prior session close. Every CSRC row's change_pct, and the CHG% sort, is therefore a multi-session move. Verified for CL=F: ShowMe change -5.84% vs true 1-day +0.34%; BZ=F -6.16% vs true +0.03%; GC=F prev 3969.6 vs true prior close 4113.5; HE=F -7.99% vs true -2.9%.

Code: quotes.py 541-546 takes meta.previousClose or chartPreviousClose from range=5d, and the value equals the first bar, not the prior session. The CHG% sort and the pane label 'day change' are therefore wrong. Wrong calculation with a false label is P1.

findings.title: FCFE cash flows discounted at WACC
findings.detail: The DCF labels yfinance freeCashflow as FCFE (levered, after debt) but discounts it at the enterprise WACC and treats the result as equity value. FCFE should use cost of equity, or the model should be FCFF with a net-debt bridge.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/dcf.py:120-134 (wacc), :147 (freeCashflow as fcfe), :170-177 (discounting, 'FCFE basis' comment); used by dcfs.py:41-47
findings.evidence: AAPL base WACC 0.099407 applied to FCFE 105,658,376,192 (= yfinance freeCashflow). Discount rate is WACC, not cost of equity. Not quantified against a cost-of-equity run.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a cost-of-equity discount rate for FCFE (rf + beta x ERP), or use FCFF discounted at WACC and subtract net debt (yfinance totalDebt 94.48B and totalCash 56.72B for AAPL).

verifier.reasoning: Code confirms the methodology mismatch. dcf.py:147 takes yfinance freeCashflow as the FCFE input, dcf.py:170-177 discounts it at the WACC, and the comment and methodology text say FCFE basis. Textbook FCFE is discounted at cost of equity. Quantified on AAPL with the live WACC call (wacc 0.10391, re_capm 0.10571, FCFE 105.66B, same growth inputs): equity value at WACC is 1725.1B and at Ke is 1685.6B, a 2.3% gap. The gap is small for AAPL because leverage is about 2%, so the effect grows for levered names. The error itself is real.

findings.title: Sensitivity grid ignores user inputs and is not centred on WACC
findings.detail: The manifest exposes discount_rate, terminal_growth and grid_width as inputs. The handler ignores them; the route injects a fixed 3x2 grid (7/9/11% x 2/3%), so the base WACC (9.94%) never appears in the heatmap. The pane has no grid controls.

findings.proposed_fix: Centre the grid on the effective WACC and terminal growth (+/-50bp, width from grid_width) and read discount_rate/terminal_growth; remove the route override of wacc_range/g_range.

b2.reference_method: Gordon growth single-stage DDM: P0 = D1/(r-g), where D1 is the next expected dividend (forward annual rate, or last declared dividends x (1+g)). Sensitivity grids should recompute D1 for each g. Non-dividend payers are flagged not applicable.

(2) {symbol:MSFT, discount_rate:0.12, growth_rate:0.03}: required_return 0.08 used, FV 80.75 (discount_rate ignored). (3) {symbol:AMZN, required_return:0.09, growth_rate:0.03}: status ok, fair_value 0.0, warning 'not applicable for non-dividend payers'. But the D0 choice is wrong. yfinance dividendRate (forward) = 3.92, trailingAnnualDividendRate = 3.71, and the last four cash dividends (2025-11-20 to 2026-08-20, each 0.91) sum to 3.64. With D0 = 3.64, D1 = 3.7492 and FV = 62.49, so the handler overstates by 7.7%. Surface check: r=9%/g=4% handler 80.752 vs consistent 81.536 (-0.96%); r=9%/g=2% handler 57.680 vs 57.120 (+0.98%). check_passed false.

findings.title: D0 taken from forward dividendRate, then grown again
findings.detail: The handler prefers yfinance dividendRate (forward, indicated annual) and labels it 'Dividend TTM'. It then multiplies by (1+g) again, so D1 double-counts one year of growth.
findings.evidence: MSFT: dividendRate 3.92 (= 4 x 0.98, not yet paid), trailingAnnualDividendRate 3.71, last four payments 3.64. Handler D0 3.92, D1 4.0376, FV 67.29. Trailing-based FV 62.49 (+7.7% overstatement).
findings.proposed_fix: Use the trailing 12m sum of ex-dividend payments (or trailingAnnualDividendRate) for D0; keep dividendRate only as a labelled forward cross-check.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. DDM MSFT returned dividend_ttm 3.92, next_dividend 4.0376 (D1 = D0*(1+g)), and FV 80.752. dcf.py:43 prefers yfinance dividendRate, and the DDM row at :71 labels it 'Dividend TTM'. yfinance confirms dividendRate 3.92 (forward indicated) versus trailingAnnualDividendRate 3.71. The last four actual payments were 0.91 each, totalling 3.64. Using a forward annual rate as D0 and then growing it again double-counts one year of growth. The label is also wrong. The overstatement of D0 versus trailing is 3.92/3.64, about 7.7%.

findings.title: Sensitivity surface holds D1 fixed across growth columns
findings.detail: Each surface cell divides the base-case D1 (computed at base g) by (r - grid_g), so the growth axis is not a true Gordon sensitivity.
findings.evidence: MSFT r=9%: g=4% cell 80.752 (consistent 81.536, -0.96%); g=2% cell 57.680 (consistent 57.120, +0.98%). Same error in every row.
findings.proposed_fix: Recompute D1 = D0*(1+grow) inside the surface loop before dividing.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. The MSFT surface at r=8% gives g=4% = 100.94 and g=2% = 67.29. Both use the base D1 = 4.0376 divided by (r - grid_g), so D1 is held fixed. A consistent Gordon value at g=4% is 3.92*1.04/(0.08-0.04) = 101.92, which is about 1% off the surface cell. Code at dcf.py:78-86 confirms the mechanism. Only the centre column is correct. The error is a real wrong calculation in the displayed sensitivity grid.

findings.title: Proxy methodology claims term frequency over recent 10-Ks; code counts all-year filing hits
findings.detail: The handler describes term-frequency counts across the company's recent 10-K filings. The code sends one EFTS query per bucket with forms=10-K and no date range, and uses hits.total.value, which is the number of matching filings. Values are all-years filing-match counts.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/esg.py:28-34 (methodology), esg.py:49-62 (terms), esg.py:115-134 (fetch, no date params), esg.py:133 (count from hits.total)
findings.evidence: EFTS direct query with entityName=AAPL gives environment 32, social 30, governance 75 (the same numbers the handler returns). Sample hits have file_date 2016-10-26 and 2017-11-03, so the window is not recent. Counts are filings containing at least one term, not term frequency.
findings.proposed_fix: Describe the signal as the number of 10-K filings containing at least one E/S/G term, add an explicit date window (e.g. last three fiscal years) if recency is claimed, or use real term counts.

verifier.reasoning: esg.py:122-127 sends only q, entityName and forms=10-K with no startdt/enddt, so the window is all years. findings.title: Total is a sum of overlapping filing counts, labelled as mentions

findings.proposed_fix: Run one OR query for the unique-filing count, or drop the total and show the three bucket counts only.

verifier.reasoning: Sidecar ESG AAPL returns totalEsg 137 = 32 + 30 + 75 (esg.py:225 sums per-bucket hit counts). Buckets are separate EFTS queries, so a filing matching several buckets is counted more than once and 137 is not a unique filing count. Rows and warnings are caveated as a proxy 'filing mentions', so this is a methodology weakness rather than a false vendor claim. field_dictionary still calls totalEsg a composite risk score, which is a minor inconsistency.

findings.title: Live SEC proxy labelled cached_snapshot
findings.detail: The proxy is fetched live from EDGAR on each call, but the payload says data_mode=cached_snapshot. The envelope says data_state=live, so the two labels contradict each other.
findings.evidence: esg_aapl.json: data.data_mode cached_snapshot, envelope data_state live, sources [sec_edgar].
findings.proposed_fix: Use data_mode=live_official (or a distinct sec_text_proxy mode) for the EFTS proxy.

findings.title: Primary Yahoo/Sustainalytics path is dead in this environment
findings.detail: The yfinance sustainability call returns nothing for AAPL, so the primary branch never yields a score. Its rows are labelled live_yfinance with data_mode delayed_reference, which the branch can never reach today.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/esg.py:154-166 (primary fetch), esg.py:109 and esg.py:181 (live_yfinance and delayed_reference labels)
findings.evidence: Direct check in this session: Ticker('AAPL').sustainability is an empty 0x0 DataFrame; quoteSummary 404 'No fundamentals data found for symbol: AAPL'. Every ESG call falls through to the EFTS proxy.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the dead branch or make it report unavailable explicitly, and stop labelling its rows live_yfinance.

findings.title: Manifest describes a different function from the handler
findings.detail: The seed says primary=internal, no vendor is wired, the default provider_mode is NOT_CONFIGURED, and no plugin returns provider_unavailable. The handler actually runs yfinance and then the EDGAR proxy, and returns status ok.
findings.evidence: esg_seed methodology text versus the live ok response for AAPL (esg_aapl.json).
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed methodology and provider chain to match the EDGAR proxy and remove the not_configured claim.

findings.title: Pane header calls the function vendor scoring
findings.detail: The pane title and doc say vendor sustainability scoring, while the default output is a SEC text proxy. The pane itself does caption proxy rows correctly, so only the header is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: ESG.tsx captions proxy rows as SEC filing-mention proxy, which is the honest behaviour.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the header to ESG (SEC text proxy when no vendor score).

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg EVTS / corporate calendar: time-sorted upcoming events from now forward, with event type, confirmed or estimated flag, and source. Dates must be real dates, and values such as EPS estimates belong in a value column.
b2.live_call: One call to POST /api/fn/EVTS {symbol:AAPL, reference:false} (pane params). Status ok, source yfinance, 50 rows, data_state live. The first row has date '3.18' and event 'earnings high'. Of 50 rows, 47 are dated before 2026-11-08. The only upcoming rows are 'earnings date' 2027-01-29 and 'ex-dividend date' 2026-11-12.
b2.independent_check: Compared against yfinance Ticker('AAPL').calendar and dividends directly. calendar['Earnings High'] = 3.18, which the handler writes into the date column as '3.18'. Dividend and ex-dividend dates (2026-08-13, 2026-11-12, dividends 0.27 on 2026-08-10) match. The check fails on the date column. Raw output: C:/Users/KULLAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e0427571f2ca10f3/3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def/scratchpad/b2/work/news-1/EVTS_1_aapl.json.

findings.title: Non-date scalars written into the date column and sorted to the top
findings.detail: _date_value falls back to str(value) for any non-date value. yfinance calendar numeric entries (Earnings High 3.18, Earnings Low 2.83, Earnings Average 2.91742, Revenue values) therefore become date strings. Because rows are sorted by string descending, the EPS value '3.18' sorts above real 2027 dates and is the first row shown.
findings.evidence: EVTS_1 first row: date '3.18', event 'earnings high', value 3.18. Independent yfinance calendar: 'Earnings High' 3.18, 'Earnings Low' 2.83, 'Earnings Average' 2.91742. Only one non-ISO date survives the 50-row cap; the other numeric rows are cut by the cap.
findings.proposed_fix: Only accept values that parse as dates into the date column. Place numeric calendar entries in the value column with an empty date, and sort on parsed datetimes.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: EVTS AAPL first row is date '3.18', event 'earnings high', value 3.18, sorted above the 2027-01-29 earnings date. evts.py:200-201 str fallback and :141 string sort confirmed. Only one non-ISO row survives the 50-row cap; the 2.83 and 2.91742 calendar rows are cut, as claimed. Evidence: .../news-1/evts_aapl.json

findings.title: Horizon, event_types, importance and symbols inputs are ignored
findings.detail: The seed declares horizon (next_6h to next_14d), event_types, importance and symbols inputs with defaults. The handler reads only reference and yfinance_timeout. The pane sends only reference, so the controls the seed describes do nothing.
findings.evidence: EVTS_1 inputEcho contains no horizon, event_types, importance or symbols. The output is the same regardless of horizon.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement the horizon filter and the other inputs, or remove them from the seed.

findings.title: Seed describes an upcoming-events ticker; handler returns mostly past dividends and actions
findings.detail: The seed promises a time-sorted forward ticker that merges ECO, CACT, EARN and central-bank events, with time_utc, countdown, importance and source_surface, sorted ascending. The handler returns only yfinance calendar, earnings_dates, actions, and the last 12 dividends and splits, newest first, with none of the seed fields.
findings.evidence: EVTS_1: 47 of 50 rows dated before 2026-11-08, for example dividend 2024-02-09. No time_utc, countdown, importance, event_type or source_surface keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Either build the forward-looking merged feed the seed describes, or rename the function and its seed to match the yfinance corporate-events data it returns.

findings.title: Action rows duplicate dividend dates with no value
findings.detail: yfinance actions are emitted as separate rows with the same date as the dividend and a null value, which adds noise to the table.
findings.evidence: EVTS_1 rows: dividend 2026-08-10T09:30 value 0.27, then action 2026-08-10T00:00 value None.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop action rows that duplicate a dividend, or merge them.

b2.reference_method: Implementation shortfall (Perold, A.F., 1988, 'The Implementation Shortfall: Paper versus Reality', Journal of Portfolio Management): IS = (avg_fill - arrival)/arrival x 1e4 x side sign, with arrival = decision price at schedule start. VWAP = sum(P x V)/sum(V) over the window. TWAP = equal time slices over the horizon.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/EXEC {action:plan, symbol:AAPL, algo:TWAP, target_qty:1000, side:BUY, horizon_seconds:600, slices:12} -> HTTP 200, status ok, asset_class EQUITY, interval 5m, 12 rows, cards {open_parents 1, needs_close 0, avg_is_bps 27.85, worst_slippage_bps -7.2, data_mode live_exchange, execution_mode planned}. Bars 2026-11-06 20:05-21:00 UTC. Also {algo:VWAP, side:SELL} and {symbol:EURUSD, algo:TWAP} returned status ok (FX via yfinance). Probe {action:plan, symbol:AAPL, algo:MARKET} (no target_qty) -> algo TWAP, filled_qty 100.0.
b2.independent_check: Pulled AAPL 5m bars with yfinance (371 bars, 2026-11-02 09:30 to 11-06 15:55 exchange time). The last 12 bars match the sidecar timestamps and closes; (H+L+C)/3 matches interval_vwap on 11 of 11 mapped bars. IS recomputed for slice 0: (343.6000061 - 342.369995)/342.369995 x 1e4 = 35.926 bps, matching the reported 35.93, so the arithmetic is right but the arrival input is wrong (arrival = last bar close, see findings). Result: check fails on methodology.

findings.title: Simulated schedule labelled live_exchange
findings.detail: The plan path replays historical 5m bars from Friday 2026-11-06 but stamps cards.data_mode 'live_exchange' (exec.py:498). It was called on Sunday 2026-11-08 00:18 UTC and the response itself says execution_mode 'planned'. The data mode is a false live claim.
findings.evidence: Live EXEC plan response: cards.data_mode 'live_exchange', cards.execution_mode 'planned', rows ts_ms 1793995500000..1793998800000 = 2026-11-06 20:05..21:00 UTC.
findings.proposed_fix: Use data_mode 'historical_replay' (or delayed_reference) and show the bar dates in the header.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: EXEC action=plan for AAPL returns cards.data_mode 'live_exchange' hard-coded (exec.py ~498) alongside cards.execution_mode 'planned'. Rows map to bars dated 2026-11-06 20:05 to 21:00 UTC, a Friday session, while the call ran Sunday 2026-11-08 00:27 UTC. Labelling a historical-bar schedule as live_exchange is a false live claim.

findings.title: Arrival price is the end of the replay window (look-ahead)
findings.detail: When arrival_price is not supplied, arrival = last bar close (exec.py:429-430). The schedule's early slices are therefore measured against a price from the end of the window, so slice 0 shows +35.93 bps and avg_is_bps 27.85 is an artefact; the last slice is 0.0 by construction. Arrival should be the decision price at the start of the schedule.
findings.evidence: Live response: arrival_price 342.369995 == last bar close 342.3699951; slice 0 bar_close 343.6000061 -> is_bps 35.93; slice 11 is_bps 0.0. Recomputed independently: 35.926 bps.
findings.proposed_fix: Default arrival to the first bar's open or close of the schedule window, or require arrival_price for plan mode.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance 5m bars (already used by this handler) provide the first-bar reference; verified 371 bars returned for AAPL.

verifier.reasoning: Code: when arrival_price is None, arrival = ref_price = last bar close (exec.py ~429-430). Reproduced: arrival_price 342.369995 equals the last bar close; slice 0 bar_close 343.60 gives is_bps 35.93, and the last slice is 0.0 by construction. avg_is_bps 27.85 is therefore measured against an end-of-window price, a methodology error.

findings.title: horizon_seconds is not honoured; slices are mapped to 55 minutes of bars
findings.detail: Twelve slices are placed on the last twelve consecutive 5-minute bars (exec.py:119 window = bars[-n:]), so the schedule spans 55 minutes while the offsets and the requested horizon are 600 seconds (0-550 s). The pace curve therefore does not correspond to the stated horizon.
findings.evidence: Live response: ts span (last - first) = 55.0 minutes; offset_s 0..550 for a 600 s horizon; slice spacing 300000 ms per slice.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick bars whose timestamps fall inside [start, start + horizon] or set the bar interval to horizon/slices.

verifier.reasoning: Code: window = bars[-n:] (exec.py ~119) places 12 slices on 12 consecutive 5-minute bars. Reproduced: offset_s runs 0 to 550 for a 600 s horizon, but ts_ms spans 2026-11-06 20:05 to 21:00 UTC, a 55.0-minute span, with slices 300000 ms apart. The pace and time profile do not match the requested horizon.

findings.title: Open-parent and needs-close cards are hard-coded
findings.detail: The plan path always reports open_parents 1 and needs_close 0 regardless of exec_monitor contents, because the plan path never reads the store. The card claims a live parent exists.
findings.evidence: Live plan response: cards.open_parents 1, needs_close 0, while orders[0].status 'planned' and no parent_id was supplied.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute open_parents from exec_monitor.list_parents, or omit the card on plan responses.

verifier.reasoning: Code: the plan-path cards hard-code open_parents 1 and needs_close 0 (exec.py ~494-495) and the plan path never reads the monitor store. Reproduced: plan response shows open_parents 1, needs_close 0, orders[0].status 'planned' and no parent_id supplied. The card asserts a live parent that does not exist.

findings.title: Interval VWAP is typical price, not volume-weighted
findings.detail: _bar_interval_vwap returns (H+L+C)/3 and ignores volume (exec.py:97-104), but the field dictionary and methodology say 'weighted by bar volume'. The label overstates the method.
findings.evidence: Recomputed (H+L+C)/3 matched interval_vwap on 11 of 11 mapped AAPL bars (yfinance 5m).
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to 'typical price' or compute a true VWAP from tick or sub-bar volume.

findings.title: Missing target_qty silently defaults to 100
findings.detail: target_qty falls back to 100.0 when absent (exec.py:337), so a plan with no quantity still shows a full 100-unit fill with no warning.
findings.evidence: Live probe {action:plan, symbol:AAPL, algo:MARKET} with no target_qty -> filled_qty 100.0 and pace 100%.
findings.proposed_fix: Return input_required when target_qty is missing or non-positive.

findings.title: ARRIVAL, MARKET and POV algo choices are ignored
findings.detail: ARRIVAL and MARKET fall through to the TWAP default (exec.py:185-187), and POV is scheduled as VWAP (exec.py:161). The seed offers all of them, so the user's choice is silently replaced.
findings.evidence: Live probe algo MARKET -> resolved algo 'TWAP'; the seed options list ARRIVAL, MARKET, POV.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement or reject the unsupported algos rather than silently substituting them.

findings.title: pace_pct is scheduled quantity, not filled quantity
findings.detail: pace_pct = cumulative scheduled qty / target (exec.py:148), while the seed defines pace as filled / scheduled. In a plan, filled_qty equals target by construction (exec.py:442), so 100% is shown as executed.
findings.evidence: Live plan rows: pace_pct rises 8.33 .. 100.0; orders[0].filled_qty 1000.0 with status 'planned'.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to schedule_pct for plans and reserve pace_pct for filled/scheduled in monitor mode.

b2.reference_method: SEC Form 4 transaction codes: P = open-market purchase, S = open-market sale, A = grant/award, M = option exercise/conversion, X = exercise of in-the-money or at-the-money derivative, F = tax withholding disposition, G = gift, D = disposition to issuer. Net insider flow counts only P and S as market buys and sells.
b2.live_call: Three calls plus SEC-only probe. (1) POST FORM4 {symbol:AAPL, months:6}: HTTP 200 in about 1 s, status ok, data_mode delayed_reference, sources [yfinance, sec_edgar], 40 rows dated 2026-04-01 to 2026-11-03, net_shares 0.0, net_notional 0.0, buyer_count and seller_count null, by_month from 6 SEC filings. (2) POST FORM4 {symbol:AAPL, months:6, transaction_types:[buy]}: same 40 rows. (3) SEC-only path (yfinance disabled, real SECEdgarAdapter, probe): 31 rows, status ok, data_mode live_official, filer null, shares null, transaction 'Form 4 filing document'.
b2.independent_check: Direction logic probed directly: 'Sale at price 230.00 - 232.00 per share.' -> direction 0 (a sale is neutral), 'Stock Award(Grant)' -> +1 (a grant counted as buying), SEC code X -> -1 (sell), code A -> +1 (buy), code M -> 0. One 10,000-share sale row gives net_shares 0 and seller_count null. The 40 yfinance rows have blank transaction and transaction_type, yet the summary reports net_shares 0.0 as a computed value. Filing URL checked: https://data.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126042149/xslF345X06/form4.xml returns 404 while the same path on www.sec.gov returns 200 text/html. check_passed false.

findings.title: Net flow reports 0.0 when no transaction direction was parsed
findings.detail: has_shares is set true for any row with a share count, even when the direction is 0 (neutral or unknown). The summary then emits net_shares 0.0 and net_notional 0.0 as if they were computed net flows. For AAPL all 40 rows have no direction.
findings.evidence: form4_aapl_6m.json: net_shares 0.0, net_notional 0.0, buyer_count null, seller_count null, with every row transaction_type ''.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit null for net_shares and net_notional unless at least one row has a classified direction.

verifier.reasoning: form4_aapl.json has 40 rows, all transaction_type '' and transaction null, and the summary reports net_shares 0.0 and net_notional 0.0 with no buyer_count or seller_count. form4.py:332 sets has_shares for any row with a share count, whatever its direction. Root cause: the yfinance mapper reads only item 'Transaction' (form4.py:160,170), which is blank, and never reads 'Text' ('Sale at price ...'), which yfinance does provide for AAPL, MSFT and NVDA. The sale rows are therefore discarded and a zero net is presented as computed.

findings.title: yfinance sale rows are classified neutral; grant rows counted as buys
findings.detail: The description keyword lists omit sale, so 'Sale at price ...' falls to 0 and is dropped from net flow. Conversely 'award' is in the buy list, so 'Stock Award(Grant)' counts as +1, contrary to the HNT-16 comment that grants are neutral.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/form4.py:406-411 (sell keywords lack sale; award in buy keywords at form4.py:410), form4.py:408-409 (HNT-16 grant comment)
findings.evidence: Probe output: 'Sale at price 230.00 - 232.00 per share.' -> 0; 'Stock Award(Grant)' -> 1; 'Purchase at price 210.00 per share.' -> 1. Summary of one 10,000-share sale row: net_shares 0.0, seller_count null.
findings.proposed_fix: Add sale to the sell keywords; remove award and grant from the buy keywords so grants are neutral.

verifier.reasoning: Probe on _infer_direction confirms 'Sale at price 230.00 - 232.00 per share.' -> 0, 'Stock Award(Grant)' -> 1, 'Purchase at price 210.00 per share.' -> 1 (form4.py:406-411). The keyword bug is real but latent: the handler never passes the yfinance 'Text' column to the classifier, and its 'Transaction' field is blank for AAPL, MSFT and NVDA, so the live path cannot reach these keywords today. It would surface if a 'Transaction' description were populated. Net-flow impact is covered by FORM4#1.

findings.title: SEC transaction codes X and A mapped to the wrong direction
findings.detail: Code X (exercise of in-the-money derivative, an acquisition) is mapped to sell (-1). Code A (grant/award, not an open-market purchase) is mapped to buy (+1). M, the usual exercise code, is neutral. Option exercises therefore read as selling and grants as buying.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/form4.py:254 (x in sell set), form4.py:390 (a in buy set), form4.py:392 (x -> -1)
findings.evidence: Probe: _infer_direction({acquiredDisposedCode:X}) = -1; code A = +1; code M = 0; _normalize_transaction_type('x') = 'sell'.
findings.proposed_fix: Map P->buy, S->sell, D/F->disposition (not a market sale), X/M->option_exercise, A->grant (neutral), G->gift (neutral).

verifier.reasoning: Probe: _infer_direction({'acquiredDisposedCode':'X'}) = -1, code A = +1, code E = +1, code M = 0 (form4.py:254 and 390). The mapping is wrong as described, and A/E contradict the HNT-16 neutral-grant treatment. However no current source supplies raw codes: the SEC adapter does not return acquiredDisposedCode and the yfinance rows carry none, so this is latent. Adjacent: normalized transaction_type 'sell' (from 'x') maps to 0 in _form4_summary_rows, so normalized sells are also dropped; not part of this finding but same root area.

findings.title: SEC-only path returns hollow rows labelled live_official
findings.detail: With yfinance absent the SEC rows contain only filing metadata: no filer, role, shares, value, price or accession. The transaction is the default text 'Form 4 filing document' and filing_url is a relative stub, yet status is ok and data_mode is live_official. The adapter never supplies the fields the handler reads.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/form4.py:182-207 (reads reportingOwner, transactionShares, accessionNumber, acquiredDisposedCode), form4.py:103-107 (live_official), backend/showme/engine/data_sources/equity/sec_edgar_adapter.py:96-110 (keys returned: accession, filingDate, reportDate, form, primaryDocument, primaryDocDescription, size, isXBRL)
findings.evidence: SEC-only probe: 31 rows, filer None, shares None, accession None, filing_url 'xslF345X06/form4.xml', transaction 'Form 4 filing document', status ok, data_mode live_official.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse the Form 4 XML ownership document for transactions, or label these rows as metadata-only with data_mode=delayed_reference and no live claim; map accession from the adapter's accession key; build absolute URLs.

verifier.reasoning: Probe _filing_rows() on the live sidecar filings list gives filer null, shares null, accession null (handler reads accessionNumber, adapter returns accession), transaction 'Form 4 filing document', filing_url the relative stub 'xslF345X06/form4.xml'. form4.py:103-107 labels the result live_official whenever parsed_rows exist and yfin_rows is empty, and status is ok. The SEC-only path therefore presents hollow rows as live official data. Not reproducible end-to-end here because yfinance is present in the sidecar, so the evidence is the direct helper call plus code path.

findings.title: Form 4 document URLs point at data.sec.gov and return 404
findings.detail: The adapter builds Archives URLs on its base_url, which is https://data.sec.gov. That host does not serve Archives documents. The same path on www.sec.gov returns the document.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/data_sources/equity/sec_edgar_adapter.py:138-143 (url built from self.base_url, base_url at sec_edgar_adapter.py:~43 set to https://data.sec.gov)
findings.evidence: form4_aapl_6m.json filings[0].url = https://data.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126042149/xslF345X06/form4.xml -> HTTP 404. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126042149/xslF345X06/form4.xml -> HTTP 200 text/html.
findings.proposed_fix: Build Archives URLs on https://www.sec.gov, keeping data.sec.gov for JSON APIs only.

verifier.reasoning: Sidecar form4 filings[0].url is https://data.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000114036126042149/xslF345X06/form4.xml. Direct curl with a SEC User-Agent gives HTTP 404 on data.sec.gov and HTTP 200 text/html on www.sec.gov for the same path. The adapter builds Archives URLs on base_url, which is https://data.sec.gov (sec_edgar_adapter.py:43, 138-143). Every Form 4 evidence link is broken.

findings.title: months and transaction_types ignored on the primary yfinance branch
findings.detail: The filters are applied only to the SEC filings list. The yfinance insider rows, which become the returned rows, are returned unfiltered.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/form4.py:95 (filter applied to SEC rows), form4.py:101 (parsed_rows = yfin_rows, unfiltered)
findings.evidence: form4_aapl_6m.json: rows dated 2026-04-01 onward although months=6 gives a window starting about 2026-05-06. form4_aapl_buy.json with transaction_types [buy] returns the same 40 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply _filter_rows to yfin_rows before summarising, the same way as SEC rows.

findings.title: Pane pairs table rows with SEC filings by array index; monthly bars come from a different list
findings.detail: The pane links row i to filings[i].url, but rows (40, yfinance) and filings (6, SEC) are different lists, so links attach to unrelated filings. by_month is built from the SEC list, so the monthly histogram does not match the table.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/FORM4.tsx:284-288 (filings[i] pairing), backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/form4.py:96-100 and form4.py:113-116 (by_month from SEC rows)
findings.evidence: form4_aapl_6m.json: rows 40, filings 6; by_month 2026-10:5 and 2026-11:1 while the table spans April to November.
findings.proposed_fix: Join links by accession, or use one list for both the table and the histogram.

findings.title: as_of falls back to request time; months are approximated as 31 days
findings.detail: When no dated rows exist, as_of is set to the current time rather than null. The lookback window uses 31-day months, so 6 months is 186 days, not a calendar period.
findings.evidence: Code path; the summary as_of for AAPL comes from the latest row date (2026-11-03), so the fallback is not hit in the live call.
findings.proposed_fix: Return as_of null when there are no dated rows; use calendar-month arithmetic.

b2.reference_method: Fund screener: AUM (totalAssets), expense ratio, YTD total return, category, with live price and day change. Values should be current or labelled with an as-of date.
b2.live_call: FSRC {query:'aum_usd >= 0', live:true}: status ok, scanned 10, matched 10 (FSRC_all_live.json). FSRC {'category = US Large Blend AND expenseRatio <= 0.001'}: matched 3 (SPY, VOO, IVV; SPLG and RSP excluded). FSRC categories TIPS, Municipal Bond, Closed-End Fund: status empty (0 rows). findings.title: Curated AUM and YTD are stale or wrong and not labelled as reference
findings.detail: AUM and YTD columns are hard-coded reference values with no as-of date and no reference tag, presented beside live prices. They differ materially from live data: GLD AUM is about half the live figure, and GLD YTD carries the wrong sign.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/screen/_funcs.py:1290-1377 (curated rows); ui/src/functions/FSRC.tsx:245-283 (AUM and YTD% columns rendered without reference marker)
findings.evidence: FSRC_all_live.json: GLD aum 58000000000, ytd_return_pct 12.4; yfinance GLD totalAssets 131009642496, close 2025-12-31 396.31 vs 372.52 today = -6.0%. SPY aum 500000000000 vs yfinance 796865200128.

Stale and wrong numbers beside a live price with no as-of date is a false current claim, so P1 stands.

findings.title: Route injects a 10-name universe, so 58 of 68 funds are never scanned
findings.detail: The routed layer sets universe to ten symbols for FSRC when the caller does not send one. The pane does not send a universe, so every category chip only sees those ten funds. Categories with real members in the reference table return empty or partial results, and the header reports 'scanned 10' with no warning.

findings.title: Manifest describes a futures screener, served function is a fund screener
findings.detail: The manifest for FSRC describes a listed-futures screener (sector energy/metals/grains, contract month, open interest), with asset classes future and commodity. The served function is a fund/ETF screener. The B1 audit therefore checked the wrong product.
findings.evidence: GET /api/manifest/FSRC intent 'Filter the listed futures universe by sector ...'; /api/function-index name 'Fund Screener' asset_classes FUND, ETF.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite fsrc_seed.py for the fund screener and re-run B1.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed mismatch. GET /api/manifest/FSRC returns name 'Futures Screener', intent 'Filter the listed futures universe by sector...', asset_classes ['future','commodity'], with futures inputs (contract_month, open interest). /api/function-index lists FSRC as 'Fund Screener' with asset_classes FUND and ETF, and the served class is FSRCFunction (_funcs.py:113-118, docstring 'Fund Screener'). fsrc_seed.py is the futures spec. The served behaviour matches the pane (fund category chips, expense ratio). This is a catalog/manifest description error that misleads the registry and the B1 audit, but it does not itself show wrong numbers, so P2 rather than P1.

b2.reference_method: Dealer gamma exposure per strike: BSM gamma from each listed option's own IV, S^2 x 100 x 0.01 dollar scaling, dealer sign convention (short calls, long puts). Call and put walls are the strikes with the largest absolute call-side and put-side gamma, not the largest net. Gamma flip is the spot level where total dealer GEX changes sign, found by recomputing GEX over a spot grid with the same chain. Canonical BSM gamma formula; no page was opened, so reference_url is null.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/GEX {symbol:SPY, live_options:true, max_expiries:1} (the exact pane request; routed layer also injects live:true). status ok, spot 735.29, expiries [2026-11-09], 29 strikes 690-835, net_gex 739658393.5, call_wall 725, put_wall 750, gamma_flip null, source_mode live_chain. Also POST {symbol:SPY} (no live_options): status ok but synthetic 3-strike grid with OI 120/180/135, summary.synthetic true. POST with max_expiries 3: net 756.86M, walls unchanged 725/750, flip null, 31 strikes. Artifacts under C:\Users\KULLAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\e0427571f2ca10f3\3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def\scratchpad\b2\work\derivative\ (gex_pane_spy.json, gex_default_spy.json, gex_spy_3exp.json, gex_flip.py).
b2.independent_check: Recomputed SPY 2026-11-09 chain from yfinance with the same BSM gamma and dollar scaling. Net GEX 739,659,825 vs engine 739,658,394 (match to 0.0002 percent); call total -145.47M and put total +885.13M match. Engine walls do NOT match the documented definition: call_wall 725 is the put-side maximum (put-only |GEX| 440.1M at 725; call-only maximum |GEX| is at 740, -63.9M). Spot-grid gamma flip is 758.08 (net +739.7M at S, +228.7M at 1.02S, -539.6M at 1.05S); engine returns null. check_passed false because the walls and the flip (headline KPIs) fail, although the per-strike arithmetic reproduces.

findings.title: Call and put walls are net-GEX extrema, not call/put walls
findings.detail: gamma_exposure.py:139-140 takes max and min of the per-strike NET GEX (call and put summed at each strike). The result is then labeled call_wall (largest positive net) and put_wall (largest negative net). On SPY 2026-11-09 the 'Call Wall' 725 is put-dominated (put GEX 440.1M, call GEX -0.0M to small) and the 'Put Wall' 750 is call-dominated (net -19.9M). The seed methodology (gex_seed.py:224-226) defines walls as the strikes with the largest absolute call gamma and largest absolute put gamma, which would give 740 (call, -63.9M) and 725 (put, +440.1M). The pane shows the handler's values as Call Wall and Put Wall (GEX.tsx:477).
findings.evidence: gex_pane_spy.json summary: call_wall 725.0, put_wall 750.0. Recalc: put-only max |GEX| at 725 = 440,106,845; call-only max |GEX| at 740 = -63,940,932; net at 750 = -19,866,378 (call-dominated).
findings.proposed_fix: Compute call_wall = argmax |call GEX| and put_wall = argmax |put GEX| separately (or argmax of absolute OI-weighted gamma per side), and align the field dictionary (gex.py:50-54) and manifest text with that definition.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced on the live sidecar with spot 735.29 (call the GEX function with spot=735.29, live_options=true): summary call_wall=725 (net +439.6M) and put_wall=750 (net -19.9M). Recomputed per side from the raw yfinance SPY 2026-11-09 chain (gex_recalc.py in scratchpad/b2/work/derivative): at 725 the put GEX is +440.1M and the call GEX is -0.55M, so the strike labelled Call Wall is put-dominated. The largest absolute call GEX is at 740 (-63.9M) and the largest absolute put GEX is at 725 (+440.1M). gex.py:139-140 takes max/min of net per-strike GEX, and the UI labels it 'Call wall' (GEX.tsx:617). The code matches its own docstring (net-based), so the defect is methodological mislabelling against the standard per-side definition rather than a coding slip. Totals check out: call -145.5M, put +885.1M, net +739.7M.

findings.title: Gamma flip reported as null while standard zero-crossing exists at 758
findings.detail: gamma_exposure.py:127-137 finds the flip by accumulating GEX from the lowest strike upward and testing for a sign change. For SPY the cumulative total never changes sign (690 onward is all positive), so flip is null and the caption reads 'no sign change in range' (GEX.tsx:524). The standard flip is the spot level where total dealer GEX changes sign, obtained by re-evaluating GEX at hypothetical spots with the same chain. Recomputing net GEX on a 90-110 percent spot grid with the same chain gives a single zero crossing at 758.08, inside the displayed strike range (690-835).
findings.evidence: Engine: summary.gamma_flip null (gex_pane_spy.json, also the 3-expiry variant). Independent spot-grid recompute (gex_flip.py): net GEX 568.8M at 0.95S, 1406.8M at 0.98S, 739.7M at S, 228.7M at 1.02S, -539.6M at 1.05S; zero crossing 758.08.
findings.proposed_fix: Report the zero crossing of total GEX recomputed across a spot grid (fixed IV and OI). Keep the strike-cumulative variant only if labeled as a secondary approximation. Change the caption so it does not say no sign change when a crossing exists in the displayed range.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: the engine returns gamma_flip=None for SPY at spot 735.29 (gex_spy_s735.json). The algorithm (gamma_exposure.py:127-137) accumulates net GEX from the lowest strike upward. The total net is +739.7M and the strikes above 750 are small and negative, so the cumulative sum never goes negative and no flip is found. The standard gamma-flip definition is the spot at which total dealer GEX changes sign. Re-evaluating GEX on a spot grid with the same chain gives a single zero crossing near 757.4 (my linear-interpolated estimate; the reviewer's 758.08 is the same crossing at a finer grid), inside the displayed strike range. The GEX.tsx:524 caption ('no sign change in range') honestly describes the cumulative method, which is why confidence is medium rather than high. The methodology gap versus the professional equivalent still stands.

findings.title: Pane scope is the nearest 1-day expiry; manifest inputs are not read by the handler
findings.detail: The pane sends max_expiries 1 (GEX.tsx:464), so the whole result is driven by 2026-11-09, one calendar day away. The manifest default is expiry_filter next_3 (gex_seed.py:150) and it also declares oi_source, iv_source, dealer_assumption, risk_free (default 0.045, gex_seed.py:152), dividend_yield (default 0.015, gex_seed.py:153), as_of, provider_mode and underlying. The handler reads none of these. Its actual defaults are rate 0.04 (gex.py:124) and q 0.0 (gex.py:125). The output does not disclose r or q. The seed also names cboe_options as primary provider (gex_seed.py:160) while the code uses yfinance only.
findings.evidence: Pane-style request returned expiries [2026-11-09] only. max_expiries 3 returned [2026-11-09, 2026-11-10, 2026-11-11] with net 756.86M. Manifest and handler defaults differ (r 0.045 vs 0.04; q 0.015 vs 0.0).
findings.proposed_fix: Either wire expiry_filter, risk_free, dividend_yield, iv_source and oi_source into the handler, or remove them from the manifest. Default the pane to a multi-expiry scope (for example next_3) or show a visible 'nearest expiry only' scope. Echo r, q and T basis in the output.

findings.title: Time-to-expiry for future expiries drops the time of day
findings.detail: For expiries after today the code uses (expiry - today).days / 365 (gamma_exposure.py:81), i.e. a whole calendar day with no close time. The same function uses a 21:00 UTC close for expiries that are today (lines ~72-80). On Sunday 2026-11-08 the 2026-11-09 expiry is therefore T = 1/365 although the Monday close is about 1.5 calendar days away from the moment of computation. Because ATM gamma scales with 1/sqrt(T), this overstates ATM gamma by about sqrt(1.5) = 1.22 (estimate from the stated times, not a measured error).
findings.evidence: gamma_exposure.py:81 'return (d - today).days / 365.0'; engine time-to-expiry for 2026-11-09 on 2026-11-08 is 1 day.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the exchange close time (16:00 ET) for every expiry date, including future ones, so T is consistent across expiries and with the same-day branch.

findings.title: Synthetic fallback returns status ok with fabricated 3-strike chain
findings.detail: When live_options is not set, gex.py:149-155 returns _model_gex, a hard-coded 3-strike ladder (strikes 0.9x/1.0x/1.1x spot with fixed OI 120/180/135 and fixed IV 0.42/0.47, gex.py:18-31). _shape_gex_payload still sets status 'ok' (gex.py:80). The synthetic flag and warning are present, but the envelope status and top-level metadata (synthetic False, data_state model) disagree with summary.synthetic true. The fallback chain path (gex.py:216-230) also injects OI 100 at 0.9x/1.0x/1.1x spot when the live chain returns no rows.
findings.evidence: POST /api/fn/GEX {symbol:SPY}: status ok, expiries ['30d'], rows at 661.76, 735.29, 808.82 with gex 53,848 / 40,093 / 58,531; summary.synthetic true; metadata.synthetic false, data_state model. Artifact gex_default_spy.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status 'reference' or 'provider_unavailable' for the synthetic model, not 'ok'. Make metadata.synthetic consistent with summary.synthetic. Return rows [] for the synthetic branch unless the caller asked for the reference grid.

findings.title: Output lacks the as-of time and contract fields the manifest requires
findings.detail: gex_seed.py must_have lists underlying, spot, as_of, strikes, data_mode, iv_source and dealer_assumption. The payload has none of as_of, iv_source or dealer_assumption (gex.py:79-105). The pane still shows a 'live chain' pill (GEX.tsx:534) on a chain whose option trades are stamped 2026-11-06 (the Friday session; checked with yfinance lastTradeDate) while the payload is produced on Sunday 2026-11-08. Nothing in the payload tells the user the snapshot age.
findings.evidence: yfinance option_chain('SPY','2026-11-09').calls lastTradeDate 2026-11-06 20:59-21:15 UTC. Engine payload keys: status, symbol, spot, expiries, rows, curve, summary, call_wall, put_wall, methodology, field_dictionary (no as_of).
findings.proposed_fix: Add as_of (chain timestamp, not request time) and iv_source, dealer_assumption to the payload. Label the mode 'delayed or last session' when the newest trade date is before the current session.
findings.keyless_source: CBOE delayed quotes JSON https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/delayed_quotes/options/SPY.json (fetched: HTTP 200, timestamp 2026-11-07 23:02:39, per-option open_interest, iv, gamma, delta)

findings.title: Seed sign convention text contradicts the handler
findings.detail: gex_seed.py methodology (around lines 218-226) and field_dict signed_gex = call_gex - put_gex (line 273) describe dealers short calls as a positive contribution. The handler and service do the opposite (call GEX negative at gamma_exposure.py:111, put GEX positive at line 121), which is the common short-call convention. The documentation is inconsistent with the numbers.
findings.evidence: SPY payload: call_gex_total -145.47M, put_gex_total +885.13M, net +739.66M, which matches the handler sign convention, not the seed formula.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the seed text and field definitions to match the implemented sign convention.

findings.detail: With the default 2 s quote timeout and 5 s screen cutoff, the softs quotes time out (empty error text) and are cancelled. The board still returns status ok, sources yfinance, and the pane does not render warnings, so the user sees 11 of 14 contracts and a softs filter with no rows.

findings.detail: Same defect as BOIL and BGAS: each row as_of is utcnow() at fetch, so the board presents a Friday close as current on a Sunday.

Raw exchange time for futures is 2026-11-06T21:59:58Z and today is Sunday. Same defect path as BGAS#2 (yfinance_adapter.py:274, _funcs.py:487).

findings.title: Open interest column is empty and contract column is a description, not a contract month
findings.detail: Every row has open_interest None and no contract_month key, so the OI column is blank. The contract column shows the description text (NYMEX Henry Hub Natural Gas front month) rather than a contract month code. The manifest table expects open_interest and contract_month.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/commodity/_funcs.py:1126-1135 (no open_interest or contract_month set); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/glco_seed.py (table_schema open_interest, contract_month)
findings.evidence: glco_all.json row keys: as_of, change, change_pct, contract, exchange, high, history, history_source, last, low, name, open, prev, sector, source, source_mode, symbol, unit, volume. open_interest values set {None} across all rows.

findings.title: Live pill and synthetic sparkline
findings.detail: The pane marks live from the hook state and the status field, without checking the backend live_* source_mode. Rows without real history get a procedural sparkline. It is labelled Illustrative and de-emphasised, but it still draws a trend shape that is not data.

findings.title: Timeout params can raise on bad input
findings.detail: quote_timeout and screen_timeout are parsed with float() without a guard, so a non-numeric value raises instead of falling back to the default.
findings.evidence: Code reading only.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap in try and fall back to the default.

b2.reference_method: World Bank WDI annual indicators NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS and GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS, each cell carrying its own observation year. The composite stress score (inflation + unemployment + 0.05*debt - growth) is an in-house proxy with no standard definition; the professional equivalent is a per-country dashboard with as-of years and a ranking over the full requested universe.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/GMM {} (pane ALL universe): HTTP 200, 6 rows. POST {top_n:14}: 14 rows. POST {countries:[US,GB,FR,DE,IT,JP,CA]} (pane G7): 6 rows. POST {countries:[EZ,CH],top_n:14}: 2 rows. Independent WB fetch for 14 countries x 4 indicators.
b2.independent_check: Fetched all 4 indicators for the 14 default economies directly from api.worldbank.org (latest non-null value per country): 56 of 56 cells match the sidecar exactly, including the observation years. Recomputed composite scores from the returned cells match to 4 dp for all 14 rows. The key output does not pass: the default ALL universe and the Fastest GDP card are computed on a silently truncated 6-row set.

findings.title: Default ALL and G7 universes silently cut to 6 rows
findings.detail: The route layer injects limit=6 into every /api/fn call and GMM reads top_n or limit, so only the six highest-score economies are returned. ALL shows 6 of 14 economies; G7 shows 6 of 7 (JP dropped). The default Fastest GDP card reads Turkey 3.6% although India (7.57% GDP growth, inside the same universe) is faster.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/gmm.py:94; backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:288 (limit 6 in generic defaults); ui/src/functions/GMM.tsx:80-94 (ALL sends {}, G7 sends 7 codes)
findings.evidence: POST /api/fn/GMM {} -> rowCount 6, codes TR,GB,BR,IT,US,CA; cards fastest_growth 'Turkey 3.6%'; inputEcho limit=6. POST {top_n:14} -> rowCount 14, fastest_growth 'India 7.6%', IN gdp_growth 7.5667 (matches WB). POST G7 -> rowCount 6, JP absent (JP score 4.4304).
findings.proposed_fix: GMM should not honour the route-injected limit (or the pane should send explicit top_n = universe size). Compute the summary cards on the full set before trimming.
findings.summary: Default universe truncated to 6 rows by injected limit

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed in code and live. _route_function_params (server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:288) sets limit=6 as a generic default for every routed call, and GMM.execute (engine/functions/macro/gmm.py:94) reads top_n or limit, then slices rows. Live POST {} returned rowCount 6 (TR,GB,BR,IT,US,CA) with inputEcho limit=6, and the Fastest GDP card reads 'Turkey 3.6%'. POST {top_n:14} returned 14 rows with 'India 7.6%' (IN gdp 7.5667). A G7 countries request returned 6 rows with JP absent. The default ALL universe is 14 economies (_DEFAULT_COUNTRIES), so the cards silently describe a truncated set. Saved responses are in scratchpad/b2/work/macro-2/gmm_all.json, gmm_top14.json and gmm_g7.json.

findings.title: EZ silently answered with Germany; CH shown as a raw code
findings.detail: Requesting the euro-area code EZ is mapped to Germany (DE) with no warning, so the euro area is presented as Germany. Switzerland (CH) passes through with the code as its label instead of a country name, even though the manifest lists CH as a selectable option.
findings.evidence: POST {countries:[EZ,CH],top_n:14} -> rows: {country:'Germany', country_code:'DE', score 6.6859}, {country:'CH', country_code:'CH', score 4.8412}; warnings []
findings.proposed_fix: Use the World Bank euro-area aggregate (EMU) for EZ or reject it with a warning; add country names for every manifest option code.

findings.title: Composite score silently drops missing components and still ranks
findings.detail: _composite_score only adds the terms that are present, so a missing debt/GDP value contributes zero stress. FR, JP and CN have no debt value from WB and are ranked as if their debt term were zero. The methodology says a missing cell stays null, but the rank is still computed as if the cell were complete.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/macro/gmm.py:298-315 (parts.append only when present; debt term at 311-312)
findings.evidence: JP score 4.4304 = 3.1725 (CPI) + 2.451 (unemployment) - 1.1931 (growth), no debt term; CN score -0.2853 with no debt term; FR score 7.6449 with no debt term. WB returns no GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS value for these three countries.
findings.proposed_fix: Score only rows with all four components, or rescale and flag the row with components_present so the rank is not silently biased.

findings.title: Stale debt observations scored without any age penalty
findings.detail: The composite uses debt values from years long before the others: IT 1992, DE 1990, IN 2018, AU 2022. Each row shows its year, but the score treats them the same as 2024 values.
findings.evidence: POST {top_n:14}: IT debt_gdp 77.2855 (year 1992), DE debt_gdp 20.8542 (year 1990); values match WB exactly, so the staleness is real and not a parsing error.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude observations older than a set age from the composite, or show them as stale and omit them from the rank.

findings.title: Route-injected 3 s timeout overrides GMM 12 s default
findings.detail: The generic route defaults set timeout=3 for every function; GMM reads timeout with a default of 12 s. A cold World Bank response above 3 s returns the provider_unavailable card in the pane. Not reproduced on a cold cache.
findings.evidence: Observed elapsed for the four live calls: 0.92 s, 1.41 s, 1.86 s, 0.27 s. Margin against the injected 3 s cap is small.
findings.proposed_fix: Exempt GMM from the generic timeout default or raise it to the handler default.

findings.title: Seed describes a different function (FRED release surprises)
findings.detail: gmm_seed.py describes a FRED release-surprise ladder (sigma surprises, consensus, movers[], BAR_LADDER chart, a top_n default of 15). The handler and pane implement a World Bank annual stress matrix with no movers, and top_n defaults to all rows. The seed comment says the window and categories inputs were removed.
findings.evidence: Seed output_contract must_have includes movers and window; the live response has rows, cards, surface and summary, with no movers or window key.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed to match the World Bank matrix, or restore the surprise engine if that is the intended product.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg HDS style: holders ranked by shares, each with % of shares outstanding (shares / shares outstanding) and a 13F/insider split. Percent of shares outstanding must be computed on the same denominator as the holder shares.
b2.live_call: Three calls. (1) POST HDS {symbol:AAPL, live:true}: HTTP 200, status ok, sources [yfinance], 24 rows (10 institutional, 10 mutual_fund, 4 major_holder aggregates), top holder Blackrock Inc. 1,162,996,939 shares, pct_outstanding null on every row. (2) POST HDS {symbol:MSFT} with no live flag: the sidecar applied the manifest default, so the result is the live yfinance result (status ok, 24 rows). (3) POST HDS {symbol:MSFT, live:true}: same as call 2.

The handler's pct_outstanding is null for every row, so the value is available in the source and dropped. Top-holder shares match the raw feed. Probe with no providers: AAPL returns three hard-coded reference rows, MSFT returns none, and an unknown symbol with live=false returns invented placeholder rows. check_passed false.

findings.title: Placeholder holder rows returned for any symbol when live is omitted
findings.detail: With live absent the handler takes the model path and returns fixed invented holder rows (1,250,000 and 450,000 shares, 1.2% and 0.4%) for any ticker. The status is reference_holders and the source is holders_model. The manifest default (live=true) and the pane (live:true) mask this in the UI, but a direct handler call reaches it.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/hds.py:24 (handler default live=false), hds.py:94-113 (_holders_model; hds.py:106-112 hard-coded rows), hds_seed.py:80-84 (manifest default live true), ui/src/functions/HDS.tsx:65
findings.evidence: Probe: HDS live=false for symbol ZZZQ returns 'Institutional holders aggregate' 1,250,000 and 'Insider and strategic holders' 450,000, status reference_holders, sources holders_model.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status unavailable with no rows when live is not requested; never synthesise holder rows for an arbitrary symbol.

verifier.reasoning: The stated trigger is not reproduced through the sidecar: a call with no live parameter returned holders_reference (real live path), so the manifest default live=true applies. Explicit live:false reproduces the defect: hds_zzzq_livefalse.json returns fixed rows 'Institutional holders aggregate' 1,250,000 and 'Insider and strategic holders' 450,000, with pct 1.2% and 0.4%, for symbol ZZZQ, status reference_holders, sources holders_model, data_state model. I reproduced the collinearity with 3y daily returns from yfinance: correlation with SPY is IWM 0.81, VLUE 0.79, MTUM 0.83, QUAL 0.96, USMV 0.70, and regressing SPY on the other five gives R2 0.948. The pane subtitle says ETF proxies, so the user-facing label is partly honest; the P1 rests on the methodology (betas not separable). Medium confidence on severity.

findings.title: Symbols that fail are dropped silently from the portfolio legs
findings.detail: BTCUSDT is not a Yahoo ticker, so its fetch returns nothing. The pairwise join drops it, and the warning is raised only when every leg fails. The pane default universe includes BTCUSDT and displays LIVE with no warning, and the equal-weight average is then computed over the surviving legs only.
findings.evidence: m1 (with BTCUSDT) and m6 (without) return the same alpha 0.05913268093983419, R2 0.4302235385954607, samples 750, metadata live true, warnings []. yfinance returned 'Quote not found for symbol: BTCUSDT'.
findings.proposed_fix: Warn and list the dropped legs (same as the factor-proxy check), and mark the result as partial when any requested symbol has no series.

findings.title: Routed defaults cut the factor and symbol fetch budget to 3 seconds, so the same request flips between live and labelled-template output
findings.detail: Every routed /api/fn call merges agent defaults that set quote_timeout 3. MARS uses quote_timeout (default 8) as the per-symbol budget, so ordinary yfinance latency drops factors and the function silently falls back to the template regression. Identical requests m2 and m6 returned different provenance.
findings.evidence: m2 vs m6 identical request: m2 provider_unavailable, factor_proxies_loaded [], samples 483, R2 0.0157; m6 live, six proxies, samples 750, R2 0.4302.
findings.proposed_fix: Give portfolio analytics their own timeout budget (at least 8 s) and do not inherit the generic 3 s routing default.

findings.title: Reference mode reports a degenerate regression as a result (R2 = 1.0)
findings.detail: With reference true, the portfolio is built from the same template as the factors, so the regression is exact. The output shows R2 1.0, alpha zero and equal 1/3 loadings. The metadata says modeled, but the headline R2 and VaR are presented as statistics.
findings.evidence: m5_reference: alpha_annualized 6.87e-16, r_squared 1.0, loadings MKT 0.3333 SMB 0.3333 HML 0.3333 MOM -0.0 QMJ 0.0 BAB 0.0, metadata data_mode modeled.
findings.proposed_fix: Suppress regression statistics in template mode, or return the template as a labelled placeholder with no R2.

findings.title: Manifest describes a different function (Mean-Reverting Allocation)
findings.detail: mars_seed names the function Mean-Reverting Allocation with universe, lookback, half-life, regime and weight outputs. The handler is a factor regression and returns none of the seed's must_have fields (weights, signal_scores, expected_half_life_days, gross_exposure). The registry name and seed therefore disagree with the handler and the pane.
findings.evidence: Function index name is Multi-Asset Risk with an empty description; seed name is Mean-Reverting Allocation.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the seed with the factor-regression contract, or move the mean-reversion spec to a separate code.

findings.title: Help text is empty and the live flag is unused
findings.detail: The function-index description for MARS is empty and its purpose text is generic. PortfolioAnalytics sends live for MARS, but the handler never reads live (it only reads reference), so the toggle there does nothing.
findings.evidence: Function index MARS description empty. buildParams MARS returns only symbols and live.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a description and remove or wire the live key.

b2.reference_method: Terminal-style world-events calendar (Bloomberg ECO/EVTS equivalent): scheduled releases with UTC timestamps, actual/forecast/previous, impact, a forward window that always covers the next high-impact event, and a visible audit trail of sources. Countdown = (event UTC - as_of). Central-bank decisions are spot-flagged. Headline tagging should be token-based with auditable matched terms.
