findings.detail: The FinanceCalendar 'keyless' supplement now returns 401 api_key_required. Its failure is only a warning. With no forward rows the envelope still says status=ok and data_mode=live_..., upcoming_count=0, next_high_impact=null, alerts_count=0. Independent GET of the endpoint: 401 {"error":"Create and verify a Finance Calendar account, then send your API key","code":"api_key_required"}. Only add a keyed provider if the user supplies a key.

An independent GET to https://www.financecalendar.com/wp-json/fc/v1/calendar returns 401 with code api_key_required. findings.title: Calendar rows silently dropped by shared row limit
findings.detail: Calendar rows and world headlines share one limit of 250, applied after a time-ordered merge. Older calendar rows are cut first, so high-impact central-bank decisions can disappear. The only trace is data_quality.rows_capped_at_limit, with no warning.
findings.evidence: Live default call: 169 world + 81 economic = 250 rows; ForexFactory raw has 116 events; 35 missing (all dated 2026-11-01..2026-11-03), including 4 High-impact RBA rows at 2026-11-03T03:30Z. data_quality.rows_capped_at_limit = 36. Independent comparison in scratchpad/b2/work/comm/indep_cmp.py.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply the limit per kind (or reserve a quota for economic rows) before merging, or do not truncate economic rows in favour of wire rows. Emit a warning when rows_capped_at_limit > 0 and mark the affected kind.

verifier.reasoning: The mechanism is real in code. Calendar rows (economic) and world rows are merged into one 'filtered' list before split_window, and then upcoming[:limit] and past[:limit-len(upcoming)] are applied (meet.py ~lines 355-372, default limit 250 at line 132). Past rows sort newest-first (world_events.py:959), so the oldest calendar rows are the ones cut. data_quality.rows_capped_at_limit is set, but no warning is emitted. The exact 35-row loss in the report (Nov 1-3 RBA rows) cannot be reproduced now: the live window has changed. A limit=20 call shows rows_capped_at_limit=155 with 0 economic rows and 20 world rows, which confirms the shared-cap behaviour but not the reported magnitude. Because the cap is disclosed in data_quality and the defect could not be reproduced at the reported scale, it is filed as P2, not P1.

findings.title: War/spot classifier flags non-war headlines as high-impact geopolitics alerts
findings.detail: _WAR_RE includes generic words (conflict, offensive, sanctions, military, escalation, mobilization). Any match makes the row war=True, which sets impact high, spot=True, pinned=True, event_type geopolitics. Spot rows drive alerts and toast notifications. Offline reproduction through the real world_rows(): 'Apple faces conflict of interest probe over board pay' -> impact high, spot True, pinned True, event_type geopolitics; 'Brand unveils offensive ad campaign' -> same; 'Bitcoin ETF records inflows as sanctions relief lifts sentiment' -> same. A plain 'Fed holds rates steady as Powell speaks' is medium/not spot.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/services/world_events.py:214-220 (_WAR_RE), world_rows() war -> impact high / spot war / pinned war
findings.evidence: scratchpad/b2/work/comm/regex_check.py output (offline, same code path as MEET). Methodology says 'wars are spot-flagged' but the match is keyword-level.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a conflict-specific phrase (war, invasion, airstrike, ceasefire, missile attack) and drop bare 'conflict', 'offensive', 'military', 'sanctions' from the spot rule (keep them as topic tags at most). Add a regression test with the three headlines above.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced offline through the real code path: world_events.world_rows() with backend venv python and PYTHONPATH=backend. 'Apple faces conflict of interest probe over board pay', 'Brand unveils offensive ad campaign' and 'Bitcoin ETF records inflows as sanctions relief lifts sentiment' each returned impact=high, spot=True, pinned=True, event_type=geopolitics. 'Fed holds rates steady as Powell speaks' returned medium, spot False. The cause is _WAR_RE (world_events.py:214-220) containing generic words (conflict, offensive, sanctions, military). world_rows() at lines 815-826 sets war=True on any match, which forces impact high. Spot and pinned rows then drive alerts (world_events.py ~1150). This is a false high-impact geopolitics classification with alert and toast side effects, not a correctly labelled feature. reference_url null.

findings.title: Country names are accepted by the schema but silently return zero rows
findings.detail: The input description promises 'ISO codes / currency codes / country names', but canonical_iso only resolves codes. 'Turkey' becomes the literal token 'TURKEY' and matches no row. The call returns status ok with rows 0, and the gate report treats 'TURKEY' as an ISO code.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/services/world_events.py:985 (wanted_iso = canonical_iso(c) or c.upper()), :360-373 (canonical_iso); backend/showme/engine/services/country_gates.py:364-367 (gate uses the same fallback); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/meet_seed.py countries description; ui/src/functions/MEET.tsx:164 and :373 (client uses ISO codes only)
findings.evidence: Live countries='Turkey,Australia': status ok, rows 0, filters_applied.countries ['Turkey','Australia'], country_gate_report countries [{iso:'TURKEY',past_7d:0,...},{iso:'AUSTRALIA',...}], warnings include 'gate shortfall: TURKEY past 7d has 0/20 events'. The same country by ISO code 'TR,AU' returns 149 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve names through COUNTRY_CATALOG/REGION_NAMES (the calendar normaliser already has such a lookup in meet.py _calendar_country) before filtering. Return an explicit warning or needs_data for unresolved tokens instead of status ok with 0 rows.

findings.title: Tag filter is a substring match, so 'US' matches Russia, Australia, refuses, usher
findings.detail: apply_filters tests tag.lower() in title/summary/terms as a raw substring, so short tags match inside longer words. The filter is therefore not a tag filter.
findings.evidence: Live tags='US': 28 rows; 20 contain no standalone US token. Examples: 'Latvian farmers protest over blood grain trade with Russia', 'Lebanese footballer refuses to give up after injuries from Israeli strike', 'Will this week's blue wave election usher in...', 'Flat, tired, cynical: Unusually gloomy Kiwis...', 'How do you broker UN climate talks... Australia'. Raw data in scratchpad/b2/work/comm/meet_tagus.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Match tags on normalized token boundaries (regex \b<tag>\b, case-insensitive) or on the structured asset_tags/topic_tags/matched_terms fields only.

findings.title: Intermittent 14 s function timeout with a country filter
findings.detail: One call with countries 'TR,AU' hit the 14 s function budget and returned provider_unavailable with no rows, while the gate chain (holidays + wire + Google News RSS) and the RSS/GDELT legs run in one budget. The next two calls with the same params finished in 2.0 s and 2.9 s, so the failure is cold-cache or slow-upstream dependent and not reproduced on demand.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/b2/work/comm/meet_tr.json: data.reason 'function timed out after 14s', status provider_unavailable, metadata.exception_type_original TimeoutError. Retries: meet_tr2.json 2.9 s ok, meet_tr_au2.json 2.0 s ok.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the gate chain its own bounded budget that always returns partial results (with a warning) before the 14 s function cap, and cache holiday/gate results per country.

findings.title: Pane second pass drops global calendar rows that the server keeps
findings.detail: The server bypasses the country filter for is_global (ALL) rows. The pane then re-filters rows with row.countries.some(...), which removes every global row, so the pane shows fewer rows than the server returned. Code-level only; not reproduced live (no ALL row in the sampled window).
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/MEET.tsx:373 (client second pass); backend/showme/engine/services/world_events.py apply_filters is_global bypass (~line 990-996)
findings.evidence: Static reading of both files. Server: 'is_global satırlar ülke filtresini bypass eder'. Client: 'return all.filter((row) => row.countries.some(...))' with countries [] for global rows.
findings.proposed_fix: In the pane, keep rows where details.is_global is true when countries are set, matching the server rule.

findings.title: Spot-alert lead-time docstring disagrees with code; toast can say '1h lead' for a 10-minute event
findings.detail: dueAlert returns the smallest lead already crossed. For a row 10 minutes away with leads [1440,60,5], crossed = {1440,60}, so the 60-minute lead fires and the toast reads '1h lead'. The docstring says 10 minutes out fires the 5-minute lead. The 5-minute lead only fires once the event is within 5 minutes.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/meet/helpers.ts:366-381 (dueAlert and docstring), ui/src/functions/MEET.tsx:425 (toast text uses leadLabel(item.lead))
findings.evidence: Static trace of dueAlert: seconds=600, crossed filter seconds<=lead*60 yields [60,1440], sorted asc, lead=60.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix the docstring, or fire the tightest lead that is crossed and label the toast with the actual remaining time instead of the lead label.

findings.title: Holiday rows labelled 'low' impact and stamped at UTC midnight; 'holiday' impact filter matches nothing
findings.detail: Nager.Date public holidays are normalised to importance 'low' and date T00:00:00Z. The impact filter offers 'holiday', but no returned row carries that bucket for holidays. The all-day holiday is also placed at 00:00 UTC, which is not the local day start.
findings.evidence: Live TR+AU response: nager_date rows 6 of 6 impact 'low', 0 rows with impact 'holiday'; all 6 stamped T00:00:00+00:00.
findings.proposed_fix: Map holidays to impact 'holiday' and mark all-day rows (no time) instead of a fake 00:00Z instant.

findings.title: data_mode label repeats a source; timeout envelope echoes wrong request
findings.detail: data_mode shows the same world source twice (gdelt_gal+gdelt_gal), overstating the number of live legs. The generic 14 s timeout envelope echoes requested {range:'3M', days:120}, which does not match MEET's params.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/b2/work/comm/meet_tagus.json data_mode 'live_forex_factory+rss+gdelt_gal+gdelt_gal'; meet_tr.json 'requested':{'limit':250,'range':'3M','days':120}.
findings.proposed_fix: De-duplicate sources before building data_mode; have the timeout envelope echo the MEET inputs.

b2.reference_method: Reg T initial and maintenance margin for equities (50 percent / 25 percent long); crypto spot is typically fully paid (no leverage) at margin-free venues; crypto derivatives have their own leverage. Buying power = excess equity divided by the initial rate.
b2.live_call: 4 calls to /api/fn/MGN. n1 default (no body): status ok, marked at average cost (warning 'refresh_prices=false'), AAPL last 180, equity 102,425, reg_t, BTC 0.5 at 95,000 cost, IM 51,212.5. n4 with refresh_prices true: AAPL 342.37, MSFT 530.61, NVDA 186.64, SPY 735.29, TLT 81.92, GLD 372.52 live, equity 122,260 (BTC still at cost, no live quote). n2 supplied mixed book (AAPL 50 at 180 plus BTC 0.5 at 95,000, cash 25,000): margin_type crypto_futures for the whole account, AAPL IM 900, BTC IM 4,750, total IM 5,650, buying power 758,500. n3 BTC-only supplied book: crypto_futures, IM 4,750, buying power 677,500. The sandbox margin_config.json is rewritten by calc (side effect, not repo).
b2.independent_check: Reproduced the margin arithmetic by hand: AAPL reg_t IM 4,500 (50 percent of 9,000), crypto_futures IM 10 percent, buying power = (equity - IM)/initial rate. For n2 the handler's 758,500 matches the crypto 10 percent formula. The alternative correct-rule values: BTC at crypto_spot 100 percent and AAPL at reg_t gives IM 52,000 and BP 29,500; reg_t for all gives BP 106,500. The arithmetic checks, so check_passed is true, but the margin-type selection (findings below) is wrong.

findings.title: Default book is marked at average cost and shown as live with no data-quality badge
findings.detail: The routed layer forces refresh_prices=false for MGN, so the default calc marks every position at average cost. The pane shows no PARTIAL or MODEL badge because portfolioDataMode returns live when no modeled or degraded flag is present. The only signal is a warning string. Equity is therefore understated versus live marks (102,425 vs 122,260 with live AAPL and others).
findings.file_line: backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:419-420 (MGN forces refresh_prices false); backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/mgn.py:137-138 and 149-150; ui/src/functions/PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1373-1374 (default live return)
findings.evidence: n1 metadata has no live or fallback flag and status ok, so the badge is hidden. n4 with refresh_prices true changes AAPL from 180 to 342.37 and equity from 102,425 to 122,260.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the forced refresh_prices=false for MGN, and set a degraded or marked_at_cost mode when any position is at cost so the pane shows a badge.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: MGN with defaults returns status ok, warnings 'Marked at average cost (refresh_prices=false): AAPL, BTC-USD, GLD, MSFT, NVDA, SPY, TLT.', and top-level data_state 'reference'. metadata has no live or fallback flag, and portfolioDataMode (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1311-1373) does not read data_state, so no PARTIAL or MODEL badge shows. However the pane renders response warnings (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:685-693, plus a 'warn' count at 387), so the at-cost marking is visible. Real, but the signal is present, so P2 rather than P1.

findings.title: Spot crypto is margined at 10 percent with 10x buying power because any CRYPTO position switches the whole account to crypto_futures
findings.detail: _margin_type_for_positions returns crypto_futures whenever any position is CRYPTO, and that rule applies to the whole account including equities. This gives a 10 percent initial rate and buying power of 10x excess equity for a spot holding, which the module's own crypto_spot rule (100 percent) contradicts. Equity AAPL is margined at 10 percent instead of 50 percent.
findings.evidence: n2: margin_type crypto_futures, AAPL IM 900 (should be 4,500 at reg_t), BP 758,500 on equity 81,500. n3 BTC-only: BP 677,500 on equity 72,500, IM 4,750 (crypto_spot would be 47,500).
findings.proposed_fix: Pick the margin rule per position (asset class and product type), not per account, and default spot crypto to crypto_spot.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced with supplied positions AAPL 50@180 and BTC-USD 0.5@95000: margin_type crypto_futures; AAPL initial_margin 900 (10% of 9,000) and BTC 4,750. mgn.py:190-198 maps any CRYPTO position to crypto_futures for the whole account, and mgn.py:80-83 applies that type. Equity is margined at the 10% crypto rate. The default auto-created account path differs (see MGN#3).

findings.title: Default accounts apply Reg T 50 percent to spot BTC, contradicting the module's own crypto_spot rule
findings.detail: Auto-created accounts take margin_type reg_t, and reg_t has no crypto exclusion, so spot BTC gets 50 percent initial margin. The rule table in the same file sets crypto_spot to 100 percent. The result understates the BTC margin requirement by half.
findings.evidence: n1: BTC-USD initial_margin 23,750 on market value 47,500 (50 percent). Recomputed crypto_spot 100 percent gives 47,500.
findings.proposed_fix: Map CRYPTO spot positions to crypto_spot when auto-creating the account.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced on the default call: account margin_type reg_t, BTC-USD initial_margin 23,750 on market value 47,500 (50%). margin_engine.py:233-238 auto-creates reg_t accounts, and reg_t's asset_classes are EQUITY/ETF only, yet the spot crypto gets reg_t's 50%. The module's own crypto_spot rule at margin_engine.py:39-45 is 100%, so the BTC requirement is understated by half.

findings.title: Manifest and pane claim broker-sourced margin with no client-side modeling; the handler models margin client-side
findings.detail: mgn_seed says margin is read from broker.account() and broker.position_margin() verbatim, forbids client-side haircut modeling, and lists credential_id as required. The handler computes haircuts and buying power from its own rule table, reads no broker, and returns sources margin_engine. The pane subtitle Borrow, maintenance and liquidation diagnostics overclaims because there is no borrow or liquidation output.
findings.evidence: n1/n2 sources ['portfolio_state','margin_engine'] (no broker). No credential_id input in the handler or the pane. Subtitle at PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:148.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed and subtitle to describe the modeled margin, or connect the broker source and label the modeled path.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed: MGN sources are ['portfolio_state','margin_engine'] with no broker source and no credential_id input. mgn_seed.py says margin comes from broker.account() and forbids client-side haircut modeling, while margin_engine computes haircuts from its own rule table. The pane subtitle at PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:146-148 promises borrow and liquidation diagnostics, and the output contains neither. False real-source claim.

findings.title: No cash or account input in the pane; cash defaults to zero, so buying power ignores actual cash
findings.detail: The MGN pane sends no parameters. The routed call has no cash, so equity equals market value and buying power is computed from market value alone. The user cannot enter cash or an account, although the function accepts cash for supplied books.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/mgn.py:79-86 (cash defaults to 0 for supplied books) and 92-100; backend/showme/engine/services/margin_engine.py:189-192; ui/src/functions/PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1371-1372 (MGN sends no params)
findings.evidence: n1 equity 102,425 equals market value (cash 0). No cash field in the response inputs.
findings.proposed_fix: Add cash and account inputs to the pane, and default cash from the saved account record rather than zero.

findings.title: Hard-coded multipliers and a leverage floor, plus a config write on every calc
findings.detail: Portfolio margin buying power is fixed at 4x, its maintenance is scaled by 0.6, and the buying-power divisor is floored at 0.05 (so FX at 2 percent shows 20x, not 50x). calc_all_accounts also writes runtime margin_config.json on every calculation.
findings.evidence: Code read. The writes were observed as a side effect of MGN calls in the sandbox.
findings.proposed_fix: Name and document the multipliers, remove the floor or document it, and make calc read-only.

b2.reference_method: Classifier direction accuracy on a chronological hold-out with a baseline (always-long / base rate), Sharpe from out-of-sample strategy daily returns (position at t times return from t to t+1), with confidence intervals on accuracy and a stated backend (LightGBM / gradient boosting if the seed model is used).

findings.detail: The Sharpe is computed as the mean and std of prediction times sign(forward N-bar return), with predictions made on the full sample including training rows. At horizon 5 the overlap of consecutive targets inflates the result, and the sign of a multi-bar return is not a bar return. A daily-return out-of-sample replication gives 0.79 at horizon 5 (server 6.82), and 1.56 at horizon 1 (server 0.76).

verifier.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed in ml_signals.py: target = np.sign(forward N-bar return) (make_features), Sharpe = mean/std of sig.shift(1) * target, so the 'returns' are +/-1 signs rather than bar returns. pred_full = m.predict(X) is computed over the full sample including training rows (in-sample). (2) {action:'search',query:'tim cook'} -> 200, 9.3 s, status ok, source_mode wikipedia_live, 4 items: 'Tim Cook | chief executive officer | Apple Inc. | wikidata:P108 | Q265852'; 'Tim Cook (historian) | Canadian War Museum'; 'Bernard McGuirk' (match_score 0); 'John Ternus | chief executive officer | Apple Inc. | Q106028933'. So the live role 'chief executive officer' for Cook is wrong as of 2026-11-08. Ternus's P39 has no P582, so his role is correct. Company (P108 Apple Q312 start 1998, no end) is correct. findings.title: Tim Cook shown as current CEO; Wikidata end-date ignored
findings.detail: The role is taken from the first Wikidata P39 claim without checking the P582 end-time qualifier. Tim Cook's 'CEO of Apple' claim ended 2026-08-31, but PEOP reports 'chief executive officer' as his current role on 2026-11-08. Apple's own newsroom says Ternus took the CEO role on 2026-09-01 and Cook became Executive Chairman. This is a live false current claim about a named executive.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/services/people_search.py:242-253 (_claim_qids: only skips rank 'deprecated', ignores P582/P580), people_search.py:376-381 (role = positions[0]; employers[0] at :384)
findings.evidence: Live peop_timcook.json item 1: role 'chief executive officer', company 'Apple Inc.'. Wikidata Q265852 P39 Q484876: P580 +2011-08-24, P582 +2026-08-31. Apple newsroom page (opened): Ternus effective Sept 1, 2026; Cook to become Executive Chairman.
findings.proposed_fix: Filter claims: drop any claim whose P582 end time is before now (and P582 with no value only if unqualified). Prefer claims with no end time or the latest P580. Ideally also prefer the claim with preferred rank. Add a regression test with Q265852.
findings.keyless_source: https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php (action=wbgetentities, props=claims; qualifiers P580/P582 are present, verified live)

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. POST /api/fn/PEOP with query 'Tim Cook' returns items[0] with role 'chief executive officer' and company 'Apple Inc.' (company_source wikidata:P108). The same item's summary text says Cook was CEO until 2026-08-31 and has been executive chairman since 2026-09-01, so the structured role field contradicts the item's own summary. Wikidata Q265852 (fetched with a User-Agent header) has P39 Q484876 rank normal with qualifiers P580 +2011-08-24 and P582 +2026-08-31. The code at backend/showme/engine/services/people_search.py:242-253 (_claim_qids) skips only rank 'deprecated' and ignores P582/P580. Lines 376-381 then take positions[0] as the current role, and line 384 takes employers[0] for company with no end-date check. The result is a false current-role claim about a named executive.

findings.title: Bundled fallback text is stale and served with status ok
findings.detail: When live search returns no persons, any query containing 'apple' returns three hard-coded entries labelled public_reference with status ok and no stale-data warning. Their role text is in the past or future tense for a 2026-11-08 date: Cook 'CEO through summer 2026', Ternus 'incoming CEO effective 2026-09-01' (he is CEO since 2026-09-01), Levinson 'Non-Executive Chairman' (superseded). Only source_date 2026-04-20 is shown.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/comm/peop.py:18-60 (PUBLIC_REFERENCE_PEOPLE, role strings at :21, :36, :51), peop.py:~118-132 (fallback when live ok but empty)
findings.evidence: Live peop_apple.json: source_mode public_reference, status ok, items Arthur Levinson / John Ternus / Tim Cook with the roles above, source_date 2026-04-20; query 'apple' returned these after live Wikipedia gave no persons.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove the static set or mark it expired after its source date with a visible warning ('reference data dated 2026-04-20, may be out of date'). Update role strings to the current state or drop the role field from the static rows. Return status needs_data when only the static fallback matches.

findings.title: Empty-state text hides the provider failure reason
findings.detail: On provider_unavailable the handler puts 'Add a person with action=upsert or broaden the search query.' first in next_actions. The pane uses next_actions[0] as the body of the 'No people matched' empty state, so a Wikipedia outage reads as 'no people exist, add one'. The real reason only appears in the footer status pill.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/comm/peop.py:152-161 (next_actions order; retry hint is second), ui/src/functions/PEOP.tsx:251-253 (emptyBody = payload.next_actions[0])
findings.evidence: Static: when provider_error is set, next_actions = ['Add a person with action=upsert...', 'Retry once the Wikipedia/Wikidata public API is reachable.'] and the pane shows only the first. Not triggered live (Wikipedia reachable).
findings.proposed_fix: Put the provider reason or retry hint first when status is provider_unavailable, and show payload.reason in the empty-state body.

findings.title: Empty or short query returns the whole local directory
findings.detail: PEOP calls pd.search(query) before any empty-query guard. An empty query builds LIKE '%%', which matches every row. A one-character query matches every row containing that letter. This contradicts the S10 guard and the seed's semantic test that an empty query returns zero rows. The sandbox directory is empty, so this was verified by code only.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/comm/peop.py:109 (pd.search before the empty-query path), backend/showme/engine/services/people_directory.py:119-126 (like = f'%{query}%'), backend/showme/manifest/seeds/peop_seed.py semantic test peop_empty_query_returns_no_rows_not_fabricated_apple_set
findings.evidence: Live stats: n_people 0. Live empty query: needs_data with 0 items (consistent only because the table is empty). Code path: an empty query reaches pd.search and returns every row once rows exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Return early for empty or single-character queries before the local search, the same way search_people and reference_people_search already do.

findings.title: Seed methodology claims tokenization, ranking and tag matching that the code does not perform
findings.detail: The seed says the directory 'tokenizes the query and ranks rows by tag/role/bio match' and that the query matches 'full name, role, company, tag'. The code runs one LIKE on the full raw query string over full_name, company, role and bio, orders by ingested_at, and never reads tags_json.
findings.evidence: people_directory.search: 'WHERE full_name LIKE ? OR company LIKE ? OR role LIKE ? OR bio LIKE ? ORDER BY ingested_at DESC' with the whole query as one pattern. Static reading.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement token AND matching with tag search and relevance ranking, or correct the seed text to describe the single-substring behaviour.

findings.title: Live results silently capped at 8 people; low-relevance noise included
findings.detail: search_people caps Wikipedia candidates at MAX_CANDIDATES=8 regardless of the caller's limit (default 25), so 'Matches' can never exceed 8 and nothing says so. Unrelated rows with match_score 0 are kept (e.g. 'Bernard McGuirk' for query 'tim cook').
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/services/people_search.py:58 and :429 (cap = min(max(limit,5),8)); people_search.py:~390-405 (match_score computed, not used as a filter)
findings.evidence: Live 'tim cook': 4 items, one with match_score 0. Code cap: min(max(25,5),8)=8.
findings.proposed_fix: Disclose the candidate cap in the response (e.g. candidates_scanned), and drop match_score 0 rows when the query has tokens.

findings.title: Company taken from a summary sentence when Wikidata has no employer
findings.detail: For Jensen Huang, Wikidata has no P108 claim, so company 'Nvidia' comes from a regex on 'founder of ...' in the Wikipedia summary (company_source 'summary_pattern'). It is labelled, but a 'founder of X' phrase can name a former or non-employer organisation and the UI presents it as the employer.
findings.evidence: Live jensen huang item: company 'Nvidia', company_source 'summary_pattern', role 'entrepreneur, engineer'. Wikidata Q305177 has no P108 claim (independent fetch).
findings.proposed_fix: Show the company as 'founded' or 'mentioned' rather than employer, or hide it unless the source is P108.

findings.title: Pane exposes only a query box; limit, company and by_company are unreachable from the UI
findings.detail: The manifest defines limit, company and the by_company action, but PEOP.tsx sends only {action:'search', query}. The pane has no company or role filter, unlike a terminal people search.
findings.evidence: Static: useFunction params contain only action and query.
findings.proposed_fix: Add company and limit controls, or document that the pane is search-only.

b2.reference_method: Brinson, Hood and Beebower (1986), Financial Analysts Journal: allocation AE_i=(wp_i-wb_i)(Rb_i-Rb), selection SE_i=wb_i(Rp_i-Rb_i), interaction IE_i=(wp_i-wb_i)(Rp_i-Rb_i). The three effects sum to the active return only when portfolio and benchmark weights each sum to 1.
b2.live_call: Calls on the sidecar: (1) no inputs -> status ok, data_state model, sources brinson_model, active return +4.15% (portfolio 10.05% vs benchmark 5.90%), alloc 0.65%, sel 1.64%, inter 1.86%, 6 sectors. The numbers are exactly the hardcoded sample in pfa.py:36-43. (2) custom weights summing to 1 (Tech/Fin/Energy vs 4-sector benchmark) -> portfolio 10.20%, benchmark 6.40%, active 3.80%, alloc 0.10%, sel -0.10%, inter 3.80%. (3) port weights summing to 0.65 and bench to 0.60 -> active 5.80% but alloc+sel+inter = 5.60%. Artifacts saved under scratchpad work/portfolio-3 as pfa_default.json, pfa_custom_ok.json, pfa_custom_badsum.json.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed every sector effect of pfa_custom_ok by hand from the same raw inputs: portfolio return 0.5*0.20+0.3*0.04+0.2*(-0.05)=0.102, benchmark 0.064, allocation 0.0112-0.0034-0.0084+0.0016=0.001, selection 0.024+0.002-0.003-0.024=-0.001, interaction 0.016+0.001-0.003+0.024=0.038. All match the handler to the printed precision, so the BHB formulas in pfa.py:56-58 are correct when weights sum to 1. For pfa_custom_badsum the residual 0.058-0.056=0.002 equals (sum wp - sum wb)*Rb_total = 0.05*0.04, so the decomposition does not reconcile when weights do not sum to 1 (no validation exists).

findings.title: Default PFA output is hardcoded sample data labelled only as model
findings.detail: With no weight/return maps the handler silently substitutes a hardcoded five-sector sample (pfa.py:34-43). The response carries no sample flag: metadata.data_state is model, sources is brinson_model, warnings is empty, status is ok. The pane's badge logic (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1332 sampleSignal) only recognises placeholder or sample tokens, so the default is shown as modeled, not sample. The only disclosure is the editor subtitle 'optional - the backend sample runs until applied' (PerformanceAttribution.tsx:487). The headline 'Active return +4.15%' therefore looks like a real attribution result.
findings.evidence: pfa_default.json: totals.active_return 0.0415; rows Technology port_weight 0.45, bench_weight 0.30, identical to pfa.py:36-43; metadata.warnings []
findings.proposed_fix: Return status sample with is_placeholder true and a warning when the maps are absent, or refuse with input_required. Do not compute a headline from the sample.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live. A default PFA call (no weight/return maps) returns hardcoded sample weights and returns (pfa.py:34-43, comment 'Sample data for UI demo') with totals.active_return 0.0415, metadata.data_state 'model', sources ['brinson_model'], warnings [], status 'ok'. The pane classifier (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx ~1332-1375) only matches sample/template/placeholder tokens, so the payload is badged 'modeled'. The only disclosure is the editor subtitle 'optional - the backend sample runs until applied' (PerformanceAttribution.tsx:487). Mitigating factor: that subtitle does tell the user a sample runs, so a P0 reading under the rubric is arguable, but P1 is the fair grade. Scratch output: scratchpad/b2/work/portfolio-3/pfa_default.json.

findings.title: Brinson effects do not reconcile when weights do not sum to 100%
findings.detail: Totals use unnormalised sums (pfa.py:47-48) and the pane does not validate weight sums (pfaParamsFor, PerformanceAttribution.tsx:100-119). When sum wp is not equal to sum wb, the sum of allocation, selection and interaction differs from the reported active return by (sum wp - sum wb) times the benchmark total return. The pane still shows the active return as a headline next to the effect ladder, so the effects visibly fail to add up.
findings.evidence: pfa_custom_badsum.json: port weights 0.45+0.20=0.65, bench weights 0.30+0.20+0.10=0.60; active_return 0.058 vs allocation 0.018 + selection 0.028 + interaction 0.010 = 0.056; gap 0.002 = 0.05 * 0.040
findings.proposed_fix: Reject or flag inputs whose weights do not sum to 1 (within tolerance). Alternatively add an explicit cash/residual term so the identity holds.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live and by algebra. Totals are unnormalised (pfa.py:47-48). The identity sum(AE+SE+IE) = RP - RB - (sum wp - sum wb)*RB holds. With port weights summing to 0.65 and bench weights to 0.60 (sidecar call), active_return 0.042 versus effect sum 0.03955, a gap of 0.00245 = 0.05 * 0.049. pfaParamsFor performs no weight-sum validation, and the response carries no warning. Scratch: scratchpad/b2/work/portfolio-3/pfa_badsum.json.

findings.title: Missing sector entries silently default to zero weight and return
findings.detail: Every lookup uses .get(s, 0) (pfa.py:52-55) and the union of sectors is taken from both maps (pfa.py:45). A sector present in one weight map but absent from the matching return map is therefore scored at 0% return with no warning. The pane cannot show this because it only sends the four maps as typed.
findings.evidence: Code path only; not reproduced live.
findings.proposed_fix: Require every sector that has a non-zero weight to have a return, and list unmatched sectors in warnings.

findings.title: Manifest describes a different function (factor regression) than the handler (BHB)
findings.detail: pfa_seed.py defines code PFA as Portfolio Factor Analysis: CAPM/FF3/FF5 regressions on Ken French factors, inputs portfolio_source, factor_model and window, HAC standard errors, and output loadings and alpha. None of that exists in pfa.py, which is a Brinson sector attribution using typed inputs. The manifest's methodology is therefore false for the shipped code. The function index shows the handler name, but the seed remains a contract conflict.
findings.evidence: Seed name 'Portfolio Factor Analysis' vs live function-index name 'Performance Attribution (Brinson)'; no factor_model input is read by the handler
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed to the Brinson contract (inputs port_weights, port_returns, bench_weights, bench_returns; outputs active, allocation, selection, interaction) or split factor attribution into its own code.

findings.title: No holdings-based attribution: sector weights and returns must be typed by hand
findings.detail: A professional attribution (Bloomberg PAT, FactSet) derives portfolio weights from the holdings and benchmark returns from the index constituents. Here the pane never reads PORT positions and there is no benchmark data feed, so the user must type eight sector maps. The result is only as good as the typed numbers.
findings.evidence: Pane sends only the four maps; no positions or benchmark symbol parameter exists in pfa.py
findings.proposed_fix: Build port weights and sector returns from PORT positions and a sector-ETF benchmark (see keyless_source).
findings.keyless_source: yfinance sector ETFs XLK, XLF, XLV, XLE, XLY, XLI (verified: closes returned on 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-08 via yfinance Ticker.history)

b2.reference_method: Prediction-market odds: implied probability = outcome price x 100 for each outcome (prices sum to about 1 in a binary market). Market liquidity is reported once per market. Topic search should use the provider's search over all open markets, not a filter over a truncated window.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/POLY: {status:open,min_liquidity_usd:10000} -> 100 markets, 200 rows, cards total liquidity 43,393,616.88 (poly_open.json). {status:closed} -> 100/100 closed=true (poly_closed.json). {status:all,min_liquidity_usd:0} -> 100/100 closed=true (poly_all.json). {query:'fed cuts',status:open} -> 0 markets, warning 'none matched the topic filter' (poly_fed.json). Raw Gamma search=fed and search=fed cuts return identical top rows (raw_fed.json, raw_fedcuts.json).
b2.independent_check: Raw Gamma per-market liquidity (slug query) = 428,864.55 for will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027, matching the backend per-market value. Backend price mapping is correct: outcomePrices [0.105, 0.895] -> implied_prob 10.5 and 89.5. The pane KPI and per-market liquidity fail: they double the value for binary markets (pane-style sum 86,787,234 vs backend card 43,393,617 for the same 100 markets). The status filter fails: status=all and status=closed both return only closed=true markets.

findings.title: Liquidity KPI and per-market liquidity double-counted
findings.detail: The pane adds liquidity_usd once per outcome row. The backend repeats the market-level liquidity on each outcome row, so a binary market counts twice. The KPI falls back to that sum because the payload has no top-level total_liquidity_usd (the backend only exposes it inside cards). Result: the Liquidity KPI is about 2x the true total and every binary market's liquidity is doubled in the table.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/POLY.tsx:194 (m.liquidity += liq per outcome row), :227-229 (totalLiquidity falls back to the sum); backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/poly.py _expand_outcome_rows (liquidity_usd repeated per outcome)
findings.evidence: poly_open.json: rows 200 for 100 markets; pane-style sum of rows = 86,787,234; backend cards total_liquidity_usd = 43,393,616.88; raw Gamma liquidity for will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027 = 428,864.55 while the pane would show about 857,700.
findings.proposed_fix: Sum liquidity once per market (or read the cards value) in POLY.tsx; keep liquidity_usd on market rows only, or de-duplicate before summing.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. POST /api/fn/POLY {} returned 200 rows for 100 markets (the rows list is what the pane reads via payload.rows, POLY.tsx:161-163). Each row carries the market-level liquidity_usd (poly.py _expand_outcome_rows, line ~213), so the row-summed liquidity is 80,126,646.49 while the true market total is 40,063,323.25, exactly 2x. Example: will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027 liquidity 428,864.06 appears on both outcome rows. The pane adds liq once per row (POLY.tsx:194) and falls back to that sum because the payload has no top-level total_liquidity_usd (total only lives in cards, poly.py ~142). Liquidity KPI and per-market liquidity are doubled for binary markets. Scratch output: C:/Users/KULLAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e0427571f2ca10f3/3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def/scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/poly_default.json

findings.title: status=all and status=closed return only closed markets
findings.detail: The handler maps all, closed and resolved to include_closed=True, and the adapter sends closed=true to Gamma. Gamma then returns only closed markets. 'all' therefore silently drops every open market, and 'resolved' is just the Gamma closed flag: the returned closed markets still have active=true and end dates in the future.
findings.evidence: poly_all.json: 100/100 markets closed=true, active=true; poly_closed.json: same; sample end_date 2026-11-08T04:59Z while run time is 2026-11-08T00:16Z. Raw Gamma closed=true sample: closed flags all true.
findings.proposed_fix: Map all to no closed filter (send no closed param), closed to closed=true, and resolved to the resolved flag where available; document that closed does not imply resolved.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced live. status=all and status=closed both return status ok with 100 markets; the slug sets are identical and all 100 have closed=true, so no open market appears under 'all'. Code: poly.py:36-41 maps all/closed/resolved to include_closed=True, active=False, and polymarket_adapter.py:72 sends closed=true to Gamma. The detail is overstated on one point: only 6 of 100 closed markets have an end_date in the future, not most of them, and 'active=true' is true for all 100. The core defect (status=all silently drops every open market, and 'resolved' is only the closed flag) is confirmed. Scratch: .../scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/poly_all.json and poly_closed.json

findings.title: Topic query effectively broken
findings.detail: The Gamma search parameter is ignored, since searches for fed and fed cuts return the same rows. The handler then applies an all-tokens literal filter over only the top 400 markets by 24h volume. Multi-word topics therefore return nothing unless every word appears literally in a top market.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/poly.py _matches_query (all-tokens filter applied after fetch) and polymarket_adapter.py fetch_markets (search param sent)
findings.evidence: raw_fed.json and raw_fedcuts.json: identical first rows (for example Xi Jinping out before 2027?). poly_fed.json: 0 markets for 'fed cuts'.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify Gamma search semantics, or use a tag or event search, and apply any-token scoring over the full result set instead of an AND filter over a truncated window.

findings.title: Pane exposes neither topic nor status controls
findings.detail: POLY.tsx sends only status open and min_liquidity_usd 10000. The seed declares query (Topic) and status options open, closed, resolved and all, but the user can reach neither the topic search nor the other statuses.
findings.evidence: POLY.tsx params literal: { status: 'open', min_liquidity_usd: 10_000 }.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a topic input and a status select to the pane, wired to the existing params.

b2.reference_method: Markowitz mean-variance: mu = mean daily return x 252, Sigma = cov x 252, Sharpe = (mu_p - rf)/sigma_p. Min-variance is long-only argmin w'Sigma w. Equal risk contribution (ERC): RC_i = w_i (Sigma w)_i / (w'Sigma w) equal for all i.
b2.live_call: Five calls. (1) pane-like {symbols 7 ETFs, mode all, live true, days 756, risk_free 0.04} -> ok, samples 518. max-Sharpe ret 19.60% vol 17.70% sharpe 0.8816. min-vol vol 9.87%. risk-parity sharpe 0.8104. (2) live false -> provider_unavailable, template returns, SPY 77% in max-Sharpe. (3) symbols SPY,TLT,ZZZNOTREAL,GLD -> status ok, warnings empty, symbols returned [SPY,TLT,GLD]. (4) min_vol with objective max_return, risk_model exp_cov, constraints max_weight 0.2, window 2Y, risk_free_rate 0.045 -> min-vol SPY 51.9%, days echoed as 120 and status provider_unavailable. Artifacts in scratchpad work/portfolio-3 as popt_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Re-downloaded the same 756-day window (518 rows, matching the handler). Max-Sharpe and min-vol: handler weights reproduce the handler's return and vol exactly; my long-only projected-gradient optimum gives min-var vol 9.865% (handler 9.865%) and max-Sharpe at rf 4% 0.8817 (handler 0.8816), so those two modes are correct. For risk parity: handler RC = [15.6, 15.5, 15.7, 6.2, 15.7, 15.7, 15.5] percent against target 14.29, so TLT is badly under-weighted in risk; my ERC solver gives equal RC 14.29 each with vol 12.30% (handler 13.55%). For min-vol and risk parity, the handler's Sharpe at rf 4% is -0.2275 and 0.5152, while the reported values are 0.1779 and 0.8104, i.e. computed at rf 0.

findings.title: Risk Parity output is not equal risk contribution
findings.detail: risk_parity() runs a fixed-step projected update (optimizer.py:245-255) with gradient (rc - target) * marg and a 1000-iteration cap with no convergence test. The resulting weights leave TLT at 6.2% of risk against a 14.3% target. The UI labels the result 'Risk Parity' and presents it as ERC.
findings.evidence: popt_pane_live.json risk_parity.weights TLT 0.2014 with RC 6.19%; independent ERC weights [0.127,0.098,0.104,0.318,0.134,0.123,0.096] give RC 14.29% each and vol 12.30% vs handler 13.55%
findings.proposed_fix: Solve ERC with a proper root-finder or Newton step (for example the Spinu or Maillard fixed point), check max |RC - 1/n| below a tolerance, and warn when it does not converge.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance (used; verified 518 daily closes for the seven ETFs)

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. risk_parity() is a fixed-step PGD with 1000 iterations and no convergence check (optimizer.py:237-257). On SPY,QQQ,IWM,TLT,GLD,EFA,EEM over 365d the handler returns TLT weight 0.2052. Independent recomputation from yfinance gives TLT risk contribution 6.2% against an equal-risk target of about 14.3%. An independent ERC solve gives TLT 0.319 and max RC deviation under 0.9%. The handler's weights are not equal risk contribution. The UI label 'Risk Parity' is the usual name, so the defect is the non-converged solver rather than the label. Vol figures differ by window, so I did not rely on them. Scratch: popt_rp.json and erc_check.py in scratchpad/b2/work/portfolio-3.

findings.title: Sharpe for min-volatility and risk-parity ignores the risk-free rate
findings.detail: min_volatility() and risk_parity() compute stats with rf hard-coded to 0.0 (optimizer.py:151 and :253). max_sharpe() uses the user rate (:205). The Mode summary table shows all three Sharpe values side by side under the RF% control, so the figures are not comparable.
findings.evidence: popt_pane_live.json: min_volatility sharpe 0.1779 (equals return/vol at rf 0; at rf 4% the value is -0.2275); risk_parity sharpe 0.8104 (at rf 4% it is 0.5152). max_sharpe 0.8816 is correct at rf 4%.

findings.title: Most manifest inputs are ignored: objective, constraints, risk_model, return_model, window, frontier_points
findings.detail: The handler reads symbols, days, mode, risk_free, allow_short and live only (port_opt.py:31-40). Mode is a fixed set of three solvers. The manifest promises objective selection (max_return, target_return, target_volatility, ...), weight caps and sector caps, four covariance estimators and three return models (port_opt_seed.py:58-134). The live call with constraints max_weight 0.2 returned a min-vol SPY weight of 51.9%.

findings.title: Symbols that fail to download are dropped silently
findings.detail: Each symbol's fetch is wrapped in a broad except that returns an empty series (port_opt.py:57-58). The result is only checked for fewer than two columns (port_opt.py:66), and the returned symbol list is whatever survived (port_opt.py:74). No warning is raised, so the optimum is computed on a smaller universe than the one requested.

findings.title: Fallback to synthetic cosine returns is labelled but produces materially different weights
findings.detail: When fewer than two symbols survive, the handler uses rpar._template_returns, a deterministic cosine series, and only labels it through metadata (port_opt.py:65-73). The live and model optima are very different (max-Sharpe SPY 21% live vs 77% model), so a user toggling LIVE/MODEL gets a different answer that reflects the template, not the market.

findings.proposed_fix: Return status provider_unavailable without weights when live data is unavailable, instead of optimising on synthetic returns.

b2.reference_method: Variance-covariance VaR = -mu h + z_alpha sigma sqrt(h); ES = -mu h + sigma sqrt(h) phi(z)/(1 - alpha); component VaR by Euler decomposition w_i (Sigma w)_i / sigma; historical VaR = empirical loss quantile.
b2.live_call: Three calls. (1) pane-like {confidence 0.95, max_positions 12, live_risk true, method parametric, days 252} -> VaR95 1d 2,016.74 (ES 2,544.04), historical VaR 1,584.12, samples 327, positions 7, coverage_pct 1.0. (2) same with max_positions 3 -> positions_analyzed 3, portfolio_total_notional 68,095 (book is 112,604), coverage_pct still 1.0, VaR 1,443.62. (3) method monte_carlo, confidence 0.99 -> response method historical, MSFT dropped with warning, positions 6, coverage 0.857. Artifacts in scratchpad work/portfolio-3.

Formula and sign conventions check out. The coverage and calendar findings below come from comparing the handler's own outputs.

findings.title: coverage_pct reports full coverage after positions are silently truncated to max_positions

Positions beyond the cap are excluded from VaR and notional without any warning. The pane always sends max_positions 12 (PortfolioAnalytics.tsx buildParams PVAR) and does not display coverage_pct, so a book of more than 12 positions silently shows a VaR for part of the book.
findings.evidence: pvar_max3_coverage.json: positions_analyzed 3 of a 7-position book, portfolio_total_notional 68,095 vs 112,604, coverage_pct 1.0, no warning

findings.title: Equity and crypto returns are mixed on a union calendar, which distorts the one-day VaR

findings.title: ERC solver returns non-equal risk contributions
findings.detail: The iteration stops when the residual change is below tol, not when the residual is small, and the update w_i <- w_i*(0.5+0.5*target_i*port_vol/(Sigma w)_i) has no w_i term, so it does not converge to the ERC condition. The output is wrong while info reports success-like fields.
findings.evidence: rpar_5_erc_days504.json: risk_contributions_pct equal the weights (SPY 33.4, QQQ 0.0, TLT 64.6, GLD 2.0 percent); info residual 0.0446 after 93 iterations. The independent ERC on the same covariance gives 25 percent each.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the cyclical update w_i <- b_i * sigma_p / (Sigma w)_i, normalize, and iterate until max |RC_i - b_i| < tol. Verified in this audit to converge to 25 percent each. Fail with a warning when it does not converge.

verifier.reasoning: risk_parity.py:49-50 stops when the change in residual is below tol rather than when the residual is small, and the update at :54-55 has no w_i term, so the fixed point is not the ERC condition. Sidecar ERC call (days 504, live) returns risk_contributions_pct SPY 33.41, QQQ ~0, TLT 64.57, GLD 2.03 (the weights themselves) with info residual 0.0446 after 93 iterations and no warning. Output is wrong and not flagged as non-converged.

findings.detail: Every /api/fn call passes through _route_function_params, which merges _agent_function_params defaults under caller params. Those defaults set days 120, range 3M, limit 6 and live true. RPAR's own default of 504 days (rpar.py:97) is therefore never reached on this route. Caller params win, so passing days=504 restores the window. Cross-cutting: this affects every function that reads days.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/server_routes/function_index.py:74; backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:289-290 (days 120, range 3M), 785-787 (defaults merged before caller params); backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/rpar.py:97 (days default 504)
findings.evidence: Every saved response inputEcho shows days 120, range 3M, limit 6, live true, even for calls that did not send them. RPAR without days gives samples 83 (live) or 119 (model); with days 504 gives samples 347 (rpar_5). Effect on output: ERC GLD weight 0.0140 at days 120 versus 0.0203 at days 504; portfolio vol 0.0893 versus 0.0844; annualized GLD vol 24.3 percent versus 26.7 percent independent.
findings.proposed_fix: Scope default injection per function: do not inject days, range, query or limit into functions whose manifest does not declare them. For RPAR honor the manifest lookback_window (1Y default) or the 504 default.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance Ticker.history (347 return rows verified for the same window)

Sidecar call without days returns inputEcho days 120 and samples 83 (live). Passing days 504 gives samples 347. The pane sends no days, so the default view uses the 120-day window. findings.title: Manifest input names ignored; undeclared universe default silently used

findings.title: Default method is inverse-vol under a Risk Parity title

findings.title: Intermittent 14 s timeout on live ERC with a foreign payload fragment
findings.detail: The first live ERC call timed out and the response carried a 'requested' block from another request (query 'bitcoin cryptocurrency', limit 6, range 3M, days 120) that RPAR never sent. The retry succeeded in 6.7 s, so the failure is intermittent. Per-symbol fetches allow 8 s each and then fall back to a second source, so worst case stacks.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/rpar.py:135-142 (8 s wait_for per symbol) and 150-156 (fallback chain); sidecar response assembly for timeouts (not located)
findings.evidence: rpar_2_live_erc.json: reason 'function timed out after 14s', status provider_unavailable, payload.requested from another request. rpar_3_live_erc_retry.json: HTTP 200 in 6.7 s.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce one overall time budget per call, fetch symbols concurrently with a shared deadline, and never echo another request's payload in a timeout response.

This engine instead builds an equal-weight 0-100 macro composite and maps it linearly to a spread of 0.1% to 12%, which is not calibrated to any market price.

findings.detail: recovery is read with float() and never clamped; the denominator is max(0.01, 1-R), so R >= 0.99 silently produces PD = spread/0.01. Seed says max 0.95 but nothing enforces it. The pane does not expose a recovery control, so this is reachable through the API and not the default UI.

findings.title: Equal-weight composite drives a PD that ranks the US as the riskiest sovereign
findings.detail: The 1Y PD is a linear transform of an uncalibrated score, so the table and card present a 'default probability' with no market basis. In the core universe the US (11.30%) ranks above Turkey (11.14%), and the Highest-risk KPI shows US. The US score comes mainly from the current-account leg (65.7) and the reserves-in-months leg (83.6, WB 2.8 months), which are structural for a reserve-currency issuer rather than default signals. The seed presents this as a Hull PD, which overstates it.

findings.proposed_fix: Relabel the output as a macro risk score, not a PD, unless calibrated to CDS or ratings; disclose the legs; or drop PD for countries without a market-implied spread.

Dropping the debt leg removes a risk factor rather than neutralising it. The explanation is only in a title tooltip.
