findings.proposed_fix: Pass quarter into the filing lookup (match the filing by reportDate) or drop the input.

findings.title: SEC User-Agent uses a placeholder contact
findings.detail: _UA is 'showMe research contact@example.com'. SEC fair-access guidance asks for a real contact address; the placeholder may be throttled or blocked.
findings.evidence: Code read only.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the operator's real contact address (from config).

b2.reference_method: Exchange session calendars: regular open, close and lunch-break times per venue plus holiday closures (exchange_calendars XTKS, XHKG, XNYS, XLON and others). Professional terminals (Bloomberg EQS/TRDH style) show current state and next open/close in venue time, including breaks.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/TRDH {} -> 1 row (BINANCE only). POST {exchanges:'NYSE,NASDAQ,LSE,FWB,TYO,HKEX,ASX,BIST,BINANCE,DERIBIT'} (pane list) -> 10 rows, including TYO next_close_utc 2026-11-09T06:00Z. Direct CalendarRegistry calls reproduce the handler's is_open and next_close.
b2.independent_check: Compared registry hours with the exchange_calendars 4.13.2 schedules for the 10 default venues: 7 match exactly (NYSE, NASDAQ, LSE, FWB, HKEX, ASX, BIST). TYO fails: registry close 15:00, exchange_calendars 15:30 since 2024-11-05, with an 11:30-12:30 break the registry does not model. HKEX has a 12:00-13:00 break the registry does not model. Next-open/close UTC values for NYSE, LSE, TYO, HKEX, ASX and BIST on 2026-11-08 match local-time rules. Holiday closures for NYSE 2026-11-26, LSE and ASX 2026-12-25, and TYO 2026-11-03 return closed. The key output fails on the two venues with breaks.

findings.title: TYO and HKEX open/close state wrong during lunch breaks and at TYO close
findings.detail: The registry has one open/close window per venue. TYO is shown closed-at-15:00 (the exchange runs to 15:30) and open through its 11:30-12:30 break; HKEX is shown open through its 12:00-13:00 break. next_close for TYO on a Monday afternoon skips the same-day close and returns Tuesday 15:00 JST.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/reference/exchange_registry.py:58 (TYO 09:00-15:00), :60 (HKEX 09:30-16:00, no break); backend/showme/engine/reference/calendar_registry.py:63-103 (is_open, next_open, next_close use a single window)
findings.evidence: exchange_calendars XTKS close_times 15:30 and break_start 11:30 / break_end 12:30; XHKG break_start 12:00 / break_end 13:00. CalendarRegistry: is_open('TYO', 2026-11-09 12:00 JST)=True (lunch); is_open('TYO', 15:15 JST)=False (still open until 15:30); next_close('TYO', Mon 15:15 JST)=2026-11-10T06:00Z; is_open('HKEX', 12:30 HKT)=True (lunch).
findings.proposed_fix: Read hours from exchange_calendars open_times, close_times and break_start/break_end times rather than the hand-typed table, and treat a break as closed.
findings.keyless_source: exchange_calendars 4.13.2 (local pip package, no network needed)

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed against exchange_calendars 4.13.2 and the function's own CalendarRegistry (reference/calendar_registry.py, used by trdh.py:35-51). XTKS close is 15:30 since 2024-11-05, with a break 11:30-12:30. XHKG has a break 12:00-13:00. EXCHANGES in exchange_registry.py:58 and :60 use a single window (TYO 09:00-15:00, HKEX 09:30-16:00, no break). Results: is_open(TYO, Mon 12:00 JST)=True (lunch, wrong); is_open(TYO, Mon 15:15 JST)=False (still open until 15:30, wrong); next_close(TYO, Mon 15:15 JST)=2026-11-10T06:00Z (skips the same-day close); is_open(HKEX, 12:30 HKT)=True (lunch, wrong). Live reproduction was not possible at the moment because today is a Sunday. A default TRDH sidecar call returns only BINANCE because the router injects exchange=BINANCE, so the evidence rests on the function's own calendar code path.

findings.title: Default call returns only BINANCE because of route-injected exchange
findings.detail: The route injects a singular exchange key from the agent profile, which the handler reads when exchanges is absent. A call with no parameters therefore returns one crypto venue, not the default 10-venue board. The pane avoids this by always sending exchanges, but other callers see one row.
findings.evidence: POST /api/fn/TRDH {} -> rowCount 1, metadata.exchanges ['BINANCE']. POST with explicit exchanges -> 10 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Stop the route from injecting exchange for TRDH, or have the handler ignore the injected key when exchanges is absent.

findings.title: Manifest inputs not implemented and output contract not met
findings.detail: trdh_seed.py defines asset_classes, regions, display_tz and now. The handler reads only exchanges or exchange. The output lacks the venues, as_of and display_tz keys the output_contract requires. The seed methodology claims lunch breaks, pre- and post-market windows, and a half-day calendar, none of which exist in the code.
findings.evidence: Live response keys: rows, surface, cards, methodology, field_dictionary, source_mode, status. No venues, as_of or display_tz. Lunch and pre/post fields absent from every row.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the seed with the implemented behaviour, or implement the filters, display timezone and break/extended sessions.

findings.title: Source list hard-coded to exchange_calendars
findings.detail: sources is always ['exchange_calendars'], even when the package is missing and the registry silently falls back to weekday-only sessions.
findings.evidence: With the package installed (4.13.2) the label is accurate; the code path without it still reports the same source.
findings.proposed_fix: Report the actual calendar source and a warning when falling back to weekdays.

b2.reference_method: Transcript Q&A: answers grounded in call text, returning 'not stated' when the transcript does not address the question; every answer cites the passage it came from.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/TRQA {symbol:AAPL, questions:[spin-off dividend question, quarterly revenue question]} -> HTTP 200, 0.6 s, status ok, sources [sec_8k_ex99, extractive_qa], source sec_8k_ex99, transcript_chars 11519. Answer 1 (spin-off dividend): model local_extractive, confidence 0.36, answer = 'installed base ... Apple's board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share'. Answer 2 (quarterly revenue): model local_extractive, confidence 0.54, answer 'The Company posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year.'
b2.independent_check: Fetched the same SEC exhibit: the text contains 'quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year' and 'cash dividend of $0.27 per share', so the revenue and dividend answers are accurate quotes. The word 'spin' does not appear in the exhibit, so the spin-off answer is not supported by the document and should have been 'not stated'. check_passed true for the figures; the spin-off answer is a separate P1.

findings.title: Q&A runs over the press release and returns unrelated passages as answers
findings.detail: TRQA fetches the same 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press release used by TRAN, while its docstring and title describe an earnings-call transcript. When no question term matches, _extractive_answer falls back to the first sentence of the document. When the match is weak but non-zero, the best partial hit is returned as the answer with a confidence value and no 'not stated' threshold, so an unsupported question gets a confident-looking answer.
findings.evidence: trqa_aapl.json: spin-off dividend question answered with a $0.27 regular dividend sentence at confidence 0.36; the exhibit does not contain 'spin'. Revenue answer correct at 0.54.
findings.proposed_fix: Return answer 'not stated in the document' below a term-coverage threshold, and label the source as press release, not transcript.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed live. Question 'Did the company announce a spin-off?' on AAPL returned answer = the first sentence of the 8-K Exhibit 99.1 document (EX-99.1 header, 'Apple reports fourth quarter results'), model local_extractive, confidence 0.46, and no 'not stated' outcome. This matches the code fallback at trqa.py:461-462 (best_total <= 0 uses sentences[0]). The reviewer's exact answer text differed (0.36, dividend sentence), but the defect is reproduced. The sources are sec_8k_ex99 and extractive_qa, but the docstring says earnings-call transcript.

findings.title: max_tokens_per_answer input ignored
findings.detail: Seed input max_tokens_per_answer is declared, but the LLM request hard-codes max_tokens=500.
findings.evidence: Code read only.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the param or remove the input.

b2.reference_method: Transcript sentiment analyzer: per-utterance FinBERT polarity attributed to the correct speaker, net score as a length-weighted mean, speaker and role rollups, and an explicit neutral/unavailable state when no model ran.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/TSAR {text: two-speaker sample, symbol: AAPL} -> HTTP 200, 0.5 s, status ok, data_mode live_official, sources [pasted_text, finbert]; 2 utterances: 0.9597 (positive) and -0.9465 (negative), summary net_score -0.1636, dominant_tone negative. POST {symbol:AAPL} only -> HTTP 200, top-level status ok but data.status no_text, data_mode not_configured, sources [transcripts_archive], warning 'no transcript text resolved'.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed net_score from the returned utterance lengths (69 and 99 characters) and FinBERT scores: (69x0.9597 + 99x(-0.9465)) / 168 = -0.1636, matching the reported value exactly. FinBERT scores are non-zero, so the model ran in the sidecar. The attribution is wrong: the second utterance, which is spoken by the CFO, is labelled 'John Ternus, CEO' and its text begins 'Kevan Parekh, CFO:'.

findings.title: Inline speaker labels not split; CFO remarks attributed to the CEO
findings.detail: When two speaker labels sit in the same paragraph with no blank line, the segmenter keeps the second label inside the first speaker's utterance. Speaker rollups and management_score then credit or debit the wrong person (here the CFO sentence is under the CEO). The utterance text still contains 'Kevan Parekh, CFO:', so the error is visible but not corrected.
findings.evidence: tsar_text.json utterances[1]: speaker 'John Ternus, CEO', role management, utterance 'Kevan Parekh, CFO: We expect headwinds ...', score -0.9465.
findings.proposed_fix: Split on every speaker-label pattern inside a block, not only at block starts, and test with inline multi-speaker input.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed by direct call to tsar._segment (python -B, synthetic input mirroring the defect). _SPEAKER_LINE (tsar.py:40) only matches at line start. With the CEO and CFO labels on separate lines, the segmenter is correct. With both labels in one paragraph, the CFO sentence is kept under 'John Ternus, CEO' as 'Kevan Parekh, CFO: We expect headwinds...'. The reviewer's tsar_text.json was not re-run (not available to me), so the evidence is by reproduction of the same code path.

findings.title: Silent neutral when FinBERT fails; FinBERT rows still labelled finbert
findings.detail: _score_finbert returns 0.0 for every text on any exception and sets a warning. The zero rows are still emitted with model 'finbert' and feed the primary aggregate, so net_score and dominant_tone become a neutral reading. The top-level status stays ok and data_mode is only signalled as 'modeled'. Trigger not reproduced live because FinBERT loaded in the sidecar.
findings.evidence: Code read only; live FinBERT returned non-zero scores (0.9597, -0.9465), so the defect is conditional.
findings.proposed_fix: On FinBERT failure, set scores to null, exclude them from the aggregate, and return status provider_unavailable.

findings.title: Envelope status and data status disagree; symbol-only path has no transcript source
findings.detail: For a symbol-only call the top-level status is ok while data.status is no_text. The symbol path reads only the local archive, so unlike TRAN and TRQA it never resolves a transcript for a ticker. The pane's default lookup therefore returns nothing without the user pasting text.
findings.evidence: tsar_aapl.json: status ok, data.status no_text, utterances 0, warning 'no transcript text resolved'.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate data.status to the envelope and state in the UI that a transcript must be pasted or archived.

b2.reference_method: WACC = E/V*Re + D/V*Rd*(1-T), with Re from CAPM (rf + beta*ERP), Rd as the current all-in yield on the issuer's or a comparable BBB/A corporate bond (FRED BAMLC0A4CBBBEY is the keyless effective-yield series), T the effective or marginal tax rate, and E/D market-value weights. Banks are normally treated with a deposit-funded D/V convention or excluded from debt weighting.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/WACC {symbol:AAPL} -> status ok, data_state live: wacc 0.103906, re_capm 0.105705, rf 0.0484, beta 1.146109 (beta_5y), erp 0.05, rd 0.0116 (rd_source fred_bbb), tax 0.21, equity_weight 0.98136, debt_weight 0.01864. POST {symbol:AAPL,rf:0.045,beta:1.2,erp:0.055,rd:0.05,tax_rate:0.15} -> wacc 0.109723, all overrides honoured. POST {symbol:AAPL,market_premium:0.08,tax_rate_override:0.35,beta_window:'1Y'} -> identical to default (ignored). POST {symbol:JPM} -> wacc 0.042247, beta 0.871888, rd 0.0116, equity_weight 0.39941, debt_weight 0.60059, re 0.091994. Raw: C:\Users\KULLAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\e0427571f2ca10f3\3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def\scratchpad\b2\work\equity-4\wacc_aapl_default.json, wacc_aapl_override.json, wacc_aapl_manifest_names.json, wacc_jpm_default.json.
b2.independent_check: rf: FRED DGS10 on 2026-11-05 = 4.84, matches rf 0.0484 (pass). Beta: my 5Y daily AAPL-vs-SPY regression (yfinance, 1254 returns) = 1.1523 versus sidecar 1.1461 (pass; the BETA function returns the same 5Y value). Rd: FRED BAMLC0A4CBBB on 2026-11-05 = 1.16 (percent OAS spread), while BAMLC0A4CBBBEY (effective yield) = 5.93. Recomputed with the yield: AAPL WACC 10.46% (sidecar 10.39%), JPM WACC 6.49% (sidecar 4.22%). Capital structure: yfinance JPM totalDebt 1,335,691,968,512 vs marketCap 888,274,812,928, so D/V = 0.60. Failed on Rd and the financial-sector weights.

findings.title: Cost of debt uses an option-adjusted spread, not a yield
findings.detail: Rd is taken from BAMLC0A4CBBB, the ICE BofA BBB option-adjusted spread in percent (1.16 on 2026-11-05), then divided by 100, giving rd 0.0116. The seed methodology says Rd comes from Aaa/Baa yields. A spread cannot stand in for a pre-tax cost of debt. The effect is that JPM WACC is understated by about 2.3 points (4.22% versus 6.49% with the yield) and AAPL by about 7 bp.
findings.evidence: wacc_aapl_default.json rd 0.0116 with rd_source fred_bbb; FRED BAMLC0A4CBBB 2026-11-05 = 1.16 versus BAMLC0A4CBBBEY 5.93.
findings.proposed_fix: Switch the series to BAMLC0A4CBBBEY (or another all-in corporate yield), keep the Aaa/Baa fallback labelled, and state the series and as-of date in the output.
findings.keyless_source: FRED keyless CSV BAMLC0A4CBBBEY

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. wacc.py:203 fetches FRED BAMLC0A4CBBB, an option-adjusted spread in percent, and :207 divides by 100. Live WACC AAPL returns rd 0.0116 with rd_source 'fred_bbb'. FRED independent check: BAMLC0A4CBBB = 1.16 (2026-11-05), BAMLC0A4CBBBEY = 5.93 (same date). A spread is not a pre-tax cost of debt, and wacc.py:156-157 methodology text cites Aaa/Baa yields. Recomputing JPM with rd 5.93%: Rd*(1-T)=0.04685; WACC = 0.3994*0.09199 + 0.6006*0.04685 = 6.49%, versus the 4.22% returned, which matches the finding's ~2.3 point understatement. AAPL effect is about 7 bp, also consistent.

findings.title: Capital-structure weights are wrong for banks and financials
findings.detail: D/V is computed as totalDebt/(marketCap+totalDebt) for any issuer with debt. The sector-default financial branch runs only when totalDebt is zero, so for banks the balance-sheet liabilities drive the weights. JPM gets D/V 0.60, which combined with the Rd error gives a WACC of 4.2%, far too low for a bank.
findings.evidence: wacc_jpm_default.json equity_weight 0.39941, debt_weight 0.60059, capital_structure_data_state live; yfinance JPM totalDebt 1.336T vs marketCap 0.888T.
findings.proposed_fix: Detect financials (sector 'Financial Services' or industry Banks/Insurance) and either use the deposit-funded convention or label the WACC as not applicable, instead of a live book-debt weight.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance info (keyless; JPM totalDebt and marketCap verified)

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed as a methodology defect. wacc.py:251-263 applies the financial sector default only in the else-branch when totalDebt+marketCap is zero. Live WACC JPM returns debt_weight 0.6006, equity_weight 0.3994, capital_structure_data_state 'live', debt_value_source 'book'. Independent yfinance check: JPM totalDebt 1,335,691,968,512 and marketCap 888,274,812,928, which yields D/V = 0.6006 and reproduces the code. The WACC of 4.22% is therefore driven by treating bank liabilities as debt. The methodology string in wacc.py:305 documents this book-debt approach, so it is a methodology gap for financials rather than a mislabel, which keeps it at P1 instead of higher. Medium confidence because a professional terminal may also handle banks by a different standard, which I did not verify against an external reference.

findings.title: ERP is a silent constant 5.0% even though a Damodaran cache exists
findings.detail: When the damodaran dependency is absent or falsy, erp falls back to a constant 0.05 with no warning, no erp_source and no 'damodaran' source. The runtime cache shows US 4.6 percent, and get_erp would return 0.046. The root cause (deps.damodaran falsy in the live sidecar) was not verified beyond reading the factory registration.
findings.evidence: wacc_aapl_default.json erp 0.05, sources ['fred','beta','yfinance'], warnings []; runtime/damodaran_erp.json payload US 4.6.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose erp_source in the output, warn when the constant is used, and make the Damodaran adapter reachable from the function deps (or read the cache directly).
findings.keyless_source: Damodaran ERP table (the cache file already holds it; keyless upstream not verified here)

findings.title: Tax rate is a hard-coded 21% with no source label
findings.detail: tax is 0.21 unless the tax_rate param is given. The seed says the default is FA-derived effective tax, which the code does not implement, and the output has no tax_source field.
findings.evidence: wacc_aapl_default.json tax_rate 0.21 with no source field.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive effective tax from income tax expense over pre-tax income (yfinance financials) and expose tax_source; keep 21% only as a labelled statutory fallback.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance financials (keyless)

findings.title: Seed inputs do not exist in the handler, and the pane exposes no inputs
findings.detail: The seed declares market_premium, beta_window and tax_rate_override. The handler reads erp, beta, rf, rd and tax_rate, so the seed's names are ignored. WACC.tsx sends an empty params object, so the user has no control over rf, beta, ERP, Rd or tax.
findings.evidence: wacc_aapl_manifest_names.json identical to wacc_aapl_default.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename handler params to the seed names (or the reverse), add the controls to the pane, and echo the assumptions in output.

findings.title: Status and data_state overstate live data
findings.detail: status is always 'ok' (wacc.py:297) and data_state reflects beta only (wacc.py:320, :331). The rf fallback of 0.04 (wacc.py:90, :277) and the constant ERP are not reflected in data_state, and the Rd spread is labelled live for JPM.
findings.evidence: wacc_jpm_default.json status ok, data_state live with rd_source fred_bbb; data_state covers beta only.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute an overall data_state from every input (rf, erp, beta, rd, capital structure) and report 'partial' or 'reference' when any is a fallback.

b2.reference_method: Sovereign 10Y benchmark yield grid where each row carries its own observation date. Spreads are yield differences in bp (yield x 100 vs UST10Y). Rows from different frequencies should not be compared on one as_of.
b2.live_call: POST {reference:false} (pane default) -> HTTP 200 ok, sources [fred], 12 rows (AU 5.283, CA 3.8825, DE 3.4695, ES 3.9230, FR 4.4771, GB 5.2421, IT 3.9860, JP 3.05, MX 9.35, RU 7.62, US 4.84, ZA 8.9471), missing_countries [TR, BR, IN, CN, ID], all as_of 2026-11-08, source fred. POST {region:em,countries:[US,TR,MX]} -> US returned (region ignored), TR missing. Artifacts in ...\scratchpad\b2\work\bond-2\WB_pane.json, WB_emregion.json.
b2.independent_check: Fetched FRED fredgraph.csv for all 17 seed series and compared the last observation with each returned yield: all 12 present values match to 0.0000. But: US DGS10 last observation 2026-11-05 (row says 2026-11-08); DE, JP, GB, CA, FR, IT, ES, AU, MX, ZA last observations are monthly, dated 2026-09-01 or 2026-08-01 (row says 2026-11-08); RU last observation 2018-06-01 (7.62) shown as 2026-11-08 'live'; TR, BR, IN, CN, ID return HTTP 404. Script: ...\bond-2\check_wb.py.

findings.title: as_of is stamped with the request date, not the observation date, so stale values read as current
findings.detail: For live rows the handler sets as_of to today's UTC date, not the FRED observation date. The pane shows that date and also prints a wall-clock 'AS OF ... UTC' caption. Monthly OECD series are therefore shown as current-day values, and RU, whose last observation is June 2018, appears as a live 2026-11-08 reading under a 'live' pill. This is a false live/as-of claim.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/wb.py:59-64 (as_of = today for non-template rows) and 151 and 127-130 (fred path); ui/src/functions/WB.tsx:300 (KPI 'AS OF {utcStamp} UTC'), 125-126 (isLiveSource) and 225-226 (live FRED pill)
findings.evidence: WB_pane.json rows: every as_of is 2026-11-08. Raw FRED last observations: DGS10 2026-11-05 4.84; IRLTLT01DEM156N 2026-09-01 3.46952; IRLTLT01JPM156N 2026-09-01 3.05; IRLTLT01RUM156N 2018-06-01 7.62.
findings.proposed_fix: Set as_of from the last retained observation date of each series (df.index[-1]) and show that date per row; caption the KPI with the data date, not the wall clock; treat rows older than a threshold as stale.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced: all live rows in wb_pane.json have as_of 2026-11-08, the request date, while the code at wb.py:59-64 sets as_of to today for non-template rows. Raw FRED last observations are DGS10 2026-11-05 at 4.84, DE and JP 2026-09-01, and RU IRLTLT01RUM156N 2018-06-01 at 7.62. The sidecar returns RU 7.62 as a source_mode fred row dated 2026-11-08, and WB.tsx:225-226 labels it 'live FRED' (isLiveSource = sourceMode === 'fred'). This is a false live/as-of claim, and the field dictionary's own statement that as_of is the observation date contradicts the code.

findings.title: Five emerging-market countries are silently dropped from the grid
findings.detail: The FRED IDs for TR, BR, IN, CN and ID return HTTP 404 on the keyless CSV endpoint. The handler records them in missing_countries, but the pane never reads that field, so the subtitle reads '12 of 12 countries' and the EM tab shows only MX, RU and ZA with no notice that TR, BR, IN, CN and ID are absent. The emerging split is therefore misleading.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/wb.py:20-41 (IDs), 144-156 (missing_countries set, not rendered); ui/src/functions/WB.tsx:247 (subtitle) and no reference to missing_countries
findings.evidence: WB_pane.json: missing_countries [TR, BR, IN, CN, ID], summary.missing_countries 5, metadata provider_errors 'keyless FRED CSV unavailable'. Direct fetch: IRLTLT01TRM156N/BRM/INM/CNM/IDM -> HTTP 404.
findings.proposed_fix: Render missing_countries in the pane (and the EM tab) with a reason, and source the missing EM yields from a current keyless source. Note that the other FRED fallbacks checked (INTGSBINM193N ends 2017; INTGSBBRM193N, INTGSBTRM193N, INTGSBCNM193N, INTGSBIDM193N return 404) are not usable.

findings.title: region and live_bonds inputs are dead, and the seed claims the wrong default
findings.detail: The handler never reads region, so region=em returns US. The pane filters client-side, so the UI is unaffected, but the backend contract is not. The seed exposes live_bonds (default False), and its methodology says the default is the template, which is false: the handler is live by default and the pane sends reference. The region semantic test in the seed would fail.
findings.evidence: WB_emregion.json: request region em, countries [US,TR,MX] -> rows US and MX returned; US is not an EM country.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement region on the backend or drop it from the seed; make the live_bonds default and methodology match the handler (live by default; reference flag).

findings.title: Delta-vs-US mixes a daily US print with monthly foreign prints
findings.detail: The grid is ranked and compared on one as_of, but US is a daily DGS10 value for 2026-11-05 while most other countries are monthly values for 2026-09-01. The Delta-vs-US column (for example DE -137 bp) therefore subtracts values from different dates and frequencies.
findings.evidence: WB_pane.json US 4.84 (2026-11-05 daily) vs DE 3.4695 (2026-09-01 monthly); the Delta is computed on these unaligned values.
findings.proposed_fix: Align all rows to the most recent common date, or show each row's age and a frequency tag, and exclude stale monthly values from the spread.

b2.reference_method: Live FX cross-rate matrix: cross = quote per base from live quotes, bid/ask from real market quotes, daily change from the last two closes. Pro WCRS shows live tradable bid/ask and change; a daily ECB fix must be labelled as such.

findings.title: ECB daily fix is shown as a live quote (green live pill)
findings.detail: source_mode live_official is the Frankfurter/ECB reference fix, dated 2026-11-06 (the Friday close), but the pane treats any live_ prefix as live and shows a green live pill on Sunday 2026-11-08. The response carries no fix date and no warning.
findings.evidence: WCRS_pane.json: source_mode live_official, meta data_mode live_official, warnings []. api.frankfurter.app latest date 2026-11-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a distinct label (for example official_daily_fix) with the fix date, and show it as delayed, not live.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. The sidecar WCRS default call returns source_mode live_official, warnings [], metadata.data_mode live_official, sources [frankfurter_ecb], and no fix date. Frankfurter latest for EUR is dated 2026-11-06 (Friday), and the sidecar ran on Sunday 2026-11-08. WCRS.tsx:132-137 sets isLive = sourceMode.startsWith('live_') and shows the pill label 'live'. The response's own methodology calls the Frankfurter/ECB legs keyless 'reference' rates, so the 'live' label contradicts the backend's own description. This is a false live claim (P1).

findings.title: Spread (pips) is a constant 0.02 percent of the rate, not a market spread
findings.detail: bid = rate*0.9999 and ask = rate*1.0001 are hard-coded, so spread_pips = rate*0.0002 scaled to pips for every pair. The column is titled Spread (pips) and shows EURUSD 2.233, EURJPY 3.535 and EURTRY 111.991 as if they were market spreads. Only the methodology text admits they are display values.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the spread column or show it as n/a unless a real bid/ask source is wired in. No keyless bid/ask source was verified (keyless_source null).

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed numerically. _funcs.py:272-273 sets bid = rate*0.9999 and ask = rate*1.0001, and spread_pips = (ask-bid)*pip_factor (line 290). Sidecar output: EURUSD spread_pips 2.233, EURJPY 3.535, EURTRY 111.991. These are constants, not market spreads. The UI header 'Spread (pips)' (WCRS.tsx:191) carries no caveat. The backend discloses in methodology and field_dictionary that bid/ask are display values around the mid, so the defect is a misleading column rather than a hidden one. I rate it P1 as a fabricated spread column, with medium confidence because the methodology text does disclose the constant spread.

findings.title: live_fx=false is ignored because of an operator-precedence fallback
findings.detail: live_enabled = _truthy(params.get('live_fx') or params.get('live', True)). A live_fx of false is falsy, so the expression falls through to the live default True. The explicit opt-out is ignored and the history legs still run.
findings.evidence: WCRS_livefx_false.json: source_mode live_official, history attached (EURJPY change -0.6016 and history of 14 points).
findings.proposed_fix: Test for None explicitly, e.g. live = params.get('live_fx', params.get('live', True)), then _truthy on that value.

findings.detail: Every row is market_state live because the default is hard-coded. as_of is the request time, not the quote time. The UI shows a live pill when status is ok, so the board presents Friday closes as live on Sunday.

b2.reference_method: Whale flow: block or large prints above a USD threshold within a stated window (24h), with the actual covered window disclosed. Crypto from exchange trade data (aggTrades or klines over the window). Equity from volume-notional over the window. FX and indices have no USD notional, so the threshold cannot apply. SEC ownership filings are listed as filings, not trades.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/WHAL: {BTCUSDT,CRYPTO,1M} -> status ok, 0 rows, 0 hits, history 60 klines (whal_btc.json); {PEPE,CRYPTO,threshold 0} -> routed to PEPEUSDT, 5 rows (whal_pepe.json); {AAPL,EQUITY,1M} -> 14 rows, all SEC Form 4 with usd null, 0 hits, history span 00:20-00:59Z on 2026-11-07 (whal_aapl.json); {GLD,ETF,10M} -> 13 rows, 0 hits (whal_gld.json); {EURUSD,FX,1M} -> 7 price-impulse rows, usd null (whal_fx.json).
b2.independent_check: Crypto: raw Binance BTCUSDT 1000 aggTrades span 8.5 min (00:11:05-00:19:37Z), zero trades at or above 1M USD (max 182,897), matching the backend; 24h quoteVolume 387.9M raw vs 388.1M backend at a different moment. Equity: raw Yahoo AAPL 1d/1m has 828 bars, 390 with notional at or above 1M USD (for example about 936M at 2026-11-06T14:30Z). Backend keeps 20 bars after its 24h cutoff and reports 0 hits. Same pattern for GLD (382 raw vs 0).

findings.title: Equity 24h window drops the last session on non-trading days
findings.detail: For lookback 24 the code tries range 1d first and stops at the first range that returns bars. Yahoo 1d returns about 16 hours of pre and post-market bars from the last session. The cutoff is wall-clock now minus 24h, so on a weekend the last session falls outside and only about 40 minutes of pre-market bars survive. The non-empty fresh list then prevents the fallback to the last 120 bars. Result: zero threshold hits and the summary 'none crossed $1,000,000' while the last session had hundreds of crossing bars. The 24h footer is also wrong.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/whal.py:359 (ranges = ['1d','5d'] for lookback <=24), :399-403 (wall-clock cutoff; return fresh or bars[-120:]); ui/src/functions/WHAL.tsx:395 (lookback footer)
findings.evidence: whal_aapl.json: history span 2026-11-07T00:20Z to 00:59Z, threshold_hits 0. Raw Yahoo 1d/1m AAPL: 828 bars, 20 inside the cutoff (0 crossing), 390 with notional at or above 1M. Keyless alternative checked: Yahoo range=5d&interval=5m returns 898 bars from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-07.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick the range by covered time (use 5d for 24h, or anchor the window to the last trading session), report the real covered window, and do not let an empty-window fallback hide the trading day.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced. Sidecar WHAL AAPL lookback_hours=24 returned history spanning 2026-11-07T00:28Z to 00:59Z (16 rows), threshold_hits 0, and summary 'none crossed $1,000,000'. Raw Yahoo 1d/1m (fetched directly, includePrePost=true) has 828 bars from 2026-11-06 09:00Z to 11-07 00:59Z, of which 390 have notional >= $1M; the 24h wall-clock cutoff (2026-11-07 00:27Z) keeps only 16 bars, none crossing. 5d/5m returns 879 bars from 2026-11-02 to 11-07 with 371 crossing. The code at whal.py:359 and :398-403 returns the non-empty fresh slice and never falls back, so the weekend 24h window is effectively empty and the 'none crossed' summary is a false negative about the last session. The footer (WHAL.tsx:395) states 24h while the data covers under 40 minutes. Scratch output: .../scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/whal_aapl.json

findings.title: lookback_hours ignored on crypto while the footer shows 24h
findings.detail: The crypto path always uses the latest 1000 aggTrades, which cover about 8.5 minutes, plus 120 one-minute klines. lookback_hours is parsed but unused on this path. The pane sends lookback_hours 24 and the footer shows '24h', and the seed says crypto uses the last lookback_hours. The footer and seed are both false.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/whal.py:67 (trade_limit fixed 1000), :68 (lookback parsed), :132-160 (_crypto_whales uses trade_limit and klines only); ui/src/functions/WHAL.tsx:160 (lookback_hours 24), :395 (footer); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/whal_seed.py:138 (claims last lookback_hours)
findings.evidence: whal_btc.json: lookback 24 in payload, rows 0. Raw Binance aggTrades BTCUSDT limit 1000: first 00:11:05Z, last 00:19:37Z (8.5 min).
findings.proposed_fix: Page aggTrades by startTime over the requested window, or use klines over lookback_hours, and display the covered window in the footer.

findings.title: Summary and counts imply a USD threshold test where none exists
findings.detail: For FX and index rows usd_value is null, so no threshold can be tested, but the summary still says none crossed $1,000,000. For equities the 14 rows are SEC Form 4 filings with no USD value and threshold_crossed false, and they are counted as threshold-tested proxies.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/whal.py:782-789 (_market_summary), :516-560 (_top_market_rows fallback); whal.py SEC row assembly around :584-645
findings.evidence: whal_fx.json: 7 rows, usd_value null for all, summary 'EURUSD returned 7 public WHAL proxy row(s), but none crossed $1,000,000.' whal_aapl.json: cards Rows 14, Threshold hits 0, all 14 rows sec_ownership_filing with usd null.
findings.proposed_fix: Report counts separately: USD-tested rows, unitless proxy rows and SEC filings. Say 'no USD basis' for FX and index rows instead of 'none crossed'.

findings.title: Severity derived from an invented USD figure
findings.detail: For price-impulse rows the severity uses abs(return) x 1,000,000 as if it were USD. A 0.067% EURUSD move becomes 67,000 'USD' and is rated low against the 1M threshold. The rating therefore changes when the user changes Min USD, even though no USD value exists.
findings.evidence: whal_fx.json: ret -0.067, impulse_vs_median 3, severity low, usd_value null.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive severity from impulse_vs_median (or volume ratio) for price-impulse rows, without a fake USD figure.

findings.title: Zero threshold marks every trade as crossed and large
findings.detail: With threshold 0, threshold_crossed is True for every trade (whal.py:304), so the summary reads 'crossed $0' and every row is typed crypto_large_trade. Also, the direct handler _binance_pair (whal.py ~694-703) falls back to '{chain}USDT' for unrecognised symbols, so calling the handler directly with an unknown symbol would query BTCUSDT. The /api/fn route canonicalises PEPE to PEPEUSDT, so this is latent and not reached through the route.
findings.evidence: whal_pepe.json: 5 rows, threshold 0, summary 'crossed $0', alert_type crypto_large_trade, provider_symbol PEPEUSDT.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an explicit ALL-trades type when threshold is 0, and reject unknown crypto symbols instead of falling back to the chain's USDT pair.

findings.title: Manifest seed describes a different alert taxonomy and filing scope
findings.detail: whal_seed.py says crypto uses the last lookback_hours, lists lookback options 1, 6, 24 and 72 (the pane fixes 24), names alert types large_trade, large_volume, sec_filing and top_holder, and says SEC EDGAR covers 13F/8-K mentions. The handler emits crypto_large_trade, large_volume_proxy, liquidity_impulse_proxy, top_volume_window, top_impulse_window and sec_ownership_filing, and reads Forms 3, 4, 5, 13D and 13G (no 13F or 8-K).
findings.file_line: backend/showme/manifest/seeds/whal_seed.py:80-85 (lookback options), :136-145 (methodology), :148 (alert_type), :138-140; whal.py SEC 'interesting' form set (around line 615)
findings.evidence: whal_aapl.json rows: alert_type sec_ownership_filing, form 4. whal_btc.json and whal_fx.json alert types as listed above.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite whal_seed.py to the shipped alert taxonomy, form set and lookback behaviour.

b2.reference_method: Bond analytics: YTM solves price = sum of PV of cashflows; Macaulay and modified duration; convexity = (1/P) d2P/dy2 in years^2; spread vs benchmark = (YTM - benchmark yield) in bp. Benchmark is a named government curve point, not a single fixed series.
b2.live_call: POST {symbol:US10Y,freq:2} -> ok, sources [fred], CMT 2026-11-05, YTM 4.84%, mod dur 7.8538, convexity 74.44, spread 0.0 bp (tautological vs DGS10). POST {symbol:US2Y,benchmark:UST2Y} -> benchmark_pct 4.84 (DGS10, not UST2Y), spread -38 bp. POST {symbol:91282CRX1,price:99.5,coupon:0.0425,years_to_maturity:10,freq:2} -> status unsupported_asset (compatibility guard classed it as EQUITY), no analytics. Face=1000 call also rejected by the same guard (symbol-based classification). Artifacts in ...\scratchpad\b2\work\bond-2\YAS_us10.json, YAS_bench2y.json, YAS_cusip.json.
b2.independent_check: Independent YTM bisection on a 99.5 / 4.25% / 10y / semi bond: 4.312082% = handler 4.312082%. Modified duration 8.070315 vs finite difference 8.070316; convexity 77.4277 vs finite difference 77.4277. US10Y par YTM equals CMT 4.84%, and modified duration and convexity match finite differences (7.853809 / 74.4429). 3M single-cashflow check: convexity 2T^2/(1+yT)^2 matches. Face scaling tested in-process (see P1). Script: ...\bond-2\check_yas.py.

findings.title: Face value is not scaled against the per-100 price, so YTM is wrong when face is not 100
findings.detail: The solver discounts cashflows scaled by face but compares them with a price quoted per 100. With face=1000 and price 99.5 the solver returns a YTM of 48.5%, instead of 4.31%. Passing the price scaled to face (995) gives the correct 4.31%. The pane does not send face, so the UI is unaffected at the default of 100, but the API contract (face is a required input) is broken.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/yas.py:218 (face read), 266 (price per 100), 276-277 (n_periods), 15-19 and 33-40 (PV uses face); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/yas_seed.py:61-71 and 77-81
findings.evidence: In-process call of the same solver execute() uses: _ytm_macaulay_modified_duration(1000.0, 99.5, 0.0425, 20, 2) -> ytm 48.497519%; _ytm_macaulay_modified_duration(1000.0, 995.0, 0.0425, 20, 2) -> 4.312082%. Independent value 4.312082%. The sidecar call with face=1000 was blocked by the asset guard, so this is reproduced in-process.
findings.proposed_fix: Scale price by face/100 (or reject face != 100 when price is per 100) and document the unit of price.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced through the sidecar with symbol US10Y (the CUSTOM symbol is rejected by the asset guard as unsupported_asset). Face 1000 with price 99.5, coupon 4.25 and 10y gives YTM 48.50% (yas_us10_f1000.json). Face 100 with the same price gives 4.3121%. The price is quoted per 100 (seed line 77, UI label 'Price (per 100 face)') but is compared against face-scaled cashflows. The defect is a wrong result for a documented API input (face), though the pane sends the default of 100 and is unaffected.

findings.title: Benchmark input is ignored and the spread is always measured against 10Y
findings.detail: The seed offers UST2Y, UST5Y, UST10Y, UST30Y, DBR10Y, JGB10Y and GILT10Y. The handler reads only numeric benchmark_rate/benchmark values; a name such as UST2Y is discarded and DGS10 is always fetched. The pane has no benchmark tenor selector, only a numeric BENCHMARK % override, and its BENCH caption does not say which curve point is used. A generic 10Y bond therefore shows a spread of exactly 0 by construction, and a 2Y bond shows -38 bp against 10Y. The methodology also claims a cached_snapshot fallback, which does not exist.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/yas.py:223-227 (non-numeric benchmark dropped), 282-291 (always _BENCHMARK_SERIES); ui/src/functions/YAS.tsx:389-397 (numeric override only) and 292 (BENCH caption); backend/showme/manifest/seeds/yas_seed.py:110-118 and 199-200
findings.evidence: YAS_bench2y.json: request benchmark UST2Y -> summary benchmark_pct 4.84, metadata benchmark DGS10, spread_bps -38.0. YAS_us10.json: spread_vs_benchmark 0.0 for US10Y vs DGS10.
findings.proposed_fix: Map UST tenors to their FRED CMT series (DGS2, DGS5, DGS30, DGS10 already present) and report the benchmark used; reject the non-US options with an explicit unavailable status; expose a tenor selector in the pane.
findings.keyless_source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DGS2 (keyless CMT; same pattern as the DGS10 used now)

findings.title: Manual bond analysis is blocked for CUSIP-style identifiers and the pane shows the wrong message
findings.detail: A CUSIP passes the pane's bond-symbol check, but the sidecar compatibility guard classifies it as EQUITY, so the call returns status unsupported_asset and the user's price, coupon and maturity are never analysed. The pane's blocked check covers only input_error and provider_unavailable, so unsupported_asset falls through to 'No analytics returned - check the bond inputs', which misdirects the user. (Desktop routing may differ from this API route; not verified in the app.)
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/YAS.tsx:144-145 (blocked check) and 269-279 (empty message); ui/src/functions/YAS.tsx:428-430 (cleanBond accepts CUSIP-like strings)
findings.evidence: YAS_cusip.json: status unsupported_asset, metadata compatibility_mode unsupported_asset, requested_asset_class EQUITY, provider_errors 'YAS does not support EQUITY'.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat unsupported_asset as a visible input/asset error with its reason; and make manual overrides route as BOND (asset class from the pane, not inferred from the symbol).

findings.title: Seed convexity expectation contradicts the computed value; units are not stated
findings.detail: The seed asserts convexity of about 200 (150 to 250) for a 30y 4% quarterly par bond and says 700 was the bug. The handler returns 421.26, which matches an independent finite-difference convexity of 421.26 in years^2. The code is right and the test expectation is wrong; the unit label 'price convexity' does not say years^2, and the convention differs from quoted house units.
findings.evidence: In-process: _ytm_macaulay_modified_duration(100,100,0.04,120,4) -> convexity 421.264. Finite-difference check (check_yas2.py): 421.26.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the semantic test to about 421 years^2 (or whatever house scaling is used), and state the unit in the field dictionary.

findings.title: Seed methodology and field metadata are inaccurate
findings.detail: The methodology gives the bisection bracket as [-0.99, 5.0], but the code brackets -1% to 500% annual (y_low=-0.01/freq, y_high=5.0/freq). It says the benchmark falls back to cached_snapshot, which does not exist. The output has no data_mode key, though must_have lists it, and provider_mode (default MODELED) is never read.
findings.evidence: Code reading; YAS_us10.json has no data_mode key at the top level of data.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the bracket and fallback text, emit data_mode, and honor or remove provider_mode.

b2.reference_method: Sovereign par yield curve by constant maturity (US Treasury par yields, as republished by FRED DGS series), ordered by tenor, with each row carrying its observation date. Non-US curves require a country-specific source; a US curve must not be substituted.
b2.live_call: 3 calls. country=US (pane default): HTTP 200, 3.6 s, source fred, live true, 11 tenors, latest_10y 4.84, every row as_of 2026-11-08. country=DE: HTTP 200, source computed_model, warning 'live curve for DE is not wired; using computed_model fallback', rows equal the static US fixture (1M 5.32, 3M 5.28, 6M 5.15, 1Y 4.92, 2Y 4.62, 5Y 4.38, 10Y 4.45). live_curve=false with tenors=[2Y,10Y]: still live FRED, 11 tenors returned. Raw responses in scratchpad/b2/work/bond-1/crvf_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Keyless FRED fredgraph CSV, latest valid observation for each of the 11 series is dated 2026-11-05: DGS1MO 4.03, DGS3MO 4.17, DGS6MO 4.19, DGS1 4.28, DGS2 4.46, DGS3 4.53, DGS5 4.59, DGS7 4.70, DGS10 4.84, DGS20 5.27, DGS30 5.25. All eleven match the handler's values exactly. The as_of field (2026-11-08, the fetch date) does not match the observation date, so that part fails and is listed as a finding.

findings.title: Non-US curves show static US fixture yields under the requested country label
findings.detail: For any non-US country the handler returns the hard-coded US-shaped curve with the country code attached, so 'Yield Curve — DE' displays US levels (10Y 4.45). The pane's notice blames a missing FRED key, which is wrong for DE: the reason is that non-US curves are not wired. The engine's warning is never rendered by CRVF.tsx, so the user sees a wrong cause.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/crvf.py:22-32 (static curve), 122 and 163 (fixture returned for any country); ui/src/functions/CRVF.tsx:175-180 (notice text 'No FRED key is configured')
findings.evidence: crvf_de.json: summary.country DE, source_mode computed_model, rows identical to _curve_model(). The notice text is at CRVF.tsx:177-179.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status provider_unavailable (or an empty curve) for non-US countries rather than a US fixture, and have the pane show the actual reason from warnings.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. Live crvf country=DE returns the US-shaped fixture (1M 5.32 ... 10Y 4.45, identical to _curve_model) with summary.country DE and source_mode computed_model. The warning 'live curve for DE is not wired' is in the payload, but CRVF.tsx never renders warnings (grep finds no 'warnings' use). The notice at CRVF.tsx ~L175-180 says 'No FRED key is configured', which gives the wrong cause. The badge does say 'model fixture' and the notice says static levels, not live, so this is not presented as live data. The core issue is that the user's country input is ignored, which is P2 rather than P0 or P1.

findings.title: As-of stamped with the fetch date, not the FRED observation date
findings.detail: Each row's as_of is today's date, while the latest FRED observation is 2026-11-05. The pane's As of column therefore presents three-day-old data as today's. The per-series observation date is available in the fetched frame but is discarded.
findings.evidence: crvf_us.json rows as_of 2026-11-08 for every tenor; keyless fredgraph DGS10 latest valid observation 2026-11-05 (4.84).
findings.proposed_fix: Carry each series' last observation date (from the frame index) into as_of.

findings.title: live_curve input is ignored; handler reads an undocumented 'reference' flag
findings.detail: The manifest declares live_curve as the switch for FRED, but the handler reads only 'reference'. live_curve=false still returns live FRED data, so a caller who turns live off gets live data silently.
findings.evidence: crvf_us_flags.json: request live_curve=false returned sources ['fred'], live true.
findings.proposed_fix: Read live_curve (and keep reference as an alias), and honour false.

findings.title: tenors input is ignored
findings.detail: The manifest says tenors filters the catalog, but the handler never reads it. A request for two tenors returns all eleven.
findings.evidence: crvf_us_flags.json: tenors=['2Y','10Y'] returned 11 rows including 1M, 3M, 6M.
findings.proposed_fix: Filter rows by requested tenors before returning, and report the filter in summary.

findings.title: Pane exposes no country, tenor or live controls
findings.detail: CRVF.tsx sends only the symbol, so the country parameter cannot be chosen in the UI. The non-US path is therefore reachable only through the API, and the UI always shows US data.
findings.evidence: CRVF.tsx useFunction call passes code, symbol and enabled only.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a country selector (limited to countries with a wired source) and the tenor filter.

b2.reference_method: Mark-to-market: MV = qty x last; unrealized = (last - avg_cost) x qty (sign-aware); weight = MV / sum(MV); total equity = cash + sum(MV) (manifest port_seed.py:179-226).
b2.live_call: Call with {} -> status ok, sources portfolio_state + yfinance, 7 positions, MV 112,608.68, cost basis 102,425.00, unrealized +10,183.68, cash 25,000 USD, by_asset_class CRYPTO 37,848.68 / EQUITY 35,196.30 / ETF 39,563.70. Call with ccy EUR, group_by sector, show_zero true -> byte-identical totals and positions. Artifacts: port_default.json and port_eur_ignored.json in scratchpad work/portfolio-3.
b2.independent_check: yfinance last closes for AAPL 342.37, MSFT 530.61, NVDA 186.64, SPY 735.29, TLT 81.92, GLD 372.52 equal the handler's last values exactly. BTC-USD handler 75,697.36 vs independent 75,690.81 (intraday 2026-11-08) is within 0.01%. Recomputed MV, cost basis (9,000+8,400+5,400+16,800+9,200+6,125+47,500=102,425) and unrealized sum match; weight_pct sums to 100.

findings.title: Manifest inputs ccy, group_by, show_zero, accounts and as_of are ignored
findings.detail: The handler reads only params _portfolio_override and positions (port.py:105-111). The manifest declares ccy as 'Reporting currency used for totals + conversions', group_by, show_zero and accounts (port_seed.py:57-97). None have any effect, and the pane sends no params, so the user has no way to set them. No FX conversion exists anywhere in the output.
findings.evidence: port_eur_ignored.json: ccy EUR, group_by sector, show_zero true -> totals identical to port_default.json (market_value 112608.68, cash 25000 USD)
findings.proposed_fix: Implement the declared inputs or remove them from the manifest. Convert non-USD holdings through the FX adapter and report the rate used.

findings.title: Total equity, day P&L, realized P&L and equity curve are missing
findings.detail: The manifest promises totals.total_equity (cash + sum MV), totals.day_pnl, realized_pnl_ytd and an equity curve (port_seed.py:169-226). The handler returns only market_value, cost_basis, unrealized_pnl, n_positions, cash and cash_by_currency (port.py:208-214). The pane headline 'Local analytics equity' is market value excluding cash (PORT.tsx:1008-1012).
findings.evidence: port_default.json totals keys: market_value, cost_basis, unrealized_pnl, n_positions, cash, cash_by_currency only
findings.proposed_fix: Add total_equity = cash + sum MV, previous-close based day_change, and realized P&L from fills, or drop those fields from the manifest and the card slots.

findings.title: Quote failures silently fall back to cost basis
findings.detail: The per-position quote call swallows all exceptions (port.py:181-182), and _position_last_price returns avg_cost when no metadata price exists (port.py:221-229). A failed quote yields last equal to avg_cost, so unrealized P&L for that position becomes zero, and yfinance is dropped from sources without any warning.
findings.evidence: Code path only; all seven quotes succeeded in the live calls, so this was not reproduced live.
findings.proposed_fix: Mark the position as quote_missing with last null and add a warning listing the symbols. Do not substitute cost.

findings.title: Weights use a stale denominator when the live overlay is active
findings.detail: In PORT.tsx the position market value is recomputed from live ticks, but weight = market_value / totals.market_value uses the snapshot total from the backend (PORT.tsx:624-630). The liveTotals guard (lines 633-650) is not applied to the weight denominator. Weights shown next to live marks can therefore stop summing to 100%.
findings.evidence: Code path only; not exercised live.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the live-adjusted total (or the guarded liveTotals) as the weight denominator.

findings.title: Function description is empty and rows drop currency
findings.detail: The function-index description for PORT is blank. The position rows carry currency null for every position even though PortfolioPosition defaults currency to USD (state.py:29), and the pane's stable-USD badge depends on that field.
findings.evidence: function-index: PORT description ''; port_default.json positions currency null
findings.proposed_fix: Add a description and pass currency through to each row.

findings.title: Live prices are labelled data_state reference
findings.detail: Live yfinance marks are present, but metadata.data_state is reference, the label used for portfolio_state, not live.
findings.evidence: port_default.json metadata.data_state reference, sources portfolio_state and yfinance
findings.proposed_fix: Derive data_state from the quote sources (live when yfinance quotes succeeded).

b2.reference_method: Terminal alert equivalent: a user-defined price/change/volume condition is armed, evaluated on each new observation, and fired once per crossing. cross_up/cross_down means a transition from one side of the threshold to the other between consecutive observations. A stored alert must either be evaluated by a running evaluator or be reported as not armed.
b2.live_call: ALRT list {} -> HTTP 200 status ok, count 0, evaluator_status not_running. ALRT add {symbol,field,direction,threshold,note} -> HTTP 200 status input_required (reason: requires non-empty condition). ALRT add {condition:'AAPL.price > 200', cooldown:'abc'} -> status ok, id aaab7639, cooldown_seconds 300 (abc silently replaced). ALRT add {condition:'zzz ??? not a rule'} -> status ok, id cc324843, enabled true. ALRT remove x2 -> removed ok. Envelope inputEcho on these calls showed BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT and query 'bitcoin cryptocurrency' (not the request).
b2.independent_check: Pane evaluation (ALRT.tsx evaluateAlert) runs client-side against quotes and is not reachable from the sidecar, so it was read but not re-run. Store behaviour was checked offline on a scratch copy (corrupt alerts.json, then one add): the corrupt file was replaced by a one-alert list, the original bytes were lost, and only the add response carried a warning. Two test alerts created on the sandbox store were removed again (remove returned status ok for both).

findings.title: Alerts stored by the function are never read or evaluated by the pane
findings.detail: The ALRT pane persists through lib/alerts.ts (Tauri preset 'alerts' or localStorage). It never calls /api/fn/ALRT (only a comment at alerts.ts:6 says it 'may duplex'). The backend store alerts.json is read only by alrt.py. An add through the function returns status ok and enabled true while the same function's list reports evaluator_status not_running, so an API caller gets a success response for a rule nothing will fire.
findings.evidence: Live add (A2) -> status ok, enabled true, id aaab7639; list (same sidecar) -> evaluator_status not_running, evaluator_note 'a background evaluator ... is not wired in this build'.
findings.proposed_fix: Either wire the pane to the function store or return an explicit stored_not_armed status on add, and make the pane and the function share one persistence path.

findings.title: Seed-declared inputs are ignored; add demands an undocumented condition string
findings.detail: alrt_seed.py declares symbol, field, direction, threshold and note (lines 57-94). The handler reads only condition, actions, recipients and cooldown and returns input_required without condition. note, field, direction and threshold are dropped without a warning.
findings.evidence: Live add with the seed's own inputs -> HTTP 200 status input_required, reason 'ALRT add requires a non-empty condition DSL string.'
findings.proposed_fix: Accept the seed's structured inputs (symbol/field/direction/threshold/note) and build the condition from them, or update the seed to the condition-string contract.

findings.title: Condition text is never validated or evaluated
findings.detail: add stores any non-empty string. The condition_examples advertised by list (AAPL.price > 200, NEWS(AAPL).importance >= 70) use a DSL that no code in the alert path parses or evaluates.
findings.evidence: Live add {condition:'zzz ??? not a rule'} -> status ok, stored verbatim (id cc324843).
findings.proposed_fix: Parse the condition with the same DSL parser used elsewhere and return input_error when it does not parse, or drop condition_examples until an evaluator exists.

findings.title: Unreadable alerts.json is overwritten by the next add (data loss)
findings.detail: _load_alerts returns ([], warning) when the file is corrupt. add then appends to that empty list and _save_alerts replaces the file, so the unreadable content is destroyed with no backup. The warning is returned only in the add response.
findings.evidence: Offline test on a scratch copy holding truncated JSON '[{"id": "old1", ...' : after one add, the file contained only the new alert and the original bytes were no longer present. Write path: scratch/corrupt_store_test.py (ALRT section).
findings.proposed_fix: Move the corrupt file aside (alerts.json.corrupt-<ts>) before the first write, or refuse writes while the load warning is set.

findings.title: Pane samples every 45 s, so crossings between samples are missed and armed-past-threshold alerts never fire
findings.detail: The pane polls every POLL_MS=45 s and fires only on an observed edge or crossing between two consecutive samples. Moves that cross and return inside one interval are missed, and an alert created while the price is already past its threshold never fires until a re-cross. The footer (ALRT.tsx:804) does disclose the 45 s client-side poll, so this is a methodology gap, not a hidden claim. The pane already has a live quote stream (useLiveQuote) that is not used for evaluation.
findings.evidence: Source reading only; no live pane test.
findings.proposed_fix: Evaluate on each live quote tick and decide explicitly whether a newly armed alert fires when already past threshold; keep the footer text in sync.

findings.title: Response inputEcho does not echo the request (shared envelope, not located in misc-1)
findings.detail: On ALRT calls the envelope inputEcho shows defaults from another function (limit 6, days 120, range 3M, query 'bitcoin cryptocurrency', symbols BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT) next to the caller's own keys. API consumers reading inputEcho see the wrong inputs.
findings.file_line: not located in this unit (sidecar response envelope); evidence in live_call
findings.evidence: ALRT add {condition, cooldown:'abc'} -> inputEcho {limit:6,...,query:'bitcoin cryptocurrency',symbols:[...],condition:'AAPL.price > 200',cooldown:'abc'}.
findings.proposed_fix: Build inputEcho only from the request params of the called function, without merging the default set of other functions.

findings.title: Invalid cooldown silently replaced with 300 s
findings.detail: cooldown parse failures fall back to 300 with no warning.
findings.evidence: Live add cooldown:'abc' -> cooldown_seconds 300, warnings [].
findings.proposed_fix: Return input_error or a warning naming the replaced value.

findings.title: Seed describes a different alert data model
findings.detail: alrt_seed.py documents rows with active, fired_count, last_fired_at and delivery channels (tray/notification/log), and its methodology says the backend dispatches notify. The handler returns condition, actions, recipients, cooldown_seconds and enabled. No fire count or fire log exists in the backend.
findings.evidence: List payload (live) has no fired_count, active or last_fired_at keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed methodology to describe the current store, or implement the documented fields.

b2.reference_method: Professional equivalent is the security description/identifiers page (Bloomberg DES/ICS style): GICS sector/industry group/industry/sub-industry for the ticker, SIC/NAICS, CIK, exchange and fiscal year end, with the source and as-of of each field. Taxonomy labels are lookups, not formulas.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/APPL {symbol:AAPL,live:true} HTTP 200; {symbol:JPM,live:true} HTTP 200; {symbol:AAPL,reference:true} HTTP 200. Saved as APPL_a1.json, APPL_a2.json, APPL_a3.json under C:/Users/KULLAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e0427571f2ca10f3/3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def/scratchpad/b2/work/equity-1/. AAPL: status ok, sector Technology, industry Consumer Electronics, NMS. JPM: status ok, Financial Services / Banks - Diversified, no GICS rows, no peers. AAPL reference: status reference_taxonomy, sector Equity.
b2.independent_check: No numeric output to recompute. Exchange codes NMS and NYQ map to the correct exchange names. The AAPL GICS rows were checked for internal consistency with the GICS hierarchy and match the hard-coded profile. Yahoo sector/industry labels were not independently re-fetched, so no pass/fail is claimed.

findings.title: Applicable Info (CIK, SIC, FYE, filings) is in the manifest but not delivered
findings.detail: The seed promises Applicable Info: SIC, GICS, primary exchange, fiscal year end, CIK and latest filing pointers. The handler returns only Yahoo sector/industry/country/exchange, the crosswalk rows and peers. The pane is titled Industry Taxonomy. None of CIK, SIC, fiscal year end or filing pointers appear in any response.
findings.evidence: APPL_a1.json keys: status, sector, industry, country, currency, exchange, exchange_name, rows, peers, methodology, field_dictionary. No cik, sic_code or fiscal_year_end keys.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add CIK/SIC/FYE from SEC EDGAR company submissions (keyless) and yfinance, or rename the manifest to match the taxonomy function.
findings.keyless_source: SEC EDGAR company submissions JSON (CIK, SIC, fiscalYearEnd); not fetched in this audit

findings.title: GICS/NAICS/ICB crosswalk exists for AAPL only
findings.detail: The crosswalk is a hard-coded dict with one entry, AAPL. For every other ticker reference_profile returns an empty dict, so only Yahoo's own sector/industry labels appear. The pane is honest about this, but the function does not deliver the GICS classification it is named for.
findings.evidence: JPM payload (APPL_a2.json) has rows Provider sector, Provider industry, Exchange, Country, Currency, Asset class only, and peers []. AAPL is the only symbol with GICS/NAICS/ICB rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Source GICS/ICB per ticker from a licensed or keyless classification feed, or label the result as provider taxonomy only.

findings.title: Reference-mode placeholder values are stamped as live_yfinance
findings.detail: When the taxonomy falls back to the template, the rows read sector Equity, industry Listed Security, exchange Exchange, country Global. _taxonomy_rows labels every provider row source_mode live_yfinance, so the API payload asserts a live provider source for placeholder values. The pane re-stamps the label, but API consumers do not get that correction.
findings.evidence: APPL_a3.json: status reference_taxonomy; rows[0] = {level: Provider sector, classification: Equity, source_mode: live_yfinance}; sources ['taxonomy_model'] in the same payload.
findings.proposed_fix: Use source_mode reference_template for template rows and keep 'live_yfinance' only for values actually returned by yfinance.

findings.title: Sources and input names do not match the data used
findings.detail: The live path reports sources ['yfinance'] even though the GICS/NAICS/ICB rows come from a hard-coded dict. The pane sends live:true, but the handler ignores it and decides the path from reference instead.
findings.evidence: APPL_a1.json sources ['yfinance'] while the AAPL GICS rows are hard-coded (_common.py:22-50).
findings.proposed_fix: List the static crosswalk as its own source, and read live (or drop it from the pane request).

b2.reference_method: CAPM beta: beta = Cov(r_i, r_m) / Var(r_m) on the sample of daily returns, with Pearson correlation and R^2 = corr^2 for the single-factor regression. The benchmark and lookback are user inputs.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/BETA {symbol:AAPL,rolling_window:60} HTTP 200 1.2 s (pane-equivalent); {symbol:AAPL,benchmark:QQQ,rolling_window:60} HTTP 200 4.4 s; {symbol:AAPL,benchmark:^GSPC,beta_window:252d,rolling_window:60} HTTP 200 2.6 s. Saved as BETA_b1.json, BETA_b2.json, BETA_b3.json under C:/Users/KULLAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e0427571f2ca10f3/3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def/scratchpad/b2/work/equity-1/. Results: SPY 1Y beta 0.5885 corr 0.3219 n=252; ^GSPC 1Y beta 0.6094; QQQ 1Y beta 0.2311. Rolling history 120 points, last 0.469 on 2026-11-06.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed from yfinance daily closes (AAPL vs SPY, pct_change on aligned closes, ddof=1). Handler 1Y/2Y/5Y betas 0.5885 / 1.0262 / 1.1461 match my recompute 0.5885 / 1.0262 / 1.1461. Correlation 1Y 0.3219 matches. QQQ 1Y recompute 0.2311 matches the handler QQQ run. Log-return betas differ slightly (0.5845 / 1.0158 / 1.1415), which is the manifest's stated method and is not what the handler does.

findings.title: Benchmark control is missing from the pane and the handler default differs from the manifest
findings.detail: The manifest declares a BENCHMARK_PICKER with default ^GSPC. The handler defaults to SPY. The pane never sends a benchmark param (only rolling_window), so the user cannot choose a benchmark and always gets SPY. The 'vs SPY' caption is hard-coded as a fallback. Passing benchmark=QQQ does change the result, so the handler supports it.
findings.evidence: SPY 1Y beta 0.5885 vs ^GSPC 0.6094 vs QQQ 0.2311 for the same AAPL input (BETA_b1/b2/b3.json). The pane request body contains only rolling_window.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a benchmark picker to BETA.tsx that sends benchmark, and set the handler default to the manifest value (^GSPC) or change the manifest to SPY.

findings.title: beta_window input is declared but not implemented; windows are hard-coded
findings.detail: The manifest declares beta_window with options 60d/126d/252d/504d/756d. The handler reads params['windows'] (1Y/2Y/5Y) and ignores beta_window. The pane shows only the fixed 1Y/2Y/5Y rows.
findings.evidence: Handler source only; the pane never sends beta_window. The output has window labels 1Y/2Y/5Y and window_days 252/504/1260.
findings.proposed_fix: Read beta_window (days) in the handler and return that window, or remove the input from the manifest.

findings.title: Methodology says log returns, handler computes simple returns
findings.detail: The manifest methodology and formula note state that beta uses log returns. The handler aligns closes and calls pct_change (simple returns). The result is a small but real difference, for example 0.5885 simple vs 0.5845 log for 1Y.
findings.evidence: Independent recompute: simple beta 0.5885 (matches handler), log beta 0.5845 (manifest method).
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one method. Either change the manifest text to simple returns (the handler's own methodology text already says that) or switch the handler to log returns.

findings.title: Manifest outputs alpha, r_squared, n_observations and assumptions are absent from the payload
findings.detail: The manifest must_have and field_dict list alpha, r_squared, n_observations and assumptions (echoed inputs). The handler returns beta, correlation, samples per window and does not echo the benchmark/window inputs in an assumptions block. The pane derives R^2 from correlation squared.
findings.evidence: BETA_b1.json rows contain window, window_days, beta, correlation, samples, annualized_volatility_target/bench only; no alpha or assumptions key.
findings.proposed_fix: Return alpha (daily intercept), r_squared and an assumptions object, or align the manifest must_have list with what is produced.

findings.title: Dead baseline branch in the pane
findings.detail: BETA.tsx still handles a 'computed_market_model' seeded baseline with a warning note. HNT-01 removed that fallback in the handler, so this branch can never run.
findings.evidence: Code read only; the handler now returns provider_unavailable with empty betas instead.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the dead baseline branch and its note.

b2.reference_method: Market-concepts education: a versioned catalogue of lessons with learning objectives, worked examples and self-check questions; completion tracked per user, not a constant.
b2.live_call: BMC {} -> HTTP 200 status ready, 13 lessons over 6 modules, progress 'not_started' on every row. BMC {layout:'wall', sources:['bot_pnl']} -> identical 13 rows (layout and sources ignored, no warning).
b2.independent_check: No numeric output to recompute. The curriculum rows were spot-checked for factual direction (for example, a higher EUR rate than USD makes EURUSD forward points negative, a discount; higher REER means overvaluation). No error found.

findings.title: Seed describes a different product, and its declared inputs are ignored
findings.detail: bmc_seed.py names the function 'Build My Custom (Brand / Marketing / Community)', declares layout and sources inputs, and says it builds KPI tiles from WATCH, ALRT and BOT PnL stores. The handler is a static 13-lesson curriculum named 'Market Concepts Education'. The live catalog shows the handler name, so the seed text is stale.
findings.evidence: Live BMC with layout 'wall' and sources ['bot_pnl'] -> identical rows, no tiles, no layout effect.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed to the curriculum contract, or implement the KPI aggregator and move the curriculum elsewhere.

findings.title: progress field is a constant and the methodology overstates it
findings.detail: The handler always returns progress 'not_started' and its methodology says rows carry a completion state. The pane tracks completion in localStorage (BMC.tsx:111-113), which the pane discloses, so nothing is shown falsely, but the backend field carries no information.
findings.evidence: Live BMC rows: progress 'not_started' for all 13 rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the progress field from the backend or describe it as a constant placeholder.

b2.not_reviewed_reason: OOS fold metrics were not recomputed independently; the fold logic (train-before-test tripwire, stitched OOS curve) was read and is structurally sound.
b2.reference_method: Walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation: anchored or rolling train window, parameters fit on train only, test slice strictly after train, metrics from the stitched OOS curve, with a sample-size guard before quoting Sharpe.
b2.live_call: {symbol:AAPL, live:false} -> status ok, sources [placeholder_no_backtest_run], is_placeholder true, measured false, metrics null (flagged). {symbol:AAPL, live:true} -> status ok, sources [yfinance], metadata days 120, walk_steps 5, oos_sharpe 2.363, oos_total_return 0.0284, oos_max_drawdown -0.0204, positive_steps_pct 0.2, trades 3, oos_cagr null, worst_fold sharpe -22.30. {symbol:ZZQXNOTREAL, live:true} -> status ok, sources [local_backtest_model], warning present, metadata synthetic_history true, oos_sharpe 4.44, is_placeholder null.
b2.independent_check: Not recomputed. Sample check on the inputs: 120 calendar days gives about 83 bars, 30 warmup bars, 5 folds, so each test slice is roughly 10-12 bars. The reported OOS Sharpe rests on 3 trades. Scratch: C:\Users\KULLAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\e0427571f2ca10f3\3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def\scratchpad\b2\work\portfolio-1\summ.py outputs.

findings.title: Headline OOS Sharpe from a 3-month history with no sample guard
findings.detail: The route forces days 120 for BTFW (_agent_runtime.py:412), giving about 83 bars and about 10-12 bars per test fold. The handler reports oos_sharpe 2.36, worst fold Sharpe -22.3 and status ok, with no warning about sample size. The methodology text says the metrics are robust to single folds, but a 3-trade OOS record cannot support a Sharpe headline.
findings.evidence: AAPL live: n_splits 5, positive_steps_pct 0.2, trades 3, oos_sharpe 2.363446715884256, oos_cagr null (history under 0.25 years), worst_fold sharpe -22.295.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce a minimum bars-per-fold and total-trades threshold, add a warning and null the Sharpe headline below it, and send an explicit window (default 1Y) from the pane.

verifier.reasoning: Real, but the severity is lower and some numbers are off. AAPL live returned status ok, oos_sharpe 2.363, oos_cagr null, positive_steps_pct 0.2, trades 3, worst fold sharpe -22.3, warnings [], with the route forcing days 120. Test folds are 3 to 5 bars, not 10 to 12 as the finding states. No sample-size guard exists, which is a professional-terminal gap (P2), but the Sharpe is computed correctly from the stitched OOS curve, so this is not a wrong calculation (P1).

findings.title: Synthetic-history fallback keeps status ok and full metrics
findings.detail: When OHLCV fails, the walk-forward runs on a sine ramp and reports OOS metrics under status ok. The warning and sources say synthetic, and the pane badge reads SAMPLE/MODEL through the local_backtest_model source match, but the payload itself does not carry is_placeholder or measured false.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/btfw.py:107-128 (fallback), 151-217 (status ok on result); pane classifier PortfolioAnalytics.tsx:1281-1289
findings.evidence: ZZQXNOTREAL live: status ok, is_placeholder null, sources [local_backtest_model], warnings contains 'synthetic placeholder history (sine ramp)', oos_sharpe 4.44.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status synthetic or placeholder, set is_placeholder and measured false, and withhold metrics as in the no-run path.

findings.title: Pane exposes no strategy, range, train split or walk-step controls
findings.detail: BTFW's pane sends only symbol and live (buildParams 1041-1042). The route forces strategy sma_crossover and days 120 (_agent_runtime.py:412). The seed declares strategy_id, walk_steps default 12, window_length 1Y and commission_bps, but the handler defaults walk_steps to 5 (btfw.py:129) and ignores window_length and commission_bps.
findings.evidence: Seed defaults walk_steps 12, window_length 1Y; observed fold count 5 and window 120 days.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose strategy, window, train_pct and walk_steps in the pane and read the declared inputs in the handler.

findings.title: Default placeholder curve is drawn as a chart
findings.detail: With live false the pane receives a straight equity ramp (btfw.py:227-288). It is flagged as a placeholder with a disclaimer and the badge appears, but the ramp is still charted in the pane.
findings.evidence: Default call: is_placeholder true, measured false, equity_curve 30 points of 1.0015^n ramp.
findings.proposed_fix: Show an empty state with the Run live prompt instead of a drawn ramp.

findings.title: Title and subtitle misdescribe the function
findings.detail: TOOL_CONFIG titles BTFW 'Backtest Forward' with subtitle 'Forward-looking portfolio template run'. The function is a historical walk-forward out-of-sample test.
findings.evidence: Function index name 'Walk-Forward Backtest'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use 'Walk-Forward Backtest' and a subtitle describing out-of-sample folds.

b2.not_reviewed_reason: Per-combo metrics were not recomputed independently; the ranking logic was read in full.
b2.reference_method: Grid search over strategy parameters; a credible tuner selects parameters on a training slice and reports the chosen set out-of-sample (seed btune_seed.py:276-281 describes this), with the in-sample sweep shown only as diagnostics.
b2.live_call: {symbol:AAPL, live_backtest:false} -> status ok, sources [yfinance], inputEcho live true, live_backtest false; best_by_sharpe fast=15, slow=30, sharpe 0.6539, combos_tested 20, metadata days 120. {symbol:AAPL, live_backtest:true} -> identical. {symbol:AAPL, live_backtest:false, live:false} -> status reference, sources [local_backtest_model], warnings [], best_by_sharpe fast=5 slow=30 sharpe 1.25 total_return 0.18 calmar 1.9 trades 10 (hard-coded).
