findings.title: Invented best-parameter results on the non-live path with no warning
findings.detail: _tune_template returns fixed Sharpe, total return and Calmar values by index. The non-live branch returns this with no warning (only sources local_backtest_model and status reference), and the timeout branch adds a warning. The result names a best parameter set with metrics that were never computed.
findings.evidence: Explicit live false: status reference, warnings [], best_by_sharpe sharpe 1.25, total_return 0.18, calmar 1.9 for AAPL, independent of the data.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status unavailable with no metrics when live is off, or put a warning on every reference path.

verifier.reasoning: Real but labelled. Sidecar live:false returned _tune_template values (best_by_sharpe fast=5,slow=30 sharpe 1.25, total_return 0.18, calmar 1.9) with status reference, warnings [] and metadata degraded and synthetic true. The non-live branch is reachable only by explicit live false or the timeout path, which adds a warning. Invented numbers without a warning are a labelling gap, so P2 rather than P1.

findings.title: MODEL toggle overridden by injected live flag
findings.detail: btune.py:104 uses live_backtest or live. The injected live true means a pane MODEL selection still runs the live sweep.
findings.evidence: live_backtest false response: sources [yfinance], inputEcho live true; identical to live_backtest true.
findings.proposed_fix: Check for explicit presence of live_backtest before falling back to live.

findings.title: Seed contract is out-of-sample; code is in-sample and ignores most declared inputs
findings.detail: btune_seed.py:276-281 asserts best parameters are picked out-of-sample, but the handler selects on the full in-sample window (btune.py:187-194 says IN-SAMPLE). Declared inputs param_grid, metric, top_n, search_mode, n_samples and train_pct are ignored (handler reads grid at btune.py:75 and never metric or top_n). Commission is hard-coded to fee 5 bps (btune.py:138), so caller fee_bps is ignored.
findings.evidence: Live AAPL run: 20 combos on about 83 bars; best fast=15 slow=30 with 2 trades; slow 100 and 200 never trade. Ranking is in-sample only.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a train/test split for parameter selection, report OOS for the chosen set, read the declared inputs, and expose fee and window in the pane.

findings.title: Failed parameter combinations skipped silently
findings.detail: Any exception inside a combo is swallowed (btune.py:149-150), so a grid/strategy mismatch quietly reduces combos_tested with no warning.
findings.evidence: Code read; not reproduced live.
findings.proposed_fix: Count skipped combos and surface them as a warning.

b2.reference_method: Chart Studies is a TECH preset (SMA20/SMA50, EMA20, Bollinger 20/2, RSI14 Wilder, ATR14 Wilder, ADX14, Stochastic, OBV, Ichimoku). Professional-terminal equivalent: indicators computed over full history and then shown for the selected window, with the interval the chart is actually on, the provider's delay status, and a visible warning when the bar count does not match the requested range. Live-path formulas match the Wilder/standard definitions checked in TECH.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/CHGS {symbol:AAPL, days:365} -> 200 in 0.89 s, status ok, sources [yfinance], metadata.alias_of TECH, data_state live. summary.last_price 342.37, rsi 51.4622, atr 8.7708, adx 17.1167, samples 250, but bars/ohlcv/rows length 60 (metadata.tail 60, inputEcho.limit 6). Pane request (CHGS.tsx:134) sends only {days}. POST {symbol:AAPL, reference:true} -> 200 in 0.04 s, status reference, data_mode modeled, last 101.4, rsi_14 54.2 (constant), sma_20 99.879, sma_50 97.5468, sources [showme_chart_model], template dates 'template-01'..'template-10'. Raw files: C:\Users\KULLAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\e0427571f2ca10f3\3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def\scratchpad\b2\work\chart\chgs_aapl_365.json and chgs_aapl_ref.json
b2.independent_check: Live-path numbers recomputed from the same 250-bar 1Y OHLCV rows that TECH returned: RSI14 Wilder 51.4622 (handler 51.4622), ATR14 8.7708 (handler 8.7708), MACD 2.0667 (handler 2.0667). CHGS summary is identical to TECH summary for the same request (last 342.37, rsi 51.4622, adx 17.1167). Numbers pass on the live path. The reference=true path uses no market data (see finding 1). ADX numeric defect is inherited from TECH and reported there.

findings.title: reference=true serves a fabricated AAPL template with hardcoded RSI
findings.detail: The reference branch returns a synthetic 10-bar template built from a base of 100 (78000 for USD-suffixed symbols), so AAPL shows last 101.4 against a live close of 342.37. rsi_14 is the literal 54.2 and sma_20/sma_50 are last*0.985 and last*0.962, i.e. not computed from any market data. The UI labels it synthetic (CHGS.tsx:257-275), so the pane is honest, but the API contradicts the seed's methodology ('never a synthetic chart template') and its semantic test chgs_default_defers_to_live_tech. Only reachable by passing reference=true, which the pane never sends.
findings.evidence: chgs_aapl_ref.json: data.last 101.4, data.rsi_14 54.2, data.sma_20 99.879, data.sma_50 97.5468, status reference, data_mode modeled; live close same symbol 342.37 (chgs_aapl_365.json summary.last_price).
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the reference branch or return status no_price_history with a reason, as the seed's methodology already states; if kept for tests, gate it behind a test-only flag and compute rsi/sma from the template rows instead of constants.

findings.title: 1Y range returns 60 bars because a leaked limit=6 is read as the bar tail
findings.detail: The routed /api/fn layer merges agent-profile defaults into every call, including limit 6 and range 3M (server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:286-291 via _route_function_params at :770). TECH reads tail from tail, then bars, then limit, and clamps to 60..5000 (tech.py:163-168), so limit 6 becomes 60. CHGS asked for days=365 and got 250 samples but only 60 bars, and the subtitle reads '60 bars'. The 1Y view's bar series and caption therefore cover about 3 months.
findings.evidence: chgs_aapl_365.json: metadata.days 365, metadata.tail 60, summary.samples 250, bars length 60, inputEcho {days:365, range:'3M', limit:6}.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not inject limit/range defaults into functions that take tail/bars, or have TECH ignore limit. Set tail from the manifest default (1000) and let days drive the window; CHGS should show the bar count it actually uses.

findings.title: 'live studies' pill is hardcoded, not derived from the data mode
findings.detail: The pill reads 'live studies' with a positive tone whenever the payload is not synthetic or an outage. It does not check data_mode, provider mode or delay. The seed's default provider_mode is DELAYED_REFERENCE (chgs_seed.py:100), while the backend stamps live_yfinance. The label is a claim the code does not verify.
findings.evidence: CHGS.tsx:380 literal 'live studies'; chgs_seed.py:100 provider_mode default DELAYED_REFERENCE; chgs_aapl_365.json metadata.data_mode live_yfinance.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the pill from payload.data_state or metadata.data_mode and show the delay label (for example 'DELAYED' or 'EOD') when the provider is not real-time.

findings.title: Study cards and table ignore the chart timeframe; the chart uses its own interval
findings.detail: CHGS sends only {days}, so the Latest values, cards and footer are always daily TECH output. The Chart rendered below fetches its own /api/bars with its own persisted interval (initialInterval 1D) and saves that interval per symbol. Switching the chart to 1h or 1w leaves the study cards on daily bars with no indicator. The seed's interval input (chgs_seed.py:66-73) is never sent by the pane.
findings.evidence: CHGS.tsx:134 params {days}; Chart.tsx:440 fetch /api/bars?interval=...; Chart.tsx:167 interval state from layout restore.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass the chart's current interval to the CHGS call (or show a 'daily studies' caption when they differ), and surface the interval used in the subtitle.

findings.title: Output contract and field dictionary name fields the live payload does not return
findings.detail: chgs_seed output_contract.must_have lists symbol, rows, last and data_mode, and field_dict lists rsi_14, sma_20, sma_50 at top level. The live TECH-alias payload has none of these top-level keys: the last price is data.summary.last_price, and data_mode is only in metadata. The pane compensates with summary.* reads, so the UI is fine, but the manifest contract is not met.
findings.evidence: chgs_aapl_365.json top-level data keys check: none of last, rsi_14, sma_20, sma_50, data_mode, symbol are present.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the manifest contract with the live payload (summary.last_price, summary.rsi) or add the top-level fields in the alias.

b2.reference_method: The live FastAPI router table (OpenAPI document) is the canonical list of REST routes; the API catalog should equal it and state its source honestly.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/DAPI {} (87 rows, source_mode curated_manifest, ignored_filter 'bitcoin cryptocurrency'); POST /api/fn/DAPI {path_filter:'broker', mutates_only:true} (4 rows, 4 state-changing); GET /openapi.json (76 paths, 90 method/path pairs). Scratch files dapi_default.json, dapi_broker_mut.json, openapi.json.
b2.independent_check: Curated manifest versus live OpenAPI: 90 method/path pairs in each. The only difference is proxy path syntax ({path:path} curated, {path} in OpenAPI). Mutating count: 26 curated rows with yes or depends, matching summary.state_changing 26. path_filter and mutates_only behave as documented. check_passed true for the table content; the base_url placeholder and the dead live-provider branch are reported below.

findings.title: Base URL is the literal placeholder http://127.0.0.1:<sidecar-port>
findings.detail: The summary base_url is a hardcoded template string, and the pane shows it as the Base URL badge. Copy-as-curl builds URLs from it, so the copied commands contain a literal <sidecar-port> and do not work.
findings.evidence: dapi_default.json summary.base_url = 'http://127.0.0.1:<sidecar-port>' on a live response.
findings.proposed_fix: Fill base_url from the real sidecar address (the engine knows its listen port), or have the pane use window.location.origin. Remove the placeholder text.

findings.title: Live router introspection is documented but never wired, so source_mode is always curated_manifest
findings.detail: The module and methodology say server.py sets deps.dapi_route_provider at startup. The attribute is declared in base_function.py and read in dapi.py, but nothing assigns it under backend/showme. Every live call reports curated_manifest. Today the curated list matches OpenAPI, but the audit claim and the drift protection it describes are not in effect.
findings.evidence: grep -rn dapi_route_provider under backend/showme returns only the declaration (base_function.py:204), the read (dapi.py:243) and docstrings. Live summary.source_mode = curated_manifest.
findings.proposed_fix: Assign dapi_route_provider during server startup (from the FastAPI app's routes), or correct the docstring, methodology and seed to say the table is always curated.

findings.title: Proxy route path syntax differs from the OpenAPI document
findings.detail: The curated row uses the Starlette converter syntax {path:path}, while OpenAPI lists {path}. This is cosmetic but makes exact comparison with the router fail.
findings.evidence: openapi.json lists /api/proxy/{path} for GET, POST and DELETE; the curated list has /api/proxy/{path:path}.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalise the path in the comparison or in the curated row.

b2.reference_method: Debt maturity profile from the issuer's contractual principal repayment schedule (next 12 months, years two to five, thereafter), as disclosed in 10-K/10-Q debt notes, in USD. Shares of the scheduled total.
b2.live_call: 3 calls. symbol=AAPL: HTTP 200, 0.6 s, sec_edgar, buckets 0-1Y 9.991, 1-3Y 14.475, 3-5Y 8.706, 5Y+ 45.506 (USD bn), total 78.678, shares 12.7/18.4/11.1/57.8. symbol=US10Y: status empty with an honest reason and next_actions. symbol=AAPL, currency=EUR, manual maturities [10, 30]: status ok, source user_input, total 40.0, currency EUR, keys still amount_usd_bn. Raw responses in scratchpad/b2/work/bond-1/ddis_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Companyfacts for Apple (fetched): NextTwelveMonths 9.991 (end 2026-09-26); Year2 9.300 + Year3 5.175 = 14.475; Year4 4.956 + Year5 3.750 = 8.706; AfterYearFive 45.506. All four buckets match the handler. Shares recomputed sum to 100.0. Check passes.

findings.title: currency input only relabels values; amounts are not converted
findings.detail: A non-USD currency is echoed in the rows and summary, but the amounts stay as amount_usd_bn values and are not converted. A user entering EUR-denominated maturities would have USD-named figures labelled EUR, and a non-USD currency is never flagged.
findings.evidence: ddis_manual.json: currency 'EUR' with rows keyed amount_usd_bn 10 and 30, total_debt_usd_bn 40.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject or convert non-USD input, and rename the keys to a currency-neutral amount with the currency stated.

findings.title: total_debt_usd_bn is the maturity-schedule sum, not balance-sheet debt
findings.detail: The 'Total' card reports the sum of scheduled principal (78.678bn for Apple). Balance-sheet long-term debt is 78.114bn (noncurrent 68.208bn plus current 9.906bn). The label overstates the reconciliation.
findings.evidence: ddis_aapl.json summary.total_debt_usd_bn 78.678; companyfacts LongTermDebtNoncurrent 68.208bn and LongTermDebtCurrent 9.906bn at end 2026-09-26.
findings.proposed_fix: Label it scheduled principal (sum of maturities) and show the balance-sheet total next to it.

b2.reference_method: General government gross debt as percent of GDP from IMF / World Bank series (latest available year with its vintage shown), with the average computed on a stated basis (GDP-weighted or explicitly unweighted), and local-currency share from an official source per country.
b2.live_call: 2 calls. No params: HTTP 200, 0.2 s, World Bank, 6 rows out of the 8 default countries: US 115.79 (2024), DE 20.85 (1990), GB 130.74 (2024), IT 77.29 (1992), TR 25.51 (2024), BR 81.86 (2024); summary avg 75.34; JP and FR are absent with no warning; KR-type rows show local_currency_share 0.0 where unlisted. countries=[US, NG, KR]: 2 rows (US, KR), NG silently dropped, no warning. Raw responses in scratchpad/b2/work/bond-1/debt_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Fetched the World Bank GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS series in full: USA 115.79 (2024), GBR 130.74 (2024), TUR 25.51 (2024), BRA 81.86 (2024), KOR 47.81 (2024) all match the handler. Latest non-null observations for DEU and ITA are 1990 (20.85) and 1992 (77.29), which match the handler's stale values. JPN and FRA have zero non-null observations in the full series. The average 75.34 recomputes from the six rows. Values pass; vintage and silent-drop issues are findings.

findings.title: Stale observations (1990, 1992) feed the table and average without a recency limit
findings.detail: The handler takes the most recent non-null observation with no maximum age, so Germany shows a 1990 value and Italy a 1992 value as the current debt/GDP. The average (75.34) mixes 1990 to 2024 vintages. The Data year column discloses the year per row, but the headline average and the max/min ranking treat them as current.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/_stubs.py:657-662 (latest non-null, no max age), 692 (average over mixed vintages)
findings.evidence: debt_default.json: DE debt_to_gdp 20.85 year '1990'; IT 77.29 year '1992'; summary.avg_debt_to_gdp 75.34. Full WB pull: DEU only non-null value in the 1966-2025 window is 1990.
findings.proposed_fix: Set a maximum observation age (for example 5 years), exclude or flag older rows, and compute the average only over current vintages.

findings.title: Countries are dropped silently: no data, unmapped codes and default-list gaps produce no warning
findings.detail: Unknown ISO codes and countries without any observation return None, and the only warning fires on a request exception. The default list of eight returns six rows, and the user's NG request is dropped with no message. JPN and FRA have no observations in this indicator at all, which the user should be told.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/bond/_stubs.py:641-642 (unmapped code returns None), 657-658 (no observation returns None), 668-669 (silent filter), 693-695 (warning only on exception)
findings.evidence: debt_default.json: 6 rows, summary.countries 6, no JP or FR and no warning. debt_ng.json: request [US, NG, KR] returns 2 rows, no NG and no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Return a warning or a per-country status for every requested code that yields no row.

findings.title: Local-currency share is an unsourced constant table, with a false 0.0 for unlisted countries
findings.detail: The local-currency shares are hard-coded numbers with no cited source, and any country not in the table gets 0.0, which renders as a real 0% local-currency share. KR shows exactly that.
findings.evidence: debt_default.json and debt_ng.json: KOR row local_currency_share 0.0 while the warning says the value is a reference.
findings.proposed_fix: Return null for unlisted countries and cite the source for each reference value.

findings.title: Pane has no country filter, so the countries input is unreachable from the UI
findings.detail: DEBT.tsx sends no parameters and passes symbol only, so the user cannot restrict or extend the country set in the UI, even though the manifest exposes countries.
findings.evidence: useFunction call passes code and symbol only.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a country multi-select that sends countries.

findings.title: Average is an unweighted mean, and the help text does not say so
findings.detail: avg_debt_to_gdp is a simple mean over countries regardless of economic size, which is not a standard sovereign aggregate. The card label does not state the basis.
findings.evidence: debt_default.json summary avg 75.34 equals the unweighted mean of the six rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Label the average as unweighted, or add a GDP-weighted average.

b2.reference_method: Point-of-interest lookup on OpenStreetMap Nominatim: viewbox-bounded search, attribution and usage policy honoured, distance by haversine from the geocoded point of the place to the queried location.
b2.live_call: DINE {location:'New York', query:'restaurant', limit:25} -> HTTP 200 in 0.55 s, status live, 25 rows, sources ['openstreetmap_nominatim'], data_state live, types all 'restaurant'. DINE with cuisine:'turkish', price_band:'$' added -> 25 rows identical by name to the unfiltered call, cuisine tags include american, chinese, italian, sushi; warnings []. A second call with location 'Istanbul' returned 5 live Istanbul places.

Recomputed haversine distance from that centre for all 25 returned rows: 0 mismatches against distance_km (tolerance 0.05 km). Rating and price null on all rows (honest).

findings.title: Declared cuisine and price_band inputs are ignored
findings.detail: dine_seed.py declares cuisine and price_band (with option lists) and says they filter results. The handler reads only location, query and limit, so both are dropped without a warning. The pane does not send them, so the UI is unaffected, but the API contract is false.
findings.evidence: Live DINE with cuisine 'turkish' and price_band '$' -> 25 rows identical by name to the unfiltered run, no warning (saved response: scratch/misc-1/dine_cuisine.json).
findings.proposed_fix: Filter on the OSM cuisine tag (price has no OSM source, so drop price_band), or remove both from the seed.

findings.title: Docstring, design label and seed describe a different provider and product
findings.detail: The handler docstring says 'Restaurant info (Yelp Fusion)' and the design export says 'Yelp Fusion restaurant info'. The code calls OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and the pane labels it correctly. The seed calls the function 'Food Picks', says there is no external provider and no network call, and expects rows=[] for an empty store, which contradicts the live handler.
findings.evidence: Live DINE returns openstreetmap_nominatim rows; no Yelp call exists in the handler.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the docstring and design label to OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and rewrite the seed to the live contract.

findings.title: Distance origin is a bounding-box midpoint labelled 'city centre'
findings.detail: The origin is the midpoint of the geocoded bounding box (_extras.py:680-682), not the city centre and not the geocoded point. For New York that midpoint (40.6971, -73.9795) lies roughly 6.8 km south of Midtown, so the distances shown are offset from the centre the label names.
findings.evidence: Geocode bbox from the independent query gives centre (40.6971, -73.9795); Midtown is about 40.758, -73.985, roughly 6.8 km north.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the geocoded point (lat/lon of the top result) as origin, or label the field 'distance from bounding-box centre'.

findings.title: Geocode picks the first of several administrative matches without disambiguation
findings.detail: Nominatim returns both New York City and New York State for q='New York'. The handler takes limit 1 and uses whichever comes first. Today this resolves to NYC, but the result depends on provider order.
findings.evidence: Independent query: first result NYC (bbox above); second result NY State (bbox 40.4766-45.0159 N, -79.7620 to -71.7910 E).
findings.proposed_fix: Prefer results with type city or boundary admin level 8, or surface the chosen match name in the payload.

NVDA live: 62 rows, splits 10:1 (2024-06-10), 4:1, 1.5:1 and older. TSLA live: 2 split rows (5:1, 3:1), no dividends. AAPL model: status modeled, dividends 0.24 and 0.23 dated 2026-11-08. findings.title: Model mode invents dividends for any equity, including non-payers
findings.detail: The model branch hard-codes two quarterly dividends (0.24 and 0.23) dated today for every EQUITY or ETF, regardless of the symbol's history. TSLA, which has no dividend history, shows them. The rows are labelled source_mode 'model' with a warning, so this is not presented as reported data, but the amounts are arbitrary.

verifier.reasoning: Reproduced. DVD TSLA with live=false returned status modeled with two dividend rows of 0.24 and 0.23, dated today (2026-11-08), with source_mode 'model'. The amounts are hard-coded at dvd.py:171-173 for every EQUITY or ETF. TSLA's live split history has no dividends. The pane shows the warning 'Model mode: rows are reference-shaped model events, not reported' (DVD.tsx:263), so the data is labelled and not presented as reported. The arbitrary amounts are still a misleading placeholder, so P2 rather than P1.

findings.title: Live failure path erases the error and claims yfinance as source
findings.detail: When events come back empty or the fetch fails, the handler clears the warnings list (so the provider error disappears) and reports sources ['yfinance'] even though no events were returned.
findings.evidence: Code-only evidence; the live success path was not affected. The fallback branch also returns a placeholder dividend row with amount 0 and status no_recent_dividend_feed.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the provider error in warnings, return sources [] on failure, and drop the placeholder dividend row.

findings.title: Silent truncation of event history
findings.detail: Dividends are capped at the last 80 events and splits at 40 with no flag, so older history is dropped without the user being told.
findings.evidence: AAPL live returns 80 of 92 dividend events in yfinance (oldest 1990-05-21 versus 1987-05-11).

b2.reference_method: Equity screener: marketCap, trailingPE, priceToBook, priceToSalesTrailing12Months, dividendYield (as fraction), beta from a fundamentals provider; predicates applied to the full universe; row limit applied to output.

EQS {'pe < 35 AND beta < 1.3'} over S&P 500: matched 18 scanned 494. 'beta < 1.3' matched 41. 'ps < 5' matched 52. Small universe (AAPL MSFT JNJ XOM KO PG) 'pe < 35' matched 4.

findings.title: row limit input ignored
findings.detail: The pane sends limit (25/50/100/...) and renders 'rows · N/limit', but the EQS handler never reads params['limit'], so output is not capped. The S&P dividend run returned 58 rows against limit 50.
findings.evidence: EQS_sp500_div.json: inputEcho.limit 50, len(data) 58, metadata.matched 58.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply params['limit'] to the returned rows (after sorting) and keep matched as the full count.

findings.title: Fundamental enrichment (beta, P/S, industry) is cache-state dependent
findings.detail: The same universe returns beta/ps populated in one query and entirely null in another. In the dividend run all 58 rows had beta None and ps None, while the beta query on the same S&P 500 list returned beta values. Null beta/ps rows are dropped silently by any predicate on them, so results depend on which query ran first.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/eqs.py:579-621 (_compose_live_row takes beta from ref only, then batch); _eval returns False on None at eqs.py:128-135
findings.evidence: EQS_sp500_div.json: beta None 58/58, ps None 58/58. Subsequent 'beta < 1.3' run over the same list: AES beta 0.92, ABBV beta 0.192, MMM 1.064 populated.
findings.proposed_fix: Fetch beta/priceToSalesTrailing12Months in the same batch as marketCap/trailingPE for every symbol, and report the per-field coverage in metadata.

findings.title: industry column empty for every row observed
findings.detail: industry is None for all sampled rows (AES, MO). yfinance provides an industry field, so the screener loses a column the professional equivalent shows.
findings.evidence: EQS_sp500_div.json rows: industry None.
findings.proposed_fix: Populate industry from the same yfinance info payload.

b2.reference_method: Professional EREV tracks consensus EPS estimate revisions: change in consensus EPS over trailing windows (7/30/60/90 days) plus counts of upward and downward estimate revisions per fiscal period.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/EREV {symbol:AAPL, live:true}: HTTP 200 in 0.1 s. status=provider_unavailable, reason 'finnhub: FINNHUB_API_KEY not set', rows/trend/revisions empty, velocity_avg null, sources []. No fabricated buckets returned (saved as erev_aapl.json). Live Finnhub buckets could not be obtained because no key is configured.
b2.independent_check: No Finnhub key, so live buckets could not be recomputed. Formula checked on synthetic buckets via the handler with a fake finnhub adapter (probe.py): period scores 31/28/31 and n 31/33/29 and avg 1.0/0.848485/1.068969 match 2*sb+b-s-2*ss and n=sb+b+h+s+ss by hand; velocity 0.220481 and net_pos_change -1/+1 and net_neg_change +2/-3 match. Check passes for the formula only.

findings.title: EREV scores analyst rating buckets, not EPS estimate revisions
findings.detail: The function name and pane title say Earnings Revisions, and the handler docstring claims EPS/revenue revisions and an EPS estimate trend. The code only weights Finnhub recommendation buckets (strongBuy..strongSell). A professional EREV measures consensus EPS estimate revisions. A keyless EPS-revision source is available, so the gap is fixable.
findings.evidence: erev_aapl.json methodology text describes only recommendation buckets. yfinance eps_trend/eps_revisions return AAPL estimate data keylessly (see keyless_source).
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to analyst recommendation momentum, or add an EPS-revision view from yfinance eps_trend/eps_revisions and label it as such.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance Ticker.eps_trend / eps_revisions

findings.title: Velocity and average shown as real zeros when no data supports them
findings.detail: With fewer than two periods the velocity is set to 0 instead of null. A period with zero analysts gets avg 0 (a neutral consensus) instead of null, so the UI shows +0.000 and a neutral score for missing coverage.
findings.evidence: probe.py: one-period input returns velocity_avg 0 and revisions []; a single all-zero bucket period returns trend avg 0 and velocity_avg 0 with status ok.
findings.proposed_fix: Return velocity_avg=None when len(trend)<2 and avg=None when n_total==0.

findings.title: Handler comments and docstring misdescribe the calculation
findings.detail: The comment says 4-week velocity, but the code is period-over-period on monthly buckets. The docstring says EPS/revenue revisions and EPS estimate trend, which are not computed.
findings.evidence: Code at erev.py:97 subtracts the previous period average; no EPS fields are read anywhere in erev.py.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the comment and docstring to match the monthly recommendation-bucket method.

findings.title: Unavailable payload labelled synthetic in the envelope
findings.detail: For provider_unavailable the envelope marks data_state=synthetic and metadata.synthetic=true. The payload is honest (no rows), but the label is misleading for a non-data state.
findings.evidence: erev_aapl.json: "data_state":"synthetic", metadata.synthetic true, status provider_unavailable.
findings.proposed_fix: Use data_state=unavailable for provider_unavailable envelopes.

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg FLDS: a mnemonic lookup that lists each field with its description and the functions that support it, covering thousands of fields.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FLDS {prefix:'pe', limit:50} (matched 7 of 35, shown 7); GET /api/function-index (142 entries, checked EQS, SRCH, MLSIG, SCREEN); cross-checked against BQL live and computed calls. Scratch files flds_pe.json, function_index.json.
b2.independent_check: The catalog says pe and market_cap are accepted by BQL get(). The live BQL call get(close,pe) returns no pe key, and the computed template returns pe equal to close. The claim fails, so check_passed is false. EQS, SRCH and MLSIG exist in the index, but no SCREEN function exists (checked against 142 indexed codes).

findings.title: Catalog advertises BQL fields that BQL cannot return
findings.detail: The field_dictionary and seed say each field is accepted by BQL, screeners or analytics. valuation, fundamental, statement and price fields are not in the OHLCV set BQL returns, so get(pe) yields no column in live mode and a fabricated value in template mode.
findings.evidence: bql_computed_default.json: get(close,pe) live returns no pe column. bql_explicit_live_false.json: pe equals close.
findings.proposed_fix: Mark each catalog field with the function contexts that actually return it (for example BQL live = OHLCV only), or add the provider mapping for the fundamental fields.

findings.title: Catalog is 35 hand-picked fields with no mnemonics, sources or availability
findings.detail: Compared with a professional field lookup, FLDS has no Bloomberg-style mnemonics (for example PX_LAST or PE_RATIO), no per-field source or provider availability, and no coverage of most fundamentals and fixed-income fields. It is a short list rather than a lookup.
findings.evidence: flds_pe.json summary.catalog_fields = 35.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a provider-mapped field registry (field, description, provider, unit, availability) and show the mapping in the pane.

findings.title: Prefix search matches substrings of descriptions, not just prefixes
findings.detail: Typing pe returns open (Session open), operating_income, cfo, capex and iv_percentile because the haystack contains pe inside other words. For an autocomplete this is noisy.
findings.evidence: flds_pe.json: matched 7, including open, operating_income, cfo, capex, iv_percentile.
findings.proposed_fix: Rank field-name prefix matches first and treat description matches as secondary, or match on word boundaries.

findings.title: Examples cite a screen DSL and a screen function that do not exist in the index
findings.detail: The technical example says screen functions use rsi, macd and atr, and the default example refers to a screen DSL. The function index has EQS, SRCH and MLSIG but no SCREEN code.
findings.evidence: function_index.json: 142 codes, SCREEN absent; EQS, SRCH, MLSIG present.
findings.proposed_fix: Point examples at functions that exist in the index, or remove the reference.

b2.reference_method: OpenSky /states/all state vectors: altitude from baro (fallback geo) in metres converted to feet at 3.28084, speed m/s to knots at 1.94384, vertical rate in m/s, no route inference without a flight-plan provider. Flight state alerts should be labelled as state observations, not risk assessments.
b2.live_call: FLY {live_flight:true, limit:25} -> HTTP 200 in 0.64 s, status live, 25 rows, sources ['opensky'], metadata data_mode live_official; cards Source time = raw epoch 1794097110 (2026-11-08T00:18:30Z). FLY {live_flight:false, limit:3} -> status live, 3 rows (flag ignored). FLY {limit:'abc'} -> HTTP 200 status provider_unavailable, reason "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'", requested echo query 'bitcoin cryptocurrency'.
b2.independent_check: Conversion check on a raw OpenSky /states/all snapshot (time 1794097131, 8,084 usable state vectors, fetched once anonymously): recomputed altitude_ft = m x 3.28084 and speed_kt = m/s x 1.94384 for all 8,084 rows, 0 mismatches with the handler formulas (_extras.py:487-488). Rows returned by the live call were normalised from a different snapshot, so the check is on the formulas and not on the same rows.

findings.title: live_flight is documented as required, but the handler ignores it
findings.detail: The pane comment says the function refuses to run without live_flight, and the header says aircraft return only when live_flight=true. The handler checks only reference; live_flight is never read, so the flag does nothing.
findings.evidence: Live FLY {live_flight:false, limit:3} -> status live with 3 aircraft.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the claim and the flag, or enforce the flag in the handler.

findings.title: Non-numeric limit is reported as an OpenSky outage
findings.detail: limit is parsed with an unguarded int() before the try block that wraps the provider call. The ValueError is caught by the generic handler at the provider step, so the user sees provider_unavailable and a wrong requested echo.
findings.evidence: Live FLY {limit:'abc'} -> HTTP 200 status provider_unavailable, reason "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'".
findings.proposed_fix: Validate limit before the provider call and return input_error naming the field.

findings.title: 'Crash risk' label overstates a vertical-rate threshold
findings.detail: Client rules label any descent at or below -2,500 ft/min (default, about 12.7 m/s) as 'FLY rule: crash risk — steep descent', and a low-altitude descent as 'crash risk'. The rule uses only vertical rate and barometric altitude, with no terrain, flight-plan, or aircraft-state input, so 'crash risk' is not supported by the data. A steep descent is a state observation, not a risk assessment.
findings.file_line: ui/src/functions/fly-alerts.ts:51 (default verticalFpm 2500), 246-249 (steep descent label), 253-256 (low altitude label)
findings.evidence: Source reading; the default threshold is 2500 ft/min, while the sample raw snapshot shows UAL2081 at -7.48 m/s (about -1,472 ft/min), which the rule does not fire on.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the rule to 'steep descent' and 'low altitude descending', and drop 'crash risk' from labels and toasts.

findings.title: Seed describes a different product (travel list) and its inputs are ignored
findings.detail: fly_seed.py names the function 'Travel Picks', describes an operator-curated list of flights and hotels with no network calls, and declares kind and destination inputs. The handler returns live OpenSky aircraft and ignores kind and destination.
findings.evidence: Live FLY returns live aircraft rows (sources opensky); the seed contract says rows=[] for an empty store.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the seed to the OpenSky contract, or move the travel list to its own function.

findings.title: Source time card is a raw epoch number
findings.detail: The card value is data.get('time') as sent by OpenSky, not an ISO UTC string, while the rows use ISO for last_contact_utc.
findings.evidence: Live card value 1794097110 (equals 2026-11-08T00:18:30Z, matching the row last_contact_utc values).
findings.proposed_fix: Convert to ISO UTC in the handler, as last_contact_utc does.

findings.title: Public quota statement could not be verified; poll volume should be checked
findings.detail: The pane and adapter state a 4000 requests/day public quota (FLY.tsx:22, 97; opensky_adapter.py:1). I could not verify it: the OpenSky API doc URLs returned 404 and the site root returned no usable text. The pane polls every 60 s (FLY.tsx:98) and the adapter fetches /states/all with no filter (opensky_adapter.py:34), which is about 1,440 unfiltered requests per day per open pane. That volume should be checked against the current OpenSky usage policy before the claim is kept.
findings.evidence: Failed fetches of openskynetwork.org/api/ and /api/rest (404); the site root returned 58 characters of text.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify the quota from the current OpenSky documentation and correct the comment; consider a bounding-box filter or a longer poll interval.

b2.reference_method: Covered interest parity with S quoted as quote-per-base: F = S*(1+r_quote*T)/(1+r_base*T), r in annual decimals, T as year fraction (CIP). Pro terminals (e.g. FRD) use live market rates or deposit/OIS curves for each currency, and show forward points in pips.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FRD. (1) {pair:EURUSD} (pane call): status ok, S=1.1143 (source live_yfinance_quote), r_base=0.035, r_quote=0.045, 3M F=1.1171, 3M forward_points=0.0028, 1Y F=1.125211. (2) Manifest-named inputs {base:EUR,quote:USD,tenor:3M,r_dom:0.02,r_for:0.05,spot_override:1.08}: response identical to (1) (S=1.1143, r 0.035/0.045, all tenors) so all six manifest inputs are ignored. (3) {pair:USDJPY,r_base:0,r_quote:0.05,spot:150}: honored, S=150 manual_input, 3M F=151.901042. (4) {pair:USDJPY} live: spot pulled live. Raw files: scratchpad/b2/work/fx/FRD_a.json, FRD_manifest.json, FRD_usdjpy_override.json, FRD_usdjpy.json.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed 3M EURUSD forward from S=1.1143, r_base=0.035, r_quote=0.045 with the handler's ACT/360 convention (T=0.25*365/360): 1.117102, engine 1.1171 (match at 4 dp). With the seed's ACT/365 text (T=0.25) the result is 1.117062, a 0.4 pip difference. Rates: yfinance ^IRX (US 13-week bill) closed 4.00 percent on 2026-11-06 (fetched), versus the 4.50 percent USD constant used by FRD. EUR rate could not be checked (FRED endpoint timed out in this session).

findings.title: CIP forwards use hard-coded 2024-06 policy rates as current inputs
findings.detail: FRD, and also FXIP, take r_base and r_quote from fixed constants stamped as the 2024-06 vintage (_REFERENCE_AS_OF). The spot is live but the rates are not, and no warning is raised for the rates (the only warning is for spot). Every forward level, forward point and the Rate diff card (1.000 pct) inherits the stale rates. A 50 bp USD error moves the 3M EURUSD forward by about S*0.005*0.25 = 0.0014 (about 14 pips).
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/fx/_funcs.py:35-46 (_REFERENCE_AS_OF='2024-06', _REFERENCE_RATES) and 600-604 (_rate_for); FRD handler ~line 386 and warnings block
findings.evidence: scratchpad/b2/work/fx/FRD_a.json: data.r_base=0.035, data.r_quote=0.045, rows[].source_mode=live_yfinance_quote, sources include reference_policy_rate, warnings=[]. yfinance ^IRX = 4.00 on 2026-11-06 vs 4.50 used for USD.
findings.proposed_fix: Fetch current deposit or policy rates from a keyless source, or expose r_base/r_quote in the FRD pane. Stamp rate vintage in the response and add a warning whenever the rate is a constant.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance ^IRX (US 13-week T-bill yield, verified 4.00 on 2026-11-06). No verified keyless EUR/JPY policy-rate source in this session (FRED CSV timed out).

verifier.reasoning: Real defect, downgraded from P1. _rate_for() (_funcs.py:600-606) falls back to the 2024-06 constants USD 0.045 and EUR 0.035 whenever r_base/r_quote are not passed, and FRD reads them as current inputs. Public data disagrees: FRED DFF (fed funds effective) last 3.88 on 2026-11-05 and FRED ECBDFR (ECB deposit rate) 2.50 on 2026-11-06. The sidecar FRD default call returns r_base 0.035 and r_quote 0.045 with warnings []. The rate-diff card shows 1.000 pct. The rates are only marked 'reference_policy_rate' in sources and in metadata.provider_errors; they are not in warnings and the UI does not caption them as reference. Recomputed 3M EURUSD forward with engine rates vs DFF/ECB rates differs by about 10.6 pips. This is stale input data with a silent fallback (P2), not a wrong formula, because the covered-interest-parity arithmetic itself is correct. Evidence folder: scratchpad/b2/work/fx (FRD_default.json, fx_check.py, rates_check.py).

findings.title: Manifest inputs (base, quote, tenor, r_dom, r_for, spot_override) are ignored
findings.detail: frd_seed.py declares base, quote, tenor, r_dom, r_for and spot_override, but the handler only reads pair/symbol/instrument and r_base/r_quote/spot. The pane sends only {pair}. Any caller who follows the manifest gets the default book silently.
findings.evidence: FRD_manifest.json is identical to FRD_a.json (S 1.1143, F 1.1171, r 0.035/0.045). Only r_base/r_quote/spot changes the output (FRD_usdjpy_override.json).
findings.proposed_fix: Map the manifest names to the handler (r_dom->r_base, r_for->r_quote, spot_override->spot, base/quote->pair) and send the rate and tenor inputs from the pane, or remove the unused inputs from the manifest.

findings.title: FRD manifest methodology states the CIP formula inverted
findings.detail: frd_seed.py says F = S*(1+r_dom*T)/(1+r_for*T) with r_dom = base-currency rate. For quote-per-base S, the standard CIP is F = S*(1+r_quote*T)/(1+r_base*T). The handler and the pane subtitle use the standard form, so the displayed numbers are correct, but the documented formula dictionary is wrong. Using the seed text on the 1.1143 / 0.035 / 0.045 example gives 1.1115 instead of 1.1171.
findings.evidence: Recomputed inverted formula: 1.1143*(1+0.035*0.25)/(1+0.045*0.25) = 1.11154. Engine FRD_a.json 3M F = 1.1171.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the seed text and formula_dict to F = S*(1+r_quote*T)/(1+r_base*T) and align the r_dom/r_for naming with base/quote.

findings.title: Day-count and units documented differently from the code
findings.detail: The seed says actual/365 and forward points in pips (x10000). The handler uses ACT/360 (years*365/360) by default and returns forward_points in raw price units (0.0028 for 3M EURUSD, which the seed would call 28 pips).
findings.evidence: FRD_a.json rows[2].forward_points=0.0028. The ACT/360 vs ACT/365 difference is about 0.4 pips at 3M.
findings.proposed_fix: Document the chosen day count per currency and state the forward-points unit in the response (or convert to pips).

b2.reference_method: Cross-exchange perpetual funding heatmap: funding rate per exchange per funding interval, cross-venue average, time-series over the chosen window, universe ranked by open interest (seed contract), annualised rate optional.
b2.live_call: FRH {limit:25, live:true}: status ok, 25 rows, sources binance/bybit/okx (FRH_l25.json). FRH {limit:50}: status ok, 50 rows, top list ranked by 24h quoteVolume including meme and single-venue symbols such as IDOLUSDT (FRH_l50.json).
b2.independent_check: Fetched directly: Binance BTCUSDT lastFundingRate 0.00005465 (ShowMe binance 5.465e-05, match); Bybit BTCUSDT fundingRate 0.0001 (ShowMe 0.0001, match); OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP fundingRate 0.0000873882758814 (ShowMe 8.73882758814e-05, match). Binance MATICUSDT 0.0001 (match), SNXXUSDT 0 (match).

findings.title: Seed inputs and heatmap semantics not implemented
findings.detail: The manifest promises an 8h/24h/3d/7d/30d window, time buckets on the x axis, top-N by open interest, quote_currency and symbol_filter, with an annualised colour scale. The handler accepts only symbols and limit; it returns one snapshot per symbol. Nothing is annualised: the unit is fraction per funding interval. The pane has no window or quote selectors.
findings.evidence: FRH metadata unit 'fraction per funding interval'; no window/bucket/quote_currency reads in frh.py.
findings.proposed_fix: Either implement the window/bucket series (Binance fapi fundingRate history) and OI ranking, or correct the seed to describe the snapshot and per-interval units.

findings.title: Universe is not the top-N by open interest
findings.detail: limit<=25 returns a hard-coded list of 25 names (_DEFAULT_SYMBOLS). limit>25 ranks by Binance 24h quoteVolume across all USDT perpetuals, which admits thin or novel listings (IDOLUSDT, ESPORTSUSDT, SNXXUSDT, SNDKUSDT, SKHYNIXUSDT, XAUUSDT) and does not match the seed's open-interest ranking. The subtitle says 'symbols' without saying how they were chosen.
findings.evidence: FRH_l50.json: symbols IDOLUSDT (binance 0.00074487 only, provider_count 1, labelled 'crowded longs'), ESPORTSUSDT, SNDKUSDT in the top 10.
findings.proposed_fix: Rank by open interest (or label the ranking basis) and exclude symbols with fewer than two venue rates from the signal column.

findings.title: Cross-venue average mixes OKX estimate with settled rates
findings.detail: OKX fundingRate is the current-period estimate (method 'current_period'), while Binance lastFundingRate is the last settled rate. Averaging them gives a rate that is not a single timestamp. Rows with one venue are averaged and labelled with the same signal as three-venue rows.
findings.evidence: OKX response for BTC-USDT-SWAP: method 'current_period', fundingRate 0.0000873882758814, settFundingRate 0.0000914028725214 (settled value available but unused).
findings.proposed_fix: Use OKX settFundingRate (settled) for consistency, and suppress the signal when provider_count < 2.

b2.reference_method: Professional FX forecast pages (Bloomberg FXFC-style) show a vendor consensus forecast by horizon with dispersion. A CIP forward is a no-arbitrage price, not a forecast; a model band must be labelled as model.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FXFC. (1) {pair:EURUSD}: spot 1.1143 (live_yfinance_quote), r_base 0.035, r_quote 0.045, vol 0.085; 1M 1.115239, 3M 1.1171, 6M 1.11985, 12M 1.125211; confidence 77.25/75.75/73.5/69.0; bands 3M 1.069742 to 1.164457. (2) {pair:USDJPY,spot:150,vol_annualized:0.1,tenors:'1M,3M'}: honored (2 rows, vol 0.10 applied), source manual_input, 3M forecast 148.496318, confidence 75.75. Raw: scratchpad/b2/work/fx/FXFC_a.json, FXFC_manual.json.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed 3M EURUSD CIP (ACT/360) = 1.117102 vs engine 1.1171; bands 1.1171 +/- 1.1143*0.085*sqrt(0.25) = 1.069742 / 1.164457, matching the engine. Confidence recomputed as max(35,min(92,78-9*T)) gives 75.75 at 3M, matching the engine, and it is identical for every pair (USDJPY 75.75 too). Realized EURUSD vol recomputed from yfinance: 1M 3.58 percent, 3M 4.18 percent (see OVDV), so the 8.5 percent default band input is about 2.4x realized.

findings.title: Confidence % is a tenor-only constant presented as model confidence
findings.detail: The confidence column (shown as a percent in the table) is 78 - 9*T clipped to [35,92]. It depends only on the tenor, not on the pair, spot, vol, data quality or any calibration, yet the UI column is simply titled Confidence. It reads as a probability-like quality score.
findings.evidence: FXFC_a.json: 77.25, 75.75, 73.5, 69.0 for EURUSD; FXFC_manual.json: 77.25 and 75.75 for USDJPY with a different spot and vol.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the confidence column, or rename it as an explicit tenor weight and say so in the UI.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed in code: _funcs.py:97 sets confidence = max(35, min(92, 78 - t*9)), which depends only on tenor T and never on pair, spot, vol or data quality. Sidecar FXFC default (EURUSD, live spot) returns 77.25, 75.75, 73.5, 69.0 for 1M/3M/6M/12M, which matches the formula exactly. The UI column is headed 'Conf.' with a percent suffix (FXFC.tsx:179-184), not 'Confidence' as the finding says, but it still reads as a probability-like score. The field_dictionary does say 'Deterministic model confidence score; lower for longer tenors', so the metric is disclosed in the API but not in the UI. A heuristic presented as a quality score is a presentation defect (P2), not a P1 calculation error.

findings.title: The forecast is the CIP forward, not a forecast
findings.detail: The forecast column equals the covered-interest-parity forward for each horizon. The pane does disclose this in its model note, but the function name and KPI label ('3M forecast') still present it as a forecast. Under the professional equivalent, a forecast is a consensus view; a CIP forward has no predictive content.
findings.evidence: FXFC_a.json: forecast 1.1171 at 3M equals the FRD 3M forward exactly.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the output to CIP forward path, or add a true consensus source. No keyless consensus FX forecast source was verified.

findings.title: Flat 8.5 percent vol default ignores the live realized vol in the same suite
findings.detail: The band vol defaults to 0.085 for every pair, including JPY and TRY pairs. The OVDV function in the same suite computes live realized vol for the pair, but FXFC does not use it, so the bands are about 2.4x the realized EURUSD 1M vol.
findings.evidence: FXFC_a.json vol_annualized=0.085 with source_mode live_yfinance_quote. yfinance EURUSD=X realized 1M (21 returns) = 3.5834 percent (independently recomputed).
findings.proposed_fix: Anchor the band vol to the same realized-vol term structure used by OVDV (or a pair-specific default), and label the source.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance EURUSD=X daily closes (already used by OVDV; recomputed here).

findings.title: Spot is labelled live with no timestamp, and disagrees with the same-day close
findings.detail: The spot 1.1143 is returned as live_yfinance_quote with no as-of time on the quote. The envelope fetched_at is 2026-11-08T00:07Z (a Sunday, thin FX liquidity). The same suite's history close for Friday 2026-11-06 is 1.12283 (0.76 percent higher), and the ECB fix dated 2026-11-06 is 1.1165. Three different EURUSD levels appear in one suite.
findings.evidence: FXFC_a.json spot 1.1143; FRD_a.json spot 1.1143; yfinance last close 2026-11-06 = 1.12283; api.frankfurter.app latest date 2026-11-06 EUR->USD 1.1165.
findings.proposed_fix: Return the quote timestamp and age, and flag quotes older than a threshold or outside the last close band as stale.
findings.keyless_source: api.frankfurter.app (ECB daily fix, verified date 2026-11-06).

b2.reference_method: FX hedge calculator: forward locks the foreign exposure at F = S*(1+r_home*T)/(1+r_foreign*T); unhedged residual stays open; output includes hedge notional, residual notional, P/L with and without hedge, and hedge cost from bid/ask (pips x notional), per the manifest. Short and long exposures must flip the hedge sign.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FXH. (1) Pane call {pair:EURUSD,hedge_ratio:0.75,days:90,usd_shock_pct:0.05,notional:1000000,base_rate:0.035,home_rate:0.045}: S 1.1143, F 1.117024, carry +2043.06, P&L if home strengthens -11885.69, weakens +15971.81. (2) Manifest-named {pair,exposure_notional:1e6,exposure_side:short_foreign,tenor:1Y,hedge_ratio:0.5,spot_shock_pct:10,bid_ask_pips:2}: result shows long-foreign sign, days 120, shock 5 percent (scenario_usd_strengthens_pct=5.0), no hedge_cost. (3) {action:forward,pair:EURUSD,days:90,...}: F 1.117024. (4) {exposures:[{currency:EUR,notional:1e6}],home_currency:USD,days:90}: base_rate silently 0.04. (5) {pair:EURUSD}: days 120 with assumed_defaults notional/base_rate/home_rate. (6) {pair:EURUSD,use_portfolio:true}: status data_unavailable. The use_portfolio call calls PortfolioState.import_legacy_crypto in the sandbox; this may have side effects there. Raw: scratchpad/b2/work/fx/FXH_*.json.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed the pane case by hand: F = 1.117024 (match); hedged notional 750000, unhedged 250000; P&L_strong = 250000*(1.1143*0.95-1.1143) + (1.117024-1.1143)*750000 = -11885.69 (match to the cent); carry 2043.06 (match).

findings.title: exposure_side is ignored, so short-foreign hedges are computed with long-foreign sign
findings.detail: The manifest exposes exposure_side (long_foreign / short_foreign), but the handler never reads it. Every exposure is treated as long foreign, so a short exposure gets the wrong hedge direction and P&L sign.
findings.evidence: FXH_manifest.json was called with exposure_side=short_foreign; pnl_if_home_strengthens = -26046.61 (long sign) and the exposure has no side field.
findings.proposed_fix: Read exposure_side and flip the sign of hedge notional, residual P&L and carry for short_foreign; return the side in the output.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. The handler fxh.py never reads exposure_side, and a grep of backend/showme finds it only in the seed manifest (fxh_seed.py:73-78, 134, 217, 251). Sidecar FXH calc with exposure_side=long_foreign and with short_foreign returns byte-identical outputs: pnl_if_home_strengthens -25712.35 and pnl_if_home_weakens 29287.65 in both. The seed says 'Sign convention: positive when shock moves with exposure_side', so the documented input is ignored and short exposures get long-foreign P&L. Severity is P2 rather than P1 because grep finds no exposure_side in ui/src: the pane never sends the input, so the wrong sign reaches API callers who pass the documented parameter, not pane users.

findings.title: Manifest output contract is not met; hedge cost and named fields are missing
findings.detail: The manifest must_have list requires hedge_notional, residual_notional, pnl_unhedged, pnl_hedged, hedge_cost and as_of. The handler returns hedged_notional_foreign, unhedged_notional_foreign, pnl_if_home_*, carry_pnl_home and no hedge_cost at all. bid_ask_pips is declared but never used. The hedge cost the methodology promises is never calculated.
findings.evidence: Keys in FXH_manifest.json: exposures, total_home_value, total_carry_pnl, total_pnl_if_home_strengthens, total_pnl_if_home_weakens, curve. hedge_cost, hedge_notional, residual_notional, pnl_unhedged, pnl_hedged are absent.
findings.proposed_fix: Add hedge_cost = hedged_notional * bid_ask_pips/10000 and the named contract fields, or update the manifest to the fields actually returned.

findings.title: Manifest spot_shock_pct and tenor are ignored; shock units differ
findings.detail: The manifest declares spot_shock_pct in percent (default 5.0) and tenor (1W..1Y). The handler reads usd_shock_pct as a decimal (default 0.05) and days, not tenor. Sending spot_shock_pct=10 silently produces a 5 percent scenario.
findings.evidence: FXH_manifest.json: scenario_usd_strengthens_pct=5.0 and days_to_maturity=120 despite spot_shock_pct=10 and tenor=1Y.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept spot_shock_pct (percent) and tenor (mapped to days) in the handler, or change the manifest names and units to match the pane.

findings.title: Router silently injects days=120 into FXH, overriding the documented default of 90
findings.detail: _route_function_params merges agent-profile defaults (days 120, live true, timeouts 3 s, limit 6) for every function call that omits them. FXH documents and implements a 90-day default, but a call with no days returns days_to_maturity 120 with no warning, and days is not listed in assumed_defaults.
findings.evidence: FXH_defaults_only.json (pair only): days_to_maturity=120, assumed_defaults=[notional, base_rate, home_rate]. FXH_pane.json (days=90 sent): days 90.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude FX functions from the agent-profile defaults, or echo injected defaults in assumed_defaults.

findings.title: Silent base_rate=0.04 fallback in the explicit-exposure path
findings.detail: When exposures are passed without base_rate, the handler uses 0.04, a value that is neither the documented DEFAULT_BASE_RATE (0.035) nor reported in assumed_defaults.
findings.evidence: FXH_noexp_rates.json: assumed_defaults=[]; forward 1.115660 = 1.1143*(1+0.045*90/365)/(1+0.04*90/365), which proves 0.04 was used.
findings.proposed_fix: Use DEFAULT_BASE_RATE and add base_rate to assumed_defaults, or require the rate.

findings.title: use_portfolio returns a misleading data_unavailable reason and mis-sizes notionals
findings.detail: Portfolio mode groups positions by currency, but position notional is quantity*avg_cost (a home-currency value, used as foreign units). The test book is all USD, so home (USD) positions are dropped and the exposure list is empty. The response then says 'No exposure has a usable spot rate' (a spot-provider message) and sets envelope status ok, which points the user at the wrong problem.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/fx/fxh.py:174-186 (_derive_exposures, notional at 184) and fxh.py:86-95 (reason text at 89)
findings.evidence: FXH_portfolio.json: data.status=data_unavailable, reason 'No exposure has a usable spot rate', envelope status ok, sources [portfolio_state].
findings.proposed_fix: Report 'no non-home currency positions' when the list is empty, and convert position value to foreign units before hedging.

b2.reference_method: FX information portal: spot with daily change, forwards from CIP, ATM implied vol from market quotes, rate differential. Implied vol must come from option quotes, not an assumption.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/FXIP {pair:EURUSD,days:90}: spot 1.1143 (yfinance), daily_change_pct -0.0595, 1M F 1.115239, 3M F 1.1171, implied_vol_atm_1m 8.45 (reference_vol_assumption), carry_annualized 0.01, base_rate 0.035 and quote_rate 0.045 (reference_policy_rate), 64 history rows, last close 2026-11-06 1.12283. Raw: scratchpad/b2/work/fx/FXIP_a.json.
b2.independent_check: daily_change_pct recomputed from the returned history: 1.1228259801864624 / 1.1234945058822632 - 1 = -0.0595 percent (match). Forwards match the FRD recomputation. Check passed.

findings.title: Field named implied_vol_atm_1m is a hard-coded 8.45 assumption
findings.detail: The 8.45 percent is the handler default, not a market implied vol. The pane caption says ASSUMPTION - NOT A QUOTE, but the field and the card are named implied, and the same suite (OVDV) reports 3.58 percent realized for EURUSD 1M. The suite therefore shows two incompatible 1M vol numbers for the same pair.
findings.evidence: FXIP_a.json: implied_vol_atm_1m=8.45, rows[5].source=reference_vol_assumption; OVDV_a.json atm_1m_vol_pct=3.5834.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to assumed_vol_atm_1m or replace with OVDV's live realized anchor and label it realized.

findings.title: Rates are the same stale 2024-06 constants, with no warning
findings.detail: FXIP takes base and quote rates from the same reference table as FRD (see FRD finding 1). Its reference notice covers only the spot, so the forwards and carry are presented with no rate-vintage warning.
findings.evidence: FXIP_a.json rows[1].value=0.035 and rows[2].value=0.045 with source reference_policy_rate; warnings=[].
findings.proposed_fix: Same as FRD: live or deposit-rate source, or a rate-vintage warning.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance ^IRX (US 13-week T-bill, 4.00 percent on 2026-11-06, verified). EUR not verified.

findings.title: Carry sign convention is shown green for the long-base reader
findings.detail: carry_annualized = r_quote - r_base (+1.0 percent here) is shown as positive/green. The caption states the formula, so it is honest, but a long-base holder pays this carry and the green tone implies the opposite.
findings.evidence: FXIP_a.json carry_annualized=0.01; FXIP.tsx tone positive when carry >= 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Show carry from the long-base perspective (r_base - r_quote) or drop the tone.

b2.reference_method: Treasury par/CMT yield curve per tenor over time (FRED DGS1MO-DGS30 daily CMT series). A professional GC/yield-curve grid shows the same curve by date and tenor; a 3D surface is an optional rendering of it.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/GC3D {days:365} -> HTTP 200, 1.37 s, sources [fred], metadata live=true data_mode=live_official, 248 dates x 10 tenors = 2480 points, dates 2025-11-10..2026-11-05. POST {days:365,reference:true} -> template: summary.days=30 (not 365), 3 dates, 30 points, source yield_curve_model. POST {days:90,tenors:[3M,30Y],live_curve:false,country:DE} -> still 10 tenors, 62 dates, 620 points, live US FRED (tenors/live_curve/country ignored). Artifacts in C:\Users\KULLAN~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\e0427571f2ca10f3\3bba841c-fb7f-440f-b54e-2b7d85c03def\scratchpad\b2\work\bond-2\GC3D_live365.json, GC3D_ref365.json, GC3D_tenors90.json.
b2.independent_check: Fetched all 10 FRED fredgraph.csv series (DGS3MO, DGS6MO, DGS1, DGS2, DGS3, DGS5, DGS7, DGS10, DGS20, DGS30) and compared every surface point: 2480 of 2480 points match within 0.005 pp, 0 dates missing in the window, latest DGS10 4.84 on 2026-11-05 matches. Script: ...\bond-2\check_gc3d.py.

findings.title: Manifest inputs tenors, live_curve and country are ignored
findings.detail: The handler reads only days, reference and fred_timeout. The seed exposes tenors (multiselect, 7-tenor default), live_curve and country, but none of them change the output: tenors 3M and 30Y were requested and all 10 tenors came back, live_curve=false still went to live FRED, and country=DE returned US FRED data with no warning. The user's selections are silently discarded.
findings.evidence: GC3D_tenors90.json: summary.tenors 10, points 620, sources [fred], no warnings, for a request with tenors [3M,30Y], live_curve false, country DE.
findings.proposed_fix: Honor tenors by filtering _FRED_TENORS; reject or implement country != US; remove live_curve or make it control reference mode; make the seed default match what is returned.

findings.title: Fallback template shows LOOK-BACK 30D regardless of the requested window
findings.detail: The template hard-codes days=30 in the payload and ignores the requested days. The pane caption reads summary.days, so a user who picks 1y in template mode sees LOOK-BACK 30D while the footer shows 365.
findings.evidence: GC3D_ref365.json: request days=365, summary.days=30, summary.dates=3. Footer status uses the pane state days (365), so the header and footer disagree.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass the clamped days into _surface_payload and build the template dates from it, or caption the pane from the requested days rather than summary.days.

findings.title: Fallback notice blames a missing FRED key
findings.detail: Whenever source_mode is not fred the pane says 'No FRED key is configured'. The engine already tries the keyless fredgraph.csv path, so a key is not the cause when that path fails. The message can give the user a false cause.
findings.evidence: Code path only; the template is also served when the keyless CSV fails (warning text 'Live FRED curve unavailable (keyed adapter or keyless CSV)').
findings.proposed_fix: Show the backend warning text instead of asserting the cause.

findings.title: Name and methodology say 3D surface; output is a 2D heat grid
findings.detail: The function is named Yield Curve 3D and its seed describes a surface, but the pane renders a tenor-by-date table with tint. The engine methodology admits the 2D fallback, but the name still overstates the output. The seed also claims business-day normalisation that gc3d.py does not perform (dates are passed through from FRED).
findings.evidence: Static reading. Output dates such as 2025-11-10 and 2025-11-12 are FRED observation dates with no normalisation step.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to 'Yield Curve Surface' or implement a real 3D view; remove the normalisation claim.

b2.reference_method: Professional equivalent is a capture-and-send workflow (capture the pane, attach, confirm recipient, send with audit trail). The handler is a plan-only stub, so the check is whether it reports its state honestly. No formula applies.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/GRAB x2: {target:current_pane, recipient:''} and {target:https://example.com, recipient:test@example.com}. Both HTTP 200, status draft_only, rows[0] capture status ready with output 'local screenshot artifact', rows[1] email status draft_only or not_configured. Envelope data_state 'live' and sources ['local_capture_plan']. Files: scratchpad/b2/work/misc-2/grab1.json, grab2.json.
b2.independent_check: No external data exists for GRAB. Checked in code and live: the handler never sends mail or captures pixels (no send path in _extras.py), the recipient is echoed back, and no artifact or draft is created.

findings.title: Capture reported ready though nothing is captured
findings.detail: The capture row says status ready with output 'local screenshot artifact', and the top-level status says draft_only, but no screenshot is taken and no draft is created. The plan implies capability that does not exist. The envelope also labels a static plan data_state live.
findings.evidence: grab1.json: rows[0]={step:capture,status:ready,output:local screenshot artifact}; data_state:live; no file written; grab2.json: status draft_only with recipient test@example.com and no draft object.
findings.proposed_fix: Use status not_implemented (or planned) for capture, drop 'ready' and 'draft_only' unless a real artifact or draft exists, and set data_state to reference for a static plan.

findings.title: Manifest seed describes a different function (shopping list)
findings.detail: grab_seed.py describes Shopping / Errands: inputs status (any/open/done) and tag, rows read from a preset store with rows=[] on an empty store, and semantic tests about store filtering. The shipped handler and pane are a screenshot-email capture plan. The catalog name is Screenshot Email while the seed name is Shopping / Errands, so the manifest contract is wrong.
findings.evidence: function-index: name 'Screenshot Email', description ''. Seed inputs 'status' and 'tag' are not read anywhere in _extras.py GRABFunction.execute.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite grab_seed.py to the screenshot-email contract (inputs target and recipient, output_contract rows and cards, semantic test: no transmission occurs).

findings.title: Envelope echoes unrelated default inputs
findings.detail: inputEcho on GRAB (and the other misc-2 calls) includes default query 'bitcoin cryptocurrency', symbols BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT and limit 6 that the GRAB handler ignores. This is confusing in a debug view.
findings.evidence: grab1.json inputEcho: {limit:6,days:120,range:3M,query:'bitcoin cryptocurrency',symbols:[BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT],live:true,target:current_pane,recipient:''}.
findings.proposed_fix: Echo only the parameters the handler declares.

b2.reference_method: Standard Black-Scholes(-Merton) Greeks with vega per 1 vol point, theta per calendar day, rho per 1 bp, aggregated as quantity x multiplier x per-contract Greek. Rates must be decimals; percent inputs must be unambiguous.
b2.live_call: 5 calls plus 1 no-rate call to /api/fn/GREEKS. g1 pane-style AAPL call (type/qty/expiry/rate, no spot/vol): delta 999.85, gamma 0.01616, vega 0.8296, theta -26.24, rho 4.434, spot 342.37 (yfinance_last_close), vol 0.2353 (realized_30d), T 0.1862. g3 SPY put (qty -5, mult 100, spot 610, K 600, vol 0.18, T 0.25, r 0.04): delta 183.51, gamma -3.4296, vega -574.26, theta 43.57, rho 2.980. g2 (r=4.0) gives identical totals to g3 (rate_source input_percent). g4 (r=0.5): delta 26.44, vega -164.45, rho 0.419. g5 (no expiry): status input_error, correctly refused. g6 (no rate): rate_source fred_DGS3MO_2026-11-05.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed Black-Scholes Greeks in python from the same inputs (scratch checks_a.py): g3 totals match to 6 decimals (delta 183.507431, vega -574.264058, theta 43.574906, rho 2.980416). g1 matches: spot 342.3699951 equals yfinance last close 2026-11-06, realized 30d vol 0.2352645 matches, and totals match to 6 decimals. Vega per 1 vol point and theta per calendar day and rho per bp scalings are verified. FRED DGS3MO last value 4.17 on 2026-11-05 equals the rate used in g6.

findings.title: Rate between 0 and 1 is read as decimal, so 0.5 (percent) prices at 50%
findings.detail: normalize_position treats any |r|<=1 as a decimal and only divides by 100 when |r|>1. A user typing 0.5 for a 0.5 percent rate gets a 50 percent rate, with no warning and rate_source set to plain input. Totals are wrong by about 100x in rate sensitivity: rho 0.42 instead of 3.29, vega -164 instead of -591, delta 26 instead of 202. The pane help text (GREEKS.tsx ~446) does not state the unit rule.
findings.evidence: g4_put_rate_0p5: r=0.5 -> totals delta 26.440022, vega -164.445748, rho 0.419048, rate_source input. Recomputed the same book at r=0.005: delta 202.088931, vega -590.752081, rho 3.291214. g2 r=4.0 and g3 r=0.04 both give vega -574.264. Rule is at greeks.py:134 (abs(rate)>1 -> /100).
findings.proposed_fix: Require an explicit unit (rate_pct or rate_bps) or refuse 0<|r|<=1 with an input_error that asks for the unit; always echo the interpreted rate in rows and sources.

verifier.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed in greeks.py:134: any |r|<=1 is taken as a decimal, |r|>1 is divided by 100. Sidecar check on one put: r=0.5 gives rate_source 'input' (no percent flag) and rho -0.639; r=0.005 gives rho -1.734. A typed 0.5 silently becomes 50%. The reviewer's 100x totals were not reproduced on my book, and the help text at GREEKS.tsx:446 does not state the rate unit. Downgraded from P1: the rule is documented in a code comment and matches the decimal convention used for vol, so the defect is silent unit ambiguity, not a miscalculation for the stated convention.

findings.title: Contract multiplier silently defaults to 100 and is not reported as an assumption
findings.detail: position_greeks uses int(pos.get('contract_size', 100)). The default is applied without an entry in assumptions_used, and the row shows contract_size as None, so the table's Mult column is blank while totals are scaled by 100. The pane help lists contract_size as optional, which hides the default.
findings.evidence: g1 (no contract_size): row contract_size None, delta 999.85 = 10 contracts x 100 x ~0.99985. assumptions_used absent from the response.
findings.proposed_fix: Record contract_size_source (input or default_100) in the row and in assumptions_used, and show the multiplier in the pane.

findings.title: European Black-Scholes is applied to listed options with no dividend yield input
findings.detail: Greeks are European closed-form values for any position, including American-style US equity options where early exercise matters, notably for puts and dividend-paying names. The dividend yield q is read from the position if present but the pane never sends it and the seed does not normalize it. The methodology says Black-Scholes, which is disclosed, but a professional book Greek (e.g. OVME-style American pricing) is not offered.
findings.evidence: position_greeks reads q = float(pos.get('q', 0.0)); GREEKS.tsx EXAMPLE_DRAFT and the pane never send q. The methodology string says Black-Scholes only.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose q as a documented input (dividend yield) in the pane, and label the model as European or add an American binomial option for listed equity options.

findings.title: Manifest methodology and semantic tests describe defaults that no longer exist
findings.detail: greeks_seed.py still says missing vol and T are substituted with 0.30 and 30 days, and tests assumptions_used for those defaults. The handler now refuses a missing expiry (input_error) and derives vol from 30-day realized history, so the seed text and tests are stale.
findings.evidence: g5 (no expiry) -> status input_error reason 'position 1 (AAPL): missing expiry (future date or years)'. The seed's semantic test greeks_missing_vol_and_T_reported_in_assumptions_used would now fail.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the methodology and semantic tests to match the current handler (expiry required, realized_30d vol, FRED DGS3MO rate).

b2.reference_method: Bloomberg ICX: full membership of a GICS sector or index (S&P 500 has 503 names, NDX 100, DAX 40, FTSE 100, CAC 40, STOXX 50, BIST 100, DJIA 30). Member prices with day change.
b2.live_call: ICX {index:'NDX'}: status ok, 29 rows, summary constituent_count 29 (ICX_ndx.json). ICX {index:'DAX'}: status ok, 10 rows (ICX_dax.json). ICX {sector:'Energy'} via /api/fn: status empty, warning "unknown index code 'AAPL STOCK'" (ICX_energy.json).
b2.independent_check: Day change AAPL -0.523003% (ShowMe) vs yfinance -0.523% (match); SAP.DE -2.3175% (ShowMe) vs yfinance -2.3175% (match). Index counts: DAX has 40 members (Wikipedia DAX page opened: 'consisting of the 40 major German blue chip companies'); ShowMe lists 10. Nasdaq-100 has 100 (Wikipedia page opened: 'issued by 100 of the largest non-financial companies'); ShowMe lists 29.

findings.title: Partial index tables presented as the full index
findings.detail: NDX returns 29 of 100 members, DAX 10 of 40, CAC 10 of 40, FTSE 10 of 100, STOXX 10 of 50, BIST 10 of 100 (counts from the bundled tables, not each index's own roster; only NDX and DAX were checked against the web). The response carries status 'ok' and the pane shows 'N constituents · DAX' with no partial flag. Only the methodology text admits they are subsets.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/screen/icx.py (_INDEX_CONSTITUENTS tables, around lines 200-305; _execute_index 626-724 returns status ok); ui/src/functions/ICX.tsx:64-73, 296-298
findings.evidence: ICX_dax.json summary constituent_count 10, status ok; ICX_ndx.json constituent_count 29. DAX count 40 and NDX count 100 confirmed on Wikipedia.
findings.proposed_fix: Set status to 'partial' with coverage (listed/official count) when a table is a subset, show that in the pane header, or load full rosters from a keyless source.

verifier.reasoning: Partly confirmed. Sidecar ICX index=DAX returns status 'ok', constituents 10, summary constituent_count 10, no partial warning. ICX index=NDX returns status 'ok', constituents 29. The bundled tables are curated subsets (icx.py _INDEX_CONSTITUENTS, methodology text at ~179-190 and the module docstring say so). The DAX 40-member and NDX 100-member sizes are canonical index sizes. The pane subtitle at ICX.tsx:298 reads '10 constituents · DAX' with no partial flag, so the user can read it as the full index. The methodology disclosure keeps this at P2 rather than P1.

findings.title: GICS sector view is a sample of 5-10 names per sector
findings.detail: Sector tables hold 5 to 10 hand-picked large caps (IT 10, Energy 6, Utilities 5, Real Estate 5), even though the bundled sp500.json has all 503 names. The sector path is therefore incomplete and labelled 'showme_gics_reference' as if it were the GICS membership.
findings.evidence: Import check: _SECTOR_CONSTITUENTS sizes {Information Technology:10, Energy:6, Utilities:5, Real Estate:5, ...}; sp500.json count 503.
findings.proposed_fix: Assign each of the 503 names to its sector (yfinance Ticker.info sector, verified) and serve full sector membership.

findings.title: sector input unreachable through /api/fn, and not exposed in the pane
findings.detail: When index is absent, the routed layer copies the agent news query into index (AAPL STOCK), so the sector branch never runs and returns an empty 'unknown index code' result. The pane always sends index, so the UI is unaffected, but the sector view is dead via the API and missing from the UI.
findings.evidence: ICX_energy.json: call with sector 'Energy' returned status empty, warnings ["unknown index code 'AAPL STOCK'"], summary index 'AAPL STOCK'.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not default index from query when sector is supplied; add a sector selector to the pane.

b2.reference_method: Language selection should use BCP 47 language tags and report translation coverage per locale computed from the message catalog (missing keys / fallback count), not a constant.
b2.live_call: POST /api/fn/LANG: {lang:zz} -> input_error with supported list (lang_zz.json); {} -> status ready, lang tr, 12 rows, lang.txt rewritten to tr (lang_default.json); {lang:de} -> selected de, requires_reload true (lang_de.json); {lang:tr} restored. Side effect: the sandbox runtime/lang.txt was written. It was set to de and then back to tr, but its value before my first call was not recorded. Its current value is tr.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed from ui/src/i18n/*.json: all 12 catalogs contain 138/138 English keys, so the 12-locale list and the selected flag are right. The per-row coverage label 'core_labels' is a constant, not derived from the catalogs, so the coverage claim fails. Identical-to-English counts: tr 9, de 15, fr 18, es 12, it 11, pt 12, ru/zh/ja/ko/ar 4 each.

findings.title: Missing lang silently switches the persisted language to Turkish
findings.detail: The handler falls back to 'tr' when lang is absent and then writes runtime/lang.txt. A parameterless call therefore overwrites the saved preference and reports status ready. The seed declares lang required=True, which the handler does not enforce.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/_extras.py:87 (target = (params.get('lang') or 'tr')) and the write just after it; backend/showme/manifest/seeds/lang_seed.py (lang InputSpec required=True)
findings.evidence: lang_default.json: status ready, lang tr, sel [tr]; the runtime/lang.txt file changed to tr from the call with no parameters.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status input_error when lang is missing, as for an unsupported code, and never write the preference without an explicit value.

findings.title: Coverage label hard-coded and misleading
findings.detail: Every row carries coverage 'core_labels' regardless of the real catalog. Sources lists showme_i18n_registry, which the handler never reads. The pane computes its own coverage, so the backend and pane disagree. Catalogs are complete at key level but 4 to 18 strings per locale equal English.
findings.evidence: ui/src/i18n: 138/138 keys in every locale; identical-to-English counts from the same files; lang_de.json rows coverage ['core_labels'].
findings.proposed_fix: Compute coverage from the catalogs (keys present, identical-to-English count) or remove the claim, and stop listing a registry source the handler does not read.

findings.title: Unsupported-language next action is generic

b2.reference_method: Order-book microstructure: spread_bps = (ask - bid)/mid*1e4; microprice = size-weighted mid; top-of-book imbalance = (bid_size - ask_size)/(sum); Kyle's lambda = price-impact slope of signed order flow on price change.
b2.live_call: MICRO {symbol:'BTCUSDT', asset_class:'CRYPTO', depth_levels:20}: status ok, live_exchange (MICRO_btc20.json). MICRO {symbol:'AAPL', asset_class:'EQUITY'}: status empty, data_mode explicit_unavailable (MICRO_aapl.json).
