Top-5/10/20 bucket imbalances from returned levels match surface values. Kyle lambda recomputed from fresh 1m klines: 8.21847e-11 vs returned 8.21869e-11 (match within bar-timing drift).

findings.title: Kyle lambda is not in the pane and is not Kyle's lambda
findings.detail: The pane does not render kyle_lambda_proxy, the depth surface buckets or top10_imbalance, although the function is named for them (MICRO.tsx:18-20 admits this). Separately, the statistic is the slope of |log return| on dollar volume, with no intercept and no signed order flow. Kyle's lambda is a price-impact slope on signed order flow, and the Binance klines already carry taker-buy volume (index 9) that would support it.
findings.evidence: Kline row length 12; index 5 volume 2.26663, index 9 taker_buy_base 0.61196. Output kyle_lambda_proxy 8.2187e-11, kyle_lambda_bps_per_1m_usd 0.82.
findings.proposed_fix: Regress signed flow (taker buy minus sell) on returns, add the intercept, label the unit, and render the lambda and depth buckets in the pane.

findings.title: Mempool Backlog is a sum over projected blocks, not the mempool count
findings.detail: Mempool Backlog = sum of nTx over the projected next blocks (8 in the response). The mempool-wide count is an endpoint the function does not call. The two agree now (56,528 backend vs 56,518 count, within the same minute), but the label describes a quantity the handler does not measure, and under heavy congestion the value is capped to the projected window.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/misc/onch.py:154 (mempool_count = sum over blocks) and :191 (row 'Mempool Backlog' with context 'Across N projected blocks')

b2.reference_method: PCA of the return covariance over an explicit lookback (typically 1 to 2 years), with sign-normalised components so a +k sigma shock has a stated direction, portfolio P&L = sum of weight x asset shock x market value, and all positions included in weights.
b2.live_call: 5 calls to /api/fn/PCAS. p1 pane request (live true, live_prices true, include_legacy true): status ok, sources yfinance, data_state live, samples 83, total_notional 114,141.5, portfolio_return +1.44pct, asset_returns only MSFT, NVDA, SPY, TLT, GLD. p5 same request plus days 504: all seven positions, samples 502, notional 112,616.9, return +2.93pct. p2 (live true, no live_prices, the MODEL toggle): status ok, sources portfolio_state_template_returns, data_state synthetic, EV ratio 0.918 on PC1, pnl -1,693.55. p3 (live false): status provider_unavailable, reason 'live=true required for PCA stress'. p4 (pc_index 1, k 2): provider_unavailable, reason 'no live return history'.
b2.independent_check: Recomputed PCA in python on the same five names (SVD on 347 daily returns): PC1 shock per name is MSFT -3.24pct, NVDA -6.42pct, SPY -1.81pct, GLD -1.79pct, TLT -0.03pct, i.e. opposite sign to the server's +5.10, +6.27, +2.18, +1.70, +0.01. Server p1 uses 83 samples, my recompute 347, so the window explains part of the gap, and the SVD sign convention explains the flip. Portfolio return on the five names is -2.41pct versus the server's +1.44pct. Weights over total (including the two unpriced positions at cost) recompute to -1.24pct. check_passed is false because the server's live result does not match a correct recompute on the same universe.

findings.title: Routed defaults shorten the window to 120 days and cap each fetch at 3 s; two positions drop out at cost while status says live
findings.detail: The routed layer injects days 120 and timeout 3 for every portfolio call. PCAS applies timeout per symbol, so slow symbols raise and are replaced by their average cost (and by 100 if avg_cost is missing). Those positions are removed from the return matrix but kept in total_notional and in the weight denominator. The response is status ok, data_state live and warnings empty. In p1, AAPL (50 at 180) and BTC-USD (0.5 at 95,000) were dropped, so 56,500 of cost-basis notional is counted with zero shock.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:289 (days 120) and 296 (timeout 3); backend/showme/engine/functions/portfolio/pcas.py:46-47, 54-65 (fallback avg_cost or 100 and empty series), 82-85 (total includes all), 87-88 (weights over total); portfolio/return_series.py align policy
findings.evidence: p1: samples 83, total_notional 114,141.49856567383 = 57,641.5 (five names at last close) + 56,500 (AAPL 50x180 and BTC 0.5x95,000). p5 with days 504 returned all seven names, samples 502, status ok. p4 failed with no live history, which shows the same transient fetch failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not inherit the 3 s routing timeout for portfolio analytics. Return a partial or input_error status and list the excluded positions when any position has no return series. Do not use avg_cost or 100 as a substitute price for a P&L shock.

verifier.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed in code: routed days=120 and timeout=3 are injected (_agent_runtime.py:289, 296; caller values override). On a per-symbol fetch exception pcas.py:54-65 substitutes avg_cost and an empty series with no warning. align_return_series drops empty series (return_series.py:66-70), while total and weights (pcas.py:82-88) still include every eligible name, so shocks are understated. I could not reproduce the drop: live_prices=true returned all seven names with data_state live, and a forced timeout of 0.01 returned an empty provider_unavailable envelope instead of the per-symbol fallback. Severity held at P2 until the partial-fallback case is observed; if it is, the false live label would justify P1.

findings.title: Sign of the k-sigma shock is arbitrary (SVD sign), so +3 sigma can be a gain or a loss
findings.detail: factor_shock uses the raw SVD row sign for the chosen component and applies +k*sigma with no sign normalisation. The same book and window can therefore show opposite P&L for the same nominal shock. The UI and the methodology text present it as a directional stress.
findings.evidence: Server p1 PC1 +3 sigma: portfolio +1.44pct. Recompute on the same five names: PC1 loadings negative, +3 sigma gives -2.41pct.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalise each component sign (for example positive loading on the market or the largest-weight asset) and report both +k and -k scenarios.

findings.title: MODEL toggle returns synthetic cosine template returns with status ok and a P&L headline
findings.detail: With live true and no live_prices (what the MODEL toggle sends), the function returns deterministic cosine-wave template returns, not market data. The response keeps status ok, the headline P&L is shown, and the template universe includes all seven names, unlike the live path. The data-quality badge is the only disclosure.
findings.evidence: p2: status ok, sources portfolio_state_template_returns, metadata synthetic true, EV ratio [0.918, 0.0815, 0.0004, 0, 0] (rank-1 artifact of the generator), portfolio_pnl -1,693.55.
findings.proposed_fix: Return status reference (not ok) with no P&L headline when template returns are used, and state the synthetic generator in the reason.

findings.title: Seed inputs and outputs for multi-PC shocks are not implemented
findings.detail: pcas_seed promises n_factors (model assumption), shock_set per component, lookback_window and frequency, and outputs components, shock_impacts and aggregate_impact. The handler stresses one component per call (pc_index), ignores n_factors and lookback_window, and returns no aggregate or per-component impact list. The pane therefore cannot run the documented correlated multi-factor stress.
findings.evidence: Handler reads pc_index, k_sigma, top_n, days, live, live_prices only. Response keys: asset_returns, top_loadings, explained_variance_ratio, no aggregate_impact or shock_impacts.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement n_factors with per-component shocks and an aggregate, or narrow the manifest to what is implemented.

b2.reference_method: Professional reading-queue equivalent (Bloomberg-style saved stories / reading list): a user's saved items shown in full, filtered only by filters the user actually sets, with honest read/unread state. Status default from manifest (unread,in_progress) returned [a2,a1], so the manifest default and the handler default (all statuses) differ. counts() = unread 2, read 1 matches the store.

findings.title: Default queue silently filtered to crypto peer symbols
findings.detail: When the caller sends no symbols/watchlist, the routed /api/fn layer injects the agent peer group (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT) as `symbols`. READ then keeps only saved items whose matched_symbol is in that set, so AAPL/MSFT saved articles disappear from the default view. The pane (READ.tsx:105-109) sends only limit and status, so the default pane view is affected. The KPI 'Unread' still counts the full queue, so the header can disagree with the list.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/news/read.py:78-80 and 97-102; backend/showme/server_routes/_agent_runtime.py:279-300 (_agent_function_params sets symbols=peer_symbols) and 770-800 (_route_function_params merges defaults before the handler)
findings.evidence: read_default.json metadata.watchlist=[BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT] for an empty request; scratch store check: no filter -> 3 rows, injected filter -> 1 row (a2 BTCUSDT only), AAPL a1 and MSFT a3 hidden.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not inject the peer group into READ (add READ to the exclusion list in _route_function_params or drop symbols from the READ defaults). Treat symbols as a filter only when the caller explicitly sends it.

verifier.reasoning: Confirmed. _route_function_params (_agent_runtime.py:770-800) takes defaults from _agent_function_params, which sets symbols=peer_symbols, and READ is not excluded. Live READ with {} returns metadata.watchlist=[BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT]. READ (read.py:78-80, 97-102) passes that as the symbol filter. Isolated reproduction with ReadingListStore in a temp DB (3 saved rows AAPL/BTCUSDT/MSFT): no filter returns 3 rows; the injected peer filter returns only BTCUSDT. counts() is unfiltered, so the KPI disagrees with the list. Severity downgraded to P2 because this is a silent injected filter (silent fallback) rather than a wrong calculation. The pane (READ.tsx) sends only limit and status (plus symbol when set), so the default view is affected.

findings.title: A missing last price reads as a -100% move and is labelled live
findings.detail: When the quote has a previous close but no last price, last becomes 0 and the change becomes -100%. The row still carries quote_type live.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/screen/sect.py:126 (chg_pct = ((last or 0) / (prev or 1) - 1) * 100 if prev else None); row quote_type live set in the same block
findings.evidence: Stub reproduction (sect_stub.py, no sidecar call, nothing written to the repo): quote last=None, close_prev=100 gives change_pct -100.0 and quote_type live. Normal quote gives +1.0.
findings.proposed_fix: If last is None, set change_pct None and quote_type unavailable. Never coalesce a missing price to 0.

verifier.reasoning: The arithmetic defect is real but latent, so it is not a live P1. sect.py:126 computes ((last or 0)/(prev or 1)-1)*100 when prev is truthy, so last None gives -100, and row quote_type 'live' is set at :132 regardless. However, no path through the wired yfinance adapter produces last None with a truthy close_prev. The fast_info path raises when last_price is None (yfinance_adapter.py ~265-266). The chart path sets last = regularMarketPrice or previousClose, so last None implies previousClose is falsy, which also makes close_prev falsy (lines 255-280). The Stooq race path sets close_prev None (~line 345). The stub reproduction is correct for the arithmetic but was not reached through a live call. Only a future provider returning last None would hit it.

findings.title: Live mode delivers only 1D change, so MTD, QTD and YTD are not computed
findings.detail: The live path hard-codes live_period 1D. The pane discloses this in a warning, but the function is described as a day/MTD/QTD/YTD heatmap, and the requested period has no effect on live values.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/screen/sect.py:113 (live_period = '1D'); description line in sect.py header; pane MarketHeatmap.tsx:68-75 sends period
findings.evidence: SECT_ytd.json: period YTD, change_pct_period 1D, warning 'SECT live mode currently delivers intraday 1D changes only'.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute period returns from daily history: last close divided by the last close before the period start, minus 1.
findings.keyless_source: yfinance daily history from 2026-01-01 for XLK returned a usable first close (144.30) and last close (164.74) for YTD.

findings.title: Model-mode MTD, QTD and YTD values are the 1D model multiplied by fixed factors
findings.detail: In model mode the period values are the daily model number times fixed factors (2.4, 4.6, 8.8). They are not measurements. The rows are labelled model, so this is a labelling and methodology issue, not a false live claim.
findings.evidence: SECT_model.json: XLK YTD change_pct 3.696 = 0.42 x 8.8; status model, quote_type model.
findings.proposed_fix: Show model periods as illustrative only, or drop them, and do not present them as period returns.

findings.detail: The handler takes only the first regex hit for customer-concentration wording and a 3,221-character window around it. That window does not contain the 'represented 22%' sentence. On the whole document the regex captures the preceding clause, producing names such as 'l year 2026, sales to one direct customer' rather than a counterparty label.
findings.file_line: backend/showme/engine/functions/equity/splc.py:78 (first-hit section only); backend/showme/engine/core/sec_taxonomy.py:98-108 (find_section_window), :112-114 (_NAME_NEAR_PCT captures the preceding clause)

findings.proposed_fix: Scan all concentration matches across the document rather than the first window, and constrain the name group to a company name or the phrase 'one direct customer' with an explicit label.

The FRED live_rate path (ovme.py:113-118) uses DGS1, a 1-year Treasury yield, for any maturity T; the pane does not send live_rate, so this is API-only.

blind_spots.area: Unverified high-severity findings in functions with check=false
blind_spots.why: Many P0/P1 findings sit in functions with no numeric recomputation, including CRPR (2xP0), SAT (2xP0), FTS (2xP0), CPF, WETR, TLDR, ACCT, TRA, MOST, TSOX, CORR, DARK, DPF, LITM, COUN, NSE, TCA, EXEC and FXGO. Their severities are unconfirmed, so the highest-risk items may be false positives or understated.
blind_spots.suggestion: Require a reproducible test or independent recomputation for every P0/P1 with check=false, starting with the P0 list, before trusting the severity ranking.

blind_spots.why: APPL, ALRT, BMC, GRAB, SOSC, TOP, BMTX, BTFW, BTUNE and LOTS have no numeric check at all. TOP (P0), BMTX (P0) and LOTS (P0) are among them, so these were effectively reviewed by reading only.
blind_spots.suggestion: Decide whether each one has numeric output. If it does, run the recomputation; if it does not, record that explicitly as non-numeric so the gap is visible.

blind_spots.area: Intraday timing, as-of dates and market calendars
blind_spots.why: A static review and a numeric recomputation both use a fixed snapshot. They cannot see stale quotes, mixed as-of timestamps across fields, time zone or session-close mismatches, holiday calendars, or ex-dividend and settlement date logic. This matters for GEX, OMON, IVOL, FXH, FX and bond functions.
blind_spots.suggestion: Replay each numeric function against timestamped snapshots taken at different times of day, with mixed as-of inputs and a holiday or half-day calendar, and assert that outputs carry the correct as-of time.

blind_spots.area: Provider outages, empty and partial responses
blind_spots.why: The review inspects code paths but does not inject failures. Empty arrays, 429 or timeout responses, partial field sets and null vendor values are the usual source of silent wrong numbers or crashes in terminal functions such as DAPI, FLDS, BQL and the bulk price-history paths.
blind_spots.suggestion: Add fault-injection tests with empty, null, truncated, rate-limited and timed-out provider responses for each data-fetching function, and check that each one degrades visibly rather than returning plausible values.

blind_spots.why: The workspace sits under a Turkish-locale Windows profile (Kullanıcı). Decimal comma versus dot, thousands separators, dd.mm versus mm/dd dates and Turkish-dotted-I case folding can all corrupt parsed numbers or tickers without any calculation error that a formula recomputation would catch.
blind_spots.suggestion: Run parsing and formatting tests under tr-TR and en-US inputs, including negative numbers, percentages, dates and tickers containing I or ı, and compare parsed values to expected values.

blind_spots.why: Findings on tables, sorting, truncation, chart axes, label overlap, responsive layout and stale state after a refresh are invisible to code reading and to numeric checks.
blind_spots.suggestion: Render each screen with representative data (empty, one row, very large values, negatives) at desktop and phone widths, capture screenshots, and check console errors on each one.

blind_spots.why: Functions that share inputs can disagree while each looks correct alone: DCF, DCFS and WACC; PORT, PORT_OPT and PORT_WHATIF; GREEKS, OVME and OVDV; and CRVF, DDIS and DEBT. The review was per function, so these mismatches were not checked.
blind_spots.suggestion: Build a consistency matrix of shared inputs and outputs (for example, the same WACC or the same option price fed through each function) and assert equality or documented differences.

blind_spots.why: reviewed=true only says a function was read. It does not show branch coverage, error paths, or the edge cases that matter in financial code, such as zero or negative denominators, division by zero in ratios, and sign flips in P&L or greeks.
blind_spots.suggestion: Measure branch coverage for each function and add targeted tests for zero, negative, NaN and extreme inputs, then confirm that each surviving finding is backed by a test or repro.

blind_spots.why: Findings reported so far are not shown to have been fixed or re-verified, and the review did not state whether it searched for hardcoded API keys, eval or unsafe string-built requests, or unescaped output.
blind_spots.suggestion: After fixes, re-run the failing checks to confirm them, and run a secrets and injection scan (keys in source, eval, unvalidated query parameters) across the repository.
